- `isValidationPayload(value)`, `ValidationError`, `flattenFieldErrors(rhfErrors)`, `findField(root, name)`, `focusField(el)`, `focusFirstInvalid(root, errors)`, `formDataToObject(formData)`.

## Accessibility

- The summary is a `role="alert"` region; each error is a link that focuses its field.
- Fields carry `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` pointing at their messages.
- While processing the form is `aria-busy` and the submit button is `aria-busy` + `aria-disabled` (it keeps focus).

---

<!-- docs/form-scaffolding/form-field.md -->

# FormField

A label, a control, help text and error messages, laid out **stacked** (label above) or **inline** (label beside). Inline labels fall back to stacked when the field is narrow.

```tsx
import { FormField, TextInput } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<FormField label="Email" name="email" help="We'll send the receipt here." required>
  <TextInput type="email" />
</FormField>
```

The control inside receives `id`, `name`, `aria-describedby` (help and errors), `aria-invalid`, `aria-required`, `required` and `disabled`. Props set directly on the control win.

## Label layouts

```tsx
<FormField label="Name" labelLayout="inline">…</FormField>

// For a whole form or section
<FormLayoutProvider labelLayout="inline">…</FormLayoutProvider>

// For the whole app
<OnuProvider labelLayout="inline">…</OnuProvider>
```

The inline label column is `--onu-label-width` wide (12rem by default). Below about 28rem of container width the field stacks. In RTL the label sits on the right.

## Errors

Pass `error` directly, or provide server errors to every field by `name` with `FormErrorsProvider`. Laravel's 422 `errors` object works as is, including array fields:

```tsx
<FormErrorsProvider errors={errors /* e.g. Inertia's usePage().props.errors */}>
  <FormField label="Item" name="items[0][name]">
    {" "}
    {/* reads errors["items.0.name"] */}
    <TextInput />
  </FormField>
</FormErrorsProvider>
```

## Props

| Prop          | Type                              | Default              | Description                                              |
| ------------- | --------------------------------- | -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label`       | `ReactNode`                       |                      | Visible label                                            |
| `name`        | `string`                          |                      | Field name; wires `name` and server errors               |
| `id`          | `string`                          | generated            | Control id                                               |
| `help`        | `ReactNode`                       |                      | Help text under the control                              |
| `error`       | `string \| string[]`              |                      | Error message(s), merged with server errors              |
| `required`    | `boolean`                         | `false`              | Shows the required marker and sets `aria-required`       |
| `disabled`    | `boolean`                         | from form            | Disables the control                                     |
| `labelLayout` | `'stacked' \| 'inline'`           | from form / provider | Label layout                                             |
| `hideLabel`   | `boolean`                         | `false`              | Hide the label visually, keep it for screen readers      |
| `labelAside`  | `ReactNode`                       |                      | Content beside the label, e.g. a "Forgot password?" link |
| `classNames`  | `{ label, control, help, error }` |                      | Classes for each part                                    |

## Hooks

- `useFormField()`: the current field (`id`, `invalid`, `required`, …) or `null`.
- `useFormFieldControl(props)`: the props a custom control should spread to be wired to the field.

## Accessibility

- The label is a real `<label for>`; help and errors are linked with `aria-describedby`.
- Errors are announced in a polite live region.
- The required marker is hidden from screen readers; the control carries `aria-required`.

---

<!-- docs/form-scaffolding/form-context.md -->

# Form layout & errors

Providers that configure every [`FormField`](./form-field.md) inside them.

## FormLayoutProvider

Sets the label layout and disabled state for a group of fields. Nested providers override outer ones; a field's own props override both.

```tsx
import { FormLayoutProvider } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<FormLayoutProvider labelLayout="inline" disabled={processing}>
  …
</FormLayoutProvider>
```

[`Form`](./form.md), [`FormGroup`](./form-group.md) and [`Fieldset`](./fieldset.md) render one for their `labelLayout` and `disabled` props, so you rarely need it directly.

### Props

| Prop          | Type                    | Default                            | Description                         |
| ------------- | ----------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `labelLayout` | `"stacked" \| "inline"` | outer provider, then `OnuProvider` | Label layout for every field inside |
| `disabled`    | `boolean`               | outer provider, then `false`       | Disables every field inside         |
| `children`    | `ReactNode`             |                                    |                                     |

## FormErrorsProvider

Provides server-side validation errors by field name. Accepts Laravel's 422 `errors` object: keys in dot notation, values as a string or an array of strings.

```tsx
import { FormErrorsProvider } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<FormErrorsProvider errors={{ email: ["The email has already been taken."] }}>
  <FormField label="Email" name="email">
    <TextInput />
  </FormField>
</FormErrorsProvider>
```

Field names in bracket notation (`items[0][name]`) are matched to dot notation (`items.0.name`). A field's own `error` prop is shown first, then the server errors for its `name`. [`Form`](./form.md) renders this provider for its `errors` prop.

### Props

| Prop       | Type                                                      | Default | Description                                 |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `errors`   | `Record<string, string \| string[] \| undefined> \| null` |         | Errors keyed by field name, in dot notation |
| `children` | `ReactNode`                                               |         |                                             |

## Helpers

| Export                      | Description                              |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `useLabelLayout(explicit?)` | Effective label layout for a field       |
| `useFormDisabled()`         | Disabled state from the nearest provider |
| `useFieldErrors(name)`      | Server errors for a field name           |
| `toDotNotation(name)`       | `items[0][name]` → `items.0.name`        |

## Accessibility

The providers render no markup; they only change what each [`FormField`](./form-field.md) renders:

- **Errors.** A field with server errors gets `aria-invalid="true"` and its messages in a polite live region linked with `aria-describedby`, so they are read with the field and announced when they arrive. The providers do not move focus; [`Form`](./form.md) focuses the first invalid field when errors arrive.
- **Disabled.** `disabled` sets the native `disabled` attribute on every control, which also removes them from the tab order and from form submission. To keep values readable and focusable (for example while a request is in flight), prefer `readOnly` on the controls.
- **Inline labels** stay real `<label>` elements tied to their control, and fall back to stacked in narrow containers, so a narrow column or a zoomed-in page does not squeeze the control.

---

<!-- docs/form-scaffolding/form-group.md -->

# FormGroup

Lays out related fields in a responsive grid and sets their label layout. Columns respond to the group's own width (container queries), so a two-column group inside a narrow card stacks to one column.

```tsx
import { FormGroup, FormField, TextInput } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<FormGroup columns={2}>
  <FormField label="First name">
    <TextInput />
  </FormField>
  <FormField label="Last name">
    <TextInput />
  </FormField>
  <FormField label="Address" className="col-span-full">
    <TextInput />
  </FormField>
</FormGroup>
```

## Props

| Prop          | Type                    | Default   | Description                          |
| ------------- | ----------------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `columns`     | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4`      | `1`       | Columns on wide containers           |
| `labelLayout` | `'stacked' \| 'inline'` | inherited | Label layout for the fields inside   |
| `disabled`    | `boolean`               | inherited | Disable the fields inside            |
| `className`   | `string`                |           | Classes for the root (the container) |
| `classNames`  | `{ grid }`              |           | Classes for the grid                 |

Column breakpoints: 2 columns from a 36rem wide group, 3–4 columns from 56rem. `formGroupVariants` is exported.

## Accessibility

A layout container only; it adds no roles. Use a [`Fieldset`](./fieldset.md) when the group needs a title that screen readers announce.

---

<!-- docs/form-scaffolding/fieldset.md -->

# Fieldset / FormSection

A titled section of a form: a real `<fieldset>` with a `<legend>`, an optional description, and an optional collapse toggle. `FormSection` is an alias.

```tsx
import { Fieldset, FormField, TextInput } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<Fieldset legend="Permanent address" description="As registered with the Department of National Registration.">
  <FormField label="Island" name="island">
    <TextInput />
  </FormField>
</Fieldset>
```

## Collapsible

```tsx
<Fieldset legend="Advanced settings" collapsible defaultOpen={false}>
  …
</Fieldset>
```

The legend becomes a toggle button. A collapsed section stays in the DOM, so its fields are still submitted, and it opens itself when one of its fields needs focus: a native `invalid` event, a link in the [error summary](./validation-summary.md), or [`Form`](./form.md) focusing the first invalid field. Custom containers can do the same by listening for the `onu:reveal` event.

## Variants

`plain` (default), `card` (bordered card) and `separated` (a rule above every section but the first). `fieldsetVariants` is exported.

## Props

| Prop           | Type                                        | Default   | Description                                          |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------- | --------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `legend`       | `ReactNode`                                 |           | Section title                                        |
| `description`  | `ReactNode`                                 |           | Text under the title, linked with `aria-describedby` |
| `variant`      | `'plain' \| 'card' \| 'separated'`          | `plain`   | Look                                                 |
| `collapsible`  | `boolean`                                   | `false`   | Show / hide toggle                                   |
| `defaultOpen`  | `boolean`                                   | `true`    | Initial state when collapsible                       |
| `open`         | `boolean`                                   |           | Controlled state                                     |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void`                   |           | Called when the state changes                        |
| `labelLayout`  | `'stacked' \| 'inline'`                     | inherited | Label layout for the fields inside                   |
| `disabled`     | `boolean`                                   | inherited | Disables every control inside (native)               |
| `hideLegend`   | `boolean`                                   | `false`   | Hide the legend visually                             |
| `classNames`   | `{ legend, description, content, trigger }` |           | Classes for each part                                |

## Accessibility

- Screen readers announce the legend when focus enters the section.
- The collapse toggle is a button with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`.

| Key                                 | Action                         |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | Expand or collapse the section |

## RTL

The chevron sits at the inline end; the legend aligns to the inline start.

---

<!-- docs/form-scaffolding/label.md -->

# Label

shadcn's `Label` with a required marker or an "(optional)" note. [`FormField`](./form-field.md) renders labels for you; use `Label` for custom layouts.

```tsx
import { Label } from "@javaabu/onu"

<Label htmlFor="name" required>Name</Label>
<Label htmlFor="nickname" optional>Nickname</Label>
```

The shadcn primitive is still available from `@javaabu/onu/primitives`.

## Props

| Prop       | Type      | Default | Description                                   |
| ---------- | --------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | Adds the [required marker](./required-marker.md) |
| `optional` | `boolean` | `false` | Adds a muted "(optional)" note                |
| `invalid`  | `boolean` | `false` | Destructive colour                            |

All Radix `Label.Root` props are passed through.

## Accessibility

The marker is `aria-hidden`; mark the control itself `required`. The optional note is read as part of the label. Both strings are translated (`form.optional`).

---

<!-- docs/form-scaffolding/required-marker.md -->

# RequiredMarker

The `*` shown after a required field's label. [`FormField`](./form-field.md) adds it when `required` is set.

```tsx
import { RequiredMarker } from '@javaabu/onu';

<label>Name <RequiredMarker /></label>
<RequiredMarker symbol="(required)" />
```

## Props

| Prop        | Type     | Default | Description                                |
| ----------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `symbol`    | `string` | `"*"`   | Marker text                                |
| `className` | `string` |         | Merged with the default `text-destructive` |

Every other `<span>` prop is passed through.

## Accessibility

The marker is hidden from screen readers (`aria-hidden="true"`), so a label is not read as "Name star". Mark the control itself with `required` (or `aria-required`), which screen readers announce as "required". With `required`, [`FormField`](./form-field.md) adds the marker and sets `required` / `aria-required` on its control; [`Label`](./label.md) only adds the marker, so set `required` on your control yourself. The marker has a translated tooltip (`common.required`: "Required" / "ލާޒިމް") for mouse users. On long forms, explain the `*` once at the top.

---

<!-- docs/form-scaffolding/field-errors.md -->

# FieldErrors

Error messages for one field, each with an error icon. [`FormField`](./form-field.md) renders it for you.

```tsx
import { FieldErrors } from '@javaabu/onu';

<FieldErrors errors={['The name field is required.']} />
<FieldErrors errors={errors.name} firstOnly />
```

## Props

| Prop        | Type                         | Default | Description                                     |
| ----------- | ---------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `errors`    | `string \| string[] \| null` |         | Messages to show; empty strings are skipped     |
| `firstOnly` | `boolean`                    | `false` | Show only the first message                     |
| `className` | `string`                     |         | Container classes (destructive text by default) |

Other `<div>` props (such as `id`) are passed to the container. With no messages the container stays mounted and empty.

## Accessibility

The container is a polite live region (`aria-live="polite"`) that stays mounted, so errors that appear after a submit are announced without moving focus. The icon before each message is decorative (`aria-hidden`); the text carries the meaning, so an error is never shown by colour alone.

Give the container an `id`, reference it from the control's `aria-describedby` and set `aria-invalid` on the control. [`FormField`](./form-field.md) does all three for you.

---

<!-- docs/form-scaffolding/validation-summary.md -->

# ValidationSummary (AJAX validation errors)

An error summary for the top of a form. It lists every error, and each one is a link that moves focus to its field. It accepts Laravel's 422 response body as is. [`Form`](./form.md) renders it for you; use it directly when you handle requests yourself. `AjaxValidationErrors` is an alias.

```tsx
import { ValidationSummary } from "@javaabu/onu"

// The whole 422 body…
<ValidationSummary errors={response.data} />

// …or just the errors object
<ValidationSummary errors={{ email: ["The email has already been taken."], "items.0.name": "Required" }} />
```

Links find fields by `name` in the closest `<form>` (or `root`), matching dot and bracket notation: `items.0.name` finds `name="items[0][name]"`. A collapsed [`Fieldset`](./fieldset.md) around the field opens first.

## Props

| Prop          | Type                                                        | Default                 | Description                                    |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `errors`      | `Record<string, string \| string[]> \| { message, errors }` |                         | Errors, or a Laravel 422 body                  |
| `message`     | `ReactNode`                                                 |                         | General message when there are no field errors |
| `title`       | `ReactNode`                                                 | "There are N problems…" | Heading                                        |
| `labels`      | `Record<string, ReactNode>`                                 |                         | Field labels shown before each message         |
| `root`        | `RefObject<HTMLElement>`                                    | closest form            | Where to look for fields                       |
| `focusOnShow` | `boolean`                                                   | `false`                 | Move focus to the summary when it appears      |
| `classNames`  | `{ title, list, item, link, message }`                      |                         | Classes for each part                          |

Renders nothing when there are no errors and no message.

## Accessibility

- `role="alert"`, labelled by its heading, and focusable (`tabIndex=-1`) so it can receive focus after a failed submit.
- Each error is a real link; activating it focuses and scrolls to the field.
- Colour is not the only signal: the heading has an error icon and states the number of problems.

| Key              | Action                       |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>   | Move between error links     |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> | Focus the field for the link |

## RTL and Dhivehi

The heading is pluralised in both locales ("މި ފޯމުގައި 2 މައްސަލަ ވޭ"). The list indents from the inline start.

---

<!-- docs/form-scaffolding/help-text.md -->

# HelpText

Supporting text under a control. [`FormField`](./form-field.md) renders it from the `help` prop and links it with `aria-describedby`.

```tsx
import { HelpText } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<HelpText id="name-help">As shown on your ID card.</HelpText>
```

## Props

| Prop        | Type                        | Default | Description                                                |
| ----------- | --------------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`        | `string`                    |         | Reference it from the control's `aria-describedby`         |
| `className` | `string`                    |         | Merged with the defaults (`text-sm text-muted-foreground`) |
| `children`  | `ReactNode`                 |         | The help text                                              |
| `ref`       | `Ref<HTMLParagraphElement>` |         |                                                            |

Every other `<p>` prop is passed through.

## Accessibility

`HelpText` is a plain paragraph: it is read as the control's description only when the control points at it with `aria-describedby`. [`FormField`](./form-field.md) gives it an id and links it (with any error messages), so screen readers read the label and then the help. Put what users need before typing (formats, limits) in help text rather than in a placeholder, which disappears on input and is not reliably read.

---

<!-- docs/form-scaffolding/form-container.md -->

# FormContainer

A card-style layout for a form: a header (title, description, actions), the body and a footer for the buttons. It responds to its own width, so it works on a full page, in a dialog or in a narrow column. On narrow containers the footer buttons stack full width with the primary action on top.

```tsx
import { Form, FormContainer, FormField, SubmitButton, LinkButton, TextInput } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<Form onSubmit={save}>
  <FormContainer
    title="New staff member"
    description="They’ll get an email invitation."
    footer={
      <>
        <LinkButton href="/staff" variant="outline">
          Cancel
        </LinkButton>
        <SubmitButton>Invite</SubmitButton>
      </>
    }
  >
    <FormField label="Email" name="email">
      <TextInput type="email" />
    </FormField>
  </FormContainer>
</Form>
```

Wrap the container in the `Form` (as above) so footer buttons submit it, or give the buttons a `form="id"` attribute.

## Props

| Prop           | Type                                                       | Default | Description                            |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `title`        | `ReactNode`                                                |         | Heading; also names the region         |
| `description`  | `ReactNode`                                                |         | Text under the title                   |
| `headingLevel` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4`                                         | `2`     | Heading level                          |
| `actions`      | `ReactNode`                                                |         | Beside the title (status badge, links) |
| `media`        | `ReactNode`                                                |         | Above the title (logo)                 |
| `footer`       | `ReactNode`                                                |         | Buttons                                |
| `variant`      | `'card' \| 'plain'`                                        | `card`  | Card surface or none                   |
| `width`        | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'xl' \| 'full'`                   | `lg`    | Maximum width                          |
| `centered`     | `boolean`                                                  | `false` | Centre the header (auth pages)         |
| `classNames`   | `{ header, title, description, actions, content, footer }` |         | Classes for each part                  |

`formContainerVariants` is exported.

## Accessibility

Renders a `<section>` labelled by its title, with a real heading. The footer order puts the primary button last in the DOM (first visually when stacked), matching reading order on wide screens.

---

<!-- docs/form-scaffolding/repeating-group.md -->

# RepeatingGroup

A list of repeated rows of fields (line items, family members, contact numbers) with **Add**, **Remove** and **Move up / Move down**. It works with react-hook-form's `useFieldArray` or with a plain array in state, enforces `min` / `max`, and builds field names like `items[0][name]`.

## With a plain array

```tsx
import { RepeatingGroup, FormField, TextInput } from "@javaabu/onu"

const [members, setMembers] = useState([{ name: "" }])

<RepeatingGroup
  label="Family members"
  name="members"
  value={members}
  onChange={setMembers}
  createItem={() => ({ name: "" })}
  max={5}
>
  {({ item, index, name }) => (
    <FormField label="Name" name={name("name")}>
      <TextInput
        value={item.name}
        onChange={(e) => setMembers((m) => m.map((x, i) => (i === index ? { ...x, name: e.target.value } : x)))}
      />
    </FormField>
  )}
</RepeatingGroup>
```

## With react-hook-form

```tsx
const { fields, append, remove, move } = useFieldArray({ control: form.control, name: "items" })

<RepeatingGroup
  items={fields}
  onAdd={() => append({ name: "", qty: 1 })}
  onRemove={remove}
  onMove={move}
  name="items"
  nameFormat="dot"
  min={1}
>
  {({ name }) => (
    <FormField label="Item" name={name("name")}>
      <TextInput {...form.register(name("name") as `items.${number}.name`)} />
    </FormField>
  )}
</RepeatingGroup>
```

`name("qty")` gives `items[0][qty]` (`nameFormat="bracket"`, the Laravel form style) or `items.0.qty` (`"dot"`, react-hook-form). Server errors for `items.0.qty` reach the field either way.

## Props

| Prop          | Type                                                      | Default        | Description                                |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `children`    | `({ item, index, name, remove, canRemove }) => ReactNode` |                | Renders one row's fields                   |
| `items`       | `T[]`                                                     |                | Rows from `useFieldArray` (`fields`)       |
| `value`       | `T[]`                                                     |                | Rows of a plain controlled array           |
| `onChange`    | `(value: T[]) => void`                                    |                | Plain array updates (add, remove, reorder) |
| `createItem`  | `() => T`                                                 |                | New row for plain arrays                   |
| `onAdd`       | `() => void`                                              |                | Add handler (react-hook-form `append`)     |
| `onRemove`    | `(index) => void`                                         |                | Remove handler (react-hook-form `remove`)  |
| `onMove`      | `(from, to) => void`                                      |                | Reorder handler (react-hook-form `move`)   |
| `reorderable` | `boolean`                                                 | auto           | Show Move up / Move down                   |
| `min` / `max` | `number`                                                  | `0` / `∞`      | Limits; Remove / Add disable at the limit  |
| `name`        | `string`                                                  | `items`        | Base field name                            |
| `nameFormat`  | `'bracket' \| 'dot'`                                      | `bracket`      | Name style                                 |
| `getKey`      | `(item, index) => Key`                                    | `item.id`      | Row key                                    |
| `label`       | `ReactNode`                                               |                | Group title (names the group)              |
| `itemLabel`   | `(index, item) => ReactNode`                              | "Item {n}"     | Row title; `null` hides it                 |
| `addLabel`    | `ReactNode`                                               | "Add item"     | Add button text                            |
| `emptyText`   | `ReactNode`                                               | "No items yet" | Shown when there are no rows               |
| `disabled`    | `boolean`                                                 | `false`        | Disable the buttons                        |
| `classNames`  | `{ header, list, row, rowHeader, actions, add }`          |                | Classes for each part                      |

## Accessibility

- The group is `role="group"` named by `label`; rows are list items named "Item 1", "Item 2"…
- Every button has a specific name: "Remove item 2", "Move item 3 up".
- Focus: after **Add** it moves to the new row's first field; after **Remove** to the next row (or **Add** when the list is empty); after a move it stays on the moved row's button.
- Each change is announced in a polite live region ("Item 3 added", "Item moved to position 1").
- Row buttons are 44px on touch screens. Reordering uses buttons, so no drag gesture is needed.

| Key                                 | Action                              |
| ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>                      | Move through fields and row buttons |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | Activate Add / Remove / Move        |

## RTL and Dhivehi

Row actions sit at the inline end and stack under the fields on narrow containers. All labels and announcements are translated.

---

<!-- docs/form-scaffolding/inline-edit.md -->

# InlineEdit

Text that turns into an input when clicked, for quick edits on detail pages and tables. **Enter** saves, **Escape** cancels. Saves can be async: the editor shows progress and, if the save fails, stays open with the error.

```tsx
import { InlineEdit } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<InlineEdit label="Name" defaultValue="Aishath Shifa" onSave={(name) => api.patch(`/users/${id}`, { name })} />
```

## Thaana

```tsx
<InlineEdit label="ނަން" value={nameDv} onSave={saveDv} thaana />
```

With `thaana` the input types Thaana from a Latin keyboard and is `dir="rtl"` `lang="dv"`; the displayed value is marked `lang="dv"` too.

## Multiline

`multiline` uses a textarea: <kbd>Enter</kbd> adds a line and <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>⌘</kbd>+<kbd>Enter</kbd> saves.

## Props

| Prop             | Type                                 | Default | Description                                                 |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------ | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label`          | `string`                             |         | What is edited; used for accessible names                   |
| `value`          | `string`                             |         | Controlled value                                            |
| `defaultValue`   | `string`                             | `""`    | Uncontrolled initial value                                  |
| `onSave`         | `(value) => unknown`                 |         | Save; return a promise for a saving state, throw for errors |
| `onCancel`       | `() => void`                         |         | After Escape / Cancel                                       |
| `onChange`       | `(value) => void`                    |         | Every edit                                                  |
| `validate`       | `(value) => string \| null`          |         | Return a message to block saving                            |
| `placeholder`    | `string`                             | "Empty" | Shown when empty                                            |
| `multiline`      | `boolean`                            | `false` | Use a textarea                                              |
| `thaana`         | `boolean \| ThaanaOptions`           | `false` | Thaana keyboard                                             |
| `blurBehavior`   | `'save' \| 'cancel' \| 'none'`       | `save`  | What leaving the editor does                                |
| `renderValue`    | `(value) => ReactNode`               |         | Custom display                                              |
| `defaultEditing` | `boolean`                            | `false` | Start in edit mode                                          |
| `disabled`       | `boolean`                            | `false` | Read only                                                   |
| `inputProps`     | input props                          |         | Extra props for the input                                   |
| `classNames`     | `{ display, input, actions, error }` |         | Classes for each part                                       |

If the thrown error has a `message`, it is shown; otherwise "Couldn’t save. Please try again.".

## Accessibility

- The value is a button named "Edit Name: Aishath Shifa".
- In edit mode the input is labelled by `label` and described by the key hint; errors are announced (`role="alert"`) and linked with `aria-describedby`.
- After saving or cancelling, focus returns to the value; "Name saved" is announced.
- While saving, the input is read-only and `aria-busy`.

| Key                                         | Action                       |
| ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> (value) | Start editing                |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd>                            | Save (single line)           |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Enter</kbd>            | Save (multiline)             |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd>                           | Cancel and restore the value |

---

<!-- docs/form-scaffolding/autosave-indicator.md -->

# AutosaveIndicator

Shows whether changes are being saved automatically: **idle**, **saving**, **saved** (with relative time, "Saved 2 minutes ago") or **error** (with **Retry**). Pair it with the `useAutosave` hook.

```tsx
import { AutosaveIndicator, useAutosave } from "@javaabu/onu"

const autosave = useAutosave(draft, { onSave: (value) => api.put(`/posts/${id}/draft`, value), delay: 1000 })

<AutosaveIndicator {...autosave} />
```

Or drive it yourself:

```tsx
<AutosaveIndicator status="saved" lastSavedAt={savedAt} />
<AutosaveIndicator status="error" onRetry={retry} />
```

## Props

| Prop          | Type                                       | Default                 | Description                                 |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `status`      | `'idle' \| 'saving' \| 'saved' \| 'error'` |                         | Current state                               |
| `lastSavedAt` | `Date \| number`                           |                         | Shown as relative time, refreshed every 30s |
| `error`       | `ReactNode`                                | "Couldn’t save changes" | Error text                                  |
| `onRetry`     | `() => void`                               |                         | Shows a Retry button in the error state     |
| `compact`     | `boolean`                                  | `false`                 | Icon only (text kept for screen readers)    |

## useAutosave(value, options)

Saves `value` after it stops changing for `delay` ms. Returns `{ status, lastSavedAt, onRetry, flush }`; spread it into the indicator and call `flush()` to save immediately (e.g. on blur). A newer save always wins over a slower older one.

| Option    | Type                 | Default       | Description                |
| --------- | -------------------- | ------------- | -------------------------- |
| `onSave`  | `(value) => unknown` |               | Save; reject to show error |
| `delay`   | `number`             | `1000`        | Debounce in ms             |
| `enabled` | `boolean`            | `true`        | Pause saving               |
| `isEqual` | `(a, b) => boolean`  | JSON equality | Change detection           |

## Accessibility

Status changes are announced in a polite live region ("Saving…", "Saved", "Couldn’t save changes"). The ticking relative time is not re-announced. Status is shown with an icon and text, not colour alone.

## Dhivehi

Relative time uses the active locale's date-fns locale ("3 މިނިޓު ކުރިން ސޭވްކުރެވުނު").

---

<!-- docs/form-scaffolding/save-bar.md -->

# SaveBar

The save bar for edit pages (REQUIREMENTS §25.9). It lists each change in plain words, keeps **Save** disabled until something changed, has a **Discard** button, is a sticky side panel on desktop and a bar fixed to the bottom on phones, and warns before leaving with unsaved changes.

```tsx
import { Form, SaveBar, describeChanges } from "@javaabu/onu"

const changes = describeChanges(saved, values, { email: "Email", role: "Role" })

<Form onSubmit={save}>
  <div className="gap-6 lg:grid lg:grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_18rem] lg:items-start">
    <div className="gap-6 grid">{/* field cards */}</div>
    <SaveBar changes={changes} onDiscard={() => reset(saved)} successMessage="User saved" />
  </div>
</Form>
```

## Behaviour

- **While editing**: each change is listed, e.g. "Email changes to jane@new.com", "Role changes to Editor", "Phone is cleared". Save is disabled until there is a change.
- **Discard** calls `onDiscard`; put every field back to its saved value there.
- **Saving**: inside a [`Form`](./form.md) the Save button submits it and shows the form's processing state (spinner, no double clicks). Outside a form, pass `form="form-id"`, or `onSave` to save yourself.
- **On success**: the success message appears; the list empties once your saved values update.
- **On error**: "Your changes were not saved. Please try again." The `Form` shows each error under its field and focuses the first one.
- **Leaving**: while there are unsaved changes, closing or reloading the tab shows the browser's "Leave site?" prompt, and clicking an in-app link (including hash-router links such as `#/users`) or pressing the browser's Back button asks "You have unsaved changes. Leave anyway?". Nothing is asked once changes are saved or discarded. For programmatic visits, use [`useUnsavedChangesGuard`](./unsaved-changes-guard.md).

## describeChanges(saved, current, labels, format?)

Compares the keys in `labels` (in that order) and returns `SaveBarChange[]`. The values can be any object type, including an `interface`. `format` maps a key to a display value (each formatter receives that key's typed value) (e.g. a role id to its name). Values are formatted for the locale: numbers, dates, yes/no for booleans, lists joined with commas, `{ label }` objects by label; empty values read "… is cleared".

## Props

| Prop                         | Type                                      | Default                        | Description                                |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------ |
| `changes`                    | `{ field, value?, key?, description? }[]` | `[]`                           | What changed                               |
| `dirty`                      | `boolean`                                 | `changes.length > 0`           | Whether anything can be saved              |
| `onDiscard`                  | `() => void`                              |                                | Restore saved values                       |
| `onSave`                     | `() => unknown`                           |                                | Save yourself instead of submitting a form |
| `form`                       | `string`                                  |                                | Id of the form to submit when outside it   |
| `saving`                     | `boolean`                                 | from `Form`                    | Saving state                               |
| `status`                     | `'idle' \| 'success' \| 'error'`          | from `Form` / `onSave`         | Result of the last save                    |
| `successMessage`             | `ReactNode`                               | "Changes saved"                | e.g. "User saved"                          |
| `errorMessage`               | `ReactNode`                               | "Your changes were not saved…" |                                            |
| `title`                      | `ReactNode`                               | "Unsaved changes"              | Panel title while there are changes; it reads "No changes yet" otherwise |
| `saveLabel` / `discardLabel` | `ReactNode`                               |                                | Button text                                |
| `guard`                      | `boolean`                                 | `true`                         | Warn before leaving with unsaved changes   |
| `layout`                     | `'responsive' \| 'side' \| 'bottom'`      | `responsive`                   | Force a layout                             |
| `classNames`                 | `{ title, list, item, actions, message }` |                                | Classes for each part                      |

On phones the bar is fixed to the bottom (above the safe area) with a spacer so it never covers content; the change list collapses behind an "N unsaved changes" toggle. While nothing has changed, the bar reads "No changes yet" rather than "Unsaved changes".

Whenever the bar is fixed to the bottom (`layout="bottom"`, or `responsive` below `lg`), it lines up with the page's content column: `AppLayout`'s main area, a shadcn `SidebarInset`, or the nearest `<main>`. It follows the column as the sidebar opens, collapses or resizes, so it never covers the `AppSidebar` (in LTR or RTL). Outside such a column it spans the viewport.

## Accessibility

- An `<aside>` landmark named "Unsaved changes".
- The change list and status messages are in a polite live region; errors use `role="alert"`.
- The phone toggle has `aria-expanded`; buttons are 44px on touch screens.
- The leave dialog is an alert dialog; focus returns to where it was when the user stays.

| Key               | Action                                   |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd>  | Save (from any field, inside the `Form`) |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd> | Stay on the page (in the leave dialog)   |

---

<!-- docs/form-scaffolding/unsaved-changes-guard.md -->

# useUnsavedChangesGuard

Warns before leaving a page with unsaved changes (§25.9). [`SaveBar`](./save-bar.md) uses it; call it yourself for programmatic navigation.

```tsx
import { useUnsavedChangesGuard } from "@javaabu/onu"

const { confirmLeave, guard, dialog } = useUnsavedChangesGuard(isDirty)

return (
  <>
    …<button onClick={() => guard(() => router.visit("/users"))}>All users</button>
    {dialog}
  </>
)
```

While `dirty` is true:

- closing or reloading the tab shows the browser's own "Leave site?" warning (`beforeunload`);
- clicking a same-origin link anywhere on the page asks "You have unsaved changes. Leave anyway?". **Stay on page** keeps the user where they are; **Leave** replays the click, so router links (Inertia, Next, React Router) navigate as usual;
- pressing the browser's **Back** or **Forward** button to another page (including another hash-router route) asks the same question; **Leave** completes the move.

Links that open a new tab, downloads, modified clicks (Ctrl/⌘/Shift), in-page anchors (`#section`), other origins and anything inside `[data-unsaved-guard-ignore]` are not intercepted. Hash-router links, whose fragment starts with `/` or `!/` (`#/users`, `#!/users`), are routes, so they are guarded.

### How Back is guarded, and its limits

`popstate` fires only after the address has changed, and routers (React Router, Inertia, hash routers) react to it before a page-level listener can. So the guard uses the [Navigation API](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Navigation_API): its `navigate` event fires before a Back/Forward move and can be cancelled. The guard cancels the move, asks, and on **Leave** repeats it with `navigation.traverseTo()`, so Back, Forward and multi-step jumps (long-press on Back) all land where the user meant to go.

What cannot be done:

- Browsers without the Navigation API (older Safari and Firefox) do not let a page cancel Back; there it is not guarded. Use your router's blocking hook with `confirmLeave` (below) if you must support them.
- Browsers refuse to let a page cancel Back repeatedly without the user interacting in between (to stop "back-button traps"). Such a move goes through unguarded.
- Navigations done in code (`router.visit`, `navigate()`) are not asked about; wrap them in `guard()`.
- Leaving the site from the browser's own UI (typing a URL, closing the tab) only gets the browser's "Leave site?" prompt; its text cannot be changed.
- Set `interceptHistory: false` to turn this off.

## Router integration

Back and link clicks are covered on their own. To guard your router's programmatic navigation too, wire `confirmLeave` or `guard` into it:

```tsx
// Inertia
useEffect(
  () =>
    router.on("before", (event) => {
      if (isDirty) {
        event.preventDefault()
        guard(() => router.visit(event.detail.visit.url))
      }
    }),
  [isDirty],
)

// React Router
const blocker = useBlocker(isDirty)
useEffect(() => {
  if (blocker.state === "blocked") void confirmLeave().then((ok) => (ok ? blocker.proceed() : blocker.reset()))
}, [blocker])
```

## API

`useUnsavedChangesGuard(dirty, options?)` returns:

| Field          | Type                            | Description                               |
| -------------- | ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `confirmLeave` | `() => Promise<boolean>`        | `true` when clean or the user chose Leave |
| `guard`        | `(proceed: () => void) => void` | Runs `proceed` when it is fine to leave   |
| `dialog`       | `ReactElement`                  | The confirmation dialog; render it once   |

| Option           | Type        | Default                                   | Description                    |
| ---------------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `beforeUnload`   | `boolean`   | `true`                                    | Browser prompt on close/reload |
| `interceptLinks` | `boolean`   | `true`                                    | Ask before following links     |
| `interceptHistory` | `boolean` | `true`                                    | Ask before Back/Forward leave the page |
| `title`          | `ReactNode` | "Leave this page?"                        | Dialog title                   |
| `message`        | `ReactNode` | "You have unsaved changes. Leave anyway?" | Dialog text                    |

## Accessibility

An alert dialog (focus trapped, Escape = stay). Focus returns to the element that had it before the dialog opened.

---

<!-- docs/form-scaffolding/floating-submit.md -->

# FloatingSubmit

A submit button that floats at the bottom of the screen while the form's main submit button is scrolled out of view, so a long form can be submitted from anywhere.

```tsx
import { Form, FloatingSubmit, SubmitButton } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<Form onSubmit={submit}>
  {/* a long form … */}
  <SubmitButton>Submit application</SubmitButton>
  <FloatingSubmit>Submit</FloatingSubmit>
</Form>
```

By default it watches the first other submit button in the same form. Pass `target` (a ref) to watch something else, such as a footer. It shares the form's processing state with [`SubmitButton`](./submit-button.md).

## Props

| Prop           | Type                     | Default       | Description                         |
| -------------- | ------------------------ | ------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `target`       | `RefObject<HTMLElement>` | form's submit | Element whose visibility is watched |
| `forceVisible` | `boolean`                | `false`       | Always show                         |
| `classNames`   | `{ root, button }`       |               | Classes for the wrapper and button  |

All [`SubmitButton`](./submit-button.md) props are supported. Uses `IntersectionObserver`; without it the button never appears.

## Layout

Full width above the bottom safe area on phones; a pill at the bottom inline end (bottom right in LTR, bottom left in RTL) from `sm`.

## Accessibility

It is only rendered while visible, so it never adds a hidden tab stop. It is a normal submit button with the same name and busy state as the main one.

---

<!-- docs/form-scaffolding/submit-button.md -->

# SubmitButton

A `type="submit"` [`Button`](./button.md) that shows a spinner while the form is processing and ignores clicks until it finishes, so a form can't be submitted twice.

```tsx
import { Form, SubmitButton } from "@javaabu/onu"

<Form onSubmit={save}>
  …
  <SubmitButton>Save</SubmitButton>
</Form>

// Outside an Onu Form, or with Inertia
<SubmitButton processing={form.processing}>Save</SubmitButton>
```

Inside a [`Form`](./form.md) it follows the form's processing state automatically. The default label is "Submit" (translated).

## Props

| Prop         | Type      | Default     | Description                        |
| ------------ | --------- | ----------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `processing` | `boolean` | from `Form` | Show the spinner and block submits |

All [`Button`](./button.md) props except `type` and `loading` are supported (`variant`, `size`, `startIcon`, `loadingText`, …).

## Accessibility

While processing: `aria-busy="true"` and `aria-disabled="true"`. The button stays focusable (it is not `disabled`), so keyboard focus is not lost mid-submit.

---

<!-- docs/form-scaffolding/button.md -->

# Button

Onu's button: shadcn's `Button` with a `loading` state, `startIcon` / `endIcon`, and extra `success` and `warning` variants. It is styled like Ant Design's button: 32px tall at the default density, 14px regular text, 15px padding and 6px corners (from `--onu-radius`), with colour transitions and no shadow.

```tsx
import { Button } from "@javaabu/onu"

<Button>Save</Button>
<Button variant="outline" startIcon="add">New user</Button>
<Button variant="success" startIcon="check">Approve</Button>
<Button variant="destructive" startIcon="trash">Delete</Button>
<Button loading loadingText="Saving…">Save</Button>
```

Buttons default to `type="button"`; use [`SubmitButton`](./submit-button.md) (or `type="submit"`) to submit a form. The shadcn primitive is still available from `@javaabu/onu/primitives`.

## Icons

`startIcon` and `endIcon` take a semantic icon name (it follows the configured icon set, R6.5) or any React element. Directional icons such as `arrow-right` mirror in RTL.

```tsx
<Button endIcon="arrow-right">Next</Button>
<Button startIcon={<img src={logo} alt="" className="size-4" />}>Continue</Button>
```

## Variants

| `variant`     | Ant Design equivalent | Use                           |
| ------------- | --------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| `default`     | `type="primary"`      | Primary action (solid brand)  |
| `outline`     | default button        | Secondary actions, toolbars: card fill, grey border; the border and text turn to the brand colour on hover |
| `dashed`      | `type="dashed"`       | Add a row or item             |
| `secondary`   | `variant="filled"`    | Filled grey                   |
| `ghost`       | `type="text"`         | Icon buttons, low emphasis    |
| `link`        | `type="link"`         | Looks like a link             |
| `destructive` | `type="primary" danger` | Delete, revoke (solid red)  |
| `success`     |                       | Approve, publish              |
| `warning`     |                       | Suspend, risky but reversible |

Sizes: `xs` (24px), `sm` (28px), `default` (32px), `lg` (36px), `icon`, `icon-xs`, `icon-sm`, `icon-lg`, at the default density. On touch screens every button is at least 44px tall.

`buttonVariants({ variant, size, className })` returns the classes, for styling other elements as buttons.

## Props

| Prop          | Type                               | Default   | Description                                    |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------- | --------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `variant`     | see above                          | `default` | Style                                          |
| `size`        | see above                          | `default` | Size                                           |
| `loading`     | `boolean`                          | `false`   | Spinner, `aria-busy`, clicks ignored           |
| `loadingText` | `ReactNode`                        |           | Label while loading                            |
| `startIcon`   | `SemanticIconName \| ReactElement` |           | Icon before the label                          |
| `endIcon`     | `SemanticIconName \| ReactElement` |           | Icon after the label                           |
| `asChild`     | `boolean`                          | `false`   | Render the child element (e.g. a link) instead |

All `<button>` props are passed through; `ref` points at the button. Exposes `data-slot="button"`, `data-variant`, `data-size` and `data-loading`.

## Accessibility

- Icon-only buttons need an `aria-label`.
- Loading buttons stay focusable and are `aria-busy` + `aria-disabled`; the spinner is decorative.
- Visible focus ring on `:focus-visible`.

| Key                                 | Action   |
| ----------------------------------- | -------- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | Activate |

---

<!-- docs/form-scaffolding/link-button.md -->

# LinkButton

A link that looks like a [`Button`](./button.md). It renders through the `linkComponent` set on `OnuProvider`, so it navigates with Inertia, Next.js or your router (R16.2).

```tsx
import { LinkButton, OnuProvider } from "@javaabu/onu"
import { Link } from "@inertiajs/react"

;<OnuProvider linkComponent={Link}>
  <LinkButton href="/users/create" startIcon="add">
    New user
  </LinkButton>
  <LinkButton href="/users" variant="outline" startIcon="back">
    All users
  </LinkButton>
  <LinkButton href="https://efaas.gov.mv" external variant="link">
    eFaas
  </LinkButton>
</OnuProvider>
```

## Props

| Prop        | Type                               | Default   | Description                                                                      |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------- | --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `href`      | `string`                           |           | Destination                                                                      |
| `variant`   | Button variants                    | `default` | Style                                                                            |
| `size`      | Button sizes                       | `default` | Size                                                                             |
| `startIcon` | `SemanticIconName \| ReactElement` |           | Icon before the label                                                            |
| `endIcon`   | `SemanticIconName \| ReactElement` |           | Icon after the label                                                             |
| `external`  | `boolean`                          | `false`   | Plain `<a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">` with an external-link icon |
| `disabled`  | `boolean`                          | `false`   | Dimmed, `aria-disabled`, no `href`                                               |

All `<a>` props are passed through; `ref` points at the anchor.

## Accessibility

- It is a real link (`role="link"`), so screen readers announce it as one; use [`Button`](./button.md) for actions.
- External links add "(opens in a new tab)" for screen readers (translated).

---

<!-- docs/form-scaffolding/button-group.md -->

# ButtonGroup

Groups related buttons. By default the buttons are joined into one segmented control (shadcn's button group); `attached={false}` keeps them separate with a gap and lets them wrap.

```tsx
import { Button, ButtonGroup } from "@javaabu/onu"

<ButtonGroup label="View">
  <Button variant="outline" size="icon" aria-label="List view" startIcon="list" />
  <Button variant="outline" size="icon" aria-label="Grid view" startIcon="grid" />
</ButtonGroup>

<ButtonGroup attached={false}>
  <Button variant="outline">Cancel</Button>
  <Button>Save</Button>
</ButtonGroup>
```

`ButtonGroupText` and `ButtonGroupSeparator` come from shadcn and work inside an attached group. The shadcn primitive is still available from `@javaabu/onu/primitives`.

## Props

| Prop          | Type                         | Default      | Description                   |
| ------------- | ---------------------------- | ------------ | ----------------------------- |
| `attached`    | `boolean`                    | `true`       | Join the buttons              |
| `orientation` | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` | `horizontal` | Direction                     |
| `label`       | `string`                     |              | Accessible name for the group |

All `<div>` props are passed through.

## Accessibility

Renders `role="group"`; give it a `label` when the purpose isn't clear from the buttons. Each button is its own tab stop.

## RTL

Joined edges use logical radii, so the rounded ends swap sides in RTL.

---

<!-- docs/form-scaffolding/auth-forms.md -->

# Auth forms

Ready-made, presentational authentication forms: `SignInForm`, `RegisterForm`, `ForgotPasswordForm` and `ResetPasswordForm`. They render the fields Laravel's auth scaffolding expects, call `onSubmit` with typed values, and show the `errors`, `processing` and `status` you pass. They never make requests themselves.

```tsx
import { EfaasButton, SignInForm } from "@javaabu/onu"
import { useForm } from "@inertiajs/react"

const form = useForm({ email: "", password: "", remember: false })

<SignInForm
  onSubmit={(values) => router.post("/login", values)}
  errors={errors}
  processing={processing}
  forgotPasswordHref="/forgot-password"
  registerHref="/register"
  efaas={<EfaasButton href="/login/efaas" logo={<img src={efaasIcon} alt="" />} fullWidth />}
/>
```

`onSubmit` may also return a promise and throw a Laravel 422 body; the errors then show under the fields (see [`Form`](./form.md)).

Fields you add with `extraFields` are submitted too: `onSubmit` receives the typed built-in values plus every other named field as the form submitted it (`AuthFormValues<V>` = `V & Record<string, unknown>`).

```tsx
<SignInForm
  extraFields={<FormField label="Island" name="island"><TextInput /></FormField>}
  onSubmit={(values) => router.post("/login", { ...values, island: String(values.island ?? "") })}
/>
```

## SignInForm

Fields: `email`, `password` (with show/hide), `remember`. Values: `{ email, password, remember: boolean }`.

| Prop                 | Type        | Default | Description                                       |
| -------------------- | ----------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `forgotPasswordHref` | `string`    |         | Shows "Forgot password?" beside the password      |
| `registerHref`       | `string`    |         | Shows "Don’t have an account? Create an account"  |
| `showRemember`       | `boolean`   | `true`  | "Remember me" checkbox                            |
| `efaas`              | `ReactNode` |         | eFaas (or other SSO) button under an "or" divider |

:::info eFaas branding
Use [`EfaasButton`](./efaas-button.md), styled after the eFaas brand guide, with the eFaas icon from eFaas's brand kit as its `logo` (R16.7).
:::

## RegisterForm

Fields: `name`, `email`, `password`, `password_confirmation`, and `terms` when `termsHref` is set.

| Prop         | Type      | Description                                     |
| ------------ | --------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `signInHref` | `string`  | "Already have an account? Sign in"              |
| `termsHref`  | `string`  | Adds a required "I agree to the terms" checkbox |
| `nameThaana` | `boolean` | Type the name in Thaana (with a toggle)         |

## ForgotPasswordForm

Field: `email`. Pass `status` once the link is sent ("We have emailed your password reset link."). `signInHref` adds "Back to sign in".

## ResetPasswordForm

Fields: hidden `token`, `email`, `password`, `password_confirmation`.

| Prop            | Type      | Default | Description                 |
| --------------- | --------- | ------- | --------------------------- |
| `token`         | `string`  |         | Token from the emailed link |
| `emailReadOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | Lock the email field        |
| `signInHref`    | `string`  |         | "Back to sign in"           |

## Shared props

| Prop                   | Type                                 | Description                                      |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `onSubmit`             | `(values) => unknown`                | Typed values plus any `extraFields` values; may return a promise |
| `errors`               | `Record<string, string \| string[]>` | Server errors by field                           |
| `processing`           | `boolean`                            | Spinner on the button, fields disabled           |
| `status`               | `ReactNode`                          | Success / info message above the fields          |
| `title`, `description` | `ReactNode`                          | Override the default heading and text            |
| `logo`                 | `ReactNode`                          | Above the title                                  |
| `defaultValues`        | `Partial<Values>`                    | Initial values                                   |
| `submitLabel`          | `ReactNode`                          | Button text                                      |
| `extraFields`          | `ReactNode`                          | Extra fields before the button                   |
| `formProps`            | `<form>` props                       | `action`, `method`, `id` … for non-JS submission |

Plus every [`FormContainer`](./form-container.md) prop except `title` and `children`. Links render through the provider's `linkComponent`.

## Accessibility

- Proper `autocomplete` values (`username`, `current-password`, `new-password`, `email`, `name`) so password managers work.
- Email and password inputs stay `dir="ltr"` in RTL pages.
- The password toggle is a button with `aria-pressed` and a translated name.
- Errors are linked to fields and the first invalid field gets focus.

---

<!-- docs/form-scaffolding/efaas-button.md -->

# eFaas button

The **Sign in with eFaas** button, styled after the [eFaas brand guide](https://efaas.egov.mv/Home/Branding) (R16.7). Pass it to [`SignInForm`](./auth-forms.md)'s `efaas` slot or use it on its own. With `href` it is a plain link, so the browser does a full-page redirect to your eFaas login route (never a client-side Inertia or Next visit); without `href` it is a button.

```tsx
import { EfaasButton, SignInForm } from "@javaabu/onu"

<SignInForm onSubmit={login} efaas={<EfaasButton href="/login/efaas" fullWidth />} />

<EfaasButton intent="register" href="/register/efaas" />
<EfaasButton variant="white" iconOnly href="/login/efaas" />

// Any of the 22 official eFaas logos, by number
<EfaasButton logoVariant={18} href="/login/efaas" />                  // white "efaas" wordmark on blue
<EfaasButton logoVariant={1} variant="white" href="/login/efaas" />  // blue wordmark on white
```

## Props

Every `<a>` prop (with `href`) or `<button>` prop (without), plus:

| Prop        | Type                             | Default     | Description                                                                 |
| ----------- | -------------------------------- | ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `href`      | `string`                         |             | Render a plain link to your eFaas redirect route                            |
| `intent`    | `"sign-in" \| "register"`        | `"sign-in"` | "Sign in with eFaas" or "Register with eFaas" (translated)                  |
| `variant`   | `"blue" \| "black" \| "white"`   | `"blue"`    | eFaas colour variation                                                      |
| `size`      | `"default" \| "lg"`              | `"default"` | 40px (44px on touch screens) or 48px tall                                   |
| `shape`     | `"rounded" \| "square"`          | `"rounded"` | Corner style                                                                |
| `logoVariant` | `1`–`22` \| `"none"`          | by colour   | Which [official eFaas logo](./efaas-logo.md) to show (see below). Default: the icon made for the button colour, 15 on blue, 14 on black, 9 on white |
| `logo`      | `ReactNode`                      |             | A custom logo node instead of `logoVariant`; sized like the icon marks      |
| `iconOnly`  | `boolean`                        | `false`     | Only the icon (needs an icon mark); the wording stays as the accessible name |
| `fullWidth` | `boolean`                        | `false`     | Stretch to the container                                                    |
| `loading`   | `boolean`                        | `false`     | Spinner and "Redirecting to eFaas…"; clicks are ignored                     |
| `children`  | `ReactNode`                      |             | Replace the label (keep eFaas's wording)                                    |

## Branding

What the button follows from the eFaas brand guide:

- **Colours**: only the eFaas palette. Blue `#164998` with white text (default), black `#333333` with white text, and white with blue text and a grey `#d0d2d3` border. No custom button colours. Do not put the black button on dark backgrounds; use `white` there.
- **Typeface**: Poppins Medium for the label, Mv Waheed for Dhivehi. Onu does not load either font: load them in your app to match the guide; otherwise the app's sans-serif (or Thaana font) is used.
- **Wording**: "Sign in with eFaas" / "Register with eFaas", and `eFaas އިން ސައިން އިން ކުރައްވާ` / `eFaas އިން ރަޖިސްޓަރ ކުރައްވާ` in Dhivehi.
- **Layout**: the icon and label keep their order and position. Only the corners (`shape`) and the side padding (via `className`) may change.
- **Clear space**: keep the protected zone the guide defines around the button (X/2 on its grid) free of other graphics and text. Under `SignInForm` the "or" divider provides it.

## Logos

The button shows one of the 22 official logos from eFaas's brand kit, picked by number with `logoVariant` (the numbers are the kit's file numbers, `Efaas Logos SVG-01` … `-22`; the full list is on [EfaasLogo](./efaas-logo.md)).

- **Icon marks** (9, 10, 11, 14, 15) sit before the label: "[icon] Sign in with eFaas".
- **Every other variant** already spells "efaas" (in English or Dhivehi, some with the "Key to a digital Maldives" tagline), so it replaces the visible label. The wording stays the button's accessible name. Stacked logos (5, 6, 21, 22) make the button taller.
- Pick a logo made for the button's colour: logos for light backgrounds (1–10) on the `white` button, logos for dark backgrounds (11–22) on `blue` or `black`.
- `logoVariant="none"` shows the wording alone.

:::caution Not verified against the guide
The guide could not be opened while this component was built. The palette, typeface, wording and layout rules above come from the guide's published text; the exact button heights, icon size, white-variant text colour, the fourth colour variation and the clear-space measurement still need to be checked against [efaas.egov.mv/Home/Branding](https://efaas.egov.mv/Home/Branding).
:::

## Accessibility

A link or button named by its wording (also when `iconOnly`). The logo is decorative. The focus ring shows on every variant, the button is at least 44px tall on touch screens, and `loading` sets `aria-busy` and announces "Redirecting to eFaas…" as the name.

---

<!-- docs/form-scaffolding/efaas-logo.md -->

# eFaas logo

The 22 official eFaas logos from eFaas's brand kit, unchanged, as one component. Pick a logo by its number in the kit (`Efaas Logos SVG-01` … `-22`). [`EfaasButton`](./efaas-button.md) uses these through its `logoVariant` prop.

```tsx
import { EfaasLogo, EFAAS_LOGO_VARIANTS } from "@javaabu/onu"

<EfaasLogo />                                  // 1: blue horizontal English logo
<EfaasLogo variant={2} className="h-12" />     // blue horizontal Dhivehi logo
<EfaasLogo variant={18} decorative />          // white logo for dark backgrounds, next to text naming eFaas

EFAAS_LOGO_VARIANTS[16] // { layout: "tagline", language: "en", colour: "white", background: "dark" }
```

| # | Layout | Wordmark | Colour | Made for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Horizontal | English | Blue | Light backgrounds |
| 2 | Horizontal | Dhivehi | Blue | Light backgrounds |
| 3 | With tagline | English | Blue | Light backgrounds |
| 4 | With tagline | Dhivehi | Blue | Light backgrounds |
| 5 | Stacked, with tagline | English | Blue | Light backgrounds |
| 6 | Stacked, with tagline | Dhivehi | Blue | Light backgrounds |
| 7 | Horizontal | English | Black | Light backgrounds |
| 8 | Horizontal | Dhivehi | Black | Light backgrounds |
| 9 | Icon | | Blue tile | Light backgrounds |
| 10 | Icon | | Black tile | Light backgrounds |
| 11 | Icon | | White tile, blue mark | Dark backgrounds |
| 12 | Horizontal | Dhivehi | White, black mark | Dark backgrounds |
| 13 | Horizontal | Dhivehi | White, blue mark | Dark backgrounds |
| 14 | Icon | | White tile, black mark | Dark backgrounds |
| 15 | Icon | | White tile, blue mark | Dark backgrounds |
| 16 | With tagline | English | White | Dark backgrounds |
| 17 | Horizontal | Dhivehi | White | Dark backgrounds |
| 18 | Horizontal | English | White | Dark backgrounds |
| 19 | With tagline | Dhivehi | White, blue mark | Dark backgrounds |
| 20 | With tagline | Dhivehi | White, black mark | Dark backgrounds |
| 21 | Stacked, with tagline | Dhivehi | White | Dark backgrounds |
| 22 | Stacked, with tagline | English | White | Dark backgrounds |

## Props

Every `<svg>` prop, plus:

| Prop         | Type      | Default   | Description                                                            |
| ------------ | --------- | --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `variant`    | `1`–`22`  | `1`       | Which official logo (table above)                                      |
| `title`      | `string`  | `"eFaas"` | Accessible name                                                        |
| `decorative` | `boolean` | `false`   | Hide from assistive technology when visible text already names eFaas   |
| `className`  | `string`  | `h-10 w-auto` | Size with a height class; the width follows the logo's proportions |

## Loading

The five icon marks are bundled with the component (about 3 kB compressed). The logos with a wordmark load on first use from a separate chunk (about 40 kB compressed). While it loads, the logo keeps its size, so nothing shifts. On the server, a wordmark logo renders as that empty, correctly sized box and fills in on the client.

## Brand rules

The artwork is eFaas's, unchanged: the generator (`scripts/build-efaas-logos.mjs`) only turns each file's style classes into fill attributes, so several logos can share a page. Don't recolour, stretch or redraw the logos, and use the variant made for the background (blue or black on light, white on dark).

## Accessibility

An image (`role="img"`) named "eFaas", or hidden (`aria-hidden`) when `decorative`. Inside `EfaasButton` the logo is always decorative and the button is named by its wording.

<!-- docs/text-inputs/text-input.md -->

# TextInput

A single-line text input with optional addons and [Thaana keyboard](../guides/thaana-input.md) support. Built on shadcn's `Input` and `InputGroup`.

```tsx
import { TextInput } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<TextInput placeholder="Full name" />
```

Inside a [`FormField`](../form-scaffolding/form-field.md) the input gets its `id`, `name`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-required` and `disabled` from the field:

```tsx
<FormField label="Name" name="name" help="As shown on your ID card" required>
  <TextInput />
</FormField>
```

## Thaana

Set `thaana` to type Thaana from a Latin keyboard. The input switches to `dir="rtl"`, `lang="dv"` and the Thaana font. Add `thaanaToggle` for a button that switches between Thaana and Latin (also <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>T</kbd>).

```tsx
<TextInput thaana />
<TextInput thaana thaanaToggle />
<TextInput thaana={{ keymap: 'typewriter', paste: 'transliterate' }} />
```

## Addons

```tsx
<TextInput startAddon={<Icon name="search" />} placeholder="Search" />
<TextInput endAddon="MVR" inputMode="decimal" />
```

Addons sit at the inline start and end, so they swap sides in RTL.

## Props

| Prop           | Type                                    | Default | Description                                               |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `thaana`       | `boolean \| ThaanaOptions`              | `false` | Type Thaana from a Latin keyboard                         |
| `thaanaToggle` | `boolean`                               | `false` | Show a Thaana/Latin toggle button                         |
| `startAddon`   | `ReactNode`                             |         | Content before the input                                  |
| `endAddon`     | `ReactNode`                             |         | Content after the input                                   |
| `classNames`   | `{ root, input, startAddon, endAddon }` |         | Classes for each part                                     |
| `className`    | `string`                                |         | Classes for the input (or the group when addons are used) |

All other `<input>` props are passed to the input, and `ref` points at the `<input>`.

`ThaanaOptions`: `{ keymap?: 'phonetic' | 'phonetic-hh' | 'typewriter' | Keymap, paste?: 'keep' | 'transliterate', toggleShortcut?: false | { code, altKey?, shiftKey?, ctrlKey?, metaKey? }, defaultEnabled?: boolean }`.

## Accessibility

- Always give the input a label: a `FormField`, a `<label>`, or `aria-label`.
- The Thaana toggle has an accessible name, exposes its state with `aria-pressed`, and announces "Thaana typing on/off".

| Key                                          | Action                                                |
| -------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>T</kbd> | Switch between Thaana and Latin (when `thaana` is on) |

---

<!-- docs/text-inputs/email-input.md -->

# EmailInput

An email address input. It sets `type="email"`, `inputMode="email"` (the email keyboard on phones) and `autocomplete="email"`, turns off auto-capitalisation and spell check, and is always left-to-right, even on a Dhivehi page. Built on [`TextInput`](./text-input.md).

```tsx
import { EmailInput } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<EmailInput placeholder="aishath@example.mv" />
```

Inside a [`FormField`](../form-scaffolding/form-field.md):

```tsx
<FormField label="Email" name="email" required>
  <EmailInput showIcon />
</FormField>
```

For a sign-in form, pass `autoComplete="username"` so password managers pair it with the password field.

## Props

| Prop           | Type                                    | Default   | Description                                       |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `showIcon`     | `boolean`                               | `false`   | Show a mail icon at the inline start              |
| `autoComplete` | `string`                                | `"email"` | Autofill hint, e.g. `"username"` on sign-in forms |
| `startAddon`   | `ReactNode`                             |           | Content before the input (replaces the icon)      |
| `endAddon`     | `ReactNode`                             |           | Content after the input                           |
| `classNames`   | `{ root, input, startAddon, endAddon }` |           | Classes for each part                             |

All other `<input>` props are passed through, and `ref` points at the `<input>`. `type`, `thaana` and `thaanaToggle` are not accepted.

## RTL and Thaana

The input is forced to `dir="ltr"` (R11.7): email addresses are Latin, so the caret and text stay left-to-right inside an RTL form. It has no `thaana` prop.

## Accessibility

- Give it a label with `FormField`, a `<label>` or `aria-label`.
- Errors from the `FormField` set `aria-invalid` and are linked with `aria-describedby`.

---

<!-- docs/text-inputs/password-input.md -->

# PasswordInput

A password input with a show/hide button, a Caps Lock warning and an optional strength meter. Built on [`TextInput`](./text-input.md).

```tsx
import { PasswordInput } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<PasswordInput />
```

## Strength meter

`strength` shows a four-step meter with a text label ("Weak", "Strong", …), so colour is never the only signal. The built-in scorer (`scorePassword`) is a small, dependency-free estimate based on length, character variety, repeats and common sequences. Pass your own scorer (for example zxcvbn) for stricter checks, and always enforce the real rules on the server.

```tsx
<FormField label="New password" help="At least 12 characters">
  <PasswordInput strength />
</FormField>

<PasswordInput strength={(pw) => myScorer(pw)} /> // returns 0–4
```

With `strength`, `autoComplete` defaults to `"new-password"`; otherwise `"current-password"`.

## Props

| Prop              | Type                                                     | Default | Description                                     |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `toggleable`      | `boolean`                                                | `true`  | Show the show/hide button                       |
| `visible`         | `boolean`                                                |         | Controlled visibility                           |
| `defaultVisible`  | `boolean`                                                | `false` | Initial visibility                              |
| `onVisibleChange` | `(visible: boolean) => void`                             |         | Called when the button is pressed               |
| `capsLockWarning` | `boolean`                                                | `true`  | Warn when Caps Lock is on                       |
| `strength`        | `boolean \| (pw: string) => 0–4`                         | `false` | Show a strength meter, optionally with a scorer |
| `classNames`      | `{ wrapper, root, input, endAddon, capsLock, strength }` |         | Classes for each part                           |

All other `<input>` props are passed to the input, and `ref` points at it. `className` goes on the wrapper.

Also exported: `scorePassword(password): 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4`.

## RTL and Thaana
