Always `dir="ltr"`; no `thaana` prop (R13.3).

## Accessibility

- The toggle is a button named "Show password" with `aria-pressed`.
- The Caps Lock warning has `role="status"` and is added to the input's `aria-describedby` while shown.
- The strength label is a polite live region and is also linked with `aria-describedby`.

| Key                                               | Action                        |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>                                    | Moves to the show/hide button |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> on the button | Shows or hides the password   |

---

<!-- docs/text-inputs/sensitive-input.md -->

# SensitiveInput

A read-only display for a secret such as an API key or client secret. It shows only the last few characters (`••••••••7342`), with buttons to reveal the value and to copy it. While masked, the full value is never in the DOM, and the number of dots is fixed so the length is not leaked.

```tsx
import { SensitiveInput } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<FormField label="Live secret key">
  <SensitiveInput value="sk_live_51Hx9aBcDeFgHiJkLmN0pQ7342" />
</FormField>
```

Copy always copies the full secret, even while it is masked.

## Props

| Prop               | Type                                    | Default | Description                              |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `value`            | `string`                                |         | The secret (required)                    |
| `visibleChars`     | `number`                                | `4`     | Trailing characters shown while masked   |
| `maskLength`       | `number`                                | `8`     | Number of mask dots                      |
| `revealed`         | `boolean`                               |         | Controlled reveal state                  |
| `defaultRevealed`  | `boolean`                               | `false` | Initial reveal state                     |
| `onRevealedChange` | `(revealed: boolean) => void`           |         | Called when the reveal button is pressed |
| `revealable`       | `boolean`                               | `true`  | Show the reveal button                   |
| `copyable`         | `boolean`                               | `true`  | Show the copy button                     |
| `onCopy`           | `(value: string) => void`               |         | Called after a successful copy           |
| `classNames`       | `{ root, input, startAddon, endAddon }` |         | Classes for each part                    |

Also exported: `maskSecret(value, visibleChars?, maskLength?, maskChar?)`.

## RTL and Thaana

Always `dir="ltr"` and monospace. No `thaana` prop.

## Accessibility

- The reveal button is named "Show value" and exposes its state with `aria-pressed`; "Value shown" / "Value hidden" is announced.
- The copy button is named "Copy" and announces "Copied" (or "Could not copy") in a polite live region.
- Focusing the input selects its text.
- Buttons are 44px on touch screens.

---

<!-- docs/text-inputs/copy-input.md -->

# CopyInput

A read-only value with a copy button: share links, reference numbers, account numbers. Focusing the input selects the whole value, and the copy button announces "Copied".

```tsx
import { CopyInput } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<FormField label="Share link">
  <CopyInput value="https://portal.gov.mv/track/REF-2026-00451" />
</FormField>

<CopyInput value="REF-2026-00451" mono onCopy={() => toast.success("Copied")} />
```

The clipboard API is used where available, with an `execCommand("copy")` fallback for older browsers and non-secure contexts.

## Props

| Prop         | Type                                    | Default | Description                           |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `value`      | `string`                                |         | The value to show and copy (required) |
| `onCopy`     | `(value: string) => void`               |         | Called after a successful copy        |
| `mono`       | `boolean`                               | `false` | Use the monospace font                |
| `endAddon`   | `ReactNode`                             |         | Extra content before the copy button  |
| `classNames` | `{ root, input, startAddon, endAddon }` |         | Classes for each part                 |

All other `<input>` props are passed through. The input is always `readOnly`.

## RTL and Thaana

The value keeps the page direction unless you pass `dir` (for example `dir="ltr"` for URLs). No `thaana` prop: the value is not editable.

## Accessibility

- The copy button is named "Copy" (from the locale) and its result, "Copied" or "Could not copy", is announced in a polite live region.
- It is 44px on touch screens.

---

<!-- docs/text-inputs/number-input.md -->

# NumberInput

A numeric input with locale-aware formatting, `min` / `max` / `step`, and spinbutton keys. The value is shown formatted while the field is not focused (`12,500.00`) and as a plain number while editing (`12500`).

It is a text field with a numeric keyboard (`inputMode`), not `type="number"`, so the scroll wheel never changes the value by accident and formatting works in every locale.

```tsx
import { NumberInput } from "@javaabu/onu"

const [amount, setAmount] = useState<number | null>(1500)

<NumberInput
  value={amount}
  onValueChange={setAmount}
  min={0}
  step={0.01}
  formatOptions={{ style: "currency", currency: "MVR" }}
/>
```

`formatOptions` are `Intl.NumberFormat` options and use the active locale's `numberLocale` (Western digits for Dhivehi, R12.6). For `style: "percent"`, the value is a fraction (`0.08`) and the user edits `8`.

## Form submission

With a `name` (or inside a `FormField` with `name`), the raw number is submitted through a hidden input, so `1,234.5` is posted as `1234.5`. The visible input has no name.

## Props

| Prop                      | Type                               | Default     | Description                                           |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`                   | `number \| null`                   |             | Controlled value (`null` is empty)                    |
| `defaultValue`            | `number \| null`                   | `null`      | Initial value                                         |
| `onValueChange`           | `(value: number \| null) => void`  |             | Called as the user types or steps                     |
| `min` / `max`             | `number`                           |             | Limits (applied on blur and when stepping)            |
| `step`                    | `number`                           | `1`         | Arrow key step                                        |
| `largeStep`               | `number`                           | `step × 10` | Page Up/Down and Shift+Arrow step                     |
| `formatOptions`           | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions`         |             | Display format                                        |
| `clampOnBlur`             | `boolean`                          | `true`      | Clamp to `min` / `max` on blur                        |
| `inputMode`               | `"numeric" \| "decimal" \| "text"` | auto        | Keyboard; `numeric` for non-negative integers         |
| `startAddon` / `endAddon` | `ReactNode`                        |             | Addons, e.g. a unit (see [`UnitInput`](./unit-input.md)) |

Also exported: `parseLocaleNumber(text, numberLocale)` and `numberSymbols(numberLocale)`.

## RTL and Thaana

Always `dir="ltr"` with tabular figures. No `thaana` prop.

## Accessibility

The input has `role="spinbutton"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and `aria-valuetext` (the formatted value), following the WAI-ARIA spinbutton pattern.

| Key                                          | Action                             |
| -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> / <kbd>↓</kbd>                  | Increase / decrease by `step`      |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>↑</kbd> / <kbd>↓</kbd> | Increase / decrease by `largeStep` |
| <kbd>Page Up</kbd> / <kbd>Page Down</kbd>    | Increase / decrease by `largeStep` |

---

<!-- docs/text-inputs/quantity-stepper.md -->

# QuantityStepper

A number with large − and + buttons, for cart quantities, tickets and guest counts. Holding a button repeats the step; arrow keys work in the field. Built on [`NumberInput`](./number-input.md).

```tsx
import { QuantityStepper } from "@javaabu/onu"

const [tickets, setTickets] = useState(1)

<FormField label="Tickets">
  <QuantityStepper value={tickets} onValueChange={setTickets} min={1} max={20} />
</FormField>
```

## Sizes

`size="sm" | "default" | "lg"` (variants exported as `quantityStepperVariants`). On touch screens the buttons are at least 44px in every size; `lg` suits kiosks.

## Props

| Prop             | Type                                    | Default     | Description                               |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `value`          | `number`                                |             | Controlled value                          |
| `defaultValue`   | `number`                                | `min`       | Initial value                             |
| `onValueChange`  | `(value: number) => void`               |             | Called on every change                    |
| `min`            | `number`                                | `0`         | Lowest value                              |
| `max`            | `number`                                |             | Highest value                             |
| `step`           | `number`                                | `1`         | Step for buttons and arrow keys           |
| `size`           | `"sm" \| "default" \| "lg"`             | `"default"` | Size                                      |
| `repeatDelay`    | `number`                                | `400`       | ms before press-and-hold starts repeating |
| `repeatInterval` | `number`                                | `80`        | ms between repeats                        |
| `classNames`     | `{ root, input, decrement, increment }` |             | Classes for each part                     |

Other `NumberInput` props (`formatOptions`, `name`, `disabled`, …) are passed through.

## RTL

The − button sits at the inline start and + at the inline end, so they swap sides in RTL. The number itself stays left-to-right.

## Accessibility

- The field is a `spinbutton` (see [`NumberInput`](./number-input.md)); the buttons are named "Decrease" / "Increase" from the locale.
- The buttons are not in the tab order (the spinbutton's arrow keys do the same), but are clickable and work with voice control. At a limit they get `aria-disabled` and stop responding.
- Press-and-hold uses pointer events, so it works with touch, pen and mouse.

| Key                                       | Action                          |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> / <kbd>↓</kbd>               | Increase / decrease by `step`   |
| <kbd>Page Up</kbd> / <kbd>Page Down</kbd> | Increase / decrease by 10 steps |

---

<!-- docs/text-inputs/unit-input.md -->

# UnitInput

A number with a unit add-on: either fixed text (`kg`, `MVR`, `%`) or a unit select (`m` / `km`). Built on [`NumberInput`](./number-input.md), so it has the same formatting and keys.

```tsx
import { UnitInput } from "@javaabu/onu"

<UnitInput unit="kg" defaultValue={23} min={0} />
<UnitInput unit="MVR" unitPosition="start" step={0.01} />

<UnitInput
  units={[{ value: "m", label: "m" }, { value: "km", label: "km" }]}
  defaultUnit="km"
  unitName="distance_unit"
  name="distance"
/>
```

## Props

| Prop           | Type                                 | Default | Description                        |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------ | ------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `unit`         | `ReactNode`                          |         | Fixed unit text                    |
| `units`        | `{ value, label, disabled? }[]`      |         | Choosable units (renders a select) |
| `unitValue`    | `string`                             |         | Controlled unit                    |
| `defaultUnit`  | `string`                             | first   | Initial unit                       |
| `onUnitChange` | `(unit: string) => void`             |         | Called when the unit changes       |
| `unitName`     | `string`                             |         | Form field name for the unit       |
| `unitLabel`    | `string`                             | "Unit"  | Accessible name of the unit select |
| `unitPosition` | `"start" \| "end"`                   | `"end"` | Which side the unit sits on        |
| `classNames`   | `{ root, input, unit, unitTrigger }` |         | Classes for each part              |

All [`NumberInput`](./number-input.md) props are supported.

## RTL

The unit sits at the inline end (or start), so it swaps sides in RTL; the number stays left-to-right.

## Accessibility

The unit select is a shadcn `Select` (Radix) named "Unit" from the locale, or `unitLabel`. Use a [`FormField`](../form-scaffolding/form-field.md) label for the number.

| Key                                             | Action             |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------ |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> / <kbd>↓</kbd> in the number       | Step the value     |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> on the unit | Open the unit list |

---

<!-- docs/text-inputs/phone-input.md -->

# PhoneInput

An international phone number input built on [`react-phone-number-input`](https://gitlab.com/catamphetamine/react-phone-number-input) (libphonenumber). It formats the number as you type, defaults to the Maldives (+960), has a searchable country picker built from Onu's `Popover` and `Command`, and returns an [E.164](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E.164) value such as `+9607771234`.

```tsx
import { PhoneInput } from "@javaabu/onu"

const [phone, setPhone] = useState<string | undefined>()

<FormField label="Mobile number" name="phone">
  <PhoneInput value={phone} onValueChange={setPhone} />
</FormField>
```

Validate on the server; `isValidPhoneNumber` from `react-phone-number-input` is handy for client-side checks.

## Props

| Prop                 | Type                                              | Default | Description                                            |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`              | `string`                                          |         | Controlled E.164 value                                 |
| `defaultValue`       | `string`                                          |         | Initial E.164 value                                    |
| `onValueChange`      | `(value?: string) => void`                        |         | Called with the E.164 value, or `undefined` when empty |
| `defaultCountry`     | `Country`                                         | `"MV"`  | Country for numbers typed without `+`                  |
| `countries`          | `Country[]`                                       | all     | Limit the country list                                 |
| `countrySelect`      | `boolean`                                         | `true`  | Show the country picker                                |
| `allowInternational` | `boolean`                                         | `false` | Add an "International" choice                          |
| `international`      | `boolean`                                         |         | Always use the international format (`+960 777 1234`)  |
| `onCountryChange`    | `(country?: Country) => void`                     |         | Called when the country changes                        |
| `classNames`         | `{ root, input, countryTrigger, countryContent }` |         | Classes for each part                                  |

Other `<input>` props (`placeholder`, `disabled`, `autoComplete`, …) go to the number input, and `ref` points at it.

## RTL and Thaana

The whole field, country picker included, is forced `dir="ltr"` (R11.7). No `thaana` prop. Country names come from `Intl.DisplayNames` in the active locale, falling back to English.

## Accessibility

- The number input has `type="tel"`, `inputMode="tel"` and `autocomplete="tel"`.
- The country button is named "Country: Maldives" and opens a searchable list (cmdk listbox). Search by country name, code (`MV`) or calling code (`+960`).
- Focus returns to the country button when the list closes.

| Key                                                       | Action                 |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> on the country button | Open the country list  |
| Type                                                      | Filter countries       |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> / <kbd>↓</kbd>                               | Move through countries |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd>                                          | Choose a country       |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd>                                            | Close the list         |

---

<!-- docs/text-inputs/url-input.md -->

# UrlInput

A URL input. It sets `type="url"`, `inputMode="url"` and `autocomplete="url"`, is always left-to-right, and adds `https://` when the user leaves the field without a scheme (`javaabu.com` → `https://javaabu.com`). Built on [`TextInput`](./text-input.md).

```tsx
import { UrlInput } from "@javaabu/onu"

<UrlInput placeholder="example.mv" />
<UrlInput showIcon />
<UrlInput defaultProtocol={false} placeholder="/news/ferry-schedule" />
```

The protocol is added the way a user would type it (a native input event), so `onChange`, controlled state and `react-hook-form` all see the new value.

## Props

| Prop              | Type                                    | Default      | Description                                      |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `defaultProtocol` | `string \| false`                       | `"https://"` | Added on blur when missing; `false` turns it off |
| `showIcon`        | `boolean`                               | `false`      | Show a link icon at the inline start             |
| `classNames`      | `{ root, input, startAddon, endAddon }` |              | Classes for each part                            |

All other `<input>` props are passed through. Also exported: `normalizeUrl(value, protocol?)`.

## RTL and Thaana

Always `dir="ltr"` (R11.7). No `thaana` prop.

## Accessibility

Label it with a `FormField`, `<label>` or `aria-label`. Errors from the `FormField` are linked with `aria-describedby`.

---

<!-- docs/text-inputs/hidden-input.md -->

# HiddenInput

A hidden form value. Inside a [`FormField`](../form-scaffolding/form-field.md) it takes the field's `id` and `name`, so server errors for that name show on the field like any other control.

```tsx
import { HiddenInput } from "@javaabu/onu"

<HiddenInput name="island_id" value={42} />
<HiddenInput name="is_featured" value={true} />        // submits "1"
<HiddenInput name="tags" value={["ferry", "transport"]} /> // submits tags[]=ferry&tags[]=transport

<FormField label="Location" name="location_id" hideLabel>
  <HiddenInput value={locationId} />
</FormField>
```

## Values

| Value                | Submitted as                         |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `string` / `number`  | As text                              |
| `true` / `false`     | `"1"` / `"0"` (what Laravel expects) |
| `null` / `undefined` | `""`                                 |
| `string[]`           | One input per item, named `name[]`   |

## Props

| Prop    | Type                                              | Description                      |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| `value` | `string \| number \| boolean \| null \| string[]` | Value to submit                  |
| `name`  | `string`                                          | Field name (or from `FormField`) |

`id`, `form`, `disabled` and `ref` are passed to the `<input type="hidden">`.

## Accessibility

Hidden inputs are not shown or announced. Use them only for values the user does not need to see.

---

<!-- docs/text-inputs/textarea.md -->

# Textarea

A multi-line text input that grows with its content, with [Thaana](../guides/thaana-input.md) support and an optional character counter.

```tsx
import { Textarea } from '@javaabu/onu';

<Textarea placeholder="Remarks" />
<Textarea thaana thaanaToggle />
<Textarea showCount maxLength={500} />
<Textarea autoResize={false} rows={6} />
```

## Props

| Prop           | Type                         | Default | Description                                         |
| -------------- | ---------------------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `thaana`       | `boolean \| ThaanaOptions`   | `false` | Type Thaana from a Latin keyboard                   |
| `thaanaToggle` | `boolean`                    | `false` | Show a Thaana/Latin toggle                          |
| `autoResize`   | `boolean`                    | `true`  | Grow with the content (`field-sizing: content`)     |
| `showCount`    | `boolean`                    | `false` | Show a character counter; uses `maxLength` when set |
| `classNames`   | `{ root, textarea, footer }` |         | Classes for each part                               |

All other `<textarea>` props are passed through, and `ref` points at the `<textarea>`.

:::info

`Textarea` replaces shadcn's primitive of the same name in the main export. The plain primitive is still available from `@javaabu/onu/primitives`.

:::

## Accessibility

The counter is announced politely as it changes. Wrap the textarea in a [`FormField`](../form-scaffolding/form-field.md) or give it a label.

---

<!-- docs/text-inputs/thaana-input.md -->

# ThaanaInput

`ThaanaInput` and `ThaanaTextarea` are [`TextInput`](./text-input.md) and [`Textarea`](./textarea.md) with Thaana typing on and the Thaana/Latin toggle shown by default.

```tsx
import { ThaanaInput, ThaanaTextarea } from '@javaabu/onu';

<FormField label="ނަން">
    <ThaanaInput />
</FormField>

<ThaanaTextarea thaana={{ keymap: 'phonetic-hh' }} thaanaToggle={false} />
```

They accept every prop of the component they wrap. `thaana` takes keyboard options only (it cannot be turned off).

For the keyboard itself, including using it on your own elements, see the [Thaana input guide](../guides/thaana-input.md).

## Props

These differ from [`TextInput`](./text-input.md#props) / [`Textarea`](./textarea.md); every other prop is the same.

| Prop           | Type                                                        | Default | Description                                          |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `thaana`       | `true \| { keymap, paste, toggleShortcut, defaultEnabled }` | `true`  | Keyboard options; Thaana typing cannot be turned off |
| `thaanaToggle` | `boolean`                                                   | `true`  | Show the [Thaana/Latin toggle](./thaana-toggle.md)      |

`keymap` is `"phonetic"` (default), `"phonetic-hh"`, `"typewriter"` or a custom keymap; `paste: "transliterate"` converts pasted Latin text; `defaultEnabled: false` starts in Latin mode.

## Accessibility

- While Thaana is on, the field has `dir="rtl"` and `lang="dv"`, so screen readers can pick a Dhivehi voice and the caret moves right to left. In Latin mode it has `dir="auto"` and no `lang`.
- The field is still a native `<input>` / `<textarea>`: label it with [`FormField`](../form-scaffolding/form-field.md) as usual. The keyboard inserts text the way typing does, so the browser's undo and `onChange` keep working.
- The toggle button and <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>T</kbd> switch modes. The toggle (shown by default) also announces each change, so keep it when users may switch with the shortcut; see [`ThaanaToggle`](./thaana-toggle.md#accessibility).
- Text composed by a native Thaana keyboard or another IME passes through untouched, so users who already type Thaana are not double-converted.

---

<!-- docs/text-inputs/thaana-toggle.md -->

# ThaanaToggle

The button that switches a field between Thaana and Latin typing. Text inputs render it for you with `thaanaToggle`; use it directly with [`useThaanaInput`](../guides/thaana-input.md) on custom fields.

```tsx
import { ThaanaToggle } from "@javaabu/onu"
import { useThaanaInput } from "@javaabu/onu/thaana"

function MyField() {
  const ref = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null)
  const { enabled, toggle } = useThaanaInput(ref)
  return (
    <div className="gap-2 flex">
      <input ref={ref} dir={enabled ? "rtl" : "auto"} />
      <ThaanaToggle enabled={enabled} onToggle={toggle} />
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Props

| Prop        | Type         | Default | Description                       |
| ----------- | ------------ | ------- | --------------------------------- |
| `enabled`   | `boolean`    |         | Whether Thaana typing is on       |
| `onToggle`  | `() => void` |         | Called when the button is pressed |
| `className` | `string`     |         | Merged with the button's classes  |

Every other `<button>` prop (such as `disabled`) is passed through. The button is always `type="button"`, so it never submits a form.

## Accessibility

- A toggle button: its state is `aria-pressed` (`true` while Thaana is on) and its name is "Switch between Thaana and Latin typing" (translated, `thaana.toggle`). The visible "ދ" / "A" is `aria-hidden`; the tooltip adds the shortcut, <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>T</kbd>.
- Each change is announced through a polite [`LiveRegion`](../accessibility/live-region.md): "Thaana typing on" / "Latin typing on" (`thaana.on` / `thaana.off`), so the shortcut is heard too.
- Pressing it with the mouse does not take focus away from the field, so users keep typing where they were. It works with <kbd>Enter</kbd> and <kbd>Space</kbd> like any button.
- At least 44×44px on touch screens.

---

<!-- docs/text-inputs/otp-input.md -->

# OtpInput

A one-time code input built on shadcn's `input-otp`. It shows one slot per character, uses the numeric keyboard on phones, sets `autocomplete="one-time-code"` so iOS and Android offer the code from SMS, accepts pasted codes (spaces and dashes are removed), and can submit its form when the code is complete.

```tsx
import { OtpInput } from "@javaabu/onu"

<form onSubmit={verify}>
  <FormField label="Verification code" help="Sent by SMS to +960 777-1234">
    <OtpInput value={code} onValueChange={setCode} autoSubmit />
  </FormField>
</form>

<OtpInput length={4} size="lg" onComplete={(code) => verify(code)} />
<OtpInput groupSize={3} />                    // 123–456
<OtpInput length={8} groupSize={4} alphanumeric />
```

## Sizes

`size="sm" | "default" | "lg"` sets the slot size (variants exported as `otpSlotVariants`). Slots are at least 44px on touch screens.

## Props

| Prop            | Type                               | Default     | Description                               |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `length`        | `number`                           | `6`         | Number of characters                      |
| `groupSize`     | `number`                           |             | Split slots into groups with a separator  |
| `value`         | `string`                           |             | Controlled value                          |
| `defaultValue`  | `string`                           | `""`        | Initial value                             |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void`          |             | Called on every change                    |
| `onComplete`    | `(code: string) => void`           |             | Called when every slot is filled          |
| `autoSubmit`    | `boolean`                          | `false`     | Submit the surrounding form when complete |
| `alphanumeric`  | `boolean`                          | `false`     | Allow letters (uses the text keyboard)    |
| `size`          | `"sm" \| "default" \| "lg"`        | `"default"` | Slot size                                 |
| `classNames`    | `{ root, group, slot, separator }` |             | Classes for each part                     |

Other `<input>` props (`name`, `disabled`, `aria-*`) go to the underlying input, and `ref` points at it. Also exported: `cleanOtpPaste(text)`.

## RTL and Thaana

The slots are always left-to-right, so codes read the same as in the SMS. No `thaana` prop.

## Accessibility

- A single real `<input>` holds the code, so screen readers read it as one field. It is labelled by its `FormField`, or "One-time code" from the locale when there is no label.
- Errors from the `FormField` set `aria-invalid` on the input and outline every slot.

| Key                                       | Action                        |
| ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| Digits                                    | Fill the next slot            |
| <kbd>Backspace</kbd>                      | Delete the previous character |
| <kbd>←</kbd> / <kbd>→</kbd>               | Move between slots            |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>⌘</kbd>+<kbd>V</kbd> | Paste a whole code            |

---

<!-- docs/text-inputs/slug-input.md -->

# SlugInput

A slug generator, like `slugInput` in [`@javaabu/js-utilities`](https://github.com/Javaabu/js-utilities). While locked, the slug follows a source value (usually the title). Typing in the slug, or pressing the unlock button, switches to manual editing; the lock button generates it again. A preview shows the full URL.

```tsx
import { SlugInput, TextInput } from "@javaabu/onu"

const [title, setTitle] = useState("")

<FormField label="Title">
  <TextInput value={title} onChange={(e) => setTitle(e.target.value)} />
</FormField>
<FormField label="Slug" name="slug">
  <SlugInput source={title} prefix="https://example.mv/news/" />
</FormField>
```

On an edit page, pass the saved slug as `defaultValue` (or `value`). It then starts unlocked, so editing the title does not change a published URL until the user locks it again.

## Thaana titles

Slugs are generated with [`@sindresorhus/slugify`](https://github.com/sindresorhus/slugify). Thaana is transliterated to Latin first using the common Maldivian romanisation, so Dhivehi titles give readable slugs:

| Title                | Slug                  |
| -------------------- | --------------------- |
| މާލެ ސިޓީ ކައުންސިލް | `maale-sitee-kaunsil` |
| ހުޅުމާލެ 2026        | `hulhumaale-2026`     |
| ދިވެހިރާއްޖެ         | `dhivehiraajje`       |

`toSlug(text, { separator })` and `thaanaToLatin(text)` are exported for use elsewhere (for example on the server through a shared module).

## Props

| Prop            | Type                                        | Default                     | Description                              |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `source`        | `string`                                    | `""`                        | Text to generate from                    |
| `value`         | `string`                                    |                             | Controlled slug                          |
| `defaultValue`  | `string`                                    |                             | Initial slug                             |
| `onValueChange` | `(slug: string) => void`                    |                             | Called when the slug changes             |
| `auto`          | `boolean`                                   |                             | Controlled locked/automatic state        |
| `defaultAuto`   | `boolean`                                   | `true` when no initial slug | Start locked                             |
| `onAutoChange`  | `(auto: boolean) => void`                   |                             | Called when locking or unlocking         |
| `prefix`        | `string`                                    |                             | URL shown before the slug in the preview |
| `separator`     | `string`                                    | `"-"`                       | Word separator                           |
| `slugify`       | `(text: string) => string`                  | `toSlug`                    | Custom slug function                     |
| `classNames`    | `{ wrapper, root, input, toggle, preview }` |                             | Classes for each part                    |

Other `<input>` props are passed through; `ref` points at the input. When `readOnly`, the lock button is hidden.

## RTL and Thaana

The slug and the preview are always left-to-right. No `thaana` prop: slugs are Latin.

## Accessibility

- The lock button is named "Generate the slug automatically" and exposes the state with `aria-pressed`. Switching between automatic and manual is announced.
- The URL preview is linked to the input with `aria-describedby`.

---

<!-- docs/text-inputs/autocomplete.md -->

# Autocomplete

A free-text input with suggestions. The typed text is the value; suggestions only help fill it in (for a fixed list of choices, use a select). Follows the [WAI-ARIA combobox pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/) with list autocomplete, and supports Thaana typing.

```tsx
import { Autocomplete } from "@javaabu/onu"

<Autocomplete suggestions={["Malé", "Hulhumalé", "Addu City"]} />

<Autocomplete thaana suggestions={["މާލެ", "ހުޅުމާލެ", "ވިލިމާލެ"]} />
```

## Async suggestions

Pass a function to search a server. It is called with the query and an `AbortSignal`; requests are debounced (300 ms by default) and older requests are cancelled, so a slow response never overwrites a newer one. Loading and error states (with **Retry**) are shown and announced.

```tsx
<Autocomplete
  suggestions={async (query, { signal }) => {
    const res = await fetch(`/api/jobs?search=${encodeURIComponent(query)}`, { signal })
    const { data } = await res.json()
    return data.map((job) => ({ value: job.title, description: job.department }))
  }}
  minChars={2}
/>
```

Options are strings or `{ value, label?, description?, disabled? }`.

## Props

| Prop             | Type                                                                       | Default                  | Description                            |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ | -------------------------------------- |
| `suggestions`    | `SuggestionOption[] \| (query, { signal }) => Promise<SuggestionOption[]>` |                          | Static list or async search (required) |
| `value`          | `string`                                                                   |                          | Controlled text                        |
| `defaultValue`   | `string`                                                                   | `""`                     | Initial text                           |
| `onValueChange`  | `(value: string) => void`                                                  |                          | Called on every change                 |
| `onSelect`       | `(option) => void`                                                         |                          | Called when a suggestion is picked     |
| `debounce`       | `number`                                                                   | `300`                    | Async debounce in ms                   |
| `minChars`       | `number`                                                                   | `0` (list) / `1` (async) | Characters before suggestions show     |
| `maxSuggestions` | `number`                                                                   | `50`                     | Most suggestions shown                 |
| `openOnFocus`    | `boolean`                                                                  | `false`                  | Show suggestions on focus              |
| `renderOption`   | `(option, { active }) => ReactNode`                                        |                          | Custom option content                  |
| `thaana`         | `boolean \| ThaanaOptions`                                                 | `false`                  | Type Thaana from a Latin keyboard      |
| `thaanaToggle`   | `boolean`                                                                  | `false`                  | Show the Thaana/Latin toggle           |
| `classNames`     | `{ root, input, startAddon, endAddon, list, option }`                      |                          | Classes for each part                  |

Other [`TextInput`](./text-input.md) props (addons, `name`, `disabled`, …) are passed through.

## RTL and Thaana

With `thaana`, the input and the suggestion list are `dir="rtl"` and `lang="dv"`. Matching is case-insensitive and works for Thaana and Latin.

## Accessibility

- The input has `role="combobox"`, `aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; the highlighted option is set with `aria-activedescendant`, so focus stays in the input.
- The number of suggestions ("3 suggestions available"), loading and errors are announced in a polite live region.

| Key                         | Action                                           |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| <kbd>↓</kbd> / <kbd>↑</kbd> | Open the list / move through suggestions (wraps) |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd>            | Use the highlighted suggestion                   |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd>              | Close the list; press again to clear the text    |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>              | Close the list and move on, keeping the text     |

---

<!-- docs/text-inputs/color-picker.md -->

# ColorPicker

A colour picker built on React Aria's colour components. The trigger shows the swatch and hex value; the panel has a saturation/brightness area, a hue slider, a hex field and preset swatches. It opens in a popover on larger screens and as a bottom sheet on phones (R3.28). The value is a lowercase hex string.

```tsx
import { ColorPicker } from "@javaabu/onu"

const [colour, setColour] = useState<string | null>("#1f7a4d")

<FormField label="Brand colour" name="colour">
  <ColorPicker value={colour} onValueChange={setColour} />
</FormField>

<ColorPicker presets={["#0f766e", "#0369a1", "#7c3aed"]} />
<ColorPicker presets={[]} />  // no swatches
```

## Props

| Prop                                    | Type                                                | Default                  | Description                             |
| --------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ | --------------------------------------- |
| `value`                                 | `string \| null`                                    |                          | Controlled hex value                    |
| `defaultValue`                          | `string \| null`                                    | `null`                   | Initial value                           |
| `onValueChange`                         | `(hex: string) => void`                             |                          | Called with `#rrggbb`                   |
| `presets`                               | `string[]`                                          | `DEFAULT_COLOUR_PRESETS` | Swatches; `[]` hides them               |
| `placeholder`                           | `string`                                            | "No colour"              | Trigger text when empty                 |
| `name`                                  | `string`                                            |                          | Submit the hex value via a hidden input |
| `open` / `defaultOpen` / `onOpenChange` |                                                     |                          | Control the panel                       |
| `classNames`                            | `{ trigger, panel, area, slider, field, swatches }` |                          | Classes for each part                   |

Other `<button>` props (`disabled`, `aria-*`) go to the trigger. Also exported: `toHex(value)`, which normalises any CSS colour string to `#rrggbb`.

## RTL and Thaana

The hex value is always left-to-right; React Aria follows the active locale for slider direction. No `thaana` prop.

## Accessibility

- The trigger is a button with `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, labelled by its `FormField`. Focus returns to it when the panel closes.
- The area is a 2D slider ("Saturation and brightness"), the hue is a slider, and the presets are a listbox of named swatches ("vibrant red"), all from React Aria.

| Key                                                             | Action                         |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> on the trigger              | Open the panel                 |
| <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> <kbd>↑</kbd> <kbd>↓</kbd> in the area | Change saturation / brightness |
| <kbd>←</kbd> / <kbd>→</kbd> on the hue slider                   | Change hue                     |
| <kbd>Page Up</kbd> / <kbd>Page Down</kbd>                       | Larger steps                   |
| Arrow keys in the swatches                                      | Move between presets           |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd>                                                  | Close the panel                |

---

<!-- docs/text-inputs/icon-picker.md -->

# IconPicker

An icon picker with search and a virtualised grid ([TanStack Virtual](https://tanstack.com/virtual)), so thousands of icons stay fast. It lists every Lucide icon plus any icon sources registered on `OnuProvider` (Iconify collections, FontAwesome), remembers recently used icons, and returns a portable id such as `lucide:house`, `tabler:home` or `fa:regular:house` that [`DynamicIcon`](../guides/icons.md) renders (R6.7).

```tsx
import { DynamicIcon, IconPicker } from "@javaabu/onu"

const [icon, setIcon] = useState<string | null>("lucide:ship")

<FormField label="Menu icon" name="icon">
  <IconPicker value={icon} onValueChange={setIcon} />
</FormField>

{icon && <DynamicIcon id={icon} />}
```

## More icon sets

Register sources once on the provider; the picker shows a set filter when there is more than one.

```tsx
import tabler from "@iconify-json/tabler/icons.json"
import { iconifySource } from "@javaabu/onu/icons/iconify"

<OnuProvider iconSources={[iconifySource({ collections: [tabler] })]}>
```

Restrict a picker to some sets with `sets={["lucide"]}`.

## Props

| Prop                                    | Type                                     | Default   | Description                                                  |
| --------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                 | `string \| null`                         |           | Controlled icon id                                           |
| `defaultValue`                          | `string \| null`                         | `null`    | Initial id                                                   |
| `onValueChange`                         | `(id: string \| null) => void`           |           | Called on pick (or `null` when removed)                      |
| `sets`                                  | `string[]`                               | all       | Source prefixes to include                                   |
| `clearable`                             | `boolean`                                | `true`    | Show "Remove icon"                                           |
| `recentLimit`                           | `number`                                 | `12`      | Recently used icons kept in `localStorage`; `0` turns it off |
| `placeholder`                           | `string`                                 | "No icon" | Trigger text when empty                                      |
| `name`                                  | `string`                                 |           | Submit the id via a hidden input                             |
| `open` / `defaultOpen` / `onOpenChange` |                                          |           | Control the panel                                            |
| `classNames`                            | `{ trigger, panel, search, grid, cell }` |           | Classes for each part                                        |

Also exported: `lucideIconIds()` and `filterIconIds(ids, query)`.

## RTL

The grid flows in the reading direction, and ←/→ follow the visual order in RTL (R11.5). Icon names and the search field are left-to-right.

## Accessibility

- The trigger is a button with `aria-haspopup="dialog"`; focus moves to the search field when the panel opens and back to the trigger when it closes. On phones the panel is a bottom sheet.
- The search field is a combobox controlling a listbox of icons; the highlighted icon is set with `aria-activedescendant`, and each icon is named after its id. The number of matches is announced.

| Key                                       | Action                                 |
| ----------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| Type                                      | Filter icons                           |
| <kbd>←</kbd> / <kbd>→</kbd>               | Previous / next icon (mirrored in RTL) |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> / <kbd>↓</kbd>               | Row up / down                          |
| <kbd>Page Up</kbd> / <kbd>Page Down</kbd> | Five rows up / down                    |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd>                          | Pick the highlighted icon              |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd>                            | Close                                  |

---

<!-- docs/text-inputs/signature-pad.md -->

# SignaturePad

A signature pad built on [`signature_pad`](https://github.com/szimek/signature_pad). Draw with a finger, pen or mouse; undo the last stroke or clear; the result is a PNG data URL. The canvas resizes with its container (and the device pixel ratio) without losing the drawing. "Type your name" is offered as a keyboard and screen-reader alternative, and also produces a PNG.

It is exported from the media entry point, and `signature_pad` is an optional peer dependency:

```bash
npm install signature_pad
```

```tsx
import { SignaturePad } from "@javaabu/onu/media"

;<SignaturePad label="Applicant signature" onValueChange={setSignature} name="signature" />
```

## Props

| Prop                                    | Type                                | Default         | Description                                                   |
| --------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `onValueChange`                         | `(dataUrl: string \| null) => void` |                 | Called after each stroke or typed change; `null` when cleared |
| `defaultValue`                          | `string \| null`                    |                 | A saved data URL to start from                                |
| `penColor`                              | `string`                            | text colour     | Ink colour                                                    |
| `backgroundColor`                       | `string`                            | transparent     | Fill of the exported image                                    |
| `minWidth` / `maxWidth`                 | `number`                            | `0.75` / `2.75` | Stroke width range                                            |
| `disabled`                              | `boolean`                           | `false`         | Stop drawing and disable the buttons                          |
| `allowTyped`                            | `boolean`                           | `true`          | Offer "Type your name"                                        |
| `mode` / `defaultMode` / `onModeChange` | `"draw" \| "type"`                  | `"draw"`        | Control the mode                                              |
| `thaana`                                | `boolean \| ThaanaOptions`          |                 | Thaana typing for the typed name                              |
| `name`                                  | `string`                            |                 | Submit the data URL via a hidden input                        |
| `label`                                 | `string`                            |                 | Accessible name of the group                                  |
| `classNames`                            | `{ canvas, toolbar, typed }`        |                 | Classes for each part                                         |

Also exported: `renderTypedSignature(text, options?)`.

:::info
The ink follows the theme's text colour by default, so a signature drawn in dark mode exports with light ink. Pass `penColor` (and `backgroundColor`) when the image will be printed or shown on a fixed background.
:::

## RTL and Thaana

The pad works the same in both directions. The typed name accepts `thaana`, so Dhivehi names can be typed from a Latin keyboard.

## Accessibility

- The canvas has `role="img"` and an accessible name that tells the user they can type their name instead.
- Draw / Type are toggle buttons with `aria-pressed`; Undo and Clear are labelled buttons, 44px on touch screens.
- "Signature captured" and "Signature cleared" are announced.
- The canvas uses `touch-action: none` so drawing does not scroll the page; the buttons are the gesture alternatives (R3.27).

| Key                                 | Action                                                 |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>                      | Move between Draw/Type, the name field and the buttons |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | Switch mode, undo or clear                             |

---

<!-- docs/text-inputs/tags-input.md -->

# TagsInput

A chips input for keywords, topics and similar lists. <kbd>Enter</kbd> or a comma adds the typed tag, <kbd>Backspace</kbd> in an empty field removes the last one, and pasting a comma- or newline-separated list adds every item. Suggestions (static or async), a maximum and Thaana typing are supported. Built on shadcn's `Badge` and Onu's suggestion list.

```tsx
import { TagsInput } from "@javaabu/onu"

const [tags, setTags] = useState<string[]>([])

<FormField label="Topics" name="topics">
  <TagsInput value={tags} onValueChange={setTags} suggestions={["Transport", "Tourism", "Health"]} />
</FormField>

<TagsInput thaana thaanaToggle />
<TagsInput max={3} />
<TagsInput transform={(t) => (t.trim().length >= 2 ? t.trim().toUpperCase() : null)} />
```

With a `name`, each tag is submitted as `name[]`.

## Props

| Prop              | Type                                                   | Default          | Description                                |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `value`           | `string[]`                                             |                  | Controlled tags                            |
| `defaultValue`    | `string[]`                                             | `[]`             | Initial tags                               |
| `onValueChange`   | `(tags: string[]) => void`                             |                  | Called when tags change                    |
| `suggestions`     | `SuggestionOption[] \| async (query, { signal }) => …` |                  | Suggestions; tags already added are hidden |
| `max`             | `number`                                               |                  | Maximum number of tags                     |
| `allowDuplicates` | `boolean`                                              | `false`          | Allow the same tag twice                   |
| `delimiters`      | `string[]`                                             | `[",", "Enter"]` | Keys / characters that add a tag           |
| `transform`       | `(tag) => string \| null`                              | trim             | Normalise or reject (`null`) a tag         |
| `thaana`          | `boolean \| ThaanaOptions`                             | `false`          | Type Thaana from a Latin keyboard          |
| `thaanaToggle`    | `boolean`                                              | `false`          | Show the Thaana/Latin toggle               |
| `debounce`        | `number`                                               | `300`            | Async suggestion debounce                  |
| `classNames`      | `{ root, tag, input, list, option }`                   |                  | Classes for each part                      |

Other `<input>` props go to the text field, and `ref` points at it.

## RTL and Thaana

With `thaana`, the field types Thaana (`dir="rtl"`, `lang="dv"`), and the Thaana comma `،` also adds a tag. Each chip uses `dir="auto"`, so mixed Dhivehi and English tags display correctly.

## Accessibility

- The text field is a combobox when suggestions are available (same keys as [`Autocomplete`](./autocomplete.md)).
- Each chip has a remove button named "Remove {tag}". Adding and removing tags is announced.
- When the maximum is reached, "You can add up to N tags" is linked to the field with `aria-describedby`.

| Key                                | Action                                                       |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>,</kbd>    | Add the typed tag (Enter on an empty field submits the form) |
| <kbd>Backspace</kbd> (empty field) | Remove the last tag                                          |
| <kbd>↓</kbd> / <kbd>↑</kbd>        | Move through suggestions                                     |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd>                     | Close suggestions                                            |

---

<!-- docs/text-inputs/qr-code-scanner.md -->

# QrCodeScanner

A QR code scanner. It opens the camera with `getUserMedia`, decodes frames with the browser's `BarcodeDetector`, and loads the [`barcode-detector`](https://github.com/Sec-ant/barcode-detector) polyfill (ZXing in WebAssembly) only where the native API is missing (R8.2). It shows clear states for the permission prompt, a blocked camera, no camera and unsupported browsers, has a torch toggle when the camera supports one, and always offers manual entry. The camera stops when a code is found (unless `continuous`) and when the component unmounts.

It is exported from the media entry point, and `barcode-detector` is an optional peer dependency:

```bash
npm install barcode-detector
```

```tsx
import { QrCodeScanner } from "@javaabu/onu/media"

<QrCodeScanner onScan={(value) => checkIn(value)} />
<QrCodeScanner continuous autoStart onScan={addTicket} />
```

The camera only starts after the user presses **Start camera** (or with `autoStart`), and browsers only allow it on HTTPS or `localhost`.

## States

| Status        | Shown                                                      |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `idle`        | Start camera button and manual entry                       |
| `requesting`  | "Waiting for camera permission…"                           |
| `scanning`    | Camera preview with a frame, Stop and (if supported) torch |
| `denied`      | How to allow the camera, plus manual entry                 |
| `no-camera`   | No camera found, plus manual entry                         |
| `unsupported` | The browser cannot scan, plus manual entry                 |
| `error`       | The camera could not be started                            |

## Props

| Prop             | Type                                        | Default           | Description                             |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `onScan`         | `(value: string) => void`                   |                   | Called with the decoded text (required) |
| `formats`        | `string[]`                                  | `["qr_code"]`     | Barcode formats                         |
| `continuous`     | `boolean`                                   | `false`           | Keep scanning after a result            |
| `autoStart`      | `boolean`                                   | `false`           | Start the camera on mount               |
| `manualEntry`    | `boolean`                                   | `true`            | Show the manual entry field             |
| `facingMode`     | `"environment" \| "user"`                   | `"environment"`   | Preferred camera                        |
| `scanInterval`   | `number`                                    | `250`             | ms between detection attempts           |
| `createDetector` | `(formats) => Promise<BarcodeDetectorLike>` | native / polyfill | Supply your own decoder                 |
| `onStatusChange` | `(status) => void`                          |                   | Called on every state change            |
| `onError`        | `(error) => void`                           |                   | Camera, decoder or torch errors         |
| `classNames`     | `{ video, controls, manual, message }`      |                   | Classes for each part                   |

Also exported: `createBarcodeDetector(formats?)`.

## RTL

Controls follow the page direction; the manual entry field is left-to-right because codes are Latin.

## Accessibility

- The status message is a `status` live region; problems use `role="alert"`.
- Scanned codes are announced ("Code scanned: …").
- The torch is a toggle button with `aria-pressed`; all buttons are 44px on touch screens.
- Manual entry is always available, so the component works without a camera.

| Key                                 | Action                                    |
| ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | Start / stop the camera, toggle the torch |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> in the code field  | Use the typed code                        |

---

<!-- docs/date-and-time/date-picker.md -->

# DatePicker

A date field that opens a calendar. Built on shadcn's `Calendar` (react-day-picker) inside a `Popover`, or a bottom-sheet `Drawer` on phones (R3.28). The header zooms out from days to months, years and ranges of years (REQUIREMENTS §25.1).

```tsx
import { DatePicker } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<DatePicker aria-label="Date of birth" />
```

Inside a [`FormField`](../form-scaffolding/form-field.md) the picker gets its `id`, `name`, label, help text, errors, `required` and `disabled` from the field:

```tsx
<FormField label="Joined on" name="joined_on" help="As in the contract" required>
  <DatePicker />
</FormField>
```

## Values

The value is a `Date` (local midnight) or `null`. Use it controlled or uncontrolled:

```tsx
const [date, setDate] = React.useState<Date | null>(null)
<DatePicker value={date} onChange={setDate} />
<DatePicker defaultValue={new Date(2026, 2, 12)} />
```

With a `name` (directly or from the `FormField`), a hidden input posts `yyyy-MM-dd`, so plain HTML and Laravel forms work without JavaScript glue. `parseISODate("2026-03-12")` turns a server value back into a `Date`.

## Limits and formats

```tsx
<DatePicker min={new Date()} max={addDays(new Date(), 30)} disabledDates={{ dayOfWeek: [5] }} />
<DatePicker format="EEEE, d MMMM yyyy" />
<DatePicker weekStartsOn={1} weekendDays={[0, 6]} showWeekNumber />
```

`format` is a date-fns pattern formatted with the active locale; the default is `dd/MM/yyyy`. The week start and month/day names come from the locale (`dv` gives Dhivehi names). Friday and Saturday are styled as the weekend by default.

## Props

| Prop                                    | Type                                        | Default         | Description                                       |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `value` / `defaultValue`                | `Date \| null`                              |                 | Selected date                                     |
| `onChange`                              | `(value: Date \| null) => void`             |                 | Called on select and on Clear                     |
| `format`                                | `string`                                    | `"dd/MM/yyyy"`  | date-fns display format                           |
| `placeholder`                           | `string`                                    | "Select a date" | Shown when empty                                  |
| `min` / `max`                           | `Date`                                      |                 | Earliest / latest selectable day                  |
| `disabledDates`                         | `Matcher \| Matcher[]`                      |                 | react-day-picker matchers                         |
| `weekStartsOn`                          | `0–6`                                       | locale          | First day of the week                             |
| `weekendDays`                           | `number[]`                                  | `[5, 6]`        | Days styled as weekend                            |
| `showWeekNumber`                        | `boolean`                                   | `false`         | Week number column                                |
| `name`                                  | `string`                                    |                 | Hidden input with `yyyy-MM-dd`                    |
| `required`                              | `boolean`                                   |                 | Hides Clear, sets `aria-required`                 |
| `clearable`                             | `boolean`                                   | `!required`     | Show Clear                                        |
| `disabled`                              | `boolean`                                   |                 | Field does nothing when clicked                   |
| `open` / `defaultOpen` / `onOpenChange` |                                             |                 | Panel open state                                  |
| `sheet`                                 | `"auto" \| boolean`                         | `"auto"`        | Bottom sheet on phones (`auto`), always, or never |
| `size`                                  | `"sm" \| "default" \| "lg"`                 | `"default"`     | Field height (`pickerTriggerVariants`)            |
| `today`                                 | `Date`                                      | now             | Pins "today" (tests, demos, server time)          |
| `className`                             | `string`                                    |                 | Classes for the field                             |
| `classNames`                            | `{ trigger, value, icon, content, footer }` |                 | Classes for each part                             |
| `ref`                                   | `Ref<HTMLButtonElement>`                    |                 | The field button                                  |

Every other picker in this group shares the field props from `required` down (`PickerFieldProps`).

## Accessibility

- The field is a button with `role="combobox"` and `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, named by its label plus its value. It carries `aria-invalid`, `aria-required` and the field's help/error description.
- The panel is a labelled dialog. Opening it focuses the selected day (or today); nothing is selected until a day is clicked. Closing returns focus to the field.
- Days are a grid (APG grid pattern) with full day names (`Today, Thursday, March 12th, 2026`); month changes and the selected date are announced through polite live regions.
- Keyboard arrows follow visual order, so they swap in RTL (R11.5).

| Key                                              | Action                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> on the field | Open the picker                                                                                           |
| <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd>                        | Previous / next day (or cell in the month and year views)                                                 |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> <kbd>↓</kbd>                        | Previous / next week (or row)                                                                             |
| <kbd>Page Up</kbd> / <kbd>Page Down</kbd>        | Previous / next month (year in the months view, 12 years in the years view, 144 years in the ranges view) |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Page Up/Down</kbd>         | Previous / next year (days view)                                                                          |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> / <kbd>End</kbd>                 | Start / end of the week (or row)                                                                          |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd>              | Select the highlighted day, or zoom into the highlighted cell                                             |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd>                                | Close without changing anything; focus returns to the field                                               |

## RTL and Dhivehi

With `locale="dv"` the calendar uses Dhivehi month and weekday names (from Onu's Dhivehi date-fns locale), the header chevrons mirror, and the panel follows `dir`. Dates use Western digits (R12.6).

---

<!-- docs/date-and-time/time-picker.md -->

# TimePicker

A time field that opens large hour and minute steppers with ▲/▼, an AM/PM switch, a clock-face hour grid and a minute grid (REQUIREMENTS §25.2). Popover on desktop, bottom sheet on phones.

```tsx
import { TimePicker } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<FormField label="Opens at" name="opens_at">
  <TimePicker />
</FormField>
```

## Values

The value is a `Date` (its date part is kept; changing the hour never changes the date) or `null`. An empty field gets its first time on `referenceDate` (default today). With `name`, a hidden input posts `HH:mm`.

```tsx
<TimePicker value={time} onChange={setTime} />
<TimePicker hourCycle={24} minuteStep={15} />
```

- ▲/▼ change the value by one and wrap: ▼ on 12 gives 11, ▲ on 59 minutes gives 00.
- **AM / PM** keeps the hour on the clock (9 AM ↔ 9 PM). <kbd>A</kbd> and <kbd>P</kbd> switch directly.
- Clicking the hour opens 12 cells laid out like a clock (00–23 on two rings in 24-hour mode); clicking the minute opens one cell per `minuteStep`. A minute off the grid (07 with a 5-minute step) highlights no cell. **Back** returns without changing anything.

## Props

| Prop                     | Type                            | Default          | Description                               |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------- | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `value` / `defaultValue` | `Date \| null`                  |                  | Selected time                             |
| `onChange`               | `(value: Date \| null) => void` |                  |                                           |
| `hourCycle`              | `12 \| 24`                      | locale           | 12-hour with AM/PM, or 24-hour            |
| `minuteStep`             | `number`                        | `5`              | Minutes between cells in the minute grid  |
| `format`                 | `string`                        | `h:mm a`/`HH:mm` | date-fns display format                   |
| `referenceDate`          | `Date`                          | today            | Date used when an empty field gets a time |

Plus the shared picker field props (`name`, `placeholder`, `required`, `clearable`, `disabled`, `open`, `sheet`, `size`, `className`, `classNames`, `ref`); see [DatePicker](./date-picker.md#props).

## Accessibility

- The hour and minute are `spinbutton`s with `aria-valuenow` / `aria-valuetext` ("2 PM"); ▲/▼ buttons are mouse/touch shortcuts for the same action.
- AM/PM is a labelled group of toggle buttons with `aria-pressed`.
- Grids follow the APG grid pattern with roving focus; focus returns to the number that opened them.

| Key                                             | Action                                      |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> / <kbd>↓</kbd> on a number         | Step it by one (wraps)                      |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> on a number | Open the hour or minute grid                |
| <kbd>A</kbd> / <kbd>P</kbd>                     | AM / PM (12-hour mode)                      |
| Arrow keys in a grid                            | Move between cells (clockwise on the clock) |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> / <kbd>End</kbd> in a grid      | First / last cell (row in the minute grid)  |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> in a grid                      | Pick the cell and return to the steppers    |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd>                               | Close; focus returns to the field           |

## RTL and Dhivehi

In Dhivehi, AM/PM read މކ / މފ and every label is translated. The clock face is never mirrored, since clocks read the same in every script.

---

<!-- docs/date-and-time/date-time-picker.md -->

# DateTimePicker

A calendar with a **time chip** underneath (REQUIREMENTS §25.3). Clicking the chip swaps the calendar for the [time steppers](./time-panel.md); **Back to calendar** swaps back. **Clear time** resets the time to 00:00 and keeps the date. Picking a day before any time sets 00:00.

```tsx
import { DateTimePicker } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<FormField label="Meeting starts" name="starts_at">
  <DateTimePicker />
</FormField>
```

The field shows both parts, e.g. `12/03/2026 2:30 PM`. With `name`, a hidden input posts a local ISO date-time, `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss` (Laravel's `date` rule accepts it). The panel stays open after picking a day so the time can still be set; **Done** closes it.

## Props

| Prop                                                             | Type                            | Default             | Description                                               |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value` / `defaultValue`                                         | `Date \| null`                  |                     |                                                           |
| `onChange`                                                       | `(value: Date \| null) => void` |                     |                                                           |
| `format`                                                         | `string`                        | `dd/MM/yyyy h:mm a` | date-fns display format                                   |
| `hourCycle`                                                      | `12 \| 24`                      | locale              |                                                           |
| `minuteStep`                                                     | `number`                        | `5`                 |                                                           |
| `defaultTime`                                                    | `{ hours, minutes }`            | `00:00`             | Time for a day picked before any time, and for Clear time |
| `min` / `max` / `disabledDates` / `weekStartsOn` / `weekendDays` |                                 |                     | As for [DatePicker](./date-picker.md#props)                  |

Plus the shared picker field props; see [DatePicker](./date-picker.md#props).

## Accessibility

- The time chip is a button named "Change time, 2:30 PM". Going back to the calendar returns focus to it.
- Calendar and steppers keep the keyboard models of [DatePicker](./date-picker.md#accessibility) and [TimePicker](./time-picker.md#accessibility). <kbd>Escape</kbd> closes from either view and returns focus to the field.

## RTL and Dhivehi

Calendar, chip and steppers follow the locale and direction; Dhivehi gives Dhivehi names and މކ/މފ.

---

<!-- docs/date-and-time/date-range-picker.md -->

# DateRangePicker

Two fields side by side, **From** and **To**, each opening a [DatePicker](./date-picker.md) (or a [DateTimePicker](./date-time-picker.md) with `withTime`). REQUIREMENTS §25.4.

```tsx
import { DateRangePicker, type DateRangeValue } from "@javaabu/onu"

const [range, setRange] = React.useState<DateRangeValue>({ from: null, to: null })
<FormField label="Leave period" name="leave">
  <DateRangePicker value={range} onChange={setRange} />
</FormField>
```

- Either end may be `null` for an open-ended range ("from 1 March onwards", "up to 31 March").
- Without `withTime`, `to` is the **end of that day** (23:59:59.999). With `withTime`, the To field's time defaults to 23:59.
- If To is before From, the message "End date is before start date" shows under the fields and both triggers are marked invalid.
- With `name`, hidden inputs post `name[from]` and `name[to]` (`yyyy-MM-dd`, or ISO date-time with `withTime`); override them with `names`.
- The fields stack in narrow containers (container query).

## Props

| Prop                                                                                              | Type                                       | Default                    | Description              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | -------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `value` / `defaultValue`                                                                          | `{ from: Date \| null; to: Date \| null }` | `{ from: null, to: null }` |                          |
| `onChange`                                                                                        | `(value: DateRangeValue) => void`          |                            |                          |
| `withTime`                                                                                        | `boolean`                                  | `false`                    | Pick a time for each end |
| `names`                                                                                           | `{ from?, to? }`                           | `name[from]`, `name[to]`   | Hidden input names       |
| `labels`                                                                                          | `{ from?, to? }`                           | "From", "To"               | Sub-field labels         |
| `placeholders`                                                                                    | `{ from?, to? }`                           |                            |                          |
| `format`, `min`, `max`, `disabledDates`, `weekStartsOn`, `weekendDays`, `hourCycle`, `minuteStep` |                                            |                            | Passed to both pickers   |
| `classNames`                                                                                      | `{ root, field, label, trigger, error }`   |                            | Classes for each part    |
| `ref`                                                                                             | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>`                      |                            | The group element        |

`name`, `required`, `disabled`, `clearable`, `sheet`, `size`, `today` and `aria-*` apply to both fields.

## Accessibility

- The range is a `role="group"` named by the `FormField` label (or `aria-label`, default "Date range"). Each trigger is named by the field label plus "From"/"To" plus its value; the `FormField` label points at the From field.
- The reversed-range message is a `role="alert"` and is added to each trigger's description.
- Each field has the full [DatePicker keyboard model](./date-picker.md#accessibility).

## RTL and Dhivehi

From sits at the inline start, so it is on the right in RTL. Labels and the error are translated (ފެށޭ ތާރީޚު / ނިމޭ ތާރީޚު).

---

<!-- docs/date-and-time/month-picker.md -->

# MonthPicker and YearPicker

Pick a month (or a year) from a grid of 12 that zooms out to years and ranges of years. Same calendar header and keyboard model as the [DatePicker](./date-picker.md).

```tsx
import { MonthPicker, YearPicker } from "@javaabu/onu"

<FormField label="Payroll month" name="payroll_month">
  <MonthPicker />
</FormField>
<FormField label="Year of graduation" name="year">
  <YearPicker />
</FormField>
```

The value is the first day of the month (or year) as a `Date`, or `null`. Hidden inputs post `yyyy-MM` (month) or `yyyy` (year).

## Props

| Prop                     | Type                            | Default              | Description                         |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------- | -------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `value` / `defaultValue` | `Date \| null`                  |                      | First day of the month / year       |
| `onChange`               | `(value: Date \| null) => void` |                      |                                     |
| `format`                 | `string`                        | `LLLL yyyy` / `yyyy` | date-fns display format             |
| `min` / `max`            | `Date`                          |                      | Months/years outside are greyed out |

Plus the shared picker field props; see [DatePicker](./date-picker.md#props).

## Accessibility

Months and years are APG grids with roving focus: arrows move (swapped in RTL), <kbd>Page Up</kbd>/<kbd>Page Down</kbd> change the year (12 years in the years view), <kbd>Home</kbd>/<kbd>End</kbd> go to the row start/end, <kbd>Enter</kbd> picks, <kbd>Escape</kbd> closes and returns focus.
