<!-- docs/files-and-media/media-player.md -->

# MediaPlayer

An accessible audio and video player built on [Media Chrome](https://www.media-chrome.org): play/pause, seek, time, mute and volume, captions, playback speed and full screen, with keyboard shortcuts, translated labels and Onu theming. Part of the optional media entry.

```bash
pnpm add media-chrome
```

```tsx
import { MediaPlayer } from "@javaabu/onu/media"

<MediaPlayer
  title="Coral reef restoration in Baa Atoll"
  src={[
    { src: "/video/reef.webm", type: "video/webm" },
    { src: "/video/reef.mp4", type: "video/mp4" },
  ]}
  poster="/video/reef.jpg"
  tracks={[
    { src: "/video/reef.dv.vtt", srcLang: "dv", label: "ދިވެހި", default: true },
    { src: "/video/reef.en.vtt", srcLang: "en", label: "English" },
  ]}
/>

<MediaPlayer kind="audio" title="Island news" src="/audio/news.mp3" />
```

## Props

| Prop                                      | Type                        | Default                  | Description                                                   |
| ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `src`                                     | `string \| { src, type }[]` |                          | Media URL or sources                                          |
| `kind`                                    | `"video" \| "audio"`        | `"video"`                | Media type                                                    |
| `title`                                   | `string`                    |                          | Names the player (required)                                   |
| `poster`                                  | `string`                    |                          | Video poster                                                  |
| `tracks`                                  | `MediaTrack[]`              | `[]`                     | `{ src, srcLang, label, kind?, default? }` captions/subtitles |
| `playbackRates`                           | `number[]`                  | `[0.5, 1, 1.25, 1.5, 2]` | Speeds offered                                                |
| `seekOffset`                              | `number`                    | `10`                     | Seconds per seek button                                       |
| `loop`, `muted`, `preload`, `crossOrigin` |                             |                          | Passed to the media element                                   |
| `classNames`                              | `{ media, controlBar }`     |                          | Classes for each part                                         |

## Accessibility

Every control has a label; the captions button appears when `tracks` are given (R14.10). Controls are at least 44px on touch screens. In narrow players (under 24rem) the volume slider and the seek buttons hide so the timeline keeps its room and nothing overlaps the time display; mute stays, and the arrow keys still seek.

| Key                                          | Action              |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------- |
| <kbd>Space</kbd> / <kbd>K</kbd>              | Play / pause        |
| <kbd>ArrowLeft</kbd> / <kbd>ArrowRight</kbd> | Seek back / forward |
| <kbd>M</kbd>                                 | Mute                |
| <kbd>F</kbd>                                 | Full screen         |
| <kbd>C</kbd>                                 | Captions            |

## RTL and Dhivehi

The control bar stays left-to-right in RTL, so the timeline and the seek keys match the media's time direction. Labels are registered with Media Chrome for the active locale (Dhivehi included) from the `file` namespace. Media Chrome's language setting is global, so all players on a page share the active locale.

---

<!-- docs/files-and-media/video-embed.md -->

# VideoEmbed

A click-to-load YouTube or Vimeo embed (the "lite embed" pattern): it shows a thumbnail and a play button, and loads the privacy-enhanced player (`youtube-nocookie.com`, Vimeo with `dnt=1`) only when the user presses play. Nothing is requested from the provider before that except the YouTube thumbnail (pass your own `thumbnail` to avoid even that).

```tsx
import { VideoEmbed } from "@javaabu/onu"

<VideoEmbed url="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aqz-KE-bpKQ" title="Hulhumalé phase 2 tour" />
<VideoEmbed provider="vimeo" videoId="76979871" title="Reef survey" thumbnail="/thumbs/reef.jpg" />
```

`parseVideoUrl(url)` and `videoEmbedUrl(provider, id, { start })` are exported. `t=` / `start=` in the URL sets the start time.

## Props

| Prop          | Type                                         | Default    | Description                          |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `url`         | `string`                                     |            | YouTube or Vimeo URL                 |
| `provider`    | `"youtube" \| "vimeo"`                       |            | Instead of `url`, with `videoId`     |
| `videoId`     | `string`                                     |            | Video id                             |
| `title`       | `string`                                     | (required) | Names the play button and the iframe |
| `thumbnail`   | `string`                                     | YouTube's  | Poster image (needed for Vimeo)      |
| `start`       | `number`                                     |            | Start time in seconds                |
| `aspectRatio` | `number`                                     | `16/9`     | Width / height                       |
| `notice`      | `ReactNode`                                  |            | Small print, e.g. a privacy note     |
| `classNames`  | `{ button, thumbnail, play, title, iframe }` |            | Classes for each part                |

## Accessibility

The play button is named "Play video: {title}". After it is pressed, the iframe (titled with `title`) gets focus, so keyboard users continue straight into the player. An unrecognised URL disables the button.

| Key                                 | Action        |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | Load and play |

## RTL and Dhivehi

The title overlay sits at the inline start and is isolated with `<bdi>`.

---

<!-- docs/files-and-media/file-icon.md -->

# FileIcon

A coloured icon for a file's type (image, video, audio, PDF, document, spreadsheet, presentation, archive, text), detected from the MIME type or the file extension. It uses semantic icon names, so it follows the configured icon set.

```tsx
import { FileIcon } from "@javaabu/onu"

<FileIcon name="budget.xlsx" />
<FileIcon type="application/pdf" size="lg" label="PDF document" />
```

## Props

| Prop    | Type                        | Default     | Description                                    |
| ------- | --------------------------- | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `type`  | `string`                    |             | MIME type                                      |
| `name`  | `string`                    |             | File name or URL (extension used when no type) |
| `kind`  | `FileKind`                  |             | Force a kind                                   |
| `size`  | `"sm" \| "default" \| "lg"` | `"default"` | Size (`fileIconVariants`)                      |
| `label` | `string`                    |             | Accessible label; decorative without it        |

`getFileKind({ type, name })` and `FILE_KIND_ICONS` are exported. Icons used: `file-image`, `file-video`, `file-audio`, `file-text`, `file-spreadsheet`, `file-archive`, `file`.

## Accessibility

Decorative by default (`aria-hidden`); pass `label` when the icon is the only indication of the type.

## RTL and Dhivehi

File icons are not directional and do not mirror.

---

<!-- docs/files-and-media/qr-code.md -->

# QrCode

A QR code generator. The text is encoded with [`uqr`](https://github.com/unjs/uqr) (MIT, zero dependencies) and Onu renders the SVG itself, so the dark modules use `currentColor` and follow theme tokens. It supports the four error-correction levels, a quiet zone, a centre logo (which switches to level H automatically), and optional buttons to download the code as PNG or SVG and to copy the encoded text. It is the generator counterpart of the [QR code scanner](../text-inputs/qr-code-scanner.md) and is exported from the media entry point.

```tsx
import { QrCode } from "@javaabu/onu/media"

<QrCode value="https://verify.trade.gov.mv/BL-2026-04417" label="QR code to verify licence BL-2026-04417" />

<QrCode
  value={ticket.url}
  size={200}
  logo="/logo.svg"
  caption="Scan to verify"
  download
  copyable
  filename={`ticket-${ticket.number}`}
/>
```

Text is encoded as UTF-8, so Thaana works. Text that does not fit in a QR code (about 2,900 bytes at level L, fewer at higher levels) shows an error message in place of the code.

## Colours

The code never mirrors and is rendered with tokens through the `tone` variant (`qrCodeVariants`):

| Tone                   | Result                                                                                   |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `contrast` (default)   | Dark modules on a light ground in both themes (`bg-foreground` / `text-background` dark) |
| `theme`                | Follows the theme: light modules on a dark ground in dark mode. Most phone cameras scan this, some older readers do not |
| `transparent`          | No background; modules use the current text colour. Keep enough contrast with what is behind |

Recolour with `classNames.svg`, e.g. `classNames={{ svg: "text-primary" }}`. Downloads use the colours as rendered (read with `getComputedStyle`).

## Logo

`logo` takes a URL or `{ src, size?, excavate? }`. `size` is the logo width as a fraction of the code (0.1–0.3, default 0.22). The modules behind it are cleared unless `excavate={false}`. A logo always uses error-correction level H, so the code still scans with the centre covered. For the PNG download the image must allow CORS; otherwise the PNG has the cleared area without the logo.

## Props

| Prop           | Type                                                             | Default      | Description                                         |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`        | `string`                                                         |              | Text to encode (required)                           |
| `size`         | `number`                                                         | `160`        | Width and height in CSS px; shrinks in narrow boxes |
| `level`        | `"L" \| "M" \| "Q" \| "H"`                                       | `"M"`        | Error correction (always `"H"` with a logo)         |
| `quietZone`    | `number`                                                         | `4`          | Light margin, in modules                            |
| `tone`         | `"contrast" \| "theme" \| "transparent"`                         | `"contrast"` | Colours (see above)                                 |
| `logo`         | `string \| { src, size?, excavate? }`                            |              | Centre image                                        |
| `label`        | `string`                                                         | "QR code"    | Accessible name (`aria-label` also works)           |
| `caption`      | `ReactNode`                                                      |              | Text under the code                                 |
| `showValue`    | `boolean`                                                        | `false`      | Show the encoded text under the code                |
| `download`     | `boolean \| ("png" \| "svg")[]`                                  | `false`      | Download buttons (`true` = both)                    |
| `copyable`     | `boolean`                                                        | `false`      | Copy-text button                                    |
| `filename`     | `string`                                                         | `"qr-code"`  | Download file name without extension                |
| `downloadSize` | `number`                                                         | `1024`       | Approximate PNG width in px                         |
| `onDownload`   | `(format, blob) => void`                                         |              | After a download                                    |
| `onCopy`       | `(value) => void`                                                |              | After a successful copy                             |
| `classNames`   | `{ svg, caption, value, actions, button, error }`                |              | Classes for each part                               |

Other props and `ref` go to the root `div` (`data-slot="qr-code"`, with `data-level`, `data-version` and `data-modules`).

Also exported for custom rendering: `encodeQrCode(value, level)`, `qrCodePath(modules, offset, skip?)`, `qrLogoBox(size, ratio)`, `qrCodeToSvg(matrix, options)` and `qrCodeToPng(matrix, options)`.

## Accessibility

- The code is an `img` named by `label` (default "QR code"); give it a label that says what it is for, e.g. "QR code to verify licence BL-2026-04417".
- Put the information in text as well (`showValue`, `caption` or nearby text) for people who cannot scan.
- Download and copy buttons have visible, translated labels and are 44px tall on touch screens. Copying is announced in a polite live region.
- Text that is too long is reported with `role="alert"`.

| Key                                 | Action                          |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>                      | Move between the action buttons |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | Download or copy                |

## RTL and Dhivehi

The code itself is never mirrored. Buttons and caption follow the page direction, the value is shown with `dir="auto"`, and all labels come from the `file` namespace (`file.qrCode`, `file.qrDownloadPng`, …) in English and Dhivehi.

---

<!-- docs/rich-content/wysiwyg-editor.md -->

# WYSIWYG editor

A rich text editor built on [Tiptap](https://tiptap.dev) (ProseMirror). It has a toolbar for headings, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, inline code, lists, quotes, links, images, tables, alignment, dividers and undo/redo. Every block gets `dir="auto"`, so mixed Dhivehi and English paragraphs each read in their own direction. Lists, quotes and tables get an explicit `dir` from their first strong character (a container with `dir="auto"` would ignore its paragraphs and fall back to LTR), updated while typing, and `getHTML()` includes it. A Dhivehi table therefore has its first column on the right, with cells aligned to their logical start.

Only MIT-licensed Tiptap packages are used. No Tiptap Pro or Cloud extension is needed.

```bash
pnpm add @tiptap/core @tiptap/react @tiptap/pm @tiptap/starter-kit @tiptap/extension-image @tiptap/extension-table @tiptap/extension-text-align @tiptap/extension-placeholder @tiptap/static-renderer @tiptap/suggestion shiki
```

```tsx
import { WysiwygEditor } from "@javaabu/onu/editor"

export const Example = (
  <FormField label="Body" name="body">
    <WysiwygEditor />
  </FormField>
)
```

## Value

The value is an HTML string or Tiptap JSON. The output format follows the shape of `value`/`defaultValue`, or set `format`.

```tsx
const [html, setHtml] = useState('<p>Hello</p>');
<WysiwygEditor value={html} onChange={setHtml} />

<WysiwygEditor format="json" onChange={(json) => save(json)} />
```

An empty document is `""` in HTML. With `name` (or inside a `FormField` with a `name`), a hidden input carries the value for plain form posts; JSON is posted as a string, and an empty document posts `""`, so Laravel's `required` rule works.

## Thaana

```tsx
<WysiwygEditor thaana />
<WysiwygEditor thaana={{ keymap: 'typewriter', defaultEnabled: false }} />
```

With `thaana`, typing goes through the [`ThaanaKeyboard`](./thaana-keyboard.md) extension: the toolbar gets a ދ/A toggle, <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>T</kbd> switches mode, and the content area gets `lang="dv"` and `dir="rtl"` while Thaana is on.

## Toolbar

The default toolbar is `DEFAULT_TOOLBAR`. Pass your own list, with `"|"` for separators, or `false` for none.

```tsx
<WysiwygEditor toolbar={["bold", "italic", "|", "bulletList", "orderedList", "|", "link"]} />
```

Items: `blockType`, `bold`, `italic`, `underline`, `strike`, `code`, `bulletList`, `orderedList`, `blockquote`, `codeBlock`, `link`, `image`, `table`, `alignStart`, `alignCenter`, `alignEnd`, `horizontalRule`, `undo`, `redo`, `thaana`.

In narrow containers (phones, sidebars) the less common items move into a **More** menu and the rest wrap. Alignment uses logical `start`/`center`/`end`, so it follows the text direction.

`EditorToolbar` is exported too, for building your own layout around a Tiptap editor.

## Images

The image dialog takes a URL and alt text. Pass `onImageUpload` to add an **Upload** tab; it receives the `File` and resolves to the uploaded URL.

```tsx
<WysiwygEditor
  onImageUpload={async (file) => {
    const body = new FormData()
    body.append("image", file)
    const res = await fetch("/media", { method: "POST", body })
    return (await res.json()).url
  }}
/>
```

## Props

| Prop                | Type                              | Default           | Description                                                                |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------- | ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`             | `string \| JSONContent`           |                   | Controlled content                                                         |
| `defaultValue`      | `string \| JSONContent`           |                   | Initial content                                                            |
| `onChange`          | `(value, editor) => void`         |                   | Called on every change                                                     |
| `format`            | `'html' \| 'json'`                | from the value    | Output format                                                              |
| `name`              | `string`                          |                   | Hidden input name for form posts                                           |
| `placeholder`       | `string`                          | "Start writing…"  | Shown when empty                                                           |
| `readOnly`          | `boolean`                         | `false`           | Show the content without editing or toolbar                                |
| `disabled`          | `boolean`                         | `false`           | Disable editing                                                            |
| `thaana`            | `boolean \| ThaanaOptions`        | `false`           | Type Thaana from a Latin keyboard                                          |
| `toolbar`           | `ToolbarItem[] \| false`          | `DEFAULT_TOOLBAR` | Toolbar controls                                                           |
| `headingLevels`     | `(1–6)[]`                         | `[1, 2, 3]`       | Levels in the text style menu                                              |
| `onImageUpload`     | `(file: File) => Promise<string>` |                   | Enables image upload                                                       |
| `extensions`        | `Extensions`                      |                   | Extra (MIT) Tiptap extensions                                              |
| `variant`           | `'default' \| 'ghost'`            | `'default'`       | Bordered or borderless                                                     |
| `size`              | `'sm' \| 'default' \| 'lg'`       | `'default'`       | Prose size                                                                 |
| `immediatelyRender` | `boolean`                         | `false`           | Create the editor during the first render (SPA only; keep `false` for SSR) |
| `onReady`           | `(editor) => void`                |                   | Receives the Tiptap `Editor`                                               |
| `classNames`        | `{ toolbar, content }`            |                   | Classes for each part                                                      |

Other `<div>` props go to the root, and `ref` points at the root. `editorVariants` is exported.

## Accessibility

- The content area is a `role="textbox"` with `aria-multiline`. Inside a `FormField` it is labelled by the field label and described by help and error text; `aria-invalid`, `aria-required`, `aria-readonly` and `aria-disabled` are set.
- The toolbar follows the WAI-ARIA toolbar pattern: one tab stop, arrow keys move between controls (mirrored in RTL), toggles expose `aria-pressed`.
- Link and image dialogs return focus to the button that opened them.
- Toolbar buttons are 44px on touch screens.

| Key                                                                             | Action                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| <kbd>Ctrl/⌘</kbd>+<kbd>B</kbd> / <kbd>I</kbd> / <kbd>U</kbd>                    | Bold / italic / underline    |
| <kbd>Ctrl/⌘</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>S</kbd>                                 | Strikethrough                |
| <kbd>Ctrl/⌘</kbd>+<kbd>E</kbd>                                                  | Inline code                  |
| <kbd>Ctrl/⌘</kbd>+<kbd>K</kbd>                                                  | Insert or edit a link        |
| <kbd>Ctrl/⌘</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>7</kbd> / <kbd>8</kbd>                  | Numbered / bulleted list     |
| <kbd>Ctrl/⌘</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>L</kbd> / <kbd>E</kbd> / <kbd>R</kbd>   | Align start / centre / end   |
| <kbd>Ctrl/⌘</kbd>+<kbd>Z</kbd>, <kbd>Ctrl/⌘</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Z</kbd> | Undo, redo                   |
| <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>F10</kbd>                                                   | Move focus to the toolbar    |
| <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> <kbd>Home</kbd> <kbd>End</kbd>                        | Move within the toolbar      |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd> (in the toolbar)                                                 | Back to the content          |
| <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>T</kbd>                                    | Thaana/Latin (with `thaana`) |

:::info

To show saved content without loading the editor, use [`BlockRenderer`](./block-renderer.md). It renders HTML-free, sanitised React from the JSON.

:::

---

<!-- docs/rich-content/block-editor.md -->

# Block editor

A block-based editor (page builder) on Tiptap. Type <kbd>/</kbd> for a menu of blocks, add a block below with **+**, and reorder blocks with the grip. Content is Tiptap JSON, rendered anywhere with [`BlockRenderer`](./block-renderer.md).

Blocks: text, headings 1–3, bulleted and numbered lists, quote, image, table, divider, callout, code and embed (YouTube or Vimeo).

```tsx
import { BlockEditor, BlockRenderer } from '@javaabu/onu/editor';

const [doc, setDoc] = useState<JSONContent>();

<FormField label="Content" name="content">
  <BlockEditor value={doc} onChange={setDoc} />
</FormField>

<BlockRenderer content={doc} />
```

The slash menu uses `@tiptap/suggestion` (MIT). Drag handles are built in-house on pointer events: `@tiptap/extension-drag-handle-react` is MIT but requires Yjs and the collaboration extension, which Onu does not want to force on every project.

## Limiting blocks

```tsx
<BlockEditor blockTypes={["paragraph", "heading2", "bulletList", "callout"]} />
```

Ids: `paragraph`, `heading1`, `heading2`, `heading3`, `bulletList`, `orderedList`, `blockquote`, `image`, `table`, `divider`, `callout`, `codeBlock`, `embed`.

## Moving blocks

- **Pointer, touch or pen**: drag the grip beside a block; a line shows where it will land.
- **Keyboard**: press the grip (or <kbd>Enter</kbd> on it) for **Move up**, **Move down**, **Duplicate** and **Delete**, or press <kbd>Ctrl/⌘</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>↑</kbd>/<kbd>↓</kbd> in a block.
- Moves are announced, e.g. "Block moved to position 3".

## Props

| Prop            | Type                              | Default               | Description                                  |
| --------------- | --------------------------------- | --------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `value`         | `JSONContent`                     |                       | Controlled document                          |
| `defaultValue`  | `JSONContent \| string`           |                       | Initial document (JSON or HTML to import)    |
| `onChange`      | `(json, editor) => void`          |                       | Called on every change                       |
| `name`          | `string`                          |                       | Hidden input with the JSON (empty doc: `""`) |
| `placeholder`   | `string`                          | "Type “/” for blocks" | Placeholder on empty paragraphs              |
| `blockTypes`    | `BlockTypeId[]`                   | all                   | Blocks in the "/" and "+" menus              |
| `toolbar`       | `ToolbarItem[] \| false`          | `BLOCK_TOOLBAR`       | Formatting toolbar                           |
| `thaana`        | `boolean \| ThaanaOptions`        | `false`               | Type Thaana from a Latin keyboard            |
| `onImageUpload` | `(file: File) => Promise<string>` |                       | Enables image upload                         |
| `readOnly`      | `boolean`                         | `false`               | No editing, handles or toolbar               |
| `disabled`      | `boolean`                         | `false`               | Disable editing                              |
| `extensions`    | `Extensions`                      |                       | Extra Tiptap extensions                      |
| `size`          | `'sm' \| 'default' \| 'lg'`       | `'default'`           | Prose size                                   |
| `classNames`    | `{ toolbar, content }`            |                       | Classes for each part                        |

Also `autofocus`, `immediatelyRender` and `onReady`, as on [`WysiwygEditor`](./wysiwyg-editor.md). `ref` points at the root.

## RTL and Thaana

The gutter with the handles sits at the inline start, so it is on the right in RTL. Every text block and table cell gets `dir="auto"`; lists, quotes and tables take the direction of their first strong character (updated as you type), so bullets, the quote border and the first table column sit on the right of Dhivehi text. Table cells align to their logical start. With `thaana`, typing Latin keys writes Thaana and <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>T</kbd> switches back.

## Accessibility

- The slash menu is a listbox; focus stays in the editor, which points at the highlighted option with `aria-activedescendant` and `aria-controls`. The number of results is announced.
- The **+** and grip buttons are labelled, keyboard operable and 44px on touch screens. Dragging always has the menu as an alternative.

| Key                                                                        | Action                       |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| <kbd>/</kbd>                                                               | Open the block menu          |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> <kbd>↓</kbd>, <kbd>Enter</kbd>/<kbd>Tab</kbd>, <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Move, insert, close the menu |
| <kbd>Ctrl/⌘</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>↑</kbd>/<kbd>↓</kbd>               | Move the current block       |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> at the end of a callout                                   | Continue with a paragraph    |
| <kbd>Backspace</kbd> at the start of a callout                             | Turn it into a paragraph     |
| <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>F10</kbd>, <kbd>Ctrl/⌘</kbd>+<kbd>K</kbd>              | Toolbar, link dialog         |

---

<!-- docs/rich-content/block-renderer.md -->

# Block renderer

Renders block editor (or WYSIWYG) JSON to React **without** loading the editor. It uses `@tiptap/static-renderer` with the same node definitions as the editors, so a page looks the same while editing and when published.

```tsx
import { BlockRenderer } from '@javaabu/onu/editor';

<BlockRenderer content={page.content} />
<BlockRenderer content={jsonStringFromDb} empty={<p>No content yet.</p>} />
```

## Safe by default

- No raw HTML is ever injected (`dangerouslySetInnerHTML` is not used); text is text.
- Links keep only `http(s)`, `mailto`, `tel` and relative URLs, with `rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow"`. Others render as plain text.
- Images keep only `http(s)`, relative, `blob:` and raster `data:image` sources.
- Embeds frame only YouTube (via `youtube-nocookie.com`) and Vimeo, in a sandboxed `iframe`. Other URLs become links.
- Content that doesn't fit the schema renders nothing instead of crashing.

Helpers `isSafeUrl`, `isSafeImageUrl` and `toEmbedUrl` are exported.

## Custom rendering

```tsx
<BlockRenderer
  content={doc}
  nodes={{ image: ({ node }) => <Lightbox src={node.attrs.src} alt={node.attrs.alt} /> }}
  marks={{ link: ({ mark, children }) => <InertiaLink href={mark.attrs.href}>{children}</InertiaLink> }}
  codeBlock={{ lineNumbers: true }}
/>
```

Code blocks render with [`CodeBlock`](./code-block.md); callouts get a status icon and `role="note"`.

## Props

| Prop         | Type                                   | Default     | Description                             |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------- | ----------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `content`    | `JSONContent \| string \| null`        |             | Document JSON, or a JSON string         |
| `size`       | `'sm' \| 'default' \| 'lg'`            | `'default'` | Prose size                              |
| `nodes`      | `Record<string, (props) => ReactNode>` |             | Override node rendering                 |
| `marks`      | `Record<string, (props) => ReactNode>` |             | Override mark rendering                 |
| `extensions` | `Extensions`                           |             | Extra node types (same as the editor's) |
| `codeBlock`  | `Partial<CodeBlockProps>`              |             | Props for every code block              |
| `empty`      | `ReactNode`                            |             | Shown when there is no content          |

Other `<div>` props go to the root. The prose styles are exported as `proseVariants`.

## RTL, Thaana and accessibility

Every block keeps `dir="auto"`, so Dhivehi paragraphs read right-to-left and English ones left-to-right on any page. Lists, quotes and tables get an explicit `dir` worked out from their first strong character (the browser's `dir="auto"` skips the paragraphs inside them and would fall back to LTR), so bullets, numbers, the quote border and the first table column sit at the inline start of Dhivehi text. A table and its scroll wrapper both get the direction, so columns run right-to-left in a Dhivehi table even on an English page (and the other way round), and cells align to their logical start. A table with no strong text yet (only numbers) stays `dir="auto"`. An explicit `dir` in the content wins. Prose styles avoid faux italics and bold for Thaana and use size for heading emphasis. Wide tables and code scroll inside their own container. Images keep their alt text, and embeds get a `title` (falling back to "Embedded content").

---

<!-- docs/rich-content/code-block.md -->

# Code block

Read-only code with [Shiki](https://shiki.style) syntax highlighting, a language label, a copy button and optional line numbers. Shiki is loaded lazily on first use, and code is always laid out left-to-right, even on RTL pages.

```tsx
import { CodeBlock } from '@javaabu/onu/editor';

<CodeBlock code={source} language="php" />
<CodeBlock code={source} language="tsx" title="app/page.tsx" lineNumbers highlightLines={[3, 4]} />
<CodeBlock code="MVR 1,250.00" />  {/* plain text */}
```

Light and dark mode use two Shiki themes at once (GitHub light/dark by default) through CSS variables, so switching theme needs no re-highlighting. Token colours from any theme are darkened (light mode) or lightened (dark mode) just enough to reach 4.5:1 contrast on the code background, including highlighted lines, so the block meets WCAG 2.2 AA whichever themes you pick.

## Props

| Prop             | Type                                      | Default           | Description                            |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ----------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `code`           | `string`                                  |                   | The code                               |
| `language`       | `string`                                  |                   | Shiki language id; omit for plain text |
| `title`          | `ReactNode`                               | language name     | Caption, e.g. a file name              |
| `lineNumbers`    | `boolean`                                 | `false`           | Show line numbers                      |
| `startLine`      | `number`                                  | `1`               | First line number                      |
| `highlightLines` | `number[]`                                |                   | Lines to highlight                     |
| `copyable`       | `boolean`                                 | `true`            | Show the copy button                   |
| `wrap`           | `boolean`                                 | `false`           | Wrap long lines instead of scrolling   |
| `hideHeader`     | `boolean`                                 | `false`           | Hide label and copy button             |
| `themes`         | `{ light: string; dark: string }`         | GitHub light/dark | Shiki themes                           |
| `classNames`     | `{ header, pre, line, lineNumber, copy }` |                   | Classes for each part                  |

Other `<figure>` props go to the root. `highlightCode(code, language, themes)` is exported for custom renderers.

### Languages and themes

Onu bundles a curated set of grammars, each loaded on demand: `bash`, `blade`, `css`, `dart`, `diff`, `html`, `javascript`, `json`, `jsx`, `markdown`, `php`, `python`, `sql`, `tsx`, `typescript`, `vue`, `xml` and `yaml` (aliases such as `ts`, `js`, `sh`, `yml` and `md` work too). Highlighting uses Shiki's JavaScript regex engine, so no WebAssembly is shipped. Any other language renders as plain text until you register it, and other themes likewise:

```ts
import { registerCodeLanguage, registerCodeTheme } from "@javaabu/onu/editor"

registerCodeLanguage("rust", () => import("shiki/langs/rust.mjs"))
registerCodeTheme("nord", () => import("shiki/themes/nord.mjs"))
```

Unregistered theme names fall back to GitHub light/dark.

## Accessibility

- The code area is a focusable, labelled region, so it can be scrolled with the keyboard.
- Line numbers are hidden from screen readers.
- The copy button is labelled "Copy code" and announces "Code copied".
- Syntax colours meet 4.5:1 contrast on the code background in light and dark mode.

---

<!-- docs/rich-content/translations-editor.md -->

# Translations editor

Edit translation keys side by side in English and Dhivehi (or any languages). The Dhivehi column types Thaana from a Latin keyboard. Search keys and text, show only keys with missing translations, and save each cell inline.

```tsx
import { TranslationsEditor } from "@javaabu/onu/editor"

export const Example = (
  <TranslationsEditor
    defaultValue={[
      { key: "auth.login", values: { en: "Log in", dv: "ލޮގިން" }, description: "Sign-in button" },
      { key: "auth.logout", values: { en: "Log out", dv: "" } },
    ]}
    onSave={async ({ key, locale, value }) => {
      await fetch(`/translations/${locale}/${key}`, { method: "PUT", body: JSON.stringify({ value }) })
    }}
  />
)
```

A cell saves when it loses focus (`saveOnBlur`), on <kbd>Ctrl/⌘</kbd>+<kbd>Enter</kbd>, or from its **Save** button. While saving it shows "Saving…", then "Saved"; a rejected promise shows "Couldn’t save" with **Retry**.

Rows that match "Missing only" stay visible while you type their translation, until the filter changes or the cell is saved.

## Props

| Prop                 | Type                                                       | Default          | Description                          |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `value`              | `TranslationEntry[]`                                       |                  | Controlled entries                   |
| `defaultValue`       | `TranslationEntry[]`                                       |                  | Initial entries                      |
| `onChange`           | `(entries) => void`                                        |                  | Called when any cell changes         |
| `locales`            | `{ code, label?, thaana? }[]`                              | English, Dhivehi | Language columns                     |
| `onSave`             | `({ key, locale, value, entry }) => void \| Promise<void>` |                  | Saves one cell                       |
| `saveOnBlur`         | `boolean`                                                  | `true`           | Save when a changed cell loses focus |
| `defaultMissingOnly` | `boolean`                                                  | `false`          | Start with the missing filter on     |
| `defaultSearch`      | `string`                                                   | `""`             | Initial search                       |
| `thaana`             | `boolean \| ThaanaOptions`                                 | `true`           | Thaana options for Thaana columns    |
| `readOnly`           | `boolean`                                                  | `false`          | View only                            |
| `classNames`         | `{ toolbar, list, row, key, cell }`                        |                  | Classes for each part                |

`TranslationEntry`: `{ key: string; values: Record<locale, string | null>; description?: string }`.

## Layout

In wide containers each key is a row with one column per language. Below about 672px (container query) rows become cards with a labelled field per language, so it works in a sidebar or on a phone.

## Accessibility

- Each field is named "<key> in <language>" and described by its key.
- Missing translations are marked with an icon and the word "Missing", not colour alone.
- Counts, save results and errors are announced in polite live regions.

---

<!-- docs/rich-content/custom-attribute-fields.md -->

# Custom attribute fields

Renders form fields from a schema, for custom attributes, settings or product specs, using Onu's inputs. Values go in and out as one object, input names follow Laravel's `attributes[key]` convention, and server errors map back to the right field.

```tsx
import { CustomAttributeFields, type AttributeField } from "@javaabu/onu/editor"

const schema: AttributeField[] = [
  { name: "name", label: "Property name", type: "text", required: true },
  { name: "name_dv", label: "ނަން", type: "text", thaana: true },
  { name: "island", label: "Island", type: "select", options: ["Malé", "Hulhumalé", "Maafushi"] },
  { name: "bedrooms", label: "Bedrooms", type: "number", min: 0 },
  { name: "amenities", label: "Amenities", type: "multiselect", options: ["Pool", "Jetty"] },
  { name: "furnished", label: "Furnished", type: "boolean" },
]

export const Example = (
  <CustomAttributeFields schema={schema} name="attributes" columns={2} value={values} onChange={setValues} />
)
```

## Field types

| `type`                     | Control                  | Value            | Posted as                           |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------ | ---------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `text`                     | Text input (`thaana` ok) | `string`         | `attributes[key]`                   |
| `textarea`                 | Textarea (`thaana` ok)   | `string`         | `attributes[key]`                   |
| `number`                   | Number input             | `number \| null` | `attributes[key]`                   |
| `email`, `url`, `tel`      | Input, forced LTR        | `string`         | `attributes[key]`                   |
| `date`, `time`, `datetime` | Native date/time input   | `string` (ISO)   | `attributes[key]`                   |
| `color`                    | Colour input             | `string`         | `attributes[key]`                   |
| `select`                   | Select                   | `string`         | `attributes[key]`                   |
| `radio`                    | Radio group              | `string`         | `attributes[key]`                   |
| `multiselect`              | Checkbox group           | `string[]`       | `attributes[key][]` (one per value) |
| `boolean`                  | Switch                   | `boolean`        | `attributes[key]` = `1` or `0`      |

Options are strings or `{ value, label, disabled? }`.

Field keys: `name`, `label`, `type`, `options`, `required`, `help`, `placeholder`, `disabled`, `defaultValue`, `min`, `max`, `step`, `maxLength`, `thaana`, `fullWidth`.

## Errors

Laravel's 422 errors work as they come, either through a surrounding `FormErrorsProvider` or the `errors` prop:

```tsx
<CustomAttributeFields schema={schema} name="attributes" errors={response.errors} />
// { "attributes.name": ["The name field is required."] }
```

## Props

| Prop           | Type                    | Default      | Description                              |
| -------------- | ----------------------- | ------------ | ---------------------------------------- |
| `schema`       | `AttributeField[]`      |              | Fields, in order                         |
| `value`        | `AttributeValues`       |              | Controlled values                        |
| `defaultValue` | `AttributeValues`       |              | Initial values                           |
| `onChange`     | `(values) => void`      |              | Called with all values                   |
| `name`         | `string`                |              | Wraps input names: `name[key]`           |
| `errors`       | `FormErrors`            |              | Server errors keyed by dot notation      |
| `columns`      | `1 \| 2`                | `1`          | Two columns from medium container widths |
| `labelLayout`  | `'stacked' \| 'inline'` | form default | Label layout for every field             |
| `disabled`     | `boolean`               | `false`      | Disable every field                      |
| `classNames`   | `{ field, control }`    |              | Classes for each field and control       |

## RTL, Thaana and accessibility

Every field is a [`FormField`](../form-scaffolding/form-field.md): labelled, with help and errors wired through `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid` and `aria-required`. Radio and checkbox groups are labelled by the field label. Latin-only types (email, URL, phone, number, colour) stay LTR; text fields use `dir="auto"` or Thaana. Two-column layouts stack in narrow containers, and choice targets are 44px on touch screens.

---

<!-- docs/rich-content/thaana-keyboard.md -->

# ThaanaKeyboard (Tiptap)

A Tiptap extension that types Thaana from a Latin keyboard through ProseMirror transactions rather than DOM edits (R13.2), so undo/redo, input rules and collaboration keep working. `WysiwygEditor` and `BlockEditor` use it for their `thaana` prop; use it directly in your own Tiptap editors.

```tsx
import { ThaanaKeyboard } from "@javaabu/onu/editor"

const editor = useEditor({
  extensions: [StarterKit, ThaanaKeyboard.configure({ keymap: "phonetic", paste: "transliterate" })],
})

editor.commands.toggleThaana()
editor.commands.setThaana(false)
editor.storage.thaanaKeyboard.enabled // current mode
```

## Options

| Option           | Type                                                    | Default         | Description                                |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `enabled`        | `boolean`                                               | `true`          | Start in Thaana mode                       |
| `keymap`         | `'phonetic' \| 'phonetic-hh' \| 'typewriter' \| Keymap` | `'phonetic'`    | Key layout                                 |
| `paste`          | `'keep' \| 'transliterate'`                             | `'keep'`        | Convert pasted Latin plain text            |
| `toggleShortcut` | `string \| false`                                       | `'Alt-Shift-t'` | ProseMirror key name that toggles the mode |
| `onToggle`       | `(enabled) => void`                                     |                 | Called when the mode changes               |

## How it works

- Typed characters are mapped in `beforeinput` (works with Android's keyCode 229) and in `handleTextInput`; the Thaana text is inserted as a normal typed transaction.
- <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>⌘</kbd> shortcuts never produce text input, so they pass through.
- Text from an IME or a native Thaana keyboard is left alone; whole Latin words composed by predictive keyboards are converted when composition ends.
- Toggling dispatches a transaction, so `useEditorState` sees the new mode.

## Accessibility

- The extension changes only how keys map to characters; the editor stays a normal ProseMirror text box for screen readers, and Thaana is inserted as ordinary typed text, so the editor reads, undoes and redoes it like any other input.
- <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>T</kbd> switches modes from the keyboard. Set `toggleShortcut: false` only when you offer another way to switch.
- The extension does not render a button or announce the mode. Onu's editors add a [`ThaanaToggle`](../text-inputs/thaana-toggle.md) to the toolbar (`aria-pressed`, with the change announced in a polite live region); in your own editor, render one from `editor.storage.thaanaKeyboard.enabled` and `toggleThaana()`, or announce `onToggle` with [`useAnnouncer`](../accessibility/use-announcer.md).
- Mark Thaana content with `dir="rtl"` and `lang="dv"` (Onu's editors do this from the mode) so it is read with a Dhivehi voice and laid out right to left.

---

<!-- docs/maps/map-provider.md -->

# MapProvider

Configures the map engine for every map inside it. Onu maps default to **Google Maps** (via `@vis.gl/react-google-maps`), and fall back to a keyless schematic preview when no API key is set.

```tsx
import { OnuProvider } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<OnuProvider maps={{ googleMapsApiKey: import.meta.env.VITE_GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY, mapId: "…", darkMapId: "…" }}>
  <App />
</OnuProvider>
```

Every map component reads `useOnu().maps` and adds a `MapProvider` itself when there is none above it. Add one explicitly to override settings for a subtree, or to load the Maps JavaScript API once for many maps:

```tsx
import { MapProvider } from "@javaabu/onu/maps"

;<MapProvider apiKey="…" mapId="…" region="MV">
  <MapPicker />
  <LiveMap markers={vessels} />
</MapProvider>
```

Install the optional peers for the maps entry: `@vis.gl/react-google-maps`, `terra-draw`, `terra-draw-google-maps-adapter`, `@googlemaps/markerclusterer`, `@deck.gl/core`, `@deck.gl/layers`, `@deck.gl/aggregation-layers`, `@deck.gl/google-maps` and `@turf/turf`. terra-draw, deck.gl and the clusterer are loaded on demand.

## Light, dark and language

- The colour scheme follows the page (`.dark` or `data-theme="dark"` on `<html>`). With `darkMapId` the dark Map ID is used in dark mode; otherwise Google's `colorScheme` is switched.
- Markers and shapes use theme tokens (`--primary`, `--chart-1` … `--chart-8`, `--success`, …), so they recolour with `--onu-primary`.
- Map tiles use the active locale. Google has **no Dhivehi map language**, so with `locale="dv"` tiles and Google's own controls fall back to English while Onu's UI stays in Dhivehi and RTL.
- Without a Map ID, Google's `DEMO_MAP_ID` (exported as `DEMO_MAP_ID` from `@javaabu/onu/maps`) is used so advanced markers work. An empty string counts as no Map ID, so an unset environment variable or CI secret also falls back. Set your own Map ID in production; static map images (`LocationCard`) never send `DEMO_MAP_ID`.

:::info No API key?
Without a Google Maps API key the map renders a labelled **schematic preview** (no tiles, no network) instead of crashing. Everything else, including the text alternative, keeps working. See [MapProvider](./map-provider.md).
:::

## Deprecated Google APIs

Onu never uses Google's deprecated Drawing Library or HeatmapLayer. Drawing uses **terra-draw** with its Google Maps adapter; heatmaps and replay trails use **deck.gl** through `GoogleMapsOverlay`.

## Adapter interface

Components only talk to a small `MapAdapter` interface (map, marker, circle, polygon, polyline, drawing, heatmap, trail, clusters, place search and routing). Two adapters ship: `googleMapsAdapter` and the keyless `placeholderAdapter`. A MapLibre adapter can be added later without changing component APIs:

```tsx
<MapProvider adapter={myAdapter}>…</MapProvider>
```

## Verified against Google Maps JS API

The Google adapter was driven end to end in Chromium (Playwright) against the real **Maps JavaScript API 3.66.7** (`weekly` channel, loaded by `@vis.gl/react-google-maps` 1.10), with `DEMO_MAP_ID`, terra-draw 1.37 + terra-draw-google-maps-adapter 1.7, deck.gl 9.4 and `@googlemaps/markerclusterer` 2.6. Every maps showcase demo and the Maps and operations sample pages were checked in light/LTR/English and dark/RTL/Dhivehi:

- the script loads once, every map creates a `google.maps.Map` with tiles, advanced markers, polygons, polylines and circles;
- clicks, marker selection, panning from a list outside the map, `fitBounds` / initial fit, and keeping the camera when the colour scheme switches;
- terra-draw drawing and vertex editing (polygon and route), clustering, and deck.gl heatmap and trail overlays;
- `colorScheme` follows dark mode, and with `dv` Google's labels fall back to English while Onu's UI is Dhivehi and RTL.

Limitations of that run: it had **no API key**, so Google showed its "for development purposes only" watermark and dialog, logged `NoApiKeys` / `InvalidKey` / `ApiProjectMapError`, and drew the map as a raster map. Services that need a key were not verified: geocoding search (`search={true}`) and routed directions (`MapNavigation` fell back to straight lines, as designed). Google also logs that `DirectionsService` is deprecated in favour of `google.maps.routes.Route.computeRoutes` (still supported). `@googlemaps/markerclusterer` 2.6 logs a deprecation warning about `addListener` on its cluster markers.

To repeat the check in the web app without a key, build it with `VITE_GOOGLE_MAPS_FORCE=1 VITE_GOOGLE_MAPS_MAP_ID=DEMO_MAP_ID`. The flag only exists in the web app: it wraps the app in `<MapProvider adapter={googleMapsAdapter}>`. The library itself still uses the placeholder when an app sets no key.

## Props

| Prop          | Type                | Default                             | Description                            |
| ------------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `apiKey`      | `string`            | `OnuProvider maps.googleMapsApiKey` | Google Maps API key                    |
| `mapId`       | `string`            | `OnuProvider maps.mapId`            | Map ID (vector maps, advanced markers) |
| `darkMapId`   | `string`            | `OnuProvider maps.darkMapId`        | Map ID used in dark mode               |
| `colorScheme` | `"light" \| "dark"` | page theme                          | Force a colour scheme                  |
| `region`      | `string`            | `"MV"`                              | Region bias for geocoding              |
| `adapter`     | `MapAdapter`        | Google with a key, else placeholder | The map engine                         |

## Helpers

The maps entry also exports pure helpers: `distanceMeters`, `pathLength`, `polygonArea` (turf), `formatLatLng`, `formatDistance`, `formatArea`, `formatDuration`, `boundsOf`, `googleMapsUrl`, `googleDirectionsUrl`, `staticMapUrl`, GeoJSON converters (`shapesToPolygons`, `polygonsToShapes`, `pathToLineString`), track helpers (`normalizeTrack`, `trackStateAt`) and `MALDIVES_ATOLLS`.

## Accessibility

`MapProvider` renders no UI of its own. What it sets up affects every map inside it:

- **Language.** The adapter gets the active locale; Onu's labels, controls, text alternatives and announcements are always in that locale (Dhivehi included) even though Google draws its tiles in English for `dv`.
- **Colour scheme.** Maps follow the page's dark mode, and markers and shapes use theme tokens, so contrast tuned for the theme carries over to the map.
- **No key.** Without an API key the placeholder adapter still renders a labelled map region with named zoom buttons and markers, and the list or table each Onu map pairs with keeps working.

Keyboard support, marker names and the text alternative belong to [`MapView`](./map-view.md#accessibility) and the components built on it.

---

<!-- docs/maps/map-view.md -->

# MapView

The base map. Put markers, shapes and layers inside it. `MapMarker`, `MapCircleShape`, `MapPolygonShape` and `MapPolylineShape` are the building blocks the other map components use.

```tsx
import { MapView, MapMarker, MapPolygonShape } from "@javaabu/onu/maps"

;<MapView center={{ lat: 4.1755, lng: 73.5093 }} zoom={13} onMapClick={(p) => console.log(p)}>
  <MapMarker position={{ lat: 4.1755, lng: 73.5093 }} title="Malé" onClick={() => select("male")} />
  <MapPolygonShape path={ward} tone="chart-2" />
</MapView>
```

Control the camera with `mapRef`:

```tsx
const mapRef = React.useRef<MapHandle>(null)
mapRef.current?.panTo({ lat: 4.21, lng: 73.54 }, 15)
mapRef.current?.fitBounds(boundsOf(points)!)
```

:::info No API key?
Without a Google Maps API key the map renders a labelled **schematic preview** (no tiles, no network) instead of crashing. Everything else, including the text alternative, keeps working. See [MapProvider](./map-provider.md).
:::

Verified on the real Google Maps JavaScript API (see [MapProvider](./map-provider.md#verified-against-google-maps-js-api)): map instance, advanced markers, polygons, polylines, circles, `mapRef.panTo` / `fitBounds` from buttons outside the map, marker click selection, and light/dark (the camera is kept when the colour scheme switches).

## Props

| Prop                      | Type                                            | Default         | Description                                     |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | --------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `label`                   | `string`                                        | "Map"           | Accessible name of the map region               |
| `center` / `zoom`         | `LatLng` / `number`                             | Malé / `12`     | Initial camera                                  |
| `bounds`                  | `LatLngBounds`                                  |                 | Fit these bounds once, on first render or when they are first set (data loaded later). Wins over `center`/`zoom`; a single point is centred at zoom 15|
| `onMapClick`              | `(p: LatLng) => void`                           |                 | Clicked point                                   |
| `onViewChange`            | `(view: MapViewState) => void`                  |                 | Centre, zoom and bounds after the camera stops  |
| `mapRef`                  | `Ref<MapHandle>`                                |                 | `panTo`, `fitBounds`, `getView`                 |
| `controls`                | `boolean`                                       | `true`          | Zoom / map-type controls                        |
| `gestureHandling`         | `"cooperative" \| "greedy" \| "none" \| "auto"` | `"cooperative"` | Two-finger / Ctrl+scroll so the page scrolls    |
| `overlay`                 | `ReactNode`                                     |                 | Content over the map frame (legend, info panel) |
| `className`, `classNames` | `string`, `{ root, map }`                       |                 | Overrides                                       |

`MapMarker`: `position`, `title` (accessible name), `label` (text in the pin), `tone`, `selected`, `heading` (arrow marker), `draggable`, `onDragEnd`, `onClick`, `zIndex`.
`MapCircleShape`: `center`, `radius` (m), `tone`, `editable`, `onChange`. `MapPolygonShape`: `path`, `tone`, `selected`, `onClick`. `MapPolylineShape`: `path`, `tone`, `dashed`, `width`.

Tones: `primary`, `muted`, `success`, `warning`, `destructive`, `info`, `chart-1` … `chart-8`.

## Accessibility

- The map is a labelled region. Markers with `onClick` (or `draggable`) are focusable buttons named by `title`; other markers are images with that name.
- Maps are not the only way to see data: pair them with a list or table. The higher-level map components do this for you (R14.9).

| Key                                                 | Action                                          |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>                                      | Moves between the map, its markers and controls |
| <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> <kbd>↑</kbd> <kbd>↓</kbd> | Pan the map (when the map has focus)            |
| <kbd>+</kbd> / <kbd>-</kbd>                         | Zoom in / out (when the map has focus)          |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd>                 | Activate a focused marker                       |

## RTL

Map content is geographic, so it is never mirrored. Onu's controls around and over the map (zoom buttons, notices, panels) follow the page direction.

<!-- docs/maps/map-picker.md -->

# MapPicker

Pick a point: click the map, drag the pin, search a place, use the device location, or type the latitude and longitude. Submits `name[lat]` and `name[lng]`.

```tsx
import { MapPicker } from "@javaabu/onu/maps"

;<FormField label="Business location" name="location" required>
  <MapPicker />
</FormField>
```

Controlled:

```tsx
const [value, setValue] = React.useState<LatLng | null>(null)
<MapPicker value={value} onChange={setValue} />
```

## Search

`search` is `true` by default and uses the engine's geocoder (Google Geocoding, biased to the Maldives). Pass your own function to search your API, or `false` to hide the box:

```tsx
<MapPicker search={async (query, { signal }) => (await fetch(`/api/places?q=${query}`, { signal })).json()} thaana />
```

The search box is also available on its own as `PlaceSearchBox`, and its state as the `usePlaceSearchBox({ search, minLength, debounce })` hook (debounced; older requests aborted with `AbortController`).

:::info No API key?
Without a Google Maps API key the map renders a labelled **schematic preview** (no tiles, no network) instead of crashing. Everything else, including the text alternative, keeps working. See [MapProvider](./map-provider.md).
:::

Verified on the real Google Maps JavaScript API (see [MapProvider](./map-provider.md#verified-against-google-maps-js-api)): clicking the map moves the pin and the value, and an empty picker places a pin on click.

## Props

| Prop                                  | Type                                     | Default        | Description                                 |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `value` / `defaultValue` / `onChange` | `LatLng \| null`                         |                | The picked point                            |
| `name`                                | `string`                                 | from FormField | Hidden inputs `name[lat]`, `name[lng]`      |
| `search`                              | `boolean \| PlaceSearch`                 | `true`         | Place search                                |
| `thaana`                              | `boolean \| ThaanaOptions`               |                | Thaana typing in the search box             |
| `locate`                              | `boolean`                                | `true`         | "Use my location" (when geolocation exists) |
| `coordinates`                         | `boolean`                                | `true`         | Latitude / longitude fields                 |
| `clearable`                           | `boolean`                                | not required   | "Clear" button                              |
| `center` / `zoom`                     | `LatLng` / `number`                      | Malé / `11`    | Where the map opens when empty              |
| `disabled`, `required`, `id`, `label` |                                          |                | Wired from `FormField` when inside one      |
| `className`, `classNames`             | `{ root, toolbar, search, map, fields }` |                | Overrides                                   |

Values are rounded to 6 decimals (about 10 cm).

## Accessibility

- The latitude/longitude fields are the keyboard and screen-reader alternative to the map; invalid numbers show an error.
- The search box follows the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern. The picked location is announced ("Location set to …").

| Key                                                 | Action                                          |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| <kbd>↓</kbd> / <kbd>↑</kbd>                         | Move through search results                     |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd>                                    | Choose the highlighted result                   |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd>                                      | Close the results, then clear the search        |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>                                      | Moves between the map, its markers and controls |
| <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> <kbd>↑</kbd> <kbd>↓</kbd> | Pan the map (when the map has focus)            |
| <kbd>+</kbd> / <kbd>-</kbd>                         | Zoom in / out (when the map has focus)          |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd>                 | Activate a focused marker                       |

## RTL and Thaana

Coordinate fields are always `dir="ltr"`. Set `thaana` to type Thaana place names in the search box.

# MapRadius

A centre and a radius in metres: click to place the centre, drag the handles, or type the numbers. Submits `name[lat]`, `name[lng]` and `name[radius]`.

```tsx
import { MapRadius } from "@javaabu/onu/maps"

;<FormField label="Delivery area" name="area">
  <MapRadius min={100} max={5000} step={50} defaultRadius={800} />
</FormField>
```

On Google Maps the handles are the editable `google.maps.Circle` (core Maps API, not the deprecated Drawing Library).

:::info No API key?
Without a Google Maps API key the map renders a labelled **schematic preview** (no tiles, no network) instead of crashing. Everything else, including the text alternative, keeps working. See [MapProvider](./map-provider.md).
:::

Verified on the real Google Maps JavaScript API (see [MapProvider](./map-provider.md#verified-against-google-maps-js-api)): the editable circle renders with drag handles, and clicking an empty map places the centre.

## Props

| Prop                                  | Type                                         | Default               | Description                          |
| ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `value` / `defaultValue` / `onChange` | `{ center: LatLng; radius: number } \| null` |                       | Centre and radius (m)                |
| `name`                                | `string`                                     | from FormField        | Hidden inputs                        |
| `defaultRadius`                       | `number`                                     | `500`                 | Radius when a centre is first placed |
| `min` / `max` / `step`                | `number`                                     | `10` / `50000` / `10` | Radius limits (m)                    |
| `tone`                                | `MapTone`                                    | `"primary"`           | Circle colour                        |
| `center` / `zoom` / `label`           |                                              |                       | Map setup                            |
| `disabled`, `required`, `id`          |                                              |                       | Wired from `FormField`               |
| `className`, `classNames`             | `{ root, map, fields, summary }`             |                       | Overrides                            |

## Accessibility

The radius is a numeric input and the centre has latitude/longitude fields, so everything works without the map. Changes are announced ("Radius 800 m around …"). The summary shows the radius and area.

| Key                                                 | Action                                          |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> / <kbd>↓</kbd> in the radius field     | Change the radius by `step`                     |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>                                      | Moves between the map, its markers and controls |
| <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> <kbd>↑</kbd> <kbd>↓</kbd> | Pan the map (when the map has focus)            |
| <kbd>+</kbd> / <kbd>-</kbd>                         | Zoom in / out (when the map has focus)          |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd>                 | Activate a focused marker                       |

<!-- docs/maps/map-polygon.md -->

# MapPolygon

Draw and edit polygons (zones, plots, service areas). The value is a GeoJSON `FeatureCollection` of `Polygon`s; each area is measured with turf. Drawing on Google Maps uses **terra-draw** with its Google adapter.

```tsx
import { MapPolygon, type PolygonCollection } from "@javaabu/onu/maps"

const [zones, setZones] = React.useState<PolygonCollection | null>(null)
<FormField label="Collection zones" name="zones">
  <MapPolygon value={zones} onChange={setZones} />
</FormField>
```

- **Draw area**: click to add points; click the first point (or press **Done**) to finish.
- **Edit points**: drag points; drag a midpoint to add a point.
- The list beside the map shows each area with its point count and size, and the points of the selected area. Points can be added by typing coordinates, and removed one by one.
- Feature `properties` you set (e.g. a name) are kept when shapes change.

With `name`, the GeoJSON is submitted as a JSON string.

:::info No API key?
Without a Google Maps API key the map renders a labelled **schematic preview** (no tiles, no network) instead of crashing. Everything else, including the text alternative, keeps working. See [MapProvider](./map-provider.md).
:::

Verified on the real Google Maps JavaScript API (see [MapProvider](./map-provider.md#verified-against-google-maps-js-api)): terra-draw draws a polygon by clicking, edit mode drags a vertex and updates the value, the initial value stays listed while terra-draw loads it, shapes survive a tone or colour-scheme change, and Fit to view fits the shapes.

## Props

| Prop                                  | Type                                    | Default        | Description                      |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | -------------- | -------------------------------- |
| `value` / `defaultValue` / `onChange` | `PolygonCollection \| null`             |                | GeoJSON; `null` when empty       |
| `multiple`                            | `boolean`                               | `true`         | Allow several polygons           |
| `name`                                | `string`                                | from FormField | Hidden input with the JSON       |
| `tone`                                | `MapTone`                               | `"primary"`    | Colour                           |
| `center` / `zoom` / `label`           |                                         |                | Map setup (without `center`/`zoom`, fits the shapes) |
| `disabled`, `required`, `id`          |                                         |                | Wired from `FormField`           |
| `className`, `classNames`             | `{ root, toolbar, map, list, summary }` |                | Overrides                        |

## Accessibility

- Every area can be created, reviewed and edited from the list with the keyboard; changes are announced ("Point 3 added").
- Toolbar buttons are toggle buttons (`aria-pressed`).

| Key                                                 | Action                                                    |
| --------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>                                      | Toolbar, map, area list, point list and coordinate fields |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd>                 | Select an area, remove a point, add a point               |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>                                      | Moves between the map, its markers and controls           |
| <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> <kbd>↑</kbd> <kbd>↓</kbd> | Pan the map (when the map has focus)                      |
| <kbd>+</kbd> / <kbd>-</kbd>                         | Zoom in / out (when the map has focus)                    |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd>                 | Activate a focused marker                                 |

<!-- docs/maps/map-route.md -->

# MapRoute

Draw a route as a line (patrol path, ferry line, delivery route). The value is a GeoJSON `LineString` feature and its length is measured with turf.

```tsx
import { MapRoute } from "@javaabu/onu/maps"

;<FormField label="Patrol route" name="route">
  <MapRoute onDistanceChange={(m) => setMeters(m)} />
</FormField>
```

Draw with **Draw route** (double-click the last point or press **Done**), edit with **Edit points**, or type points below the map. Points can be moved up and down in the list.

:::info No API key?
Without a Google Maps API key the map renders a labelled **schematic preview** (no tiles, no network) instead of crashing. Everything else, including the text alternative, keeps working. See [MapProvider](./map-provider.md).
:::

Verified on the real Google Maps JavaScript API (see [MapProvider](./map-provider.md#verified-against-google-maps-js-api)): terra-draw draws a line by clicking and finishing on the last point.

## Props

| Prop                                  | Type                                    | Default        | Description                |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | -------------- | -------------------------- |
| `value` / `defaultValue` / `onChange` | `RouteFeature \| null`                  |                | GeoJSON LineString feature |
| `onDistanceChange`                    | `(meters: number) => void`              |                | Length after each change   |
| `name`                                | `string`                                | from FormField | Hidden input with the JSON |
| `tone`, `center`, `zoom`, `label`     |                                         |                | Appearance and map setup; without `center`/`zoom` the map fits the route |
| `disabled`, `required`, `id`          |                                         |                | Wired from `FormField`     |
| `className`, `classNames`             | `{ root, toolbar, map, list, summary }` |                | Overrides                  |

## Accessibility

Same as [MapPolygon](./map-polygon.md): the point list is a full keyboard alternative, with **Move up / Move down** buttons to reorder points.

| Key                                                 | Action                                          |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd>                 | Move, remove or add a point                     |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>                                      | Moves between the map, its markers and controls |
| <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> <kbd>↑</kbd> <kbd>↓</kbd> | Pan the map (when the map has focus)            |
| <kbd>+</kbd> / <kbd>-</kbd>                         | Zoom in / out (when the map has focus)          |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd>                 | Activate a focused marker                       |
