<!-- docs/maps/live-map.md -->

# LiveMap

Markers that move as positions arrive, from props (polling) or a stream (WebSocket, SSE, Laravel Echo). Markers glide between updates, can be followed, and are listed as a text alternative.

```tsx
import { LiveMap } from "@javaabu/onu/maps"

<LiveMap
  markers={vessels}
  subscribe={(push) => {
    const channel = echo.channel("fleet").listen("PositionUpdated", (e) => push(e.vessel))
    return () => channel.stopListening("PositionUpdated")
  }}
  overlay={<MapInfoPanel open={!!selected} … />}
/>
```

Each marker: `{ id, position, title, heading?, tone?, status?, updatedAt? }`. Updates from `subscribe` merge into `markers` by `id`.

When the selection changes from the built-in list or from outside the map (a controlled `selectedId`, e.g. picking a vessel in your own table), the map pans to centre that marker. It does not turn on follow mode, and a tap on the marker itself does not move the map. Without `center` or `zoom`, the map fits all the markers once (also when they arrive after the first render, e.g. from a stream).

:::info No API key?
Without a Google Maps API key the map renders a labelled **schematic preview** (no tiles, no network) instead of crashing. Everything else, including the text alternative, keeps working. See [MapProvider](./map-provider.md).
:::

Verified on the real Google Maps JavaScript API (see [MapProvider](./map-provider.md#verified-against-google-maps-js-api)): streamed positions move the markers, an outside list pans to the selected marker, a map without a centre fits all markers, and a marker click opens the info panel.

## Props

| Prop                                              | Type                        | Default | Description                                               |
| ------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `markers`                                         | `LiveMapMarker[]`           | `[]`    | Current markers                                           |
| `subscribe`                                       | `(push) => unsubscribe`     |         | Stream of updates                                         |
| `selectedId` / `defaultSelectedId` / `onSelect`   | `string \| null`            |         | Selected marker                                           |
| `followId` / `defaultFollowId` / `onFollowChange` | `string \| null`            |         | Marker the camera follows                                 |
| `animationDuration`                               | `number`                    | `1000`  | Glide time in ms (`0` jumps; reduced motion always jumps) |
| `list`                                            | `boolean`                   | `true`  | Marker list (text alternative)                            |
| `overlay`                                         | `ReactNode`                 |         | Over the map, e.g. `MapInfoPanel`                         |
| `center`, `zoom`, `label`                         |                             |         | Map setup (fits the markers when neither is set)             |
| `className`, `classNames`                         | `{ root, map, list, item }` |         | Overrides                                                 |

## Accessibility

- Markers are buttons named by `title`; the list shows position, heading (as a compass direction) and the last update time.
- Follow buttons are toggles (`aria-pressed`); following is announced. Position updates are not announced, to avoid noise.
- Motion respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.

| Key                                                 | Action                                          |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> on a list item  | Select the marker and move the map to it        |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>                                      | Moves between the map, its markers and controls |
| <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> <kbd>↑</kbd> <kbd>↓</kbd> | Pan the map (when the map has focus)            |
| <kbd>+</kbd> / <kbd>-</kbd>                         | Zoom in / out (when the map has focus)          |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd>                 | Activate a focused marker                       |

---

<!-- docs/maps/map-navigation.md -->

# MapNavigation

Turn-by-turn style directions between stops: the route on the map, a summary, and a step list with Previous / Next.

```tsx
import { MapNavigation } from "@javaabu/onu/maps"

;<MapNavigation
  stops={[
    { label: "Warehouse", position: { lat: 4.1745, lng: 73.5015 } },
    { label: "Hulhumalé", position: { lat: 4.2135, lng: 73.5395 } },
  ]}
/>
```

Routing: with Google Maps the **Directions service** is used. Without one (no key, a sea route, or `routeService={false}`), or if the request fails, the component draws **straight segments** and writes compass directions ("Head north-east from IGMH to Hulhumalé"). Plug in any routing API with `routeService`:

```tsx
<MapNavigation stops={stops} routeService={async (points, { signal }) => myRouter(points, signal)} />
```

:::info No API key?
Without a Google Maps API key the map renders a labelled **schematic preview** (no tiles, no network) instead of crashing. Everything else, including the text alternative, keeps working. See [MapProvider](./map-provider.md).
:::

Verified on the real Google Maps JavaScript API (see [MapProvider](./map-provider.md#verified-against-google-maps-js-api)): markers, the dashed fallback line and the step list; a step click pans. Without an API key Google denies the Directions request and the straight-line fallback with its notice is shown, so routed directions were not verified.

## Props

| Prop                                                      | Type                                  | Default  | Description                           |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `stops`                                                   | `{ label, position, id? }[]`          |          | Two or more stops in order            |
| `routeService`                                            | `RouteService \| false`               | engine's | Routing                               |
| `activeStep` / `defaultActiveStep` / `onActiveStepChange` | `number \| null`                      |          | Highlighted step                      |
| `onRoute`                                                 | `(route: RouteResult) => void`        |          | Computed route                        |
| `externalLink`                                            | `boolean`                             | `true`   | "Open in Google Maps" directions link |
| `tone`, `label`                                           |                                       |          | Appearance                            |
| `className`, `classNames`                                 | `{ root, map, summary, steps, step }` |          | Overrides                             |

## Accessibility

- The step list is the text alternative; the current step has `aria-current="step"` and is announced ("Step 2 of 7: …").
- Stops are labelled markers (A, B, C…).

| Key                                                 | Action                                          |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> on a step       | Go to that step                                 |
| Previous / Next buttons                             | Step through the route                          |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>                                      | Moves between the map, its markers and controls |
| <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> <kbd>↑</kbd> <kbd>↓</kbd> | Pan the map (when the map has focus)            |
| <kbd>+</kbd> / <kbd>-</kbd>                         | Zoom in / out (when the map has focus)          |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd>                 | Activate a focused marker                       |

## RTL

Previous / Next chevrons mirror in RTL.

<!-- docs/maps/location-card.md -->

# LocationCard

A place at a glance: a static map thumbnail, the address, coordinates and an **Open in Google Maps** link.

```tsx
import { LocationCard } from "@javaabu/onu/maps"

;<LocationCard
  position={{ lat: 4.1771, lng: 73.5123 }}
  title="Ministry of Finance"
  address="Ameenee Magu, Malé 20379"
/>
```

The thumbnail is a Google Static Maps image (needs the API key, uses the dark Map ID in dark mode). Without a key, or if the image fails, a styled placeholder is shown instead.

## Props

| Prop                      | Type                                       | Default      | Description                             |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------------ | --------------------------------------- |
| `position`                | `LatLng`                                   |              | The place                               |
| `title`                   | `ReactNode`                                |              | Place name                              |
| `address`                 | `ReactNode`                                |              | Address (rendered in `<address>`)       |
| `placeId`                 | `string`                                   |              | Google place id for the link            |
| `zoom`                    | `number`                                   | `15`         | Thumbnail zoom                          |
| `thumbnail`               | `boolean`                                  | `true`       | Show the map image                      |
| `showCoordinates`         | `boolean`                                  | `true`       | Show coordinates                        |
| `actions`                 | `ReactNode`                                |              | Extra actions                           |
| `layout`                  | `"vertical" \| "horizontal"`               | `"vertical"` | Horizontal from medium container widths |
| `apiKey`                  | `string`                                   | provider     | Static Maps key                         |
| `className`, `classNames` | `{ media, body, title, address, actions }` |              | Overrides                               |

`locationCardVariants` is exported.

## Accessibility

- The thumbnail has alt text ("Map of …"); the placeholder is a labelled image.
- The link says it opens in a new tab (visually hidden text).

<!-- docs/maps/address-input.md -->

# AddressInput

Structured Maldivian address fields: **atoll**, **island**, **road** and **house/building name**, with an optional map pin.

```tsx
import { AddressInput } from "@javaabu/onu/maps"

;<AddressInput name="address" islands={islands} pin required />
```

Submits `address[atoll]`, `address[island]`, `address[road]`, `address[house]` and, with `pin`, `address[location][lat]` / `address[location][lng]`. Laravel errors for `address.atoll` etc. are picked up from `FormErrorsProvider`.

- The atoll list is built in (`MALDIVES_ATOLLS`: the 20 administrative atolls plus Malé City, with codes, Dhivehi names and approximate centres).
- Pass `islands` (`{ value, label, dvLabel?, atoll, position? }[]`, usually from your API) to choose the island from a list filtered by atoll; picking an island sets its atoll. Without it the island is a text field.
- With `pin`, the map follows the chosen island or atoll until a pin is placed.

Verified on the real Google Maps JavaScript API (see [MapProvider](./map-provider.md#verified-against-google-maps-js-api)): clicking the pin map sets `location` and places the pin.

## Props

| Prop                                  | Type                                                                                          | Default   | Description                                       |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `value` / `defaultValue` / `onChange` | `MaldivesAddress`                                                                             | `{}`      | `{ atoll?, island?, road?, house?, location? }`   |
| `name`                                | `string`                                                                                      |           | Field name prefix                                 |
| `islands`                             | `AddressIsland[]`                                                                             |           | Island options                                    |
| `pin`                                 | `boolean`                                                                                     | `false`   | Map pin picker                                    |
| `search`                              | `boolean \| PlaceSearch`                                                                      | `false`   | Place search for the pin                          |
| `thaana`                              | `boolean \| ThaanaOptions`                                                                    |           | Thaana typing in road, house and free-text island |
| `required`, `disabled`                | `boolean`                                                                                     |           | Atoll and island required; disables the fieldset  |
| `errors`                              | `Partial<Record<"atoll" \| "island" \| "road" \| "house" \| "location", string \| string[]>>` |           | Errors per part                                   |
| `legend`                              | `ReactNode \| null`                                                                           | "Address" | Group heading (`null` hides it visually)          |
| `labelLayout`                         | `"stacked" \| "inline"`                                                                       |           | Label layout for the fields                       |
| `className`, `classNames`             | `{ legend, grid, field, map }`                                                                |           | Overrides                                         |

## Accessibility

A `fieldset` with a `legend`; every field is a labelled `FormField` with error wiring. Selects are native, so they work with every keyboard and screen reader and open the platform picker on phones.

## RTL and Thaana

Atoll and island labels follow the locale (e.g. "ކ. މާލޭ އަތޮޅު"). Set `thaana` to type road and house names in Thaana.

---

<!-- docs/maps/map-replay.md -->

# MapReplay

Plays back a timestamped track (a vessel trip, a delivery run): play/pause, speed and a scrubber. On Google Maps the travelled trail is drawn with deck.gl's `PathLayer` through `GoogleMapsOverlay`.

```tsx
import { MapReplay } from "@javaabu/onu/maps"

;<MapReplay track={points} title="Ferry Raajje" />
```

`track` is either `{ lat, lng, time }[]` (epoch ms) or a GeoJSON `LineString` feature with `properties.timestamps` (ms or ISO strings):

```json
{ "type": "Feature", "properties": { "timestamps": ["2026-03-12T04:30:00Z", "…"] }, "geometry": { "type": "LineString", "coordinates": [[73.51, 4.17], …] } }
```

:::info No API key?
Without a Google Maps API key the map renders a labelled **schematic preview** (no tiles, no network) instead of crashing. Everything else, including the text alternative, keeps working. See [MapProvider](./map-provider.md).
:::

Verified on the real Google Maps JavaScript API (see [MapProvider](./map-provider.md#verified-against-google-maps-js-api)): the deck.gl trail attaches through `GoogleMapsOverlay`, and playback moves the marker.

## Props

| Prop                                             | Type                                         | Default            | Description                           |
| ------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------- |
| `track`                                          | `TrackPoint[] \| TrackFeature`               |                    | The track                             |
| `time` / `defaultTime` / `onTimeChange`          | `number`                                     | start              | Playback time (epoch ms)              |
| `playing` / `defaultPlaying` / `onPlayingChange` | `boolean`                                    | `false`            | Playing state                         |
| `speeds`                                         | `number[]`                                   | `[1, 10, 60, 300]` | Speed options                         |
| `defaultSpeed`                                   | `number`                                     | `60`               | Starting speed                        |
| `follow`                                         | `boolean`                                    | `true`             | Keep the marker in view while playing |
| `title`, `tone`, `label`                         |                                              |                    | Tracked object name and appearance    |
| `className`, `classNames`                        | `{ root, map, controls, scrubber, details }` |                    | Overrides                             |

## Accessibility

- The scrubber is a slider with `aria-valuetext` giving the clock time and elapsed / total duration.
- The current time, position and a track summary (points, distance, duration) are shown as text.

| Key                                         | Action                             |
| ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| <kbd>Space</kbd> / <kbd>Enter</kbd> on Play | Play / pause (at the end, restart) |
| <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> on the scrubber   | One second back / forward          |
| <kbd>Page Up</kbd> / <kbd>Page Down</kbd>   | Larger steps                       |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> / <kbd>End</kbd>            | Start / end of the track           |

## RTL

The scrubber runs right-to-left in RTL, and arrow keys follow it.

---

<!-- docs/maps/map-info-panel.md -->

# MapInfoPanel

Details of the selected marker: a side panel over the map on desktop and a bottom sheet on phones. Put it in a map's `overlay`.

```tsx
import { MapInfoPanel, MapView, MapMarker } from "@javaabu/onu/maps"

;<MapView
  overlay={
    <MapInfoPanel
      open={!!place}
      onOpenChange={(o) => !o && setPlace(null)}
      title={place?.name}
      actions={<Button>Directions</Button>}
    >
      <dl>…</dl>
    </MapInfoPanel>
  }
>
  {places.map((p) => (
    <MapMarker key={p.id} position={p.position} title={p.name} onClick={() => setPlace(p)} />
  ))}
</MapView>
```

The bottom sheet is shadcn's `Drawer` (drag down to dismiss).

Verified on the real Google Maps JavaScript API (see [MapProvider](./map-provider.md#verified-against-google-maps-js-api)): the panel opens over a Google map when a marker is clicked.

## Props

| Prop                      | Type                              | Default  | Description                       |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------- |
| `open` / `onOpenChange`   | `boolean`                         |          | Visibility                        |
| `title`                   | `ReactNode`                       |          | Heading                           |
| `description`             | `ReactNode`                       |          | Subtitle                          |
| `children`                | `ReactNode`                       |          | Details                           |
| `actions`                 | `ReactNode`                       |          | Footer buttons                    |
| `variant`                 | `"auto" \| "side" \| "sheet"`     | `"auto"` | Side on desktop, sheet below `md` |
| `className`, `classNames` | `{ header, title, body, footer }` |          | Overrides                         |

## Accessibility

- The side panel is a labelled `complementary` region. Focus moves to its heading when it opens and returns to what opened it (e.g. the marker) when it closes.
- The sheet is a dialog with focus trapping and restore.

| Key            | Action                                       |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Close                                        |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Move through the panel's content and actions |

## RTL

The side panel sits at the inline end (left in RTL).

<!-- docs/maps/route-stop-editor.md -->

# RouteStopEditor

An ordered list of stops synced with numbered markers. Add stops by clicking the map or with coordinates, rename them, drag to reorder (`@dnd-kit/react`, touch-friendly), or use the arrow buttons, and remove them.

```tsx
import { RouteStopEditor, type RouteStop } from "@javaabu/onu/maps"

const [stops, setStops] = React.useState<RouteStop[]>([])
<FormField label="Shuttle stops">
  <RouteStopEditor value={stops} onChange={setStops} name="stops" max={8} />
</FormField>
```

Each stop: `{ id, label, position: LatLng | null }`. Submits `stops[0][label]`, `stops[0][lat]`, `stops[0][lng]`, … in order. The total straight-line distance is shown.

:::info No API key?
Without a Google Maps API key the map renders a labelled **schematic preview** (no tiles, no network) instead of crashing. Everything else, including the text alternative, keeps working. See [MapProvider](./map-provider.md).
:::

Verified on the real Google Maps JavaScript API (see [MapProvider](./map-provider.md#verified-against-google-maps-js-api)): clicking the map adds a stop, and the stops and path render.

## Props

| Prop                                          | Type                                | Default | Description                  |
| --------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------- |
| `value` / `defaultValue` / `onChange`         | `RouteStop[]`                       | `[]`    | Stops in order               |
| `name`                                        | `string`                            |         | Hidden inputs                |
| `max`                                         | `number`                            |         | Maximum stops                |
| `addOnMapClick`                               | `boolean`                           | `true`  | Clicking the map adds a stop |
| `showPath`                                    | `boolean`                           | `true`  | Connect stops with a line    |
| `thaana`                                      | `boolean \| ThaanaOptions`          |         | Thaana typing in stop names  |
| `disabled`, `tone`, `center`, `zoom`, `label` |                                     |         | Without `center`/`zoom`, fits the stops |
| `className`, `classNames`                     | `{ root, map, list, item, footer }` |         | Overrides                    |

## Accessibility

- Every action has a button: move up/down, remove, edit coordinates. Reordering is announced ("Airport moved to position 2 of 4").
- The drag handle also works with the keyboard (dnd-kit: <kbd>Space</kbd> to pick up, arrows to move, <kbd>Space</kbd> to drop).

| Key                                                 | Action                                          |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| <kbd>Space</kbd> on a drag handle                   | Pick up / drop                                  |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> / <kbd>↓</kbd> while dragging          | Move the stop                                   |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd> while dragging                       | Cancel                                          |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>                                      | Moves between the map, its markers and controls |
| <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> <kbd>↑</kbd> <kbd>↓</kbd> | Pan the map (when the map has focus)            |
| <kbd>+</kbd> / <kbd>-</kbd>                         | Zoom in / out (when the map has focus)          |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd>                 | Activate a focused marker                       |

:::warning
dnd-kit's own drag announcements are in English. The editor announces the result of each move in the active locale.
:::

<!-- docs/maps/heatmap-layer.md -->

# HeatmapLayer

A density heatmap inside a `MapView`. On Google Maps it is deck.gl's `HeatmapLayer` through `GoogleMapsOverlay` (Google's own HeatmapLayer is deprecated and never used). Colours come from theme tokens.

```tsx
import { HeatmapLayer, MapView, MapLegend, HEATMAP_TONES, toneVar } from "@javaabu/onu/maps"

;<MapView
  overlay={<MapLegend items={[{ label: "Low → high", shape: "gradient", colors: HEATMAP_TONES.map(toneVar) }]} />}
>
  <HeatmapLayer points={incidents.map((i) => ({ position: i.position, weight: i.severity }))} />
</MapView>
```

:::info No API key?
Without a Google Maps API key the map renders a labelled **schematic preview** (no tiles, no network) instead of crashing. Everything else, including the text alternative, keeps working. See [MapProvider](./map-provider.md).
:::

Verified on the real Google Maps JavaScript API (see [MapProvider](./map-provider.md#verified-against-google-maps-js-api)): the deck.gl `HeatmapLayer` attaches through `GoogleMapsOverlay` and renders over the tiles.

## Props

| Prop        | Type                                      | Default              | Description                    |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `points`    | `{ position: LatLng; weight?: number }[]` |                      | Data                           |
| `radius`    | `number`                                  | `30`                 | Pixels each point spreads over |
| `intensity` | `number`                                  | `1`                  | Weight multiplier              |
| `opacity`   | `number`                                  | `0.8`                | Layer opacity                  |
| `colors`    | `(MapTone \| "#rrggbb")[]`                | `HEATMAP_TONES`      | Colour ramp, low to high       |
| `summary`   | `string \| null`                          | count + total weight | Visually hidden summary        |

## Accessibility

The layer adds a visually hidden summary ("Heatmap of 215 points, total weight 640"). A heatmap is still visual: give users a table or list of the underlying data as well (R14.9), and a legend with text.

<!-- docs/maps/viewport-marker-map.md -->

# ViewportMarkerMap

Loads markers for the visible area through your fetcher and clusters them (`@googlemaps/markerclusterer`). Requests are debounced after the map stops moving, and older requests are cancelled with `AbortController`, so a slow response never replaces a newer one.

```tsx
import { ViewportMarkerMap } from "@javaabu/onu/maps"

;<ViewportMarkerMap
  minZoom={9}
  fetcher={async (b, { zoom, signal }) => {
    const res = await fetch(
      `/api/places?north=${b.north}&south=${b.south}&east=${b.east}&west=${b.west}&zoom=${zoom}`,
      { signal },
    )
    return (await res.json()).data
  }}
/>
```

Each marker: `{ id, position, title, tone?, description? }`. Onu never makes requests itself (R16.6): the fetcher is yours.

:::info No API key?
Without a Google Maps API key the map renders a labelled **schematic preview** (no tiles, no network) instead of crashing. Everything else, including the text alternative, keeps working. See [MapProvider](./map-provider.md).
:::

Verified on the real Google Maps JavaScript API (see [MapProvider](./map-provider.md#verified-against-google-maps-js-api)): markers load for the visible area, `@googlemaps/markerclusterer` clusters them, and a cluster click zooms in.

## Props

| Prop                                            | Type                                         | Default | Description                                        |
| ----------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `fetcher`                                       | `(bounds, { zoom, signal }) => Promise<M[]>` |         | Loads markers                                      |
| `debounce`                                      | `number`                                     | `300`   | ms after the map stops                             |
| `cluster`                                       | `boolean`                                    | `true`  | Cluster markers                                    |
| `minZoom`                                       | `number`                                     |         | Below this nothing loads ("Zoom in to see places") |
| `selectedId` / `defaultSelectedId` / `onSelect` |                                              |         | Selection; `onSelect(id, marker)`                  |
| `onLoad`                                        | `(markers, bounds) => void`                  |         | After each load                                    |
| `list`                                          | `boolean`                                    | `true`  | List of loaded markers                             |
| `overlay`                                       | `ReactNode`                                  |         | E.g. `MapInfoPanel`                                |
| `center`, `zoom`, `bounds`, `label`             |                                              |         | Map setup                                          |
| `className`, `classNames`                       | `{ root, map, status, list, item }`          |         | Overrides                                          |

## Accessibility

- Loading, empty, error (with **Retry**) and "N places in view" states are announced in a polite live region.
- The list of loaded markers is the text alternative; selecting from it moves the map.

| Key                                                 | Action                                          |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> on a list item  | Select the place and move the map to it         |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>                                      | Moves between the map, its markers and controls |
| <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> <kbd>↑</kbd> <kbd>↓</kbd> | Pan the map (when the map has focus)            |
| <kbd>+</kbd> / <kbd>-</kbd>                         | Zoom in / out (when the map has focus)          |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd>                 | Activate a focused marker                       |

---

<!-- docs/maps/map-legend-swatch.md -->

# MapLegendSwatch

Colour and shape samples that match how layers are drawn, and `MapLegend`, a labelled list of them.

```tsx
import { MapLegend, MapLegendSwatch } from "@javaabu/onu/maps"

<MapLegend
  items={[
    { label: "Under way", tone: "success", shape: "pin", description: "12" },
    { label: "Ferry line", tone: "chart-3", shape: "dashed" },
  ]}
/>

<MapLegendSwatch shape="area" tone="chart-2" />
```

Shapes: `circle`, `square`, `pin`, `area`, `line`, `dashed`, `gradient` (with `colors`).

## Props

`MapLegendSwatch`:

| Prop     | Type                   | Default     | Description                                     |
| -------- | ---------------------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `tone`   | `MapTone`              | `"primary"` | Theme colour                                    |
| `shape`  | `MapLegendShape`       | `"circle"`  | Sample shape                                    |
| `colors` | `string[]`             |             | Gradient stops (CSS colours or `toneVar(tone)`) |
| `size`   | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"`      | Size (`mapLegendSwatchVariants`)                |

`MapLegend`:

| Prop          | Type                                                | Default      | Description                  |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | ---------------------------- |
| `items`       | `{ label, tone?, shape?, colors?, description? }[]` |              | Entries                      |
| `title`       | `ReactNode \| null`                                 | "Legend"     | Heading; `null` hides it     |
| `orientation` | `"vertical" \| "horizontal"`                        | `"vertical"` | Layout (`mapLegendVariants`) |
| `size`        | swatch size                                         | `"sm"`       |                              |
| `classNames`  | `{ title, list, item, swatch }`                     |              | Overrides                    |

## Accessibility

Swatches are decorative (`aria-hidden`); every entry has a text label, so colour is never the only cue (R14.6). The list is labelled by its title.
