<!-- docs/charts/bar-chart.md -->

# BarChart

A bar graph built on shadcn's [chart](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/chart) (`ChartContainer` + Recharts). Columns or horizontal bars, grouped or stacked, with a "View as table" toggle, keyboard navigation, locale-aware numbers and axes that mirror in RTL.

:::info
Charts live in the `@javaabu/onu/charts` entry and need the optional peer dependency `recharts` (v3): `pnpm add recharts`.
:::

```tsx
import { BarChart, type ChartConfig } from "@javaabu/onu/charts"

const config = {
  revenue: { label: "Revenue" },
  expenses: { label: "Expenses" },
} satisfies ChartConfig

;<BarChart
  title="Council revenue and expenses"
  description="In Maldivian Rufiyaa"
  data={[
    { island: "Malé", revenue: 4820000, expenses: 3110000 },
    { island: "Addu City", revenue: 1450000, expenses: 1220000 },
  ]}
  categoryKey="island"
  config={config}
  valueFormat="currency"
/>
```

`config` is shadcn's `ChartConfig`: one entry per data key with a `label` and an optional `color` (or `theme: { light, dark }`). Colours default to the `--chart-1` … `--chart-8` tokens, so charts follow the theme and dark mode.

## Variants

```tsx
<BarChart orientation="horizontal" … />   // categories down the side
<BarChart stacked … />                    // series stacked instead of grouped
<BarChart series={["revenue"]} … />       // draw only some keys of config
```

## Number formats

`valueFormat` sets how values appear in ticks, tooltips, the table and the screen-reader summary. Numbers always use `useOnu().locale.numberLocale`.

| Value                       | Example                                |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `"number"` (default)        | `12,345.6` (ticks are compact: `12K`)  |
| `"integer"`                 | `12,346`                               |
| `"compact"`                 | `12.3K`                                |
| `"percent"`                 | `0.256` → `25.6%`                      |
| `"currency"`                | `MVR 1,250.00` (`ރ. 1,250.00` in `dv`) |
| `Intl.NumberFormatOptions`  | any options                            |
| `(value: number) => string` | any function                           |

The helpers `formatMVR(value, numberLocale?)`, `formatValue`, `computeDelta` and the hook `useChartFormat(format)` are exported too.

## Props

| Prop                   | Type                                                         | Default              | Description                                           |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `title`                | `ReactNode`                                                  | required             | Accessible name, shown above the chart                |
| `description`          | `ReactNode`                                                  |                      | Shown under the title, linked with `aria-describedby` |
| `hideTitle`            | `boolean`                                                    | `false`              | Visually hide the title (kept for screen readers)     |
| `data`                 | `Record<string, unknown>[]`                                  | required             | One object per category                               |
| `categoryKey`          | `string`                                                     | required             | Key of the category                                   |
| `config`               | `ChartConfig`                                                |                      | Labels and colours per series                         |
| `series`               | `string[]`                                                   | keys of `config`     | Series to draw                                        |
| `orientation`          | `"vertical" \| "horizontal"`                                 | `"vertical"`         | Columns or bars                                       |
| `stacked`              | `boolean`                                                    | `false`              | Stack series                                          |
| `radius`               | `number`                                                     | `4` (`0` stacked)    | Bar corner radius                                     |
| `gradient`             | `boolean`                                                    | `true`               | Gradient fills; `false` for flat bars                 |
| `valueFormat`          | `ValueFormat`                                                | `"number"`           | See above                                             |
| `categoryFormat`       | `(value) => string`                                          |                      | Formats categories                                    |
| `categoryLabel`        | `ReactNode`                                                  | "Category"           | Table column header for categories                    |
| `showLegend`           | `boolean`                                                    | more than one series | Legend                                                |
| `showGrid`             | `boolean`                                                    | `true`               | Grid lines                                            |
| `height`               | `number`                                                     | `300`                | Height in px; width follows the container             |
| `view` / `defaultView` | `"chart" \| "table"`                                         | `"chart"`            | Controlled / initial view                             |
| `onViewChange`         | `(view) => void`                                             |                      | Called when the toggle is used                        |
| `showTableToggle`      | `boolean`                                                    | `true`               | Show the "View as table" button                       |
| `loading`              | `boolean`                                                    | `false`              | Skeleton instead of the chart                         |
| `emptyMessage`         | `ReactNode`                                                  | "No data to show"    | Shown without data                                    |
| `summary`              | `string`                                                     | generated            | Replace the screen-reader summary                     |
| `animate`              | `boolean`                                                    | `true`               | Off under reduced motion or `ChartAnimationProvider`  |
| `actions`              | `ReactNode`                                                  |                      | Extra header controls                                 |
| `className`            | `string`                                                     |                      | Classes for the `<figure>`                            |
| `classNames`           | `{ root, header, title, description, toggle, chart, table }` |                      | Classes per part                                      |

`ref` points at the `<figure>`. Every Onu chart (`LineChart`, `PieChart`, `TimeSeriesChart`, `PeriodComparisonChart`, `MapChart`) shares the props from `title` to `classNames` that are not specific to bars.

## Gradient fills

Bars are filled with a subtle gradient in the series colour: the full colour at the value end, fading to about 70% at the base (80% for stacked segments, so stacks do not look striped). Negative bars are mirrored, and horizontal bars run towards the inline end, so the gradient flips with the axis in RTL. Pass `gradient={false}` for flat bars:

```tsx
<BarChart gradient={false} … />
```

Every Onu chart with areas or bars takes the same `gradient` prop (`LineChart` and `TimeSeriesChart` areas and bars, `PeriodComparisonChart`, `Sparkline`, and `sparklineGradient` on `StatTile`). To change the default for a whole area, wrap it in `ChartStyleProvider`; a chart's own `gradient` prop still wins:

```tsx
import { ChartStyleProvider } from "@javaabu/onu/charts"

<ChartStyleProvider gradient={false}>
  <PrintableReport />
</ChartStyleProvider>
```

Gradients are SVG `<linearGradient>`s with ids unique to each chart instance (`React.useId`), so many charts can share a page. Their stops use the series colour (`var(--color-<key>)`, set by `ChartContainer` from `config` or `--chart-1…8`), so they follow the theme, dark mode and `--onu-primary`. In forced-colours (high contrast) mode every fill falls back to solid. Lines, legends, tooltip swatches, the data table and accessible names are unchanged. Pie and donut slices stay solid: adjacent slices need clear, even colours to stay distinguishable and to match the legend.

`useChartGradient(gradient?)` returns the combined setting for custom charts. The chart container carries `data-fill="gradient"` or `data-fill="solid"` for styling.

## Animation

Charts animate on mount unless `animate={false}`. Animation is always off when the user prefers reduced motion (`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, R14.8): every Onu chart then passes `isAnimationActive={false}` to its Recharts series and tooltip. To turn it off for a whole area, for example print views, kiosks or screenshot tests, wrap it in `ChartAnimationProvider`:

```tsx
import { ChartAnimationProvider } from "@javaabu/onu/charts"

<ChartAnimationProvider animate={false}>
  <Dashboard />
</ChartAnimationProvider>
```

Reduced motion still wins inside `<ChartAnimationProvider animate>`. `useChartAnimation(animate?)` returns the combined result for custom charts built on the primitives below. The visual regression tests emulate reduced motion (Playwright `reducedMotion: "reduce"`), so chart screenshots are stable.

## Primitives

The shadcn primitives are exported from the same entry for custom charts: `ChartContainer`, `ChartTooltip`, `ChartTooltipContent` (with an Onu `valueFormatter` prop), `ChartLegend`, `ChartLegendContent`, `ChartStyle` and the `ChartConfig` type. They are not exported from the package root, so `recharts` stays optional.

## RTL

In RTL the category axis is reversed (the last category sits on the left) and the value axis moves to the start (right) side. Legends follow the text direction. Arrow-key navigation follows the visual order.

## Accessibility

- The chart is a `<figure>` named by its title. The SVG has `role="application"`, is focusable, is labelled by the title and described by a generated summary (series count, data points, lowest and highest value per series).
- **View as table** swaps the chart for a real `<table>` with column and row headers, in a focusable scroll region.
- Tooltips open on hover and keyboard focus, and on tap on touch screens.
- Series are told apart by legend labels and the table, not colour alone.

| Key                                          | Action                                           |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>                               | Focus the chart, then the table toggle           |
| <kbd>ArrowLeft</kbd> / <kbd>ArrowRight</kbd> | Move between categories and show their tooltip   |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd>                             | Show or hide the tooltip for the active category |

---

<!-- docs/charts/line-chart.md -->

# LineChart

A line graph on shadcn's chart (Recharts). Multiple series, optional filled (and stacked) areas, dashed series for targets or forecasts, and gaps where values are missing.

```tsx
import { LineChart } from "@javaabu/onu/charts"

;<LineChart
  title="Tourist arrivals against target"
  data={[
    { month: "Jan", arrivals: 212400, target: 200000 },
    { month: "Feb", arrivals: 208900, target: 205000 },
    { month: "Mar", arrivals: 196300, target: 205000 },
  ]}
  categoryKey="month"
  config={{ arrivals: { label: "Arrivals" }, target: { label: "Target" } }}
  dashedSeries={["target"]}
  valueFormat="compact"
/>
```

## Areas and gaps

```tsx
<LineChart area … />                  // fill under each line
<LineChart area stacked … />          // stacked areas
<LineChart connectNulls … />          // draw across null values instead of a gap
```

A `null` (or missing) value leaves a break in the line and shows as "No data" in the table.

## Gradient fills

Areas fade from the series colour (about 50% opacity under the line) to almost clear at the baseline; areas below zero fade towards the zero line from below. Stacked bands fade less (60% to 20%) so each band stays readable where it meets the next. Lines stay solid. Pass `gradient={false}` for the flat fills, or wrap charts in `<ChartStyleProvider gradient={false}>`; see [BarChart](./bar-chart.md#gradient-fills). Forced-colours mode always draws flat fills.

## Props

Shares the common chart props (`title`, `description`, `data`, `categoryKey`, `config`, `series`, `valueFormat`, `categoryFormat`, `categoryLabel`, `showLegend`, `showGrid`, `height`, `view`, `defaultView`, `onViewChange`, `showTableToggle`, `loading`, `emptyMessage`, `summary`, `animate`, `actions`, `className`, `classNames`); see [BarChart](./bar-chart.md).

| Prop           | Type                                            | Default         | Description                                       |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `area`         | `boolean`                                       | `false`         | Fill the area under each line                     |
| `stacked`      | `boolean`                                       | `false`         | Stack areas (with `area`)                         |
| `curve`        | `"monotone" \| "linear" \| "step" \| "natural"` | `"monotone"`    | Interpolation                                     |
| `dots`         | `boolean`                                       | up to 31 points | Dot on each point                                 |
| `connectNulls` | `boolean`                                       | `false`         | Bridge missing values                             |
| `dashedSeries` | `string[]`                                      |                 | Series drawn dashed (differs by more than colour) |
| `gradient`     | `boolean`                                       | `true`          | Gradient area fills (with `area`)                 |

## RTL

The category axis is reversed in RTL (newest on the left) and the value axis sits on the right. Legends follow the text direction.

## Accessibility

Same as [BarChart](./bar-chart.md#accessibility): a named `<figure>`, a focusable SVG described by a summary, a "View as table" toggle, tooltips on focus and tap, and reduced motion respected.

| Key                                          | Action                                   |
| -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| <kbd>ArrowLeft</kbd> / <kbd>ArrowRight</kbd> | Move between points and show the tooltip |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd>                             | Show or hide the tooltip                 |

---

<!-- docs/charts/pie-chart.md -->

# PieChart

A pie or donut chart on shadcn's chart (Recharts). The donut shows the total (or your own label) in the middle; the table lists each slice's value and share.

```tsx
import { PieChart } from "@javaabu/onu/charts"

;<PieChart
  title="Applications by channel"
  variant="donut"
  data={[
    { name: "eFaas portal", value: 6420 },
    { name: "Island council", value: 2190 },
    { name: "Walk-in", value: 1340 },
  ]}
/>
```

## Centre label

```tsx
<PieChart variant="donut" centerLabel={{ value: "MVR 4.2M", label: "Budget" }} … />
<PieChart variant="donut" centerLabel={null} … />   // no centre label
```

## Gradient fills

Pie and donut slices stay solid, also when other charts use gradient fills: adjacent slices need even, clearly different colours to stay distinguishable and to match the legend.

## Props

Also takes the common chart props (`title`, `description`, `valueFormat`, `height`, `view`, `defaultView`, `onViewChange`, `showTableToggle`, `loading`, `emptyMessage`, `summary`, `animate`, `actions`, `className`, `classNames`); see [BarChart](./bar-chart.md).

| Prop          | Type                        | Default        | Description                             |
| ------------- | --------------------------- | -------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `data`        | `Record<string, unknown>[]` | required       | One object per slice                    |
| `nameKey`     | `string`                    | `"name"`       | Slice name key                          |
| `valueKey`    | `string`                    | `"value"`      | Slice value key                         |
| `config`      | `ChartConfig`               |                | Labels/colours keyed by slice name      |
| `variant`     | `"pie" \| "donut"`          | `"pie"`        | Donut leaves a hole with a centre label |
| `centerLabel` | `{ value, label? } \| null` | total, "Total" | Donut centre content                    |
| `showLegend`  | `boolean`                   | `true`         | Legend                                  |
| `nameLabel`   | `ReactNode`                 | "Category"     | Table header for slice names            |

`pieSlices(data, nameKey, valueKey, config)` returns the computed slices (share, colour) if you need them elsewhere.

## RTL

Slices start at 12 o'clock and run clockwise in LTR, counter-clockwise in RTL. The legend follows the text direction.

## Accessibility

- The summary names the chart type, number of slices, total and the largest slice with its share.
- **View as table** lists value and share per slice.
- Slices are named in the legend and the tooltip, so colour is not the only cue.

| Key                                          | Action                           |
| -------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>                               | Focus the chart, then the toggle |
| <kbd>ArrowLeft</kbd> / <kbd>ArrowRight</kbd> | Move between slices              |

---

<!-- docs/charts/time-series-chart.md -->

# TimeSeriesChart

A line, area or bar chart on a real time axis, optionally stacked. Dates are formatted with the active locale (Dhivehi month names in `dv`), missing steps can be filled in as gaps, and a brush lets people zoom into a range.

```tsx
import { TimeSeriesChart } from "@javaabu/onu/charts"

;<TimeSeriesChart
  title="Velana International Airport, daily passengers"
  data={[
    { date: "2026-09-01", arrivals: 5120, departures: 4980 },
    { date: "2026-09-02", arrivals: 5310, departures: 5040 },
    { date: "2026-09-04", arrivals: 6010, departures: 5770 },
  ]}
  config={{ arrivals: { label: "Arrivals" }, departures: { label: "Departures" } }}
  interval="day"
  brush
/>
```

Rows may come in any order; they are sorted oldest first. Dates can be `Date` objects, ISO strings or timestamps. Rows with an invalid date are dropped.

## Gaps

`null` values break the line. With `interval` (`"hour" | "day" | "week" | "month"`), missing steps are inserted too (3 September above), so a missing day is a visible gap rather than a straight line across it. `connectNulls` bridges gaps instead.

## Stacked areas and bars

`stacked` adds the series up, so the top edge is the total: use `variant="area"` for stacked areas or `variant="bar"` for stacked bars (a stacked `"line"` chart is drawn as stacked areas). Bars are centred on their date, and the axis is padded by half a step so the first and last bars are whole. The data table and summary still list each series on its own, and the time axis is mirrored in RTL as usual.

```tsx
<TimeSeriesChart
  title="Tourist arrivals by stay type"
  variant="bar"
  stacked
  data={rows}
  config={{ resorts: { label: "Resorts" }, guesthouses: { label: "Guesthouses" } }}
  interval="month"
/>
```

## Gradient fills

Areas fade from the series colour to almost clear at the baseline (stacked bands fade less), and bars run from a lighter base to the full colour at the top. Plain lines have no fill. Pass `gradient={false}` for flat fills, or set it for an area with `ChartStyleProvider`; see [BarChart](./bar-chart.md#gradient-fills).

## Zoom

`brush` adds a range slider under the chart. Drag the handles, or focus one and use the arrow keys. While zoomed, a **Reset zoom** button appears and "Showing 2 Sep 2026 to 4 Sep 2026" is announced in a polite live region.

## Props

Also takes the common chart props (`title`, `description`, `config`, `series`, `valueFormat`, `showLegend`, `showGrid`, `height`, `view`, `defaultView`, `onViewChange`, `showTableToggle`, `loading`, `emptyMessage`, `summary`, `animate`, `actions`, `className`, `classNames`); see [BarChart](./bar-chart.md).

| Prop                | Type                                   | Default     | Description                             |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `data`              | `Record<string, unknown>[]`            | required    | One object per point in time            |
| `dateKey`           | `string`                               | `"date"`    | Key of the date                         |
| `interval`          | `"hour" \| "day" \| "week" \| "month"` |             | Fill missing steps with gaps            |
| `dateFormat`        | `string` (date-fns)                    | by interval | Tick format (`d MMM`, `MMM yyyy`, time) |
| `tooltipDateFormat` | `string` (date-fns)                    | by interval | Tooltip and table format                |
| `variant`           | `"line" \| "area" \| "bar"`            | `"line"`    | How series are drawn                    |
| `area`              | `boolean`                              | `false`     | Filled areas (same as `variant="area"`) |
| `stacked`           | `boolean`                              | `false`     | Stack the series (areas or bars)        |
| `brush`             | `boolean`                              | `false`     | Brush to zoom                           |
| `connectNulls`      | `boolean`                              | `false`     | Bridge gaps                             |
| `gradient`          | `boolean`                              | `true`      | Gradient area and bar fills             |

Hourly data uses the locale's `hourCycle`. `normalizeTimeSeries(data, dateKey, interval)` and `toTimestamp(value)` are exported.

## RTL

Time runs right to left in RTL: the newest date is on the left, the value axis is on the right and the brush is mirrored to match. The data table always lists dates oldest first.

## Accessibility

- The summary includes the date range ("From 1 Sep 2026 to 30 Sep 2026.") and each series' lowest and highest value.
- The table lists every date, with "No data" for gaps.

| Key                                          | Action                                                                |
| -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| <kbd>ArrowLeft</kbd> / <kbd>ArrowRight</kbd> | On the chart: move between points. On a brush handle: move the handle |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd>                             | Show or hide the tooltip                                              |

---

<!-- docs/charts/period-comparison-chart.md -->

# PeriodComparisonChart

Compares the current period with the previous one: headline totals with a delta percentage and an up/down indicator, the two periods overlaid (previous dashed, or as muted bars), and a table with the change per step.

```tsx
import { PeriodComparisonChart } from "@javaabu/onu/charts"

;<PeriodComparisonChart
  title="Applications this week"
  data={[
    { day: "Sun", current: 412, previous: 380 },
    { day: "Mon", current: 538, previous: 471 },
    { day: "Tue", current: 497, previous: 502 },
  ]}
  categoryKey="day"
  currentLabel="This week"
  previousLabel="Last week"
/>
```

## Lower is better

For costs, wait times or complaints, set `positiveIsGood={false}` so a fall is shown as good (green) and a rise as bad.

```tsx
<PeriodComparisonChart variant="bar" valueFormat="currency" positiveIsGood={false} … />
```

## Gradient fills

With the default `gradient`, the line variant washes the area under the current period's line with a soft gradient (it is not a separate series: no legend entry or tooltip row), and the bar variant fills bars from a lighter base to the full colour. `gradient={false}` draws plain lines and flat bars; see [BarChart](./bar-chart.md#gradient-fills).

## Props

Also takes the common chart props (`title`, `description`, `valueFormat`, `categoryFormat`, `categoryLabel`, `height`, `view`, `defaultView`, `onViewChange`, `showTableToggle`, `loading`, `emptyMessage`, `summary`, `animate`, `actions`, `className`, `classNames`); see [BarChart](./bar-chart.md).

| Prop             | Type                           | Default           | Description                      |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------ | ----------------- | -------------------------------- |
| `data`           | `Record<string, unknown>[]`    | required          | One object per step              |
| `categoryKey`    | `string`                       | required          | Key of the step label            |
| `currentKey`     | `string`                       | `"current"`       | Current period value key         |
| `previousKey`    | `string`                       | `"previous"`      | Previous period value key        |
| `currentLabel`   | `ReactNode`                    | "This period"     | Label of the current period      |
| `previousLabel`  | `ReactNode`                    | "Previous period" | Label of the previous period     |
| `variant`        | `"line" \| "bar"`              | `"line"`          | Lines or grouped bars            |
| `aggregate`      | `"sum" \| "average" \| "last"` | `"sum"`           | How headline totals are computed |
| `positiveIsGood` | `boolean`                      | `true`            | Whether an increase is good      |
| `hideTotals`     | `boolean`                      | `false`           | Hide the headline totals         |
| `gradient`       | `boolean`                      | `true`            | Gradient wash and bar fills      |

## RTL

The step axis is reversed in RTL and the value axis sits on the right. Percentages keep their sign before the number (`+8%`).

## Accessibility

- The change is shown with an arrow icon, a sign and a colour, never colour alone. Screen readers hear "Up 8%" / "Down 2%" / "No change".
- The summary states both totals and the change; the table has a **Change** column per step.

| Key                                          | Action                   |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| <kbd>ArrowLeft</kbd> / <kbd>ArrowRight</kbd> | Move between steps       |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd>                             | Show or hide the tooltip |

---

<!-- docs/charts/sparkline.md -->

# Sparkline

A tiny inline line or area chart with no axes, labels or tooltip, for trends in tables, stat tiles and text.

```tsx
import { Sparkline } from "@javaabu/onu/charts"

;<Sparkline label="Daily sign-ups" data={[12, 14, 13, null, 18, 21, 19, 24]} />
<Sparkline label="Revenue" variant="area" color="var(--chart-2)" height={48} data={values} />
```

`data` is a list of numbers (`null` leaves a gap) or objects with a `valueKey`.

## Props

| Prop          | Type                             | Default          | Description                                      |
| ------------- | -------------------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `data`        | `(number \| null)[] \| object[]` | required         | Values                                           |
| `valueKey`    | `string`                         | `"value"`        | Key of the value for object data                 |
| `label`       | `string`                         | required         | What the values are; used in the accessible name |
| `variant`     | `"line" \| "area"`               | `"line"`         | Line or filled area                              |
| `color`       | `string`                         | `var(--chart-1)` | Any token or CSS colour                          |
| `height`      | `number`                         | `32`             | Height in px; width follows the container        |
| `valueFormat` | `ValueFormat`                    | `"number"`       | Formats the values in the summary                |
| `animate`     | `boolean`                        | `false`          | Animate (off under reduced motion, see below)    |
| `gradient`    | `boolean`                        | `true`           | Fade the area fill towards the baseline          |
| `className`   | `string`                         |                  | Classes for the wrapper                          |

Other `<div>` props are passed to the wrapper.

## Gradient fills

The `"area"` variant fades from the line colour to almost clear at the bottom. `gradient={false}` gives the flat 20% fill. `<ChartStyleProvider gradient={false}>` changes the default for every chart inside; see [BarChart](./bar-chart.md#gradient-fills).

## RTL

The line runs right to left in RTL, so the latest value is on the left, matching the other charts.

## Accessibility

A sparkline is too small for a data table toggle. Instead the wrapper is `role="img"` with a full summary as its name, e.g. "Daily sign-ups: 8 values, from 12 to 24. Lowest 12, highest 24." It is not focusable. When a sparkline is the only place a figure appears, show the figure as text next to it too.

Animation follows the same rules as the other charts: never under `prefers-reduced-motion`, and not inside `<ChartAnimationProvider animate={false}>` (see [BarChart](./bar-chart.md#animation)).

---

<!-- docs/charts/stat-tile.md -->

# StatTile

KPI tiles: a label, a formatted value, a delta (arrow + sign + semantic colour), an optional icon and sparkline, and a loading skeleton. `StatTiles` lays them out in a responsive grid.

```tsx
import { StatTile, StatTiles } from "@javaabu/onu/charts"

;<StatTiles>
  <StatTile label="Applications" value={1284} previousValue={1102} icon="file-text" sparkline={[80, 92, 88, 104]} />
  <StatTile label="Revenue" value={2481500} previousValue={2610200} valueFormat="currency" icon="credit-card" />
  <StatTile label="Average wait" value="3.4 days" delta={-0.18} positiveIsGood={false} deltaContext="vs last month" />
  <StatTile label="Active users" value={18240} loading={isLoading} />
</StatTiles>
```

## Chart card (Ant Design Pro)

The tile is Ant Design Pro's **ChartCard**: a muted label row, a 30px regular-weight figure, a 46px chart slot and a footer row under a line. Add an info button after the label with `tip`, and put any mini chart (bars, a `ProgressBar`, trend text) in the slot with `chart` instead of `sparkline`:

```tsx
<StatTile
  label="Service target"
  tip="Applications closed within 14 days"
  value={0.78}
  valueFormat="percent"
  chart={<ProgressBar value={78} size="sm" aria-label="Service target: 78%" />}
  footer="Daily average 12"
/>
```

## As a link

```tsx
<StatTile asChild label="Pending approvals" value={17}>
  <a href="/approvals">Pending approvals</a>
</StatTile>
```

The child element becomes the tile and the tile content is placed inside it.

## StatTile props

| Prop               | Type                                               | Default              | Description                                |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `label`            | `ReactNode`                                        | required             | What the figure is                         |
| `value`            | `number \| string \| null`                         | required             | Numbers are formatted with `valueFormat`   |
| `valueFormat`      | `ValueFormat`                                      | `"number"`           | See [BarChart](./bar-chart.md#number-formats) |
| `previousValue`    | `number`                                           |                      | Compute the delta from it                  |
| `delta`            | `number \| null`                                   |                      | Change as a ratio, when you have it        |
| `deltaContext`     | `ReactNode`                                        | "vs previous period" | Text after the delta                       |
| `positiveIsGood`   | `boolean`                                          | `true`               | Whether an increase is good                |
| `icon`             | `SemanticIconName \| ReactNode`                    |                      | Icon at the inline end of the header       |
| `sparkline`        | `(number \| null)[]`                               |                      | Small trend under the figure               |
| `sparklineVariant` | `"line" \| "area"`                                 | `"area"`             | Sparkline style                            |
| `sparklineGradient` | `boolean`                                         | `true`               | Gradient sparkline area (see [Sparkline](./sparkline.md#gradient-fills)) |
| `loading`          | `boolean`                                          | `false`              | Skeletons, `aria-busy`                     |
| `chart`            | `ReactNode`                                        |                      | A mini chart in the 46px slot (instead of `sparkline`) |
| `tip`              | `ReactNode`                                        |                      | Info button with a tooltip after the label |
| `footer`           | `ReactNode`                                        |                      | Footer row under a line                    |
| `size`             | `"sm" \| "default" \| "lg"`                        | `"default"`          | Padding and figure size                    |
| `asChild`          | `boolean`                                          | `false`              | Render as the child element                |
| `className`        | `string`                                           |                      | Classes for the root                       |
| `classNames`       | `{ label, value, icon, delta, sparkline, footer }` |                      | Classes per part                           |

`statTileVariants` (cva) is exported.

## StatTiles props

| Prop        | Type          | Default | Description                     |
| ----------- | ------------- | ------- | ------------------------------- |
| `columns`   | `2 \| 3 \| 4` | `4`     | Most columns on wide containers |
| `className` | `string`      |         | Classes for the grid            |

The grid uses container queries: one column in narrow containers, two from 28rem, and three or four on wide ones, so it also works in sidebars and narrow cards.

## RTL and Dhivehi

The icon sits at the inline end and the delta keeps its sign before the number. String values use `dir="auto"`.

## Accessibility

- A tile is a `role="group"` named by its label (a link when `asChild`).
- The delta is conveyed by icon, sign and colour, and announced as "Up 16.5%" / "Down 4.9%".
- Figures use tabular numerals.
- While loading, the tile is `aria-busy` and announces "Loading…".

---

<!-- docs/charts/delta-indicator.md -->

# DeltaIndicator

A change indicator: an arrow icon, a signed percentage and a semantic colour. Used by [StatTile](./stat-tile.md) and [PeriodComparisonChart](./period-comparison-chart.md), and handy in tables.

```tsx
import { DeltaIndicator } from "@javaabu/onu/charts"

;<DeltaIndicator value={0.124} />                          // ↑ +12.4%
<DeltaIndicator current={182000} previous={171500} />      // computed
<DeltaIndicator value={0.08} positiveIsGood={false} variant="badge" context="vs last month" />
```

## Props

| Prop             | Type                | Default  | Description                                      |
| ---------------- | ------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`          | `number \| null`    |          | Change as a ratio (`0.12` = +12%)                |
| `current`        | `number`            |          | With `previous`, the change is computed          |
| `previous`       | `number`            |          | Previous value (0 gives no percentage)           |
| `positiveIsGood` | `boolean`           | `true`   | `false` for costs, wait times, complaints        |
| `variant`        | `"text" \| "badge"` | `"text"` | Plain or with a tinted background                |
| `context`        | `ReactNode`         |          | Muted text after the delta, e.g. "vs last month" |
| `className`      | `string`            |          | Classes for the root `<span>`                    |

`deltaIndicatorVariants` (cva) is exported. The root carries `data-direction` (`up | down | flat`) and `data-sentiment` (`positive | negative | neutral`).

## RTL

The percentage is rendered `dir="ltr"` so the sign stays before the number in Dhivehi text.

## Accessibility

Direction is shown by the icon and the sign as well as colour (WCAG 1.4.1). The visible figure is hidden from screen readers and replaced by words: "Up 12.4%", "Down 5%" or "No change" (translated in `dv`).

---

<!-- docs/charts/map-chart.md -->

# MapChart

A choropleth map: regions shaded by value on Google Maps, drawn with a deck.gl `GeoJsonLayer` (`GoogleMapsOverlay`). It has a stepped legend, a tap/hover read-out and a data table. Without a Google Maps API key it shows an accessible notice and the table instead.

:::info
Needs the optional peers `@vis.gl/react-google-maps`, `@deck.gl/core`, `@deck.gl/layers` and `@deck.gl/google-maps`. The map code is loaded lazily, only when an API key is configured.
:::

```tsx
import { OnuProvider } from "@javaabu/onu"
import { MapChart } from "@javaabu/onu/charts"

;<OnuProvider maps={{ googleMapsApiKey: "…", mapId: "…", darkMapId: "…" }}>
  <MapChart
    title="Resident population by atoll"
    geojson={atolls}
    data={[
      { id: "K", value: 22400 },
      { id: "S", value: 34500 },
    ]}
    regionLabel="Atoll"
  />
</OnuProvider>
```

`geojson` is a `FeatureCollection` of polygons. Each feature is matched to `data` by `properties[featureIdKey]` (or `feature.id`), and named by `properties[featureNameKey]`.

## Props

Also takes the common chart props (`title`, `description`, `valueFormat`, `height`, `view`, `defaultView`, `onViewChange`, `showTableToggle`, `loading`, `emptyMessage`, `summary`, `actions`, `className`, `classNames`); see [BarChart](./bar-chart.md).

| Prop             | Type                        | Default          | Description                                |
| ---------------- | --------------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `geojson`        | `GeoJsonFeatureCollection`  | required         | Region shapes                              |
| `data`           | `Record<string, unknown>[]` | required         | One value per region                       |
| `idKey`          | `string`                    | `"id"`           | Region id key in `data`                    |
| `valueKey`       | `string`                    | `"value"`        | Value key in `data`                        |
| `featureIdKey`   | `string`                    | `"id"`           | Feature property matching `data[idKey]`    |
| `featureNameKey` | `string`                    | `"name"`         | Feature property used as the name          |
| `steps`          | `number`                    | `5`              | Colour steps (equal intervals)             |
| `color`          | `string`                    | `var(--chart-1)` | Base colour; steps are lighter mixes of it |
| `center`         | `{ lat, lng }`              | the Maldives     | Initial centre                             |
| `zoom`           | `number`                    | `6`              | Initial zoom                               |
| `regionLabel`    | `ReactNode`                 | "Region"         | Table header for regions                   |
| `height`         | `number`                    | `400`            | Map height in px                           |

Helpers `choroplethScale`, `choroplethRegions` and `stepOpacity` are exported.

## Theming

The fill colour is a theme token resolved at runtime (deck.gl needs RGB), and is re-resolved when the theme switches. In dark mode the map uses `darkMapId` (if set) and Google's dark colour scheme. The map UI language follows the active locale.

## Accessibility

- With no API key: a `role="note"` notice explains why the map is missing, and the data table is shown.
- With a key: the map sits in a region named by the title and described by the summary (range of values). Hovering or tapping a region announces "Kaafu: 22,400" in a polite live region.
- The legend lists every step with its range, plus "No data".
- **View as table** lists every region and value, so the data is fully available without the map.

| Key                                   | Action                                             |
| ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>                        | Reach the map's zoom controls and the table toggle |
| Arrow keys, <kbd>+</kbd>/<kbd>-</kbd> | Pan and zoom the focused map (Google Maps)         |

---

<!-- docs/listing-pages/listing-page.md -->

# ListingPage

A complete index page, laid out as REQUIREMENTS §25.6 describes: a header with the title, the main action and secondary links (Trash, with a dot when it isn't empty), status tabs, a toolbar with the [search box](./search-box.md), [Filters](./filter-panel.md), [Columns](./column-visibility.md) and [Export](./export-menu.md), the [filter pills](./active-filter-chips.md), the [table](./data-table.md) with bulk actions and row menus, and [pagination](./pagination.md).

```tsx
import { applyListingState, Button, ListingPage, useListingState } from "@javaabu/onu"

function Users({ users }: { users: User[] }) {
  const state = useListingState() // search, filters, sort and page live in the URL
  const { rows, total } = applyListingState(users, state) // or fetch from your API

  return (
    <ListingPage
      title="Users"
      state={state}
      columns={columns}
      data={rows}
      total={total}
      noun={{ one: "user", other: "users" }}
      filters={filters}
      primaryAction={<Button>New user</Button>}
      trashHref="/users/trash"
      trashHasItems
      bulkActions={[{ id: "delete", label: "Delete", destructive: true, run: (ids) => api.delete(ids) }]}
      rowActions={(user) => [
        { id: "view", label: "View", href: `/users/${user.id}` },
        { id: "edit", label: "Edit", href: `/users/${user.id}/edit`, permitted: user.can.update },
        { id: "delete", label: "Delete", destructive: true, onSelect: () => api.delete([user.id]) },
      ]}
      getRowHref={(user) => `/users/${user.id}`}
      onExport={(format) => download(`/users/export?format=${format}&${state.toSearchParams()}`)}
    />
  )
}
```

Without a server export, `onExport={(format) => exportRows({ format, rows, columns, filename: "users" })}` builds CSV, Excel or PDF in the browser; see [`exportRows`](./export-rows.md).

With a server, call your API with `state.toSearchParams()` (Laravel / spatie-query-builder names: `search`, `sort=-created_at`, `page`, `per_page`, `filter[status][]=active`) and pass the page of rows and the total. The table, pills and empty states follow the same state.

## Card layout (Ant ProTable)

`variant="card"` (the default inside a panel [`AppLayout`](../layout-and-navigation/app-layout.md)) lays the page out like Ant Design Pro's ProTable:

- the header is [`PageTitle`](../layout-and-navigation/page-title.md)'s **PageHeader band**: breadcrumbs (`breadcrumbs`, or the layout's), the title with `tags`, the links as outlined buttons and the main action at the end, the description with key `figures`, and the status `tabs` as line tabs with an ink bar;
- an optional **query form** card: `queryFilters` shows those filters inline ([`FilterPanel variant="form"`](./filter-panel.md#query-form)), labelled fields in a grid with **Reset**, **Filter** and **Expand**, while the Filters button keeps the rest of `filters`; or pass your own `queryForm`;
- the list in a **table card**: a toolbar row with the `tableTitle` and the search at the start and Filters, Columns, Sort by, Export and `toolbarEnd` at the end, the filter pills, then the table (flush in the card) or your view, and the pagination.

```tsx
<ListingPage
  title="Applications"
  tableTitle="Application list"
  filters={filters}
  queryFilters={filters.filter((f) => ["service", "island", "assignee", "email"].includes(f.key))}
  figures={[{ label: "In review", value: 34 }]}
  tabs={tabs}
  {...tableProps}
/>
```

`variant="default"` (the default elsewhere) keeps the header, toolbar and table stacked on the page. Every other prop works the same in both.

## Other views

Pass `children` to replace the table, e.g. with a [`ListView`](./list-view.md) or [`GridView`](./grid-view.md) chosen by a [`ViewSwitcher`](./view-switcher.md) in `toolbarEnd`. The page keeps the pagination footer (from `total`, `pagination`, `perPageOptions` and `noun`) below your view, and adds a **Sort by** menu to the toolbar for the `columns` marked `sortable`, since a list or grid has no sortable headers:

```tsx
<ListingPage {...props} toolbarEnd={<ViewSwitcher value={state.view ?? "table"} onValueChange={state.setView} />}>
  {state.view === "grid" ? <GridView items={rows} title={(u) => u.name} /> : undefined}
</ListingPage>
```

## Props

All [`DataTable`](./data-table.md) props, plus:

| Prop                          | Type                                             | Default             | Description                                                |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `title`                       | `ReactNode`                                      |                     | Page heading (`h1`)                                        |
| `description`                 | `ReactNode`                                      |                     | Text under the title                                       |
| `primaryAction`               | `ReactNode`                                      |                     | Main action; also shown in the "no records" empty state    |
| `links`                       | `{ label, href, icon?, dot?, dotLabel? }[]`      |                     | Secondary links next to the title                          |
| `trashHref` / `trashHasItems` | `string` / `boolean`                             |                     | Adds a Trash link, with a dot when it isn't empty          |
| `state`                       | `ListingController`                              | `useListingState()` | Listing state (see [`useListingState`](./use-listing-state.md)) |
| `filters`                     | `FilterDefinition[]`                             | `[]`                | Filters for the panel and pills                            |
| `searchable`                  | `boolean`                                        | `true`              | Show the search box                                        |
| `searchPlaceholder`           | `string`                                         |                     | Placeholder of the search box                              |
| `searchThaana`                | `boolean \| ThaanaOptions`                       |                     | Type Thaana in the search box                              |
| `onExport` / `exportOptions`  | `(format) => void \| Promise` / `ExportOption[]` |                     | Show the Export menu                                       |
| `columnToggle`                | `boolean`                                        | `false`             | Show the Columns menu                                      |
| `tabs` / `tabsFilterKey`      | `FilterTab[]` / `string`                         | – / `"status"`      | Status tabs that set one filter                            |
| `toolbarEnd`                  | `ReactNode`                                      |                     | Extra toolbar content                                      |
| `variant`                     | `"card" \| "default"`                            | `"card"` in a panel `AppLayout` | ProTable card layout or stacked                 |
| `tableTitle`                  | `ReactNode`                                      |                     | Card layout: title at the start of the table card          |
| `queryFilters`                | `FilterDefinition[]`                             |                     | Card layout: filters in an inline query form               |
| `queryForm`                   | `ReactNode`                                      |                     | Card layout: a custom form above the table card            |
| `breadcrumbs`                 | `BreadcrumbsItem[]`                              | the layout's        | Card layout: breadcrumbs in the header band                |
| `tags` / `figures`            | `ReactNode` / `{ label, value }[]`               |                     | Card layout: tags after the title, key figures             |
| `children`                    | `ReactNode`                                      |                     | Replaces the table; pagination and Sort by stay            |

## Accessibility

- The page is a `section` named by its `h1`. The search box is a `search` landmark.
- The Trash dot has screen reader text ("Trash has items").
- Everything below follows the components it is built from; see their pages for keyboard support.

## RTL and Dhivehi

Everything mirrors in RTL. Pass `searchThaana` for Thaana search, and Dhivehi nouns (`{ one: "މީހާ", other: "މީހުން" }`) for the built-in sentences.
