<!-- docs/listing-pages/use-listing-state.md -->

# useListingState

State for an index page — search, sort, page, rows per page, filters, view, selection and column visibility — with the rules from REQUIREMENTS §25.6 built in:

- searching, filtering, sorting and changing rows-per-page go back to page 1;
- paging, searching, filtering and sorting clear the selection;
- sorting a column starts ascending, the same column flips the direction, another column starts ascending again;
- search, filters, sort, page, rows-per-page and view are kept in the address bar with `history.replaceState`, so reloading or sharing the link shows the same view, and Back leaves the page instead of undoing each change.

```tsx
import { useListingState } from "@javaabu/onu"

const state = useListingState({ defaultState: { perPage: 25, sort: { id: "created_at", desc: true } } })

const { data } = useQuery({
  queryKey: ["users", state.toSearchParams().toString()],
  queryFn: () => fetch(`/api/users?${state.toSearchParams()}`).then((r) => r.json()),
})
```

## URL format

Laravel / spatie-query-builder style: `?search=jane&sort=-name&page=2&per_page=50&filter[status][]=active&filter[created][from]=2026-03-01&view=grid`. Defaults are left out: page 1, and any search, sort, rows-per-page, view or filters equal to `defaultState` (so a default `sort: { id: "submitted", desc: true }` never shows as `?sort=-submitted`). Clearing a non-empty default writes an empty parameter (`sort=`, `filter[status]=`) so a reload keeps it cleared. `toSearchParams()` is for your API, so it always includes the sort, filters and `per_page`. Use `paramPrefix` when a page has more than one listing, `paramNames` to rename parameters, and `url: false` to keep the state out of the URL.

## Options

| Option                    | Type                         | Default | Description                                                  |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `defaultState`            | `Partial<ListingState>`      |         | Starting state; URL values win                               |
| `url`                     | `boolean`                    | `true`  | Mirror the state in the URL with `replaceState`              |
| `paramPrefix`             | `string`                     | `""`    | Prefix for every URL parameter                               |
| `paramNames`              | `Partial<ListingParamNames>` |         | Rename `search`, `sort`, `page`, `perPage`, `filter`, `view` |
| `onChange`                | `(state) => void`            |         | Called after each change (not on mount)                      |
| `defaultSelection`        | `string[]`                   | `[]`    | Selected row ids (never in the URL)                          |
| `defaultColumnVisibility` | `Record<string, boolean>`    | `{}`    | `{ email: false }` hides a column                            |

## Returned controller

| Field                                                     | Type                                                       | Description                                                      |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `search`, `page`, `perPage`                               | `string`, `number`, `number`                               | `page` is 1-based                                                |
| `sort`                                                    | `{ id, desc? } \| null`                                    |                                                                  |
| `filters`                                                 | `FilterValues`                                             | Applied filters, by key                                          |
| `view`                                                    | `string \| undefined`                                      | `table`, `list`, `grid`, `kanban`, …                             |
| `selection` / `columnVisibility`                          | `string[]` / `Record<string, boolean>`                     |                                                                  |
| `activeFilterCount` / `isFiltered`                        | `number` / `boolean`                                       | Badge count; whether a search or filter is applied               |
| `setSearch`, `clearSearch`                                | `(search) => void`, `() => void`                           | Back to page 1, clears the selection                             |
| `toggleSort` / `setSort`                                  | `(id) => void` / `(sort \| null) => void`                  | Same column flips; a new column starts ascending; back to page 1 |
| `setPage`, `setPerPage`                                   | `(n) => void`                                              | Paging clears the selection; `setPerPage` goes back to page 1    |
| `setFilters`, `setFilter`, `removeFilter`, `clearFilters` | replace all / `(key, value \| undefined)` / `(key)` / `()` | Back to page 1, clears the selection                             |
| `setView`                                                 | `(view) => void`                                           |                                                                  |
| `setSelection`, `toggleSelected`, `clearSelection`        | `(ids)` / `(id, selected?)` / `()`                         |                                                                  |
| `setColumnVisibility`                                     | `(visibility) => void`                                     |                                                                  |
| `reset`                                                   | `() => void`                                               | Back to `defaultState`                                           |
| `toSearchParams`                                          | `() => URLSearchParams`                                    | For your API: always includes sort, filters and `per_page`       |

## Helpers

- `applyListingState(rows, state, { searchFields?, filterFns?, sortValue?, locale? })` searches, filters, sorts (with `Intl.Collator`, so Thaana sorts correctly) and pages an in-memory array. Returns `{ rows, total }`.
- `listingStateToSearchParams(state)` / `parseListingSearchParams(params)` convert to and from URL parameters.
- `isFilterValueEmpty(value)` and `cleanFilters(filters)`.

Filter values are strings, string arrays (multi-select) or `{ field?, from?, to? }` date ranges with `yyyy-MM-dd` dates. Yes/No filters use `"1"` / `"0"`; the deleted-records filter uses `"with"` / `"only"` (absent means hide), like Laravel's `withTrashed` / `onlyTrashed`.

## Accessibility

The hook renders nothing; the listing components you pass it to announce its changes. [`DataTable`](./data-table.md) announces a new sort ("Sorted by Name, ascending") and [`Pagination`](./pagination.md)'s "Showing 26–50 of 312" summary is a polite live region, so paging, searching and filtering are heard without moving focus. State changes never move focus themselves.

Because the URL is updated with `history.replaceState`, Back leaves the listing instead of stepping through every keystroke and filter change, which is what keyboard and screen-reader users expect from Back. Reloading or sharing the link restores the same view.

---

<!-- docs/listing-pages/data-table.md -->

# DataTable

The listing table, built on [TanStack Table](https://tanstack.com/table) v9 (column model, visibility and selection) and shadcn's `Table`. It implements the table parts of REQUIREMENTS §25.6: sortable headers, row checkboxes with a select-all-on-this-page box, the [bulk action bar](./bulk-actions.md), [⋯ row menus](./row-actions.md), [empty states](./empty-state.md), the trash view, labelled cards on phones and the [pagination](./pagination.md) footer.

```tsx
import { DataTable, useListingState, type DataTableColumn } from "@javaabu/onu"

const columns: DataTableColumn<User>[] = [
  { id: "name", header: "Name", sortable: true, primary: true },
  { id: "email", header: "Email", sortable: true },
  { id: "status", header: "Status", cell: (u) => <StatusBadge status={u.status} /> },
  { id: "balance", header: "Balance", numeric: true, sortable: true, cell: (u) => mvr.format(u.balance) },
]

const state = useListingState()
;<DataTable
  columns={columns}
  data={page.data}
  total={page.meta.total}
  state={state}
  noun={{ one: "user", other: "users" }}
/>
```

The table always shows the rows it is given (it never sorts or pages by itself): fetch the page from your server with `state.toSearchParams()`, or use `applyListingState` for in-memory data.

## Behaviour

- **Sorting**: clicking a sortable header sorts ascending and shows an arrow; clicking again reverses; another header starts ascending. Headers expose `aria-sort` and the change is announced ("Sorted by Name, ascending").
- **Selection**: row checkboxes; the header checkbox selects or clears every row on this page and shows a dash when only some are selected. As soon as a row is selected the bulk bar appears.
- **Row actions**: `rowActions(row)` lists the ⋯ menu; only `permitted` actions show; destructive ones confirm ("Delete Jane Doe?").
- **Opening a record**: `getRowHref` makes the primary column a link (through `OnuProvider linkComponent`) and clicking the row follows it; or use `onRowClick`.
- **Empty states**: "No users yet" with `emptyAction`, or "No users match your search" naming the search and filters with Clear search / Clear filters.
- **Trash**: `trash` removes checkboxes and the bulk bar; use `trashActions(t, { onRestore, onForceDelete })` for the ⋯ menu.
- **Look**: Ant Design's table: a grey (`--muted`, #fafafa) header with semibold labels and short split lines between header cells, 12px 16px cells (`density="compact"` gives 8px, `comfortable` 16px), hairline row dividers, a #fafafa hover and selected rows in the brand's lightest step (`--primary-1`). The table has no outer frame; put it in a [Card](../layout-and-navigation/card.md) for one. Sort arrows are grey, and brand-coloured on the sorted column.
- **Phones**: below 768px (or `layout="cards"`) each row becomes a card with every value labelled by its column; a Sort by menu replaces the headers and a Select all checkbox sits above the cards.

## Props

| Prop                                 | Type                                                            | Default               | Description                                           |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `columns`                            | `DataTableColumn<T>[]`                                          |                       | Column definitions (below)                            |
| `data`                               | `T[]`                                                           |                       | Rows of the current page                              |
| `getRowId`                           | `(row) => string`                                               | `row.id`              | Stable id                                             |
| `getRowName`                         | `(row) => string`                                               | primary column        | Name used in "Select …" and "Delete …?"               |
| `state`                              | `ListingController`                                             | internal (no URL)     | From `useListingState()`                              |
| `total`                              | `number`                                                        |                       | Total rows; shows the pagination footer               |
| `pagination`                         | `boolean`                                                       | `total !== undefined` | Show the footer                                       |
| `perPageOptions`                     | `number[]`                                                      | `[10, 25, 50, 100]`   | Rows-per-page choices                                 |
| `noun`                               | `{ one, other }`                                                | records               | What is listed                                        |
| `selectable`                         | `boolean`                                                       | with bulk actions     | Show checkboxes                                       |
| `bulkActions`                        | `BulkAction[]`                                                  |                       | See [Bulk actions](./bulk-actions.md)                      |
| `onBulkSuccess`                      | `(message) => void`                                             |                       | After a bulk action succeeds                          |
| `rowActions`                         | `(row) => RecordAction[]`                                       |                       | ⋯ menu items                                          |
| `getRowHref`                         | `(row) => string \| undefined`                                  |                       | Record URL                                            |
| `onRowClick`                         | `(row) => void`                                                 |                       | Called when a row is clicked                          |
| `loading`                            | `boolean`                                                       |                       | Skeleton rows, `aria-busy`                            |
| `trash`                              | `boolean`                                                       |                       | Trash view                                            |
| `emptyAction`/`empty`                | `ReactNode`                                                     |                       | Main action for, or a replacement of, the empty state |
| `filters`                            | `FilterDefinition[]`                                            |                       | To name active filters in the no-results state        |
| `layout`                             | `"auto" \| "table" \| "cards"`                                  | `"auto"`              | Cards below 768px                                     |
| `caption`                            | `string`                                                        |                       | Accessible name                                       |
| `striped`, `stickyHeader`, `density` | `boolean`, `boolean`, `"compact" \| "default" \| "comfortable"` |                       | Variants (`dataTableVariants`)                        |
| `classNames`                         | `{ table, header, row, cell, cards, card, footer, toolbar }`    |                       | Classes for each part                                 |

`DataTableColumn<T>`: `id`, `header` (text), `headerContent?`, `accessor?` (key or function), `cell?`, `sortable?`, `hideable?`, `primary?`, `align?`, `numeric?` (tabular figures, end-aligned), `hideOnCards?`, `className?`, `headerClassName?`.

## Accessibility

| Key                                 | Action                                                      |
| ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>                      | Moves through header buttons, checkboxes, links and ⋯ menus |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | Sorts by a header, ticks a checkbox, opens a menu           |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd>                   | Closes a ⋯ menu and returns focus to it                     |

The header checkbox reports `aria-checked="mixed"` when some rows are selected. Selected rows have `aria-selected`. Sort changes and the selected count are announced. Each checkbox is a 24×24px target (WCAG 2.5.8) with the 16px box drawn inside, so it never crowds a sortable first column; on touch screens the hit area grows to 44px.

## RTL

Columns, checkboxes and menus mirror in RTL; numeric columns stay end-aligned. Pass a Dhivehi `noun` for the built-in sentences.

---

<!-- docs/listing-pages/filter-panel.md -->

# FilterPanel

The **Filters** button and its panel (REQUIREMENTS §25.7): a dropdown on desktop and a bottom sheet on phones. The button shows how many filters are applied.

```tsx
import { FilterPanel, type FilterDefinition } from "@javaabu/onu"

const filters: FilterDefinition[] = [
  {
    type: "select",
    key: "status",
    label: "Status",
    options: [
      { value: "active", label: "Active" },
      { value: "banned", label: "Banned" },
    ],
  },
  { type: "select", key: "island", label: "Island", options: islands }, // searchable when long
  {
    type: "date-range",
    key: "created",
    label: "Date",
    fields: [
      { value: "created_at", label: "Created" },
      { value: "updated_at", label: "Updated" },
    ],
  },
  { type: "boolean", key: "verified", label: "Verified email" },
  { type: "text", key: "email", label: "Email contains" },
  { type: "trashed", key: "trashed", label: "Deleted records" },
]

;<FilterPanel filters={filters} value={state.filters} onApply={state.setFilters} />
```

## Query form

`variant="form"` renders the filters inline instead of behind a button: Ant ProTable's **QueryFilter**, a card-friendly form with labelled fields in a responsive grid (labels end-aligned with a colon from 576px up), and **Reset**, **Filter** and **Expand** / **Collapse** at the end. Only the first `collapsedCount` fields (default 3) show until Expand.

```tsx
<Card padded={false}>
  <FilterPanel variant="form" filters={queryFilters} value={state.filters} onApply={state.setFilters} className="p-6" />
</Card>
```

- Changes are a draft until **Filter** (or <kbd>Enter</kbd>); **Reset** clears this form's fields and keeps any other filters.
- The form follows the applied filters when chips, tabs or Clear all change them.
- Short multi-selects are a dropdown (not a row of checkboxes) so every field stays one line.
- It is a `<form>` named "Filters" (`formLabel` to change it).

[`ListingPage`](./listing-page.md) shows one above its table card when you pass `queryFilters`.

## Behaviour

- Changes in the panel are a draft: the list doesn't change until **Apply**.
- **Cancel**, <kbd>Escape</kbd> or clicking outside close the panel and throw the draft away.
- **Clear all** removes every filter straight away and closes the panel.
- Each filter has its own **Clear** link.
- Reopening the panel always shows the filters currently applied.

## Filter types

| `type`       | Control                                                                                                                                 | Value                    |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `select`     | Checkboxes for short lists; a searchable list (shadcn `Popover` + `Command`) for long ones or `searchable`. `multiple: false` picks one | `string[]` (or `string`) |
| `date-range` | A "Date" select when `fields` has several dates, then From / To pickers (shadcn `Calendar`)                                             | `{ field?, from?, to? }` |
| `boolean`    | Any / Yes / No select                                                                                                                   | `"1"` \| `"0"`           |
| `text`       | A text box (`thaana` supported)                                                                                                         | `string`                 |
| `trashed`    | Hide / Include / Only                                                                                                                   | `"with"` \| `"only"`     |
| `custom`     | Your `render({ value, onChange, id, definition })`                                                                                      | anything                 |

Every definition also accepts `render` (replace the built-in control) and `format(value)` (the pill text).

## Props

| Prop                    | Type                                                       | Default         | Description                            |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | --------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `filters`               | `FilterDefinition[]`                                       |                 | Filters on offer                       |
| `value`                 | `FilterValues`                                             |                 | Applied filters                        |
| `onApply`               | `(filters) => void`                                        |                 | Apply (and `{}` on Clear all)          |
| `open` / `onOpenChange` | `boolean` / `(open) => void`                               |                 | Controlled open state                  |
| `sheet`                 | `boolean`                                                  | below 768px     | Force the bottom sheet or the dropdown |
| `trigger`               | `ReactNode`                                                | Filters + count | Button content                         |
| `align`                 | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"`                             | `"start"`       | Dropdown alignment                     |
| `variant`               | `"popover" \| "form"`                                      | `"popover"`     | Button and panel, or an inline query form |
| `collapsedCount`        | `number`                                                   | `3`             | Form: fields shown before Expand       |
| `defaultExpanded`       | `boolean`                                                  | `false`         | Form: start expanded                   |
| `formLabel`             | `string`                                                   | "Filters"       | Form: accessible name                  |
| `classNames`            | `{ trigger, badge, content, body, filter, label, footer }` |                 | Classes for each part                  |

## Accessibility

The panel is a `dialog` named "Filters"; each filter's control is labelled by its name. The button's name includes the count ("Filters, 2 applied"). Focus returns to the button when the panel closes.

| Key               | Action                                   |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd> | Close without applying                   |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>    | Move through the filters and the buttons |

## RTL and Thaana

The panel and the bottom sheet mirror in RTL; the calendar follows the locale's week start and month names. Text filters accept `thaana: true`.

---

<!-- docs/listing-pages/active-filter-chips.md -->

# ActiveFilterChips

One pill per applied filter under the toolbar (REQUIREMENTS §25.7): "Status: Active", "Created: 1 Mar → 31 Mar", "Created: from 1 Mar". ✕ removes that filter; **Clear all** appears with two or more pills. Nothing renders when no filters are applied.

```tsx
import { ActiveFilterChips } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<ActiveFilterChips
  filters={filters}
  value={state.filters}
  onRemove={state.removeFilter}
  onClearAll={state.clearFilters}
/>
```

Dates show as "1 Mar" (with the year when it isn't this year), using the active locale. Use a definition's `format(value)` to customise a pill or return `null` to hide it. `useActiveFilterChips(filters, value)` and `formatFilter(definition, value, t, dateLocale)` give you the same text for your own UI.

## Filter labels for your own UI

For a custom "no results" state or a summary line, use the hooks below. They format with the active locale (dates, Yes/No, option labels) exactly like the pills.

```tsx
import { EmptyState, useActiveFilterLabels, useFormatFilter } from "@javaabu/onu"

const labels = useActiveFilterLabels(filters, state.filters) // ["Status: Active", "Created: 1 Mar → 31 Mar"]
<EmptyState variant="no-results" noun={noun} filters={labels} onClearFilters={state.clearFilters} />

const formatFilter = useFormatFilter()
formatFilter(statusFilter, "active") // "Status: Active" (null when the value is empty)
```

| Helper                                   | Returns                                                     |
| ---------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `useActiveFilterLabels(filters, value)`  | `string[]`, one "Label: value" per applied filter, in order |
| `useFormatFilter()`                      | `(definition, value) => string \| null`                     |
| `useActiveFilterChips(filters, value)`   | `{ key, label, text }[]`                                    |
| `formatFilterLabel({ label, text })`     | `"Label: text"`                                             |
| `formatFilter(definition, value, t, dateLocale)` | `{ label, text } \| null`, without hooks                |

## Props

| Prop         | Type                               | Description                            |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `filters`    | `FilterDefinition[]`               | Definitions (labels and options)       |
| `value`      | `FilterValues`                     | Applied filters                        |
| `onRemove`   | `(key) => void`                    | ✕ on a pill                            |
| `onClearAll` | `() => void`                       | Shows Clear all with two or more pills |
| `classNames` | `{ list, chip, remove, clearAll }` | Classes for each part                  |

## Accessibility

The pills are a list inside a region named "Active filters". Each ✕ is a button named "Remove filter Status: Active"; after removing one, focus moves to the next ✕ so keyboard users don't lose their place. Targets grow to 44px on touch screens.

---

<!-- docs/listing-pages/search-box.md -->

# SearchBox

The search box of an index page. Typing does nothing until the user presses <kbd>Enter</kbd> or leaves the box after changing the text (REQUIREMENTS §25.6), so a request isn't sent for every keystroke. Clearing the box and pressing Enter shows everything again.

```tsx
import { SearchBox } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<SearchBox value={state.search} onSearch={state.setSearch} placeholder="Search users…" />
<SearchBox thaana onSearch={setQuery} />
```

## Props

| Prop            | Type                           | Default | Description                                |
| --------------- | ------------------------------ | ------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `value`         | `string`                       |         | The applied search; the box resets to it   |
| `defaultValue`  | `string`                       | `""`    | Uncontrolled start value                   |
| `onSearch`      | `(value) => void`              |         | Enter, blur after a change, or ✕           |
| `onValueChange` | `(value) => void`              |         | Every keystroke (draft)                    |
| `submitOnBlur`  | `boolean`                      | `true`  | Submit when leaving the box after a change |
| `clearable`     | `boolean`                      | `true`  | ✕ button that clears and submits           |
| `thaana`        | `boolean \| ThaanaOptions`     |         | Type Thaana from a Latin keyboard          |
| `landmark`      | `boolean`                      | `true`  | Wrap in `<form role="search">`             |
| `classNames`    | `{ root, input, icon, clear }` |         | Classes for each part                      |

Other `<input>` props are passed through; inside a [`FormField`](../form-scaffolding/form-field.md) it is wired automatically. `ref` points at the input.

## Accessibility

A `searchbox` named "Search" (or your label) inside a `search` landmark.

| Key               | Action                      |
| ----------------- | --------------------------- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd>  | Search                      |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd> | Put back the applied search |

## RTL and Thaana

The icon and ✕ swap sides in RTL. With `thaana` the box types Thaana and sets `dir="rtl"` and `lang="dv"`.

---

<!-- docs/listing-pages/pagination.md -->

# Pagination

Pagination for listings, laid out like Ant Design's: "Showing 26–50 of 312 users" at the start, then numbered pages between the previous and next arrows, then a rows-per-page select (10 / 25 / 50 / 100). Page items are 32px with 6px corners; the current page is outlined in the brand colour. The numbers collapse to "Page 2 of 13" in narrow containers. It reads Laravel paginators and API resource collections directly (R16.4).

```tsx
import { Pagination } from "@javaabu/onu"

<Pagination page={state.page} perPage={state.perPage} total={312} noun={{ one: "user", other: "users" }}
  onPageChange={state.setPage} onPerPageChange={state.setPerPage} />

// Laravel: `UserResource::collection($users->paginate())` or `$users->paginate()` as JSON
<Pagination paginator={response} />

// Just Previous / Next, with their labels
<Pagination page={page} total={312} numbered={false} onPageChange={setPage} />
```

`Pagination` is exported from `@javaabu/onu` (it replaces the shadcn primitive of the same name there; the primitive stays in `@javaabu/onu/primitives`).

## Behaviour

- Previous is disabled on the first page and Next on the last (or when a simple paginator has no `next_page_url`).
- With numbered pages the previous and next buttons are icon-only (their accessible names stay "Go to previous page" / "Go to next page"). Without a total (simple paginators) or with `numbered={false}` they show their labels.
- With `getPageHref`, or a paginator with a `path` / `links`, pages are links rendered with `OnuProvider linkComponent` (Inertia, Next). Plain clicks still call `onPageChange` when given.

## Props

| Prop              | Type                                                 | Default             | Description                           |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `page`            | `number`                                             | `1`                 | Current page                          |
| `perPage`         | `number`                                             | `25`                | Rows per page                         |
| `total`           | `number`                                             |                     | Total rows                            |
| `hasNextPage`     | `boolean`                                            |                     | When the total is unknown             |
| `paginator`       | `LaravelResourceCollection \| LaravelPaginationMeta` |                     | Laravel response; overrides the above |
| `onPageChange`    | `(page) => void`                                     |                     |                                       |
| `onPerPageChange` | `(perPage) => void`                                  |                     | Shows the rows-per-page select        |
| `perPageOptions`  | `number[]`                                           | `[10, 25, 50, 100]` |                                       |
| `getPageHref`     | `(page) => string`                                   |                     | Render pages as links                 |
| `numbered`        | `boolean`                                            | `true`              | Numbered pages                        |
| `showSummary`     | `boolean`                                            | `true`              | The "Showing …" text                  |
| `noun`            | `{ one, other }`                                     | records             |                                       |
| `size`            | `"default" \| "sm"`                                  |                     | `paginationVariants`                  |
| `classNames`      | `{ summary, controls, perPage, pages, button }`      |                     |                                       |

Helpers: `normalizePagination(response)` and `getPageItems(page, lastPage)`.

## Accessibility

A `navigation` landmark named "Pagination". The current page has `aria-current="page"`; buttons are named "Go to page 3", "Go to next page". The summary is a polite live region, so page changes are announced. Targets are 44px on touch screens.

## RTL

The arrows and the order mirror in RTL. Numbers use Western digits in Dhivehi (R12.6).

---

<!-- docs/listing-pages/per-page.md -->

# PerPage

A rows-per-page select (shadcn `Select`), used by [`Pagination`](./pagination.md). Changing it should send the list back to page 1, which [`useListingState`](./use-listing-state.md) does.

```tsx
import { PerPage } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<PerPage value={state.perPage} onValueChange={state.setPerPage} />
<PerPage value={24} onValueChange={setSize} options={[12, 24, 48]} label="Cards per page" />
```

## Props

| Prop            | Type                                | Default             | Description                                    |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `value`         | `number`                            |                     | Current size (added to the options if missing) |
| `onValueChange` | `(perPage) => void`                 |                     |                                                |
| `options`       | `number[]`                          | `[10, 25, 50, 100]` |                                                |
| `label`         | `ReactNode \| null`                 | "Rows per page"     | `null` hides it visually (it stays the name)   |
| `size`          | `"sm" \| "default"`                 | `"default"`         | 32px (`default`, Ant's page-size changer) or 28px |
| `disabled`      | `boolean`                           |                     |                                                |
| `classNames`    | `{ root, label, trigger, content }` |                     |                                                |

## Accessibility

A combobox labelled by the visible label. Arrow keys move through the sizes, <kbd>Enter</kbd> picks one, <kbd>Escape</kbd> closes.

---

<!-- docs/listing-pages/bulk-actions.md -->

# BulkActionBar

The bulk action bar (REQUIREMENTS §25.6). It appears as soon as one row is selected and shows "3 selected", the actions and **Clear selection**. [`DataTable`](./data-table.md) renders it for you from `bulkActions`.

```tsx
import { BulkActionBar, type BulkAction } from "@javaabu/onu"

const actions: BulkAction<unknown>[] = [
  {
    id: "status",
    label: "Change status",
    defaultValue: "active",
    form: ({ id, value, onChange }) => <StatusSelect id={id} value={value} onChange={onChange} />,
    run: (ids, status) => api.updateStatus(ids, status),
    successMessage: (n) => `${n} users updated`,
  },
  { id: "delete", label: "Delete", destructive: true, run: (ids) => api.delete(ids) },
]

;<BulkActionBar selected={state.selection} actions={actions} noun={noun} onClearSelection={state.clearSelection} />
```

## Behaviour

- An action with `form` first shows that small form in the bar, with Apply and Cancel.
- A destructive action (or one with `confirm`) asks first: "Delete 3 selected users?" with Cancel and Delete.
- While `run` is pending the bar shows a spinner and its buttons are disabled.
- When it finishes, a success message appears ("3 users deleted" for `id: "delete"`; otherwise `successMessage`, the string `run` returned, or "Label: 3 users done") and the selection clears.
- If `run` throws, the error shows in the bar and the selection is kept.

## Props

| Prop               | Type                                     | Description     |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------- | --------------- |
| `selected`         | `string[]`                               | Selected ids    |
| `actions`          | `BulkAction[]`                           | See below       |
| `onClearSelection` | `() => void`                             |                 |
| `noun`             | `{ one, other }`                         | What is listed  |
| `onSuccess`        | `(message, action, ids) => void`         | After success   |
| `onError`          | `(error, action) => void`                | After a failure |
| `classNames`       | `{ bar, count, actions, form, message }` |                 |

`BulkAction<V>`: `id`, `label`, `icon?`, `destructive?`, `confirm?` (`boolean` or `{ title, description, confirmLabel }`), `form?`, `defaultValue?`, `run(ids, value)`, `successMessage?`, `permitted?` (`false` hides it).

## Accessibility

The bar is a region named "Bulk actions"; the count is a polite live region, so "3 selected" is announced. Confirmations are alert dialogs that return focus where they were opened. After success, focus moves to the result message so it isn't lost when the bar goes away; errors are `role="alert"`.

---

<!-- docs/listing-pages/row-actions.md -->

# RowActions

The ⋯ menu at the end of a row (REQUIREMENTS §25.6), on shadcn's `DropdownMenu`. Only actions the user can do are listed; destructive ones close the menu and then ask "Delete Jane Doe?".

```tsx
import { RowActions, trashActions } from "@javaabu/onu"

<RowActions
  name={user.name}
  actions={[
    { id: "view", label: "View", icon: "eye", href: `/users/${user.id}` },
    { id: "edit", label: "Edit", icon: "edit", href: `/users/${user.id}/edit`, permitted: user.can.update },
    { id: "delete", label: "Delete", icon: "trash", destructive: true, separator: true, onSelect: () => api.delete(user.id) },
  ]}
/>

// Trash view: Restore, and Delete permanently (confirms first)
const { t } = useTranslation()
<RowActions name={user.name} actions={trashActions(t, { onRestore, onForceDelete })} />
```

## `RecordAction`

| Field                   | Type                                              | Description                                          |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                    | `string`                                          | `delete` / `force-delete` get the built-in questions |
| `label`                 | `ReactNode`                                       |                                                      |
| `icon`                  | `string`                                          | Semantic icon name                                   |
| `href`                  | `string`                                          | Link (provider's link component)                     |
| `onSelect`              | `() => void \| Promise`                           | The confirmation shows a spinner until it settles    |
| `destructive`           | `boolean`                                         | Red; confirms unless `confirm: false`                |
| `confirm`               | `boolean \| { title, description, confirmLabel }` | Ask first                                            |
| `permitted`             | `boolean`                                         | `false` leaves it out                                |
| `disabled`, `separator` | `boolean`                                         |                                                      |

## Props

| Prop         | Type                           | Default | Description                                                   |
| ------------ | ------------------------------ | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`       | `string`                       |         | The record's name: "Actions for Jane Doe", "Delete Jane Doe?" |
| `actions`    | `RecordAction[]`               |         | See above                                                     |
| `align`      | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"` | `"end"` | Menu alignment                                                |
| `classNames` | `{ trigger, content }`         |         | Classes for the ⋯ button and the menu                         |
| `ref`        | `Ref<HTMLButtonElement>`       |         | The ⋯ button                                                  |

Other button props are passed to the ⋯ button. Renders nothing when no action is permitted.

## Accessibility

The button is named "Actions for Jane Doe". Arrow keys move through the menu, <kbd>Enter</kbd> chooses, <kbd>Escape</kbd> closes it and focus returns to ⋯. After a confirmation closes, focus also returns to ⋯.

---

<!-- docs/listing-pages/record-actions-menu.md -->

# RecordActionsMenu

Actions in a record page header (e.g. Logs, Approve, Delete — REQUIREMENTS §25.8). From 640px the first `maxVisible` actions are buttons and the rest go in a "More actions" menu; on phones every action is in the menu. Only permitted actions show, and risky ones confirm first.

```tsx
import { RecordActionsMenu } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<RecordActionsMenu
  name="Jane Doe"
  actions={[
    { id: "logs", label: "Logs", icon: "history", href: "/users/1/logs" },
    { id: "approve", label: "Approve", confirm: true, onSelect: approve },
    { id: "delete", label: "Delete", destructive: true, onSelect: remove, permitted: can.delete },
  ]}
/>
```

## Props

| Prop         | Type                           | Default     | Description                   |
| ------------ | ------------------------------ | ----------- | ----------------------------- |
| `name`       | `string`                       |             | Used in confirmations         |
| `actions`    | `RecordAction[]`               |             | See [RowActions](./row-actions.md) |
| `maxVisible` | `number`                       | `2`         | Buttons before the menu       |
| `size`       | `"sm" \| "default"`            | `"default"` |                               |
| `classNames` | `{ button, trigger, content }` |             |                               |

## Accessibility

Buttons and menu items are reachable with <kbd>Tab</kbd> and the arrow keys; <kbd>Escape</kbd> closes the menu. Confirmations return focus to what opened them.

---

<!-- docs/listing-pages/empty-state.md -->

# EmptyState

Empty states for listings (REQUIREMENTS §25.6), on shadcn's `Empty`:

- `no-records`: "No users yet", a short explanation and the main action;
- `no-results`: "No users match your search", naming the search and filters, with **Clear search** and/or **Clear filters**;
- `trash`: "Trash is empty".

```tsx
import { EmptyState } from "@javaabu/onu"

<EmptyState noun={{ one: "user", other: "users" }} action={<Button>New user</Button>} />
<EmptyState variant="no-results" noun={noun} search="jane" filters={["Status: Active"]}
  onClearSearch={state.clearSearch} onClearFilters={state.clearFilters} />
```

## Props

| Prop                              | Type                                      | Default        | Description                  |
| --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `variant`                         | `"no-records" \| "no-results" \| "trash"` | `"no-records"` | `emptyStateVariants`         |
| `bordered`                        | `boolean`                                 | `false`        | Dashed border                |
| `noun`                            | `{ one, other }`                          | records        |                              |
| `title`, `description`            | `ReactNode`                               |                | Replace the built-in text    |
| `icon`                            | `string \| ReactNode \| null`             | per variant    |                              |
| `action`                          | `ReactNode`                               |                | Main action                  |
| `search`, `filters`               | `string`, `string[]`                      |                | Named in the no-results text; [`useActiveFilterLabels`](./active-filter-chips.md#filter-labels-for-your-own-ui) builds `filters` |
| `onClearSearch`, `onClearFilters` | `() => void`                              |                | Show the clear buttons       |
| `classNames`                      | `{ media, title, description, content }`  |                |                              |

## Accessibility

The state is a `status` region, so a search that empties the list is announced.

<!-- docs/listing-pages/view-switcher.md -->

# ViewSwitcher

Switches a listing between table, list, grid and board views. A single-choice toggle group (shadcn `ToggleGroup`).

```tsx
import { ViewSwitcher } from "@javaabu/onu"

<ViewSwitcher value={state.view ?? "table"} onValueChange={state.setView} />
<ViewSwitcher views={["list", "grid", { value: "map", label: "Map", icon: "map-pin" }]} showLabels />
```

Store the view in [`useListingState`](./use-listing-state.md) (`state.view`) to keep it in the URL.

## Props

| Prop            | Type                            | Default                               | Description                    |
| --------------- | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `value`         | `ListingView`                   |                                       | Controlled view                |
| `defaultValue`  | `ListingView`                   | `"table"`                             |                                |
| `onValueChange` | `(view) => void`                |                                       |                                |
| `views`         | `(ListingView \| ViewOption)[]` | `["table", "list", "grid", "kanban"]` | Built-ins get labels and icons |
| `showLabels`    | `boolean`                       | `false`                               | Text next to the icons         |

## Accessibility

A `radiogroup` named "View"; each icon button has its view's name. Arrow keys move between views, following visual order in RTL.

---

<!-- docs/listing-pages/column-visibility.md -->

# ColumnVisibility

A "Columns" menu with a checkbox per column, to show or hide table columns. The menu stays open while toggling.

```tsx
import { ColumnVisibility } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<ColumnVisibility columns={columns} value={state.columnVisibility} onValueChange={state.setColumnVisibility} />
```

[`DataTable`](./data-table.md) hides columns set to `false` in `state.columnVisibility` (TanStack's column visibility).

## Props

| Prop            | Type                                    | Default | Description                            |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `columns`       | `{ id, header, hideable?, primary? }[]` |         | `DataTableColumn`s work as they are    |
| `value`         | `Record<string, boolean>`               |         | `false` hides; missing ids are visible |
| `onValueChange` | `(value) => void`                       |         |                                        |
| `showLabel`     | `boolean`                               | `true`  | "Columns" text (from 640px)            |
| `classNames`    | `{ trigger, content, item }`            |         |                                        |

Primary columns and columns with `hideable: false` are not listed.

## Accessibility

Items are `menuitemcheckbox`es. Arrow keys move, <kbd>Space</kbd>/<kbd>Enter</kbd> toggles, <kbd>Escape</kbd> closes and returns focus to the button.

<!-- docs/listing-pages/filter-tabs.md -->

# FilterTabs

Status tabs above a listing, with counts: "All 312 · Active 280 · Banned 32". Built on shadcn `Tabs`; on narrow screens the tabs scroll sideways. The default `line` variant looks like Ant Design's line tabs: 32px apart over a hairline, brand-coloured text and a 2px ink bar on the active tab, and grey count pills that turn to the brand colour on the active tab.

```tsx
import { FilterTabs } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<FilterTabs
  controls="users-table"
  value={(state.filters.status as string) ?? "all"}
  onValueChange={(v) => state.setFilter("status", v === "all" ? undefined : v)}
  tabs={[
    { value: "all", label: "All", count: 312 },
    { value: "active", label: "Active", count: 280 },
    { value: "banned", label: "Banned", count: 32 },
  ]}
/>
```

[`ListingPage`](./listing-page.md) does this for you with its `tabs` prop.

## Props

| Prop                     | Type                                    | Default  | Description                                |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `tabs`                   | `{ value, label, count?, disabled? }[]` |          |                                            |
| `value` / `defaultValue` | `string`                                |          |                                            |
| `onValueChange`          | `(value) => void`                       |          |                                            |
| `variant`                | `"line" \| "default"`                   | `"line"` | Underline or pills                         |
| `controls`               | `string`                                |          | Id of the listing (set as `aria-controls`) |
| `classNames`             | `{ list, tab, count }`                  |          |                                            |

## Accessibility

A `tablist` named "Filter by status"; the selected tab has `aria-selected`, and counts are part of each tab's name ("Active (280)"). Arrow keys move between tabs (mirrored in RTL), <kbd>Home</kbd>/<kbd>End</kbd> go to the first and last.

---

<!-- docs/listing-pages/export-menu.md -->

# ExportMenu

An **Export** button with a menu of formats (CSV, Excel, PDF). The menu does not build the file: your `onExport(format)` does, either by asking the server with the current filters or in the browser with [`exportRows`](./export-rows.md) from `@javaabu/onu/export`. While the returned promise is pending the button shows a spinner and is disabled.

```tsx
import { ExportMenu } from "@javaabu/onu"

<ExportMenu onExport={(format) => download(`/users/export?format=${format}&${state.toSearchParams()}`)} />
<ExportMenu onExport={exportFile} scopeLabel="312 users, current filters"
  options={["csv", { format: "json", label: "JSON", icon: "code", description: "For developers" }]} />
```

Without a server export, build the file in the browser from the rows you have (CSV, Excel and a print-ready PDF; see [`exportRows`](./export-rows.md)):

```tsx
import { useExportRows } from "@javaabu/onu/export"

const exportRows = useExportRows()
<ExportMenu onExport={(format) => exportRows({ format, rows, columns, filename: "users", title: "Users" })} />
```

## Props

| Prop         | Type                                                                     | Default                   |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------- |
| `onExport`   | `(format) => void \| Promise`                                            |                           |
| `options`    | `(ExportFormat \| { format, label?, icon?, description?, disabled? })[]` | `["csv", "excel", "pdf"]` |
| `scopeLabel` | `ReactNode`                                                              | Text above the options    |
| `classNames` | `{ trigger, content, item }`                                             |                           |

## Accessibility

A menu button. "Exporting…" and "Export ready" are announced through a polite live region; the button has `aria-busy` while working.

---

<!-- docs/listing-pages/export-rows.md -->

# exportRows (client-side export)

Builds a **CSV**, **Excel** or **PDF** file in the browser from the rows you already have, for apps without a server export. It lives in its own entry point, `@javaabu/onu/export`, so it never adds to the core bundle. It fits the [`ExportMenu`](./export-menu.md) and [`ListingPage`](./listing-page.md) `onExport` prop in one line.

```tsx
import { useExportRows, type ExportColumn } from "@javaabu/onu/export"

const columns: ExportColumn<Payment>[] = [
  { header: "Reference", accessor: "reference" },
  { header: "Name", accessor: (p) => (dv ? p.nameDv : p.name) },
  { header: "Island", accessor: "island.name" }, // dotted paths work
  { header: "Amount", accessor: "amount", type: "currency" },
  { header: "Paid on", accessor: "paidAt", type: "date" },
]

function Payments() {
  const exportRows = useExportRows() // uses the OnuProvider locale and direction
  return (
    <ListingPage
      {...props}
      onExport={(format) => exportRows({ format, rows: allMatchingRows, columns, filename: "payments", title: "Payments" })}
    />
  )
}
```

`exportRows(options)` works outside React too; pass `locale: "dv"` (or an Onu locale object) and, if needed, `dir`. Export **every row that matches the current search and filters**, not just the visible page: with [`applyListingState`](./use-listing-state.md) that is `applyListingState(all, { ...state, page: 1, perPage: Infinity }, options).rows`.

## Formats

| Format  | What you get                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Needs              |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------ |
| `csv`   | UTF-8 with a byte order mark (so Excel opens Dhivehi correctly), RFC 4180 quoting, CRLF line endings. Text cells starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab or CR get a leading `'` (formula-injection guard); real numbers such as `-40` are written as numbers.                         | nothing            |
| `excel` | An `.xlsx` workbook: bold, frozen header row, numbers and currency stay numeric (with a `"MVR "#,##0.00` / `"ރ. "#,##0.00` number format), dates are real dates, and the sheet reads **right to left** when `dir` is `rtl`. Thaana text is stored as-is.                             | `write-excel-file` |
| `pdf`   | Opens the browser's print dialog with a styled, paginated table (title, scope line, "Generated …" date and row count, the header row repeated on every page, page numbers). The user picks **Save as PDF**. It uses the page's Onu fonts, so Thaana renders in MV Waheed / Faruma. | nothing            |

Excel loads `write-excel-file` with `import()` on the first Excel export. Install it only if you offer Excel:

```bash
npm install write-excel-file
```

The PDF is printed by the browser, not drawn by a PDF library: browser text shaping is the only reliable way to render Thaana correctly, and it adds no dependency. Landscape is used for more than five columns (`orientation` to override).

## Options

| Option                         | Type                                  | Default        | Description                                                                 |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------- | -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `format`                       | `"csv" \| "excel" \| "pdf"`           |                | `"xlsx"` is accepted for Excel; anything else throws                       |
| `rows`                         | `T[]`                                 |                | The records                                                                 |
| `columns`                      | `ExportColumn<T>[]`                   |                | See below                                                                   |
| `filename`                     | `string`                              | `"export"`     | The extension is added; for PDF it is the document title the browser offers |
| `title`                        | `string`                              |                | PDF heading; Excel sheet name unless `sheetName` is set                     |
| `scope`                        | `string`                              |                | PDF line under the title, e.g. "Status: Approved · 312 applications"        |
| `locale` / `dir`               | `OnuLocale \| "en" \| "dv"` / `"ltr" \| "rtl"` | `"en"` / the locale's | Dates, numbers, yes/no and built-in text; `useExportRows` fills them in |
| `delimiter`, `bom`             | `string`, `boolean`                   | `","`, `true`  | CSV                                                                         |
| `sheetName`, `fontFamily`      | `string`                              |                | Excel sheet name (31 characters); default font (Excel and PDF)              |
| `orientation`, `generatedAt`   | `"portrait" \| "landscape"`, `Date`   |                | PDF                                                                         |

### Columns

| Field      | Type                                                                    | Description                                                                                                                 |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `header`   | `string`                                                                | Header cell                                                                                                                 |
| `accessor` | `string \| (row, index) => unknown`                                     | Property name (dotted paths allowed) or function                                                                             |
| `type`     | `"text" \| "number" \| "currency" \| "date" \| "datetime" \| "boolean"` | Without it, each value is typed by what it is (number, `Date`, boolean, else text). Values that do not fit become text.     |
| `format`   | `(value, row) => string`                                                | Text for CSV and PDF (and Excel text columns). Number, currency and date columns stay numeric/dates in Excel.              |
| `decimals` | `number`                                                                | Decimal places (currency default 2)                                                                                          |
| `width`    | `number`                                                                | Excel column width in characters (default: fitted to the content)                                                           |

## Building blocks

Each format has its own helpers, useful for tests or for sending the file somewhere else:

| Function                                    | Returns                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `toCsv(rows, columns, options?)`            | The CSV text (with BOM)                                     |
| `exportCsv({ rows, columns, filename })`    | Saves the `.csv`                                            |
| `buildExcelSheet(rows, columns, options?)`  | The cells and sheet options handed to `write-excel-file`    |
| `toExcelBlob(rows, columns, options?)`      | `Promise<Blob>` of the `.xlsx`                              |
| `exportExcel({ rows, columns, filename })`  | Saves the `.xlsx`                                           |
| `buildPrintDocument(rows, columns, opts?)`  | The print-ready HTML document (every value HTML-escaped)    |
| `printHtml(html)`                           | Prints a document through a hidden iframe                   |
| `exportPdf({ rows, columns, title })`       | Opens the print dialog                                      |
| `escapeCsvFormula`, `quoteCsvField`, `escapeHtml`, `downloadBlob` | The small pieces above                  |

## Accessibility

The export runs from the [`ExportMenu`](./export-menu.md), which announces "Exporting…" and "Export ready" in a polite live region and keeps `aria-busy` on the button until the file is saved or the print dialog has opened. The print frame is hidden from assistive technology (`aria-hidden`, not focusable) and removed after printing. The PDF table uses real `th scope="col"` headers.

## RTL and Dhivehi

- With `dir: "rtl"` (automatic for Dhivehi through `useExportRows`), Excel sheets are right to left and the PDF document is `dir="rtl" lang="dv"`.
- Dates use the locale's date-fns locale in the PDF ("12 މާޗު 2026"); CSV and Excel use ISO dates and real date cells.
- Currency follows `common.currency` ("MVR 1,250.00" / "ރ. 1,250.00"); booleans use `common.yes` / `common.no`.
- Text cells are wrapped in `<bdi>` in the PDF, so Latin and Thaana values each read in their own direction while the column keeps the page alignment.

---

<!-- docs/listing-pages/filter-submit.md -->

# FilterSubmit

Submit and Reset buttons for a classic filter form, e.g. a server-rendered filter bar above a table. The submit button is `type="submit"`; `loading` shows a spinner and blocks double submits.

```tsx
import { FilterSubmit } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<form method="get" action="/users">
  <FormField label="Name">
    <TextInput name="search" />
  </FormField>
  <FilterSubmit loading={processing} onReset={() => router.get("/users")} />
</form>
```

For an interactive listing prefer the [`FilterPanel`](./filter-panel.md).

## Props

| Prop                         | Type                | Default            | Description                             |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------- | ------------------ | --------------------------------------- |
| `loading`                    | `boolean`           | `false`            | Spinner, `aria-busy`, disabled          |
| `onReset`                    | `() => void`        |                    | Shows Reset                             |
| `resetDisabled`              | `boolean`           |                    |                                         |
| `submitLabel` / `resetLabel` | `ReactNode`         | "Filter" / "Reset" |                                         |
| `form`                       | `string`            |                    | Form id when the buttons sit outside it |
| `classNames`                 | `{ submit, reset }` |                    |                                         |

## Accessibility

Standard buttons; <kbd>Enter</kbd> in any field of the form submits it.

<!-- docs/listing-pages/list-view.md -->

# ListView

Records as a vertical list: media (avatar, icon), title, description and details, with optional checkboxes and a ⋯ menu per item. Clicking an item opens it.

```tsx
import { ListView } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<ListView
  aria-label="Users"
  items={rows}
  title={(u) => u.name}
  description={(u) => u.email}
  media={(u) => <Avatar>…</Avatar>}
  meta={(u) => <Badge>{u.status}</Badge>}
  getHref={(u) => `/users/${u.id}`}
  selection={state.selection}
  onSelectionChange={state.setSelection}
  itemActions={(u) => [{ id: "edit", label: "Edit", href: `/users/${u.id}/edit` }]}
/>
```

## Props

| Prop                              | Type                                                | Default           | Description                               |
| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `items`                           | `T[]`                                               |                   |                                           |
| `getId` / `getName`               | `(item) => string`                                  | `item.id` / title | Id and accessible name                    |
| `title`                           | `(item) => ReactNode`                               |                   | Links to the record when `getHref` is set |
| `description`, `meta`, `media`    | `(item) => ReactNode`                               |                   |                                           |
| `renderItem`                      | `(item, { checkbox, actions, title }) => ReactNode` |                   | Replace the layout                        |
| `getHref` / `onItemClick`         | `(item) => string` / `(item) => void`               |                   | Opening an item                           |
| `itemActions`                     | `(item) => RecordAction[]`                          |                   | ⋯ menu                                    |
| `selection` / `onSelectionChange` | `string[]` / `(ids) => void`                        |                   | Checkboxes                                |
| `loading`, `empty`                | `boolean`, `ReactNode`                              |                   | Skeletons, empty state                    |
| `variant`                         | `"divided" \| "cards"`                              | `"divided"`       |                                           |
| `classNames`                      | `{ item, media, body, meta }`                       |                   |                                           |

## Accessibility

A list (`ul`) with your `aria-label`; each item's title is a real link, so keyboard users reach it with <kbd>Tab</kbd>. Clicking elsewhere on the item is a mouse shortcut for that link.

<!-- docs/listing-pages/grid-view.md -->

# GridView

Records as a responsive grid of cards. Columns follow the space available (`repeat(auto-fill, minmax(…))`), not the viewport, so the grid also works in a sidebar or a narrow column.

```tsx
import { GridView } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<GridView
  aria-label="Council offices"
  items={offices}
  title={(o) => o.name}
  description={(o) => o.address}
  media={(o) => <img src={o.photo} alt="" />}
  getHref={(o) => `/offices/${o.id}`}
  minItemWidth="14rem"
/>
```

Props are the same as [`ListView`](./list-view.md), plus `minItemWidth` and without `variant`. Selection checkboxes sit on the card's start corner.

## Props

| Prop                              | Type                                                | Default           | Description                                              |
| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `items`                           | `T[]`                                               |                   |                                                          |
| `getId` / `getName`               | `(item) => string`                                  | `item.id` / title | Id, and the name used in "Select …" and "Actions for …"  |
| `title`                           | `(item) => ReactNode`                               |                   | Links to the record when `getHref` is set                |
| `description`, `meta`             | `(item) => ReactNode`                               |                   | Body text (two lines at most) and small details          |
| `media`                           | `(item) => ReactNode`                               |                   | 16:9 area at the top of the card, e.g. an `<img alt="">` |
| `renderItem`                      | `(item, { checkbox, actions, title }) => ReactNode` |                   | Replace the card's layout                                |
| `getHref` / `onItemClick`         | `(item) => string` / `(item) => void`               |                   | Opening an item                                          |
| `itemActions`                     | `(item) => RecordAction[]`                          |                   | ⋯ menu                                                   |
| `selection` / `onSelectionChange` | `string[]` / `(ids) => void`                        |                   | Checkboxes (shown when `onSelectionChange` is set)       |
| `loading`, `empty`                | `boolean`, `ReactNode`                              |                   | Six skeleton cards; content for no items                 |
| `minItemWidth`                    | `string`                                            | `"16rem"`         | Smallest card width before the grid drops a column       |
| `aria-label`                      | `string`                                            |                   | Name of the list                                         |
| `className`                       | `string`                                            |                   | Classes for the grid                                     |
| `classNames`                      | `{ item, media, body, meta }`                       |                   | Classes for each part                                    |

## Accessibility

A list (`ul`) of cards named by your `aria-label`; each title is a real link, so keyboard users reach it with <kbd>Tab</kbd>. Clicking elsewhere on a card is a mouse shortcut for that link. While `loading`, the list has `aria-busy="true"`. Images in `media` are usually decorative next to the title: give them `alt=""`. Cards keep the DOM order in the grid, so reading and tab order match what is on screen in both directions.

<!-- docs/listing-pages/kanban-board.md -->

# KanbanBoard

A board of columns with cards that move between them, on [`@dnd-kit/react`](https://dndkit.com). Cards can be dragged with a mouse, by touch (press and hold, so the page still scrolls), or with the keyboard, and every card also has a **Move to…** menu as a non-drag alternative (R3.27).

```tsx
import { KanbanBoard } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<KanbanBoard
  columns={[
    { id: "submitted", title: "Submitted", accentClassName: "bg-chart-1" },
    { id: "review", title: "In review" },
    { id: "approved", title: "Approved" },
  ]}
  items={applicationsByStatus}
  getName={(a) => a.reference}
  canMove={(move) => move.to !== "submitted"}
  onItemsChange={(next, move) => {
    setApplications(next)
    api.move(move.id, move.to, move.index)
  }}
  renderCard={(a, { handle, moveMenu }) => (
    <div className="gap-2 p-2 flex items-center">
      {handle}
      <span>{a.reference}</span>
      {moveMenu}
    </div>
  )}
/>
```

## Props

| Prop            | Type                                                    | Description                       |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `columns`       | `{ id, title, accentClassName?, actions? }[]`           |                                   |
| `items`         | `Record<columnId, T[]>`                                 |                                   |
| `getId`         | `(item) => string`                                      | Default `item.id`                 |
| `getName`       | `(item) => string`                                      | Handle label and announcements    |
| `renderCard`    | `(item, { handle, moveMenu, isDragging }) => ReactNode` |                                   |
| `onItemsChange` | `(items, { id, from, to, index }) => void`              | After a drop or a Move to… choice |
| `canMove`       | `(move) => boolean`                                     | Refuse moves (workflow rules)     |
| `emptyColumn`   | `ReactNode`                                             | Text in empty columns             |
| `disabled`      | `boolean`                                               |                                   |
| `classNames`    | `{ column, header, list, card }`                        |                                   |

## Accessibility

Each column is a region named by its title with a count ("3 items"). Moves are announced in the active locale, with item names.

| Key                                 | Action (on a drag handle) |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| <kbd>Space</kbd> / <kbd>Enter</kbd> | Pick up / drop            |
| Arrow keys                          | Move while picked up      |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd>                   | Cancel the move           |

## RTL

Columns flow from the right in RTL; on phones the board scrolls sideways with snap points.

<!-- docs/listing-pages/tree-view.md -->

# TreeView

A tree of records (folders, categories, atolls and islands, org units) on React Aria's `Tree`, which implements the WAI-ARIA tree grid pattern. Supports expand/collapse, actions and optional selection with checkboxes.

```tsx
import { TreeView, type TreeNode } from "@javaabu/onu"

const nodes: TreeNode[] = [
  { id: "kaafu", label: "Kaafu Atoll", icon: "folder", children: [{ id: "male", label: "Malé City" }] },
]

<TreeView aria-label="Islands" items={nodes} defaultExpandedKeys={["kaafu"]} onAction={(id) => open(id)} />
<TreeView aria-label="Islands to include" items={nodes} selectionMode="multiple" selectedKeys={ids} onSelectionChange={setIds} />
```

## Partial selection and propagation

In multiple selection, a parent that isn't selected but has selected rows under it shows a dash (`aria-checked="mixed"`). React Aria's `Tree` has no selection propagation of its own, so Onu adds it: with `selectionPropagation`, ticking a parent ticks every enabled row under it, unticking clears them, and a parent becomes ticked when all of its enabled children are (and unticked when one is cleared). `onSelectionChange` receives the full, propagated list. `propagateTreeSelection(items, previous, next, disabled?)` is exported for server-side or custom use.

```tsx
<TreeView items={nodes} selectionMode="multiple" selectionPropagation selectedKeys={ids} onSelectionChange={setIds} />
```

## Props

| Prop                                                         | Type                                                                             | Default      |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ |
| `items`                                                      | `TreeNode[]` (`id`, `label`, `icon?`, `end?`, `children?`, `disabled?`, `href?`) |              |
| `selectionMode`                                              | `"none" \| "single" \| "multiple"`                                               | `"none"`     |
| `selectedKeys` / `defaultSelectedKeys` / `onSelectionChange` | `string[]`                                                                       |              |
| `selectionPropagation`                                       | `boolean`                                                                        | `false`      |
| `expandedKeys` / `defaultExpandedKeys` / `onExpandedChange`  | `string[]`                                                                       |              |
| `onAction`                                                   | `(id) => void`                                                                   |              |
| `empty`                                                      | `ReactNode`                                                                      | "No results" |
| `classNames`                                                 | `{ item, content, chevron, checkbox }`                                           |              |

## Accessibility

| Key                         | Action                             |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> / <kbd>↓</kbd> | Previous / next row                |
| <kbd>→</kbd> / <kbd>←</kbd> | Expand / collapse (swapped in RTL) |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd>            | Action                             |
| <kbd>Space</kbd>            | Select (when selection is on)      |

The chevrons are named "Expand"/"Collapse" in the active locale and grow to 44px on touch screens.

# SortableList

A list the user can put in order (menu items, steps, priorities), on `@dnd-kit/react`: drag the handle with a mouse or by touch (press and hold), use the keyboard on the handle, or use the **Move up / Move down** buttons.

```tsx
import { SortableList } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<SortableList
  aria-label="Menu items"
  items={items}
  getName={(i) => i.title}
  onReorder={(next, { id, from, to }) => setItems(next)}
  renderItem={(item, { handle, moveButtons }) => (
    <div className="gap-2 p-2 flex items-center rounded-lg border">
      {handle}
      <span className="flex-1">{item.title}</span>
      {moveButtons}
    </div>
  )}
/>
```

## Props

| Prop          | Type                                                              | Default   |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- |
| `items`       | `T[]`                                                             |           |
| `getId`       | `(item) => string`                                                | `item.id` |
| `getName`     | `(item) => string`                                                |           |
| `renderItem`  | `(item, { handle, moveButtons, index, isDragging }) => ReactNode` |           |
| `onReorder`   | `(items, { id, from, to }) => void`                               |           |
| `moveButtons` | `boolean`                                                         | `true`    |
| `disabled`    | `boolean`                                                         |           |
| `classNames`  | `{ item, handle }`                                                |           |

## Accessibility

| Key (on a handle)                        | Action                    |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| <kbd>Space</kbd> / <kbd>Enter</kbd>      | Pick up / drop            |
| Arrow keys                               | Move while picked up      |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd>                        | Cancel                    |
| <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>↑</kbd>/<kbd>↓</kbd> | Move by one straight away |

The new position is announced ("Home moved to position 2 of 4") in the active locale.
