<!-- docs/listing-pages/reorderable-table.md -->

# ReorderableTable

Drag-and-drop row reordering for tables (route stops, menu items, priorities), on `@dnd-kit/react` and shadcn's `Table`. Each row has a drag handle that works with a mouse, by touch (press and hold) and with the keyboard; <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>↑</kbd>/<kbd>↓</kbd> on a handle moves the row by one.

```tsx
import { ReorderableTable } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<ReorderableTable
  caption="Ferry route stops"
  rows={stops}
  getName={(s) => s.island}
  onReorder={(next) => setStops(next)}
  columns={[
    { id: "island", header: "Island", cell: (s) => s.island },
    { id: "time", header: "Departs", cell: (s) => s.time },
  ]}
/>
```

## Props

| Prop         | Type                                 | Default  |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------ | -------- |
| `columns`    | `{ id, header, cell, className? }[]` |          |
| `rows`       | `T[]`                                |          |
| `getId`      | `(row) => string`                    | `row.id` |
| `getName`    | `(row) => string`                    |          |
| `onReorder`  | `(rows, { id, from, to }) => void`   |          |
| `disabled`   | `boolean`                            |          |
| `caption`    | `string`                             |          |
| `classNames` | `{ table, row, handle }`             |          |

## Accessibility

Handles are buttons named "Drag to reorder Malé" with `aria-keyshortcuts`. Keyboard dragging works as in [SortableList](./sortable-list.md); moves are announced.

<!-- docs/listing-pages/editable-data-grid.md -->

# EditableDataGrid

A spreadsheet-like table for quick edits (order lines, stock counts, rates), following the WAI-ARIA grid pattern. Values are validated before they are saved; `onCellChange` can also reject a value (e.g. after a server check).

```tsx
import { EditableDataGrid } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<EditableDataGrid
  aria-label="Supply order"
  rows={lines}
  columns={[
    { id: "item", header: "Item", editable: true, required: true },
    { id: "itemDv", header: "ބައިގެ ނަން", editable: true, thaana: true },
    {
      id: "qty",
      header: "Qty",
      editable: true,
      type: "number",
      align: "end",
      validate: (v) => (Number(v) <= 0 ? "Must be more than 0" : undefined),
    },
    { id: "unit", header: "Unit", editable: true, type: "select", options: units },
    { id: "total", header: "Total", align: "end", accessor: (l) => l.qty * l.price },
  ]}
  onCellChange={async ({ rowId, columnId, value }) => {
    const error = await api.update(rowId, columnId, value)
    if (error) return error // stays in edit mode and shows the message
    setLines(/* … */)
  }}
/>
```

## Props

| Prop           | Type                                                             | Description                                                                                                                                                          |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `columns`      | `EditableColumn[]`                                               | `id`, `header`, `accessor?`, `cell?`, `editable?`, `type?` (`text` \| `number` \| `select`), `options?`, `required?`, `validate?`, `thaana?`, `align?`, `className?` |
| `rows`         | `T[]`                                                            |                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `getRowId`     | `(row) => string`                                                | Default `row.id`                                                                                                                                                     |
| `onCellChange` | `({ rowId, columnId, value, row }) => void \| string \| Promise` | Return an error message to reject                                                                                                                                    |
| `classNames`   | `{ table, header, cell, editor, error }`                         |                                                                                                                                                                      |

## Keyboard

| Key                                                        | Action                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Arrow keys                                                 | Move between cells (left/right follow RTL)                       |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> / <kbd>End</kbd>                           | First / last cell in the row (with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>: in the grid) |
| <kbd>PageUp</kbd> / <kbd>PageDown</kbd>                    | Up / down 10 rows                                                |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>F2</kbd>                           | Edit the cell                                                    |
| Typing                                                     | Start editing with that character                                |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> (editing)                                 | Save and move down                                               |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> / <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Tab</kbd> (editing) | Save and move to the next / previous cell                        |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd> (editing)                                | Cancel                                                           |

## Accessibility

Only one cell is in the tab order (roving `tabindex`). Read-only cells have `aria-readonly`; an invalid edit sets `aria-invalid`, links the message with `aria-describedby`, and announces it. Saves are announced. Thaana columns type Thaana.

<!-- docs/listing-pages/search-results.md -->

# SearchResults

Search results grouped by type (Services, News, Pages), with a count per group and the search words highlighted. `Highlight` marks words in any text.

```tsx
import { Highlight, SearchResults } from "@javaabu/onu"

<SearchResults
  query="passport renewal"
  loading={isFetching}
  groups={[
    { id: "services", label: "Services", total: 12, moreHref: "/search?type=services", items: [{ id: "1", title: "Passport renewal", description: "…", href: "/services/passport" }] },
    { id: "news", label: "News", items: news },
  ]}
/>

<Highlight text="Renew your passport online" query="passport" />
```

## Show more on the same page

Without `onShowMore`, a group's `moreHref` is a "View all" link to another page. With `onShowMore(groupId, group)`, groups with more results than shown (`total` greater than the items, or `hasMore`) get a **Show more** button instead: append the next results to that group's `items`. Return a promise (or set the group's `loadingMore`) to show a spinner on the button meanwhile.

```tsx
const [news, setNews] = useState(firstNews)

<SearchResults
  query={query}
  groups={[{ id: "news", label: "News", total: 48, items: news }]}
  onShowMore={async (groupId) => {
    const next = await api.search(query, { type: groupId, offset: news.length })
    setNews((items) => [...items, ...next])
  }}
/>
```

When the new results arrive, focus moves to the first of them and "3 more News results shown" is announced. If the promise rejects, "Couldn't load more results" is announced and focus stays on the button.

## Props

| Prop          | Type                                                    | Description                                        |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `query`       | `string`                                                | Words to highlight                                 |
| `groups`      | `{ id, label, items, total?, moreHref?, moreLabel?, hasMore?, loadingMore? }[]` | Empty groups are hidden                            |
| `loading`     | `boolean`                                               | Skeletons                                          |
| `onSelect`    | `(item, group) => void`                                 | For items without `href`                           |
| `onShowMore`  | `(groupId, group) => void \| Promise`                   | Show more of a group in place (replaces the link)  |
| `hideSummary` | `boolean`                                               | Hide "12 results for …" (stays for screen readers) |
| `classNames`  | `{ summary, group, heading, item, mark, more }`         | `more`: the "View all" link or "Show more" button  |

Items: `id`, `title`, `description?`, `href?`, `meta?`, `icon?`.

## Accessibility

The results are a section labelled by the summary heading, which is a live region ("12 results for “passport”"). Each group is a labelled section with an `h3`. Matches use `<mark>`. Highlighting is case-insensitive and works for Thaana.

The **Show more** button has `aria-busy` and `aria-disabled` while loading (it keeps focus). When results arrive, focus moves to the first new result, so keyboard and screen reader users continue where the list grew; the loading, loaded and failed states are announced through a polite live region.

| Key                                 | Action                          |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>                      | Move between results and the Show more button |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | Open a result or show more      |

## RTL and Dhivehi

All text comes from the `listing` namespace ("އިތުރު ޚިދުމަތްތައް ދައްކާ"). Results use logical spacing, so icons sit at the inline start in both directions.

---

<!-- docs/listing-pages/load-more.md -->

# LoadMore

A **Load more** button for lists and grids, with "Showing 1–20 of 312" and an announcement of how many items arrived. With `auto` it also loads when it scrolls into view (the button stays as a fallback).

```tsx
import { LoadMore } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<LoadMore
  loaded={items.length}
  total={meta.total}
  onLoadMore={fetchNextPage}
  loading={isFetchingNextPage}
  noun={{ one: "user", other: "users" }}
/>
```

If `onLoadMore` returns a promise, the button shows a spinner until it settles (no `loading` prop needed).

## Props

| Prop         | Type                    | Default          |
| ------------ | ----------------------- | ---------------- |
| `loaded`     | `number`                |                  |
| `total`      | `number`                |                  |
| `hasMore`    | `boolean`               | `loaded < total` |
| `loading`    | `boolean`               |                  |
| `onLoadMore` | `() => void \| Promise` |                  |
| `auto`       | `boolean`               | `false`          |
| `noun`       | `{ one, other }`        | records          |
| `classNames` | `{ button, summary }`   |                  |

## Accessibility

The button has `aria-busy` while loading; "Loaded 20 more users" is announced through a polite live region, and "All 312 users shown" replaces the button at the end.

<!-- docs/listing-pages/filter-condition-builder.md -->

# FilterConditionBuilder

Advanced filters as conditions — "Status is Active **and** Island is one of Malé, Hulhumalé" — on [`react-querybuilder`](https://react-querybuilder.js.org), with Onu controls (native selects, inputs, buttons, checkbox), translations and an RTL-aware layout.

`react-querybuilder` is an optional peer dependency, so the builder has its own entry point:

```bash
pnpm add react-querybuilder
```

```tsx
import { FilterConditionBuilder, formatQuery, type ConditionGroup } from "@javaabu/onu/query-builder"

const [query, setQuery] = useState<ConditionGroup>({ combinator: "and", rules: [] })

<FilterConditionBuilder
  query={query}
  onQueryChange={setQuery}
  fields={[
    { name: "name", label: "Name" },
    { name: "status", label: "Status", valueEditorType: "select", values: [{ name: "active", label: "Active" }] },
    { name: "island", label: "Island", valueEditorType: "multiselect", values: islands },
    { name: "balance", label: "Balance", inputType: "number" },
  ]}
/>

formatQuery(query, "sql")      // or "parameterized", "mongodb", "jsonlogic", …
```

## Props

| Prop                                       | Type                            | Default | Description                 |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------- | ------- | --------------------------- |
| `fields`                                   | `ConditionField[]`              |         | react-querybuilder `Field`s |
| `query` / `defaultQuery` / `onQueryChange` | `ConditionGroup`                |         |                             |
| `allowGroups`                              | `boolean`                       | `true`  | Nested groups               |
| `showNotToggle`                            | `boolean`                       | `false` | "Not" on groups             |
| `disabled`                                 | `boolean`                       |         |                             |
| `classNames`                               | `{ group, header, body, rule }` |         |                             |

Operator and combinator labels come from the `listing` locale namespace.

## Accessibility

Every select and input is labelled (Field, Operator, Value, Match); remove buttons are named "Remove condition" / "Remove group". Nested groups are indented with a start border, which mirrors in RTL. Number, date and other Latin-only inputs are forced `dir="ltr"`.

---

<!-- docs/overlays/modal.md -->

# Modal

A dialog with a simple `title` / `description` / `footer` API, built on shadcn's `Dialog` (Radix). It traps focus, returns focus to whatever opened it, scrolls inside its body when the content is long, and on phones becomes a bottom sheet (default) or a full-screen page.

```tsx
import { Button, Modal, ModalClose } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<Modal
  trigger={<Button>Edit staff member</Button>}
  title="Edit staff member"
  description="Changes are visible to the HR team straight away."
  footer={
    <>
      <ModalClose asChild>
        <Button variant="outline">Cancel</Button>
      </ModalClose>
      <Button onClick={save}>Save changes</Button>
    </>
  }
>
  <FormField label="Full name">
    <TextInput defaultValue="Aishath Ali" />
  </FormField>
</Modal>
```

## Controlled

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)

<Modal open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} title="Transfer MVR 1,250.00">
  …
</Modal>
```

Without a `trigger`, focus still returns to the element that had focus when the modal opened.

## Sizes and phones

`size` sets the width from the `sm` breakpoint up: `sm`, `md` (default), `lg`, `xl` or `full`.

`mobile` sets the presentation below 640px:

| `mobile`          | On phones                                          |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `sheet` (default) | Slides up from the bottom, with safe-area padding  |
| `fullscreen`      | Covers the screen; good for forms and long content |
| `dialog`          | Stays a centred dialog                             |

## Composing

For full control use the parts. They are the same pieces `Modal` uses.

```tsx
import {
  ModalRoot,
  ModalTrigger,
  ModalContent,
  ModalHeader,
  ModalTitle,
  ModalDescription,
  ModalBody,
  ModalFooter,
  ModalClose,
} from "@javaabu/onu"

;<ModalRoot>
  <ModalTrigger asChild>
    <Button>Transfer</Button>
  </ModalTrigger>
  <ModalContent size="sm" mobile="fullscreen">
    <ModalHeader>
      <ModalTitle>Transfer MVR 1,250.00</ModalTitle>
      <ModalDescription>To Mohamed Naseem</ModalDescription>
    </ModalHeader>
    <ModalBody>Transfers after 2 PM are processed the next working day.</ModalBody>
    <ModalFooter>
      <ModalClose asChild>
        <Button variant="outline">Cancel</Button>
      </ModalClose>
      <Button>Transfer</Button>
    </ModalFooter>
  </ModalContent>
</ModalRoot>
```

## Props

| Prop           | Type                                                           | Default   | Description                                         |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `title`        | `ReactNode`                                                    |           | Heading and accessible name (required)              |
| `description`  | `ReactNode`                                                    |           | Text under the title; the accessible description    |
| `hideTitle`    | `boolean`                                                      | `false`   | Hide the title visually, keep it for screen readers |
| `footer`       | `ReactNode`                                                    |           | Actions bar                                         |
| `trigger`      | `ReactNode`                                                    |           | Element that opens the modal (`asChild`)            |
| `open`         | `boolean`                                                      |           | Controlled open state                               |
| `defaultOpen`  | `boolean`                                                      | `false`   | Initial state when uncontrolled                     |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void`                                      |           | Called when the modal opens or closes               |
| `size`         | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'xl' \| 'full'`                       | `'md'`    | Width from `sm` up                                  |
| `mobile`       | `'sheet' \| 'fullscreen' \| 'dialog'`                          | `'sheet'` | Presentation on phones                              |
| `closeButton`  | `boolean`                                                      | `true`    | Show the × button                                   |
| `className`    | `string`                                                       |           | Classes for the panel                               |
| `classNames`   | `{ overlay, header, title, description, body, footer, close }` |           | Classes for each part                               |

Other props (e.g. `onEscapeKeyDown`, `onInteractOutside`) go to Radix `Dialog.Content`; `ref` points at the panel. `modalContentVariants` is exported for reuse.

## Accessibility

- Uses the WAI-ARIA dialog pattern: `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal`, labelled by the title and described by the description.
- Focus moves into the modal on open, is trapped inside, and returns to the opener on close (R14.4).
- The close button is labelled "Close" in the active locale.

| Key                                              | Action                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> / <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Tab</kbd> | Move between controls inside the modal |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd>                                | Close and return focus                 |

## RTL

The panel, header close button and footer actions use logical properties, so they mirror in RTL. Titles and body text follow the page direction; Thaana fields inside use `thaana` as usual.

---

<!-- docs/overlays/confirm-dialog.md -->

# ConfirmDialog

Asks the user to confirm an action, built on shadcn's `AlertDialog`. Use it as a component, or ask from anywhere with the promise-based `useConfirm()` / `confirm()`. It supports a destructive variant, "type the name to confirm", and async actions with a spinner.

## Component

```tsx
import { Button, ConfirmDialog } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<ConfirmDialog
  trigger={<Button variant="destructive">Delete</Button>}
  variant="destructive"
  title="Delete 3 selected users?"
  description="They will be moved to the trash."
  onConfirm={() => api.delete(ids)}
/>
```

When `onConfirm` returns a promise, the confirm button shows a spinner, both buttons are disabled, and the dialog stays open until the promise settles. If it rejects, the dialog stays open and shows the error message.

## Promise API

Mount a `ConfirmProvider` once, near the root of your app:

```tsx
import { ConfirmProvider } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<OnuProvider>
  <ConfirmProvider>
    <App />
  </ConfirmProvider>
</OnuProvider>
```

Then ask from a component with `useConfirm()`, or from anywhere (router guards, stores) with `confirm()`:

```tsx
import { confirm, useConfirm } from "@javaabu/onu"

const ask = useConfirm()

async function onDelete() {
  const ok = await ask({
    title: "Delete Aishath Ali?",
    variant: "destructive",
    onConfirm: () => api.delete(user.id), // optional: spinner until it settles
  })
  if (ok) toast("User deleted")
}

// A string is shorthand for the title.
if (await confirm("Leave without saving?")) router.visit(url)
```

The promise resolves `true` when confirmed and `false` when cancelled (Cancel, Escape). Asking again while a dialog is open resolves the earlier one with `false`. Without a `ConfirmProvider`, `confirm()` falls back to the browser's `window.confirm` with the string title and description.

## Type to confirm

```tsx
<ConfirmDialog variant="destructive" title="Delete Kulhudhuffushi?" confirmText="Kulhudhuffushi" />
```

The confirm button stays disabled until the text matches. If `confirmText` contains Thaana, the field types Thaana from a Latin keyboard.

## Props

`ConfirmDialog` takes the `ConfirmOptions` (also accepted by `confirm()`) plus dialog state:

| Prop                                  | Type                                                                    | Default                    | Description                                  |
| ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `title`                               | `ReactNode`                                                             | "Are you sure?"            | The question                                 |
| `description`                         | `ReactNode`                                                             |                            | What will happen                             |
| `confirmLabel`                        | `ReactNode`                                                             | "Confirm" / "Delete"       | Confirm button text                          |
| `cancelLabel`                         | `ReactNode`                                                             | "Cancel"                   | Cancel button text                           |
| `variant`                             | `'default' \| 'destructive'`                                            | `'default'`                | Destructive colours and a warning icon       |
| `icon`                                | `SemanticIconName \| false`                                             | `warning` when destructive | Icon beside the title                        |
| `confirmText`                         | `string`                                                                |                            | Text the user must type to enable the button |
| `onConfirm`                           | `() => unknown`                                                         |                            | Runs on confirm; may return a promise        |
| `errorMessage`                        | `ReactNode`                                                             | error's message            | Shown when `onConfirm` fails                 |
| `onCancel`                            | `() => void`                                                            |                            | Runs on Cancel / Escape                      |
| `trigger`                             | `ReactNode`                                                             |                            | Element that opens the dialog                |
| `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` |                                                                         |                            | Controlled / uncontrolled state              |
| `children`                            | `ReactNode`                                                             |                            | Extra content under the description          |
| `classNames`                          | `{ content, icon, title, description, input, footer, confirm, cancel }` |                            | Classes for each part                        |

`ConfirmProvider` takes `defaults?: ConfirmOptions` applied to every request.

## Accessibility

- Uses the WAI-ARIA alert dialog pattern (`role="alertdialog"`), labelled by the title and described by the description.
- Focus starts on **Cancel** (the safe choice), or on the text field with `confirmText`, and returns to the opener on close, also when opened with `confirm()`.
- While the action runs, the dialog is `aria-busy` and "Working…" is announced; errors use `role="alert"`.

| Key               | Action                                                   |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>    | Move between Cancel, Confirm and the field               |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd>  | Activate the focused button; confirm from the text field |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd> | Cancel (not while the action is running)                 |

## RTL and Dhivehi

All built-in strings come from the `overlay` and `common` locale namespaces. Buttons and the icon swap sides in RTL.

---

<!-- docs/overlays/slide-over.md -->

# SlideOver

A panel that slides in from the side, for detail views, quick edits and filters. Built on shadcn's `Sheet`. The `side` is **logical** (`start` / `end`), so it flips in RTL. The header and footer stay put while the body scrolls.

```tsx
import { Button, SlideOver, SlideOverClose } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<SlideOver
  trigger={<Button>Edit vessel</Button>}
  title="Edit vessel"
  description="MV Hithadhoo Express, registration P-2041"
  footer={
    <>
      <SlideOverClose asChild>
        <Button variant="outline">Cancel</Button>
      </SlideOverClose>
      <Button onClick={save}>Save</Button>
    </>
  }
>
  <FormField label="Vessel name">
    <TextInput defaultValue="Hithadhoo Express" />
  </FormField>
</SlideOver>
```

## Sides and sizes

- `side="end"` (default) is on the right in LTR and on the left in RTL; `side="start"` is the opposite.
- `size`: `sm`, `md` (default), `lg`, `xl` or `full`. On phones the panel leaves a 2.5rem strip of the page visible (except `full`).

## Composing

`SlideOverRoot`, `SlideOverTrigger`, `SlideOverContent` (`side`, `size`), `SlideOverHeader` (`closeButton`), `SlideOverTitle`, `SlideOverDescription`, `SlideOverBody`, `SlideOverFooter` and `SlideOverClose` are exported. `physicalSide(side, dir)` maps a logical side to `left` / `right`.

## Props

| Prop                                           | Type                                                  | Default | Description                            |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `title`                                        | `ReactNode`                                           |         | Heading and accessible name (required) |
| `description`                                  | `ReactNode`                                           |         | Accessible description                 |
| `footer`                                       | `ReactNode`                                           |         | Sticky action bar                      |
| `trigger`                                      | `ReactNode`                                           |         | Element that opens the panel           |
| `side`                                         | `'start' \| 'end'`                                    | `'end'` | Edge it slides from                    |
| `size`                                         | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'xl' \| 'full'`              | `'md'`  | Width                                  |
| `closeButton`                                  | `boolean`                                             | `true`  | Show the × button                      |
| `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `modal` |                                                       |         | Dialog state                           |
| `className`                                    | `string`                                              |         | Classes for the panel                  |
| `classNames`                                   | `{ header, title, description, body, footer, close }` |         | Classes for each part                  |

`ref` points at the panel. `slideOverVariants` is exported.

## Accessibility

- A modal dialog (`role="dialog"`), labelled by its title. Focus is trapped inside and returns to the opener on close.
- The header and footer respect the safe-area insets on notched phones.

| Key               | Action                 |
| ----------------- | ---------------------- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>    | Move between controls  |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd> | Close and return focus |

## RTL

Use `start` / `end`, never left/right: the panel and its slide animation flip with the direction.

---

<!-- docs/overlays/bottom-sheet.md -->

# BottomSheet

A pull-up panel anchored to the bottom of the screen. Drag it down to dismiss, drag between snap points, or use the close / expand buttons and <kbd>Escape</kbd>, so the gesture is never the only way. Built on shadcn's `Drawer` (vaul), kept behind Onu's own API so the library can be swapped later (R4.3).

```tsx
import { BottomSheet, BottomSheetClose, Button } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<BottomSheet
  trigger={<Button>Filter by island</Button>}
  title="Filter by island"
  footer={
    <BottomSheetClose asChild>
      <Button>Apply</Button>
    </BottomSheetClose>
  }
>
  …
</BottomSheet>
```

## Snap points

```tsx
<BottomSheet title="Malé → Hulhumalé ferry" snapPoints={[0.4, 1]}>
  …
</BottomSheet>
```

Snap points are fractions of the screen height (`0.4`) or pixel strings (`"320px"`), smallest first. The sheet opens at the first one. An expand/collapse button in the header switches between the first and last. Control it with `activeSnapPoint` / `onActiveSnapPointChange`.

## Not dismissible

```tsx
<BottomSheet open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} dismissible={false} closeButton={false} title="Terms" footer={…} />
```

## Composing

`BottomSheetRoot`, `BottomSheetTrigger`, `BottomSheetContent` (`size`, `handle`, `snapping`), `BottomSheetHeader` (`closeButton`, `expandButton`), `BottomSheetTitle`, `BottomSheetDescription`, `BottomSheetBody`, `BottomSheetFooter` and `BottomSheetClose` are exported.

## Props

| Prop                                                             | Type                                                                  | Default | Description                                       |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `title`                                                          | `ReactNode`                                                           |         | Heading and accessible name (required)            |
| `hideTitle`                                                      | `boolean`                                                             | `false` | Hide the title visually                           |
| `description`                                                    | `ReactNode`                                                           |         | Accessible description                            |
| `footer`                                                         | `ReactNode`                                                           |         | Action bar                                        |
| `trigger`                                                        | `ReactNode`                                                           |         | Element that opens the sheet                      |
| `snapPoints`                                                     | `(number \| string)[]`                                                |         | Heights to snap to                                |
| `activeSnapPoint`, `defaultSnapPoint`, `onActiveSnapPointChange` |                                                                       |         | Snap point state                                  |
| `dismissible`                                                    | `boolean`                                                             | `true`  | Allow drag, outside click and Escape to close     |
| `handleOnly`                                                     | `boolean`                                                             | `false` | Only the handle starts a drag                     |
| `handle`                                                         | `boolean`                                                             | `true`  | Show the drag handle                              |
| `closeButton`                                                    | `boolean`                                                             | `true`  | Show the × button                                 |
| `size`                                                           | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'full'`                                      | `'md'`  | Max width on wider screens (full width on phones) |
| `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `modal`                   |                                                                       |         | Dialog state                                      |
| `classNames`                                                     | `{ handle, header, title, description, body, footer, close, expand }` |         | Classes for each part                             |

## Accessibility

- A modal dialog labelled by its title; focus is trapped and returns to the opener on close.
- The drag handle is decorative (`aria-hidden`); the close and expand buttons are the accessible alternatives (R3.27). The expand button exposes `aria-expanded`.
- The content is padded for the home indicator (`env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`, R3.30).

| Key               | Action                   |
| ----------------- | ------------------------ |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>    | Move between controls    |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd> | Close (when dismissible) |

## RTL

The header buttons sit at the inline end and swap sides in RTL. Built-in labels ("Close", "Expand", "Collapse") are translated.

---

<!-- docs/overlays/popover-panel.md -->

# PopoverPanel

A non-modal panel anchored to a trigger, for small forms, filters and extra details: Onu's simple-API **popover**. Built on shadcn's `Popover`; the primitive parts (`Popover`, `PopoverTrigger`, `PopoverContent`, …) are also exported for custom layouts. With `mobile="sheet"` it becomes a [bottom sheet](./bottom-sheet.md) on phones (R3.20).

```tsx
import { Button, PopoverPanel } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<PopoverPanel
  trigger={<Button variant="outline">Set budget</Button>}
  title="Monthly budget"
  closeButton
  footer={<Button size="sm">Save</Button>}
>
  <FormField label="Amount (MVR)">
    <TextInput inputMode="decimal" />
  </FormField>
</PopoverPanel>
```

## On phones

```tsx
<PopoverPanel mobile="sheet" trigger={<Button>Filters</Button>} title="Filters">
  …
</PopoverPanel>
```

Below 768px this renders a `BottomSheet` with the same title, content and footer. `title` is required for the sheet.

## Props

| Prop                                  | Type                                                  | Default     | Description                               |
| ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `trigger`                             | `ReactNode`                                           |             | Element that toggles the panel (required) |
| `title`                               | `ReactNode`                                           |             | Heading; the panel's accessible name      |
| `description`                         | `ReactNode`                                           |             | Accessible description                    |
| `footer`                              | `ReactNode`                                           |             | Actions, aligned to the inline end        |
| `closeButton`                         | `boolean`                                             | `false`     | Show a × button                           |
| `mobile`                              | `'popover' \| 'sheet'`                                | `'popover'` | Presentation on phones                    |
| `side`, `align`, `sideOffset`, …      |                                                       |             | Radix `Popover.Content` positioning props |
| `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` |                                                       |             | Open state                                |
| `className`                           | `string`                                              |             | Classes for the panel                     |
| `classNames`                          | `{ header, title, description, body, footer, close }` |             | Classes for each part                     |

## Accessibility

- The panel is a non-modal `dialog` labelled by its title, and the trigger exposes `aria-expanded` / `aria-controls`.
- Focus moves into the panel on open and back to the trigger on close. Clicking outside closes it.

| Key                                 | Action                  |
| ----------------------------------- | ----------------------- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | Toggle from the trigger |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>                      | Move through the panel  |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd>                   | Close and return focus  |

## RTL

`side="left"` / `"right"` are physical (Radix); prefer `top` / `bottom` with `align="start" | "end"`, which follow the direction.

---

<!-- docs/overlays/tip.md -->

# Tip

A **tooltip** that also works on touch screens. With a mouse it shows on hover, with a keyboard on focus, and on touch screens on a tap or a long press, because nothing may depend on hover alone (R3.26). Built on shadcn's `Tooltip`; the primitive parts are also exported.

```tsx
import { Button, Icon, Tip } from "@javaabu/onu"

// An ⓘ button labelled "More information" (tap to show on touch).
<Tip content="A 10% service charge applies to bookings made in resorts." />

// Describe a control. It has its own action, so on touch the tip opens with a long press.
<Tip content="Print receipt">
  <Button size="icon" aria-label="Print receipt" onClick={print}>
    <Icon name="print" />
  </Button>
</Tip>
```

:::caution
A tip must never be the only place for information. Repeat anything important in visible text, and give icon buttons an `aria-label` (the tip adds a description, not a name).
:::

## Touch behaviour

| `touch`      | On touch screens                                                                                   |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `tap`        | A tap toggles the tip (default for the ⓘ button and plain triggers)                                |
| `long-press` | A tap runs the trigger's action; a 0.5s press shows the tip (default when the child has `onClick`) |

Tapping elsewhere or pressing <kbd>Escape</kbd> closes it.

## Props

| Prop                                  | Type                    | Default  | Description                          |
| ------------------------------------- | ----------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `content`                             | `ReactNode`             |          | Tip text (required)                  |
| `children`                            | `ReactElement`          | ⓘ button | Trigger; must accept a ref and props |
| `touch`                               | `'tap' \| 'long-press'` | auto     | How the tip opens on touch           |
| `delayDuration`                       | `number`                | `300`    | Hover delay in ms                    |
| `disabled`                            | `boolean`               | `false`  | Render only the trigger              |
| `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` |                         |          | Open state                           |
| `side`, `align`, `sideOffset`, …      |                         |          | Radix `Tooltip.Content` props        |
| `className`                           | `string`                |          | Classes for the tip                  |

## Accessibility

- The tip has `role="tooltip"` and describes the trigger (`aria-describedby`) while open.
- The default ⓘ trigger is a real button with a translated label and a 44px touch target on coarse pointers.

| Key               | Action                    |
| ----------------- | ------------------------- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>    | Focus the trigger to show |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd> | Hide                      |

## RTL and Dhivehi

The "More information" label is translated, and `side="left"` / `"right"` follow Radix's physical sides; prefer `top` / `bottom`.

---

<!-- docs/overlays/action-menu.md -->

# ActionMenu

A **dropdown menu** of actions built from an `items` array, on shadcn's `DropdownMenu` (Radix). Items take semantic icons, shortcut hints, destructive styling, links, checkbox and radio items, submenus, and an optional confirmation step. The primitive parts (`DropdownMenu`, `DropdownMenuItem`, …) are also exported.

```tsx
import { ActionMenu, type MenuItem } from "@javaabu/onu"

const items: MenuItem[] = [
  { label: "View", icon: "eye", href: `/users/${user.id}` },
  { label: "Edit", icon: "edit", shortcut: "⌘E", onSelect: edit },
  { label: "Archive", icon: "archive", hidden: !can("archive") },
  { type: "separator" },
  {
    type: "sub",
    label: "Move to island",
    icon: "map-pin",
    items: islands.map((island) => ({ label: island.name, onSelect: () => move(island) })),
  },
  { type: "separator" },
  {
    label: "Delete",
    icon: "trash",
    variant: "destructive",
    confirm: { title: `Delete ${user.name}?`, variant: "destructive" },
    onSelect: remove,
  },
]

;<ActionMenu items={items} />
```

Without a `trigger`, a ⋯ icon button labelled "More actions" opens the menu. Pass `label` to name it per row (e.g. "Actions for Aishath Ali").

## Item types

| `type`           | Fields                                                                                      |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `item` (default) | `label`, `icon`, `shortcut`, `variant`, `href`, `confirm`, `onSelect`, `disabled`, `hidden` |
| `checkbox`       | `label`, `icon`, `shortcut`, `checked`, `onCheckedChange` (menu stays open)                 |
| `radio`          | `label` (heading), `value`, `onValueChange`, `options: { value, label, icon, disabled }[]`  |
| `sub`            | `label`, `icon`, `items`                                                                    |
| `group`          | `label`, `items`                                                                            |
| `label`          | `label`                                                                                     |
| `separator`      |                                                                                             |

`hidden` items are left out (list only what the user can do, §25.6), and separators left dangling are dropped. `href` items render through the `OnuProvider` link component (Inertia, Next). `confirm` (options or a title string) closes the menu, asks with [`confirm()`](./confirm-dialog.md), and runs `onSelect` only when confirmed; mount a `ConfirmProvider` for the styled dialog.

## Props

| Prop                                           | Type                           | Default        | Description                               |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | -------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `items`                                        | `MenuItem[]`                   |                | Menu entries (required)                   |
| `trigger`                                      | `ReactNode`                    | ⋯ button       | Element that opens the menu               |
| `label`                                        | `string`                       | "More actions" | Accessible name of the default trigger    |
| `align`                                        | `'start' \| 'center' \| 'end'` | `'end'`        | Alignment to the trigger                  |
| `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `modal` |                                |                | Menu state                                |
| `className`                                    | `string`                       |                | Classes for the menu                      |
| `classNames`                                   | `{ trigger, item }`            |                | Classes for the default trigger and items |

Other props go to Radix `DropdownMenu.Content` (`side`, `sideOffset`, …).

## Accessibility

Follows the WAI-ARIA menu button pattern. Focus returns to the trigger when the menu closes. Items are at least 44px tall on touch screens.

| Key                                                | Action                              |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> / <kbd>↓</kbd> | Open from the trigger               |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> / <kbd>↓</kbd>                        | Move between items                  |
| <kbd>→</kbd> (LTR) / <kbd>←</kbd> (RTL)            | Open a submenu                      |
| <kbd>←</kbd> (LTR) / <kbd>→</kbd> (RTL)            | Close a submenu                     |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd>                                   | Choose                              |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd>                                  | Close and return focus              |
| Letters                                            | Jump to an item by its first letter |

## RTL

Submenus open toward the inline end (left in RTL), the submenu chevron mirrors, and shortcut hints keep their Latin order.

---

<!-- docs/overlays/context-action-menu.md -->

# ContextActionMenu

A **context menu** (right-click menu) built from the same `items` as [`ActionMenu`](./action-menu.md), on shadcn's `ContextMenu` (Radix). On touch screens it opens with a long press. The primitive parts (`ContextMenu`, `ContextMenuItem`, …) are also exported.

```tsx
import { ActionMenu, ContextActionMenu } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<ContextActionMenu items={fileActions} asChild>
  <div tabIndex={0} className="…">
    permit-2041.pdf
    <ActionMenu items={fileActions} label="Actions for permit-2041.pdf" />
  </div>
</ContextActionMenu>
```

:::caution
Context menus are hard to discover and need a mouse, a long press or a special key. Always offer the same actions somewhere visible too, such as an `ActionMenu` on the row.
:::

## Props

| Prop           | Type                      | Default | Description                                                    |
| -------------- | ------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `items`        | `MenuItem[]`              |         | Menu entries, as for `ActionMenu` (required)                   |
| `children`     | `ReactNode`               |         | The area that opens the menu                                   |
| `asChild`      | `boolean`                 | `false` | Use the child as the area instead of wrapping it in a `<span>` |
| `disabled`     | `boolean`                 | `false` | Turn the menu off                                              |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` |         | Called when the menu opens or closes                           |
| `className`    | `string`                  |         | Classes for the menu                                           |
| `classNames`   | `{ trigger, item }`       |         | Classes for the area and items                                 |

## Accessibility

Follows the WAI-ARIA menu pattern once open. To open it from the keyboard, make the area focusable (`tabIndex={0}`) and press the <kbd>Menu</kbd> key or <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>F10</kbd>.

| Key                                               | Action                   |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| <kbd>Menu</kbd> / <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>F10</kbd> | Open at the focused area |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> / <kbd>↓</kbd>                       | Move between items       |
| <kbd>→</kbd> (LTR) / <kbd>←</kbd> (RTL)           | Open a submenu           |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd>                                  | Choose                   |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd>                                 | Close                    |

## Touch

A long press (about 0.7s) opens the menu at the finger. The area suppresses the iOS link callout so the press isn't hijacked.

## RTL

Submenus open toward the inline end and the chevron mirrors in RTL.

---

<!-- docs/overlays/command-palette.md -->

# CommandPalette

A <kbd>⌘</kbd><kbd>K</kbd> / <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>K</kbd> command palette for jumping to pages, records and commands from the keyboard. Built on shadcn's `Command` (cmdk) inside an Onu [`Modal`](./modal.md). Static groups filter instantly; an async `search` is debounced and aborts stale requests. It remembers recent choices, supports Thaana input, and announces result counts.

```tsx
import { CommandPalette, type CommandPaletteGroup } from "@javaabu/onu"

const groups: CommandPaletteGroup[] = [
  {
    heading: "Pages",
    items: [
      { id: "dashboard", label: "Dashboard", icon: "home", href: "/" },
      { id: "staff", label: "Staff", icon: "users", href: "/staff", keywords: ["employees", "މުވައްޒަފުން"] },
    ],
  },
  {
    heading: "Actions",
    items: [{ id: "new-permit", label: "New permit", icon: "add", shortcut: "⌘N", onSelect: createPermit }],
  },
]

;<CommandPalette
  groups={groups}
  search={(query, { signal }) =>
    fetch(`/api/search?q=${encodeURIComponent(query)}`, { signal })
      .then((r) => r.json())
      .then((json) => json.data.map((u) => ({ id: `user-${u.id}`, label: u.name, href: `/users/${u.id}` })))
  }
  searchHeading="Staff"
  onNavigate={(href) => router.visit(href)}
/>
```

Mount it once (e.g. in your layout). The shortcut toggles it from anywhere; you can also pass a `trigger` or control `open`.

## Searching

- Static items match when every word of the query appears in `value` (or the string `label`) or `keywords`. Case and Latin accents are ignored ("male" finds "Malé").
- `search(query, { signal })` runs after `debounce` ms (default 250) once the query has `minQueryLength` characters (default 1). A newer query, or closing the palette, aborts the earlier request through `signal`, and late answers are ignored (R16.5).
- Return items (shown under `searchHeading`) or groups. Errors show "Search failed" with a **Retry** button.

## Recent items

Chosen items are remembered in `localStorage` (`recent={{ storageKey, max }}`, default 5) and shown under "Recent" when the query is empty. Pass `recent={false}` to turn it off. Storage failures are ignored.

## Props

| Prop                                  | Type                                                | Default            | Description                         |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ | ----------------------------------- |
| `groups`                              | `CommandPaletteGroup[]`                             | `[]`               | Static items, filtered locally      |
| `search`                              | `(query, { signal }) => Promise<Item[] \| Group[]>` |                    | Async search                        |
| `searchHeading`                       | `ReactNode`                                         |                    | Heading for async items             |
| `debounce`                            | `number`                                            | `250`              | Debounce in ms                      |
| `minQueryLength`                      | `number`                                            | `1`                | Minimum query length for `search`   |
| `recent`                              | `boolean \| { storageKey?, max? }`                  | `true`             | Remember chosen items               |
| `shortcut`                            | `string \| false`                                   | `'k'`              | Key used with ⌘ / Ctrl              |
| `thaana`                              | `boolean \| ThaanaOptions`                          |                    | Type Thaana in the search box       |
| `placeholder`                         | `string`                                            | translated         | Search box placeholder              |
| `title`                               | `string`                                            | "Command palette"  | Accessible name                     |
| `emptyMessage`                        | `(query) => ReactNode`                              | "No results for …" | Empty state                         |
| `footer`                              | `boolean`                                           | `true`             | Key hints (hidden on touch screens) |
| `onNavigate`                          | `(href) => void`                                    | `location.assign`  | Router for `href` items             |
| `onItemSelect`                        | `(item) => void`                                    |                    | Called for every chosen item        |
| `closeOnSelect`                       | `boolean`                                           | `true`             | Close after choosing                |
| `trigger`                             | `ReactNode`                                         |                    | Element that opens the palette      |
| `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` |                                                     |                    | Open state                          |
| `classNames`                          | `{ input, list, group, item, empty, footer }`       |                    | Classes for each part               |

`CommandPaletteItem`: `{ id, label, value?, keywords?, icon?, description?, shortcut?, href?, onSelect?, disabled? }`. `matchesCommandItem` and `normalizeSearch` are exported for custom filtering.

## Accessibility

- A modal dialog with a combobox and listbox (cmdk); the active option is tracked with `aria-activedescendant`.
- "Searching…", the result count and "Search failed" are announced through a polite live region.
- Focus returns to whatever had it before the palette opened, including when opened with the shortcut.
- On phones it is full screen with a close button.

| Key                                                      | Action                       |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| <kbd>⌘</kbd>+<kbd>K</kbd> / <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>K</kbd> | Open or close                |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> / <kbd>↓</kbd>                              | Move between results (wraps) |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd>                                         | Choose                       |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd>                                        | Close                        |

## RTL and Thaana

With `thaana`, the search box types Thaana from a Latin keyboard (with a toggle). Add Dhivehi names to `keywords` so both scripts find an item. Shortcut hints keep their Latin order in RTL.

---

<!-- docs/loading/spinner.md -->

# Spinner

A spinning loading indicator with a screen-reader label. It is a polite live region (`role="status"`), so the label ("Loading…" by default, translated) is announced when it appears.

```tsx
import { Spinner } from "@javaabu/onu"

<Spinner />
<Spinner size="lg" tone="primary" />
<Spinner showLabel label="Fetching permits…" />

<Button disabled={saving}>
  {saving ? <Spinner label="Saving…" /> : null}
  Save
</Button>
```

This replaces the shadcn `Spinner` exported from the package root. The vendored primitive is still available from `@javaabu/onu/primitives`. Differences: `className` and `ref` go to the wrapping `<span>` (use `size` or `classNames.icon` to size the icon), and the label is translated and actually exposed to screen readers.

## Props

| Prop         | Type                                   | Default     | Description                                 |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `size`       | `'xs' \| 'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'xl'` | `'sm'`      | Icon size (12–32px)                         |
| `tone`       | `'current' \| 'primary' \| 'muted'`    | `'current'` | Colour (`current` inherits the text colour) |
| `label`      | `ReactNode`                            | "Loading…"  | Screen-reader text                          |
| `showLabel`  | `boolean`                              | `false`     | Show the label beside the spinner           |
| `className`  | `string`                               |             | Classes for the root `<span>`               |
| `classNames` | `{ icon, label }`                      |             | Classes for the parts                       |

Other `<span>` props and `ref` go to the root. `spinnerVariants` is exported.

## Accessibility

- `role="status"` with a visually hidden label; the icon is `aria-hidden`.
- Don't put a spinner where nothing is loading, and don't stack several announcements: inside a button that already changes its text to "Saving…", pass the same `label`.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the icon stops spinning; the label still tells users that something is loading.

## RTL

The spinner is non-directional and doesn't mirror. With `showLabel`, the label sits at the inline end.

---

<!-- docs/loading/skeleton.md -->

# Skeleton presets

Ready-made skeletons for the most common shapes: `SkeletonText`, `SkeletonCard` and `SkeletonTable`. They are built from shadcn's `Skeleton` (also exported for custom shapes) and use the `muted` token, so they work in light and dark mode.

```tsx
import { SkeletonCard, SkeletonTable, SkeletonText } from "@javaabu/onu"

<SkeletonText lines={3} />
<SkeletonCard avatar lines={3} actions={2} />
<SkeletonTable rows={10} columns={5} selectable />
```

## Props

### SkeletonText

| Prop         | Type                   | Default        | Description                                |
| ------------ | ---------------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `lines`      | `number`               | `3`            | Number of lines                            |
| `widths`     | `string[]`             | 100%, last 60% | Widths per line (cycled)                   |
| `size`       | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'`         | Line height, to match the text it replaces |
| `classNames` | `{ line }`             |                | Classes for each line                      |

### SkeletonCard

| Prop         | Type                                     | Default | Description                   |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------- |
| `media`      | `boolean`                                | `false` | 16:9 image area at the top    |
| `avatar`     | `boolean`                                | `false` | Round avatar beside the title |
| `lines`      | `number`                                 | `2`     | Body lines                    |
| `actions`    | `number`                                 | `0`     | Button-shaped bars at the end |
| `classNames` | `{ media, avatar, title, line, action }` |         | Classes for each part         |

### SkeletonTable

| Prop         | Type                    | Default | Description           |
| ------------ | ----------------------- | ------- | --------------------- |
| `rows`       | `number`                | `5`     | Body rows             |
| `columns`    | `number`                | `4`     | Columns               |
| `header`     | `boolean`               | `true`  | Header row            |
| `selectable` | `boolean`               | `false` | Checkbox column       |
| `classNames` | `{ header, row, cell }` |         | Classes for each part |

The table is a container (`@container/skeleton-table`): in narrow containers only the first two columns show, as tables turn into cards on phones (R3.20).

All three accept `label` (screen-reader text, default "Loading…"), `className` and other `<div>` props.

## Accessibility

Each preset is one `role="status"` region named "Loading…" (translated); the shapes inside are `aria-hidden`, so screen readers hear one announcement rather than a list of empty boxes. Put `aria-busy="true"` on the region being loaded if it stays mounted. The pulse animation stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## RTL

Shapes use logical properties and fill from the inline start, so they mirror in RTL.

---

<!-- docs/loading/placeholder-input.md -->

# PlaceholderInput

A skeleton shaped like a form field (label, control and optional help text), for forms whose values are still loading. It follows the same stacked/inline [label layout](../form-scaffolding/form-field.md) as `FormField`, so the page doesn't jump when the real fields arrive.

```tsx
import { FormField, PlaceholderInput, TextInput } from "@javaabu/onu"

function ProfileForm({ user, loading }: Props) {
  if (loading) {
    return (
      <>
        <PlaceholderInput />
        <PlaceholderInput control="textarea" help />
        <PlaceholderInput control="switch" />
      </>
    )
  }
  return (
    <FormField label="Full name">
      <TextInput defaultValue={user.name} />
    </FormField>
  )
}
```

## Props

| Prop          | Type                                                          | Default         | Description                    |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `control`     | `'input' \| 'textarea' \| 'select' \| 'checkbox' \| 'switch'` | `'input'`       | Shape of the control           |
| `label`       | `boolean`                                                     | `true`          | Show a label placeholder       |
| `help`        | `boolean`                                                     | `false`         | Show a help-text placeholder   |
| `labelLayout` | `'stacked' \| 'inline'`                                       | form / provider | Label layout, like `FormField` |
| `srLabel`     | `string`                                                      | "Loading…"      | Screen-reader text             |
| `className`   | `string`                                                      |                 | Classes for the root           |
| `classNames`  | `{ label, control, help }`                                    |                 | Classes for each part          |

Checkboxes and switches keep their label-beside-control shape in both layouts (R3.34). Inline layout falls back to stacked in narrow containers, like `FormField`. Controls are 44px tall on touch screens, matching the real inputs.

## Accessibility

Each placeholder is a `role="status"` region named "Loading…" (translated) with `aria-hidden` shapes. When many fields load together, consider one `LoadingOverlay` or a single status message for the form instead.

## RTL

The label column sits on the inline start (right in RTL), as in `FormField`.

---

<!-- docs/loading/loading-overlay.md -->

# LoadingOverlay

Covers a container (a card, table or form) while it loads or saves. The container gets `aria-busy`, the content underneath becomes `inert`, and a status message is announced. The overlay only appears after a short `delay`, so quick loads don't flicker.

```tsx
import { LoadingOverlay } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<LoadingOverlay loading={isFetching} message="Refreshing payments…" className="rounded-xl">
  <PaymentsCard />
</LoadingOverlay>
```

Full screen, e.g. while submitting an application:

```tsx
<LoadingOverlay loading={submitting} fullScreen message="Submitting…" />
```

## Props

| Prop         | Type                                     | Default | Description                                     |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `loading`    | `boolean`                                |         | Show the overlay (required)                     |
| `message`    | `ReactNode`                              |         | Visible text under the spinner                  |
| `delay`      | `number`                                 | `200`   | Wait (ms) before showing; `0` shows immediately |
| `fullScreen` | `boolean`                                | `false` | Cover the viewport instead of the container     |
| `blur`       | `boolean`                                | `true`  | Blur the content underneath                     |
| `className`  | `string`                                 |         | Classes for the container                       |
| `classNames` | `{ content, overlay, spinner, message }` |         | Classes for each part                           |

The root is a `relative` `<div>`; other `<div>` props pass through. `useDelayedFlag(value, delay)` is exported for your own delayed indicators.

## Accessibility

- `aria-busy` is set on the container while `loading` is true.
- While the overlay is visible, the content is `inert` (not focusable or clickable).
- A `role="status"` region, always mounted, announces the message (or "Loading…") when the overlay appears.

## RTL

The overlay is centred and direction-neutral; messages follow the page direction.

---

<!-- docs/loading/page-progress.md -->

# PageProgress

A thin bar at the top of the page that shows a navigation or long request is in progress, like NProgress. Control it with `pageProgress.start()` / `done()` or the `usePageProgress(loading)` hook. It grows from the inline start (right to left in RTL) and drops its animations under reduced motion.

Mount it once, e.g. in your layout:

```tsx
import { PageProgress } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<PageProgress />
```

## Hooking up a router

```ts
import { router } from "@inertiajs/react"
import { pageProgress } from "@javaabu/onu"

router.on("start", () => pageProgress.start())
router.on("finish", () => pageProgress.done())
```

Or from a component, while something loads:

```tsx
import { usePageProgress } from "@javaabu/onu"

function Report() {
  const { isLoading } = useQuery(…)
  usePageProgress(isLoading)
  …
}
```

`start()` calls nest: the bar finishes after the same number of `done()` calls (`done(true)` forces it). `set(0.5)` and `inc(0.1)` move it manually. Use `createPageProgress()` for a separate bar (e.g. inside a panel with `position="absolute"`).

## Props

| Prop         | Type                                                             | Default        | Description                                     |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `controller` | `PageProgressController`                                         | `pageProgress` | Which controller to follow                      |
| `height`     | `number`                                                         | `3`            | Thickness in px                                 |
| `delay`      | `number`                                                         | `150`          | Wait (ms) before showing; fast loads never show |
| `position`   | `'fixed' \| 'absolute'`                                          | `'fixed'`      | Top of the viewport or of the nearest container |
| `color`      | `'primary' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'destructive' \| 'info'` | `'primary'`    | Bar colour                                      |
| `className`  | `string`                                                         |                | Classes for the track                           |
| `classNames` | `{ bar }`                                                        |                | Classes for the bar                             |

## API

| Export                                        | Description                                                                                     |
| --------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pageProgress`                                | Shared controller: `start`, `done(force?)`, `set(0–1)`, `inc(amount?)`, `getState`, `subscribe` |
| `createPageProgress({ trickleMs, finishMs })` | Create a separate controller                                                                    |
| `usePageProgress(loading, controller?)`       | Show the bar while `loading` is true                                                            |
| `usePageProgressState(controller?)`           | Read `{ active, value }`                                                                        |

## Accessibility

The bar is a `role="progressbar"` named "Loading page" (translated) with `aria-valuenow`. It is decorative for sighted users, so also show a real loading state (skeleton, overlay) for the content being loaded. Width transitions are disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## RTL

The bar is anchored with `inset-inline-start`, so it fills from the right in RTL (R11.6).

---

<!-- docs/loading/progress-bar.md -->

# ProgressBar

A determinate or indeterminate progress bar with an optional label and value text, in semantic colours. Built on Radix `Progress` (shadcn's `Progress` is still exported as a primitive). It fills from the inline start, so it is mirrored in RTL.

```tsx
import { ProgressBar } from "@javaabu/onu"

<ProgressBar label="Uploading permit-2041.pdf" value={40} />
<ProgressBar label="Files imported" value={7} max={12} formatValue={(v, max) => `${v} of ${max}`} color="info" />
<ProgressBar label="Leave balance used" value={96} color="destructive" size="sm" />

// Indeterminate: no value.
<ProgressBar label="Preparing export…" />
```

## Props

| Prop          | Type                                                                        | Default     | Description                                       |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`       | `number \| null`                                                            |             | Current value; omit for indeterminate             |
| `max`         | `number`                                                                    | `100`       | Maximum                                           |
| `label`       | `ReactNode`                                                                 |             | Visible label; also the accessible name           |
| `showValue`   | `boolean`                                                                   | with label  | Show the value text                               |
| `formatValue` | `(value, max) => string`                                                    | percent     | Custom value text, also used for `aria-valuetext` |
| `color`       | `'primary' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'destructive' \| 'info' \| 'muted'` | `'primary'` | Indicator colour                                  |
| `size`        | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'`                                                      | `'md'`      | Track height                                      |
| `aria-label`  | `string`                                                                    | "Progress"  | Name when there is no `label`                     |
| `className`   | `string`                                                                    |             | Classes for the wrapper                           |
| `classNames`  | `{ header, label, value, track, indicator }`                                |             | Classes for each part                             |

Values are clamped to `0…max`. The percent text uses the active locale's number format. `ref` points at the track (`role="progressbar"`). `progressTrackVariants` and `progressIndicatorVariants` are exported.

## Accessibility

- `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemax` and `aria-valuetext` (e.g. "40%" or your `formatValue` text); indeterminate bars omit the value.
- The bar is named by its visible label (`aria-labelledby`) or `aria-label`.
- Colour is never the only signal: pair warning colours with a label or value text (R14.6).
- The indeterminate sweep uses the Web Animations API and is replaced by a static bar under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## RTL

The indicator fills from the inline start (right in RTL), and the indeterminate sweep runs in the reading direction. Custom value text is isolated (`dir="auto"`) so "7 of 12" stays in order in RTL.

---

<!-- docs/layout-and-navigation/app-layout.md -->

# AppLayout

The application shell: a **Skip to content** link, the sidebar, a header, the main content, an optional footer and an optional phone **bottom navigation**. It wraps shadcn's `SidebarProvider`, so the sidebar collapses to icons (or off-canvas) on desktop, becomes an off-canvas drawer below 768px, and sits on the inline start in RTL.

```tsx
import { AppHeader, AppLayout, AppSidebar, BottomNav, Logo, UserProfile } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<AppLayout
  sidebar={
    <AppSidebar
      groups={groups}
      currentHref={url}
      header={<Logo src="/logo.svg" alt="Onu" text="Onu" />}
      footer={<UserProfile name="Aishath Shifa" subtitle="Admin" onSignOut={signOut} />}
    />
  }
  header={<AppHeader sidebarTrigger actions={<NotificationCenter notifications={items} />} />}
  bottomNav={<BottomNav items={quickLinks} currentHref={url} />}
>
  {children}
</AppLayout>
```

With Inertia, pass `usePage().url` as `currentHref` and set `OnuProvider linkComponent={Link}` once.

## Panel (the default)

`variant="panel"` is Proton Mail's shell: the sidebar and the header sit on the **app shell colour** (a warm grey, `#f5f4f2` light and `#16141c` dark), and the page is a **white panel** with a 12px rounded top-start corner and a 1px shell line on its top and start edges (logical properties, so it mirrors in RTL; below 768px the panel fills the screen). Inside it, `AppHeader`, `AppSidebar`, `PageTitle` and `ListingPage` pick their shell looks by default: the header on the shell colour with a wide rounded search, Proton's sidebar, Ant's PageHeader band and the ProTable card.

- `background="layout"` gives the panel Ant's light layout grey (`#f5f5f5`, `#141414` dark) for dashboards made of cards.
- `breadcrumbs` (a `BreadcrumbsItem[]`) is the page's trail. A page header band shows it; pages without one show it above the content.
- `variant="flat"` is the previous look: the content fills the body, the header is bordered and the sidebar keeps its edge line.

The shell colours come from the semantic shell tokens (`--shell`, `--shell-foreground`, `--shell-border`, `--shell-field`, `--shell-hover`, `--shell-active`, `--shell-weak`) with Proton's values as fallbacks, so they follow a theme that defines them. See [Theming](../guides/theming.md).

## Layout

- `<main id="main-content" tabindex="-1">` holds the page (inside the panel, with the footer). The skip link targets it, so keyboard users can jump past the navigation.
- With `bottomNav`, the main area gets extra bottom padding (plus the safe-area inset) on phones so nothing hides behind the bar.
- The sidebar state is stored in a cookie by shadcn (`sidebar_state`); read it on the server and pass `defaultSidebarOpen` to avoid a flash.

## Props

| Prop                  | Type                                        | Default          | Description                                          |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `sidebar`             | `ReactNode`                                 |                  | Usually an `AppSidebar`                              |
| `header`              | `ReactNode`                                 |                  | Usually an `AppHeader` with `sidebarTrigger`         |
| `footer`              | `ReactNode`                                 |                  | Footer inside the content column                     |
| `bottomNav`           | `ReactNode`                                 |                  | Phone bottom navigation, usually a `BottomNav`       |
| `defaultSidebarOpen`  | `boolean`                                   | `true`           | Initial desktop sidebar state                        |
| `sidebarOpen`         | `boolean`                                   |                  | Controlled desktop sidebar state                     |
| `onSidebarOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void`                   |                  | Called when the sidebar opens or closes              |
| `skipLink`            | `boolean`                                   | `true`           | Render a skip link first                             |
| `mainId`              | `string`                                    | `"main-content"` | Id of `<main>` (the skip link target)                |
| `contentWidth`        | `'full' \| 'wide' \| 'default' \| 'narrow'` | `'full'`         | Maximum width of the content                         |
| `variant`             | `'panel' \| 'flat'`                         | `'panel'`        | Content on a white panel against the shell, or flat  |
| `background`          | `'default' \| 'layout'`                     | `'default'`      | Panel background: the page colour or the layout grey |
| `breadcrumbs`         | `BreadcrumbsItem[]`                         |                  | The page's trail (shown by the page header band)     |
| `classNames`          | `{ body, panel, main, content, breadcrumbs }` |                | Classes for the content column, panel, `<main>`, wrapper and trail |
| `className`           | `string`                                    |                  | Classes for the root (`SidebarProvider` wrapper)     |

Other `<div>` props go to the root. `useAppLayout()` returns the surrounding layout's `variant` and `breadcrumbs` (or `null`), for components that adapt to the shell.

## Accessibility

- Landmarks: `banner` (header), `navigation` (sidebar, bottom nav), `main`, `contentinfo` (footer).
