- The skip link is the first tab stop and moves focus to `<main>`.
- On phones the sidebar drawer traps focus, closes with <kbd>Escape</kbd> and returns focus to the toggle.

| Key                                       | Action                           |
| ----------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> (first)                    | Shows the "Skip to content" link |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>⌘</kbd>+<kbd>B</kbd> | Toggle the sidebar               |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd>                         | Close the phone drawer           |

## RTL

Everything uses logical properties: the sidebar is on the right in RTL, and the sidebar toggle icon mirrors.

---

<!-- docs/layout-and-navigation/app-header.md -->

# AppHeader

The top bar of an app or portal: an optional sidebar toggle, a logo, the main content (page title, breadcrumbs, navigation or search) and actions at the inline end. Sticky by default, with padding for the notch (`env(safe-area-inset-top)`).

```tsx
import { AppHeader, Logo, NotificationCenter, ThemeToggle, UserProfile } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<AppHeader
  sidebarTrigger
  logo={<Logo src="/logo.svg" alt="Onu" />}
  actions={
    <>
      <ThemeToggle />
      <NotificationCenter notifications={items} />
      <UserProfile compact name="Ahmed Ali" onSignOut={signOut} />
    </>
  }
>
  <Breadcrumbs items={crumbs} />
</AppHeader>
```

`sidebarTrigger` needs `AppLayout` (or a `SidebarProvider`) above it. On phones the toggle opens the sidebar drawer.

## On the shell

Inside a panel `AppLayout` (the default) the header uses `variant="shell"`, Proton's header: the app shell colour with no bottom line, 60px tall, a wide 40px rounded **search** on the shell's field colour (put a `SearchBox` in `children`; it grows to 36rem), and quiet 36px icon buttons with a grey hover. A `UserProfile` in the actions shows its avatar as a rounded square and, below 768px, only the avatar.

```tsx
<AppHeader
  sidebarTrigger
  actions={
    <>
      <ThemeToggle />
      <NotificationCenter notifications={items} />
      <UserProfile name="Aishath Shifa" subtitle="shifa@atoll.mv" onSignOut={signOut} align="end" />
    </>
  }
>
  <SearchBox placeholder="Search applications" onSearch={search} />
</AppHeader>
```

Outside a panel layout the default is still `variant="default"` (the page background with a bottom border).

## Props

| Prop             | Type                                | Default     | Description                               |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `logo`           | `ReactNode`                         |             | Start of the header                       |
| `children`       | `ReactNode`                         |             | Middle area (fills the remaining space)   |
| `actions`        | `ReactNode`                         |             | End of the header                         |
| `sidebarTrigger` | `boolean`                           | `false`     | Show the sidebar toggle                   |
| `variant`        | `'shell' \| 'default' \| 'plain' \| 'primary'` | `'shell'` in a panel `AppLayout`, else `'default'` | Shell colour, bordered, borderless, or primary-coloured |
| `sticky`         | `boolean`                           | `true`      | Stick to the top while scrolling          |
| `classNames`     | `{ start, center, end, trigger }`   |             | Classes for each area                     |

`appHeaderVariants` is exported. The height is `--onu-header-height` (3.5rem; 3.75rem on the shell). Other `<header>` props are passed through, including `ref`.

## Accessibility

- Rendered as `<header>`, the `banner` landmark when it is not inside `<main>`.
- The sidebar toggle has the translated label "Toggle sidebar" and is 44px on touch screens.

| Key                                       | Action             |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------ |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>⌘</kbd>+<kbd>B</kbd> | Toggle the sidebar |

## RTL

Start and end swap in RTL; the toggle icon mirrors.

---

<!-- docs/layout-and-navigation/top-nav.md -->

# TopNav

Horizontal main navigation for headers, built on shadcn's `navigation-menu`. Items with `items` open a dropdown panel. Below the `md` breakpoint (768px) it collapses to a **menu button** that opens a drawer with the same items as a [`SideNav`](./side-nav.md).

```tsx
import { TopNav } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<TopNav
  currentHref={url}
  items={[
    { label: "Home", href: "/" },
    {
      label: "Services",
      items: [
        { label: "ID cards", href: "/services/id", description: "Apply or renew", icon: "user" },
        { label: "Passports", href: "/services/passports" },
      ],
    },
    { label: "News", href: "/news", badge: 2 },
  ]}
  logo={<Logo src="/logo.svg" alt="gov.mv" />}
/>
```

Items use the shared `NavItem` shape: `{ label, href?, icon?, badge?, description?, isActive?, disabled?, external?, items?, onSelect? }`. Links render through `OnuProvider linkComponent` (R16.2).

## Active state

The item whose `href` matches `currentHref` gets `aria-current="page"`. With the default `match="prefix"`, `/news/123` keeps **News** active (the longest matching parent wins). A parent of the active item is highlighted too.

## Props

| Prop           | Type                                      | Default    | Description                               |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ---------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `items`        | `NavItem[]`                               |            | Navigation items                          |
| `currentHref`  | `string`                                  |            | Current URL path                          |
| `match`        | `'prefix' \| 'exact'`                     | `'prefix'` | How `currentHref` matches                 |
| `logo`         | `ReactNode`                               |            | Top of the phone drawer                   |
| `mobileFooter` | `ReactNode`                               |            | Bottom of the phone drawer (e.g. Sign in) |
| `mobileSide`   | `'start' \| 'end'`                        | `'end'`    | Side the drawer slides in from            |
| `navLabel`     | `string`                                  | "Main"     | Accessible name of the navigation         |
| `classNames`   | `{ list, link, content, trigger, sheet }` |            | Classes for each part                     |

## Accessibility

- A `navigation` landmark; dropdown triggers expose `aria-expanded`.
- The phone drawer is a dialog: focus is trapped, <kbd>Escape</kbd> closes it and focus returns to the menu button. It closes after a link is chosen.

| Key                                 | Action                       |
| ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>                      | Move between top-level items |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | Open a dropdown              |
| <kbd>↓</kbd>                        | Move into an open dropdown   |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd>                   | Close the dropdown or drawer |

## RTL

The list and dropdowns mirror; the drawer opens from the inline end (the left in RTL).

---

<!-- docs/layout-and-navigation/menu-bar.md -->

# MenuBar

A desktop-style application menu bar (File, Edit, View …) described as data. Built on shadcn's `Menubar` (Radix, WAI-ARIA menubar pattern). The bar scrolls sideways when it does not fit.

```tsx
import { MenuBar } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<MenuBar
  menus={[
    {
      label: "File",
      items: [
        { label: "New", icon: "add", shortcut: "⌘N", onSelect: create },
        { label: "Save", icon: "save", shortcut: "⌘S", onSelect: save },
        { type: "separator" },
        { type: "sub", label: "Export", items: [{ label: "PDF" }, { label: "CSV" }] },
      ],
    },
    {
      label: "View",
      items: [
        { type: "checkbox", label: "Word wrap", checked: wrap, onCheckedChange: setWrap },
        { type: "radio", value: zoom, onValueChange: setZoom, options: [{ value: "100", label: "100%" }] },
      ],
    },
  ]}
/>
```

## Entries

| `type`             | Fields                                                                 |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `"item"` (default) | `label`, `icon`, `shortcut`, `href`, `disabled`, `variant`, `onSelect` |
| `"separator"`      |                                                                        |
| `"label"`          | `label`                                                                |
| `"checkbox"`       | `label`, `checked`, `onCheckedChange`, `shortcut`, `disabled`          |
| `"radio"`          | `value`, `onValueChange`, `options: { value, label, disabled }[]`      |
| `"sub"`            | `label`, `icon`, `items`                                               |

## Props

| Prop         | Type                         | Description           |
| ------------ | ---------------------------- | --------------------- |
| `menus`      | `{ label, items }[]`         | The menus             |
| `classNames` | `{ trigger, content, item }` | Classes for each part |
| `className`  | `string`                     | Classes for the bar   |

Other Radix `Menubar.Root` props are passed through.

## Accessibility

| Key                             | Action                                |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| <kbd>←</kbd> / <kbd>→</kbd>     | Move between menus (mirrored in RTL)  |
| <kbd>↓</kbd> / <kbd>Enter</kbd> | Open a menu                           |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> / <kbd>↓</kbd>     | Move between items                    |
| <kbd>→</kbd>                    | Open a submenu (<kbd>←</kbd> in RTL)  |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd>               | Close and return focus to the trigger |

Shortcut hints are visual only; register the shortcuts yourself.

## RTL

Direction comes from `OnuProvider`, so arrow keys follow the visual order and submenus open to the left.

---

<!-- docs/layout-and-navigation/mega-menu.md -->

# MegaMenu

Header navigation whose items open wide panels with several columns of links (each with an optional icon and description) and an optional featured area. Built on shadcn's `navigation-menu`. On phones it collapses to a menu button and a drawer with one accordion section per item.

```tsx
import { Card, MegaMenu } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<MegaMenu
  items={[
    {
      label: "Citizens",
      columns: [
        {
          title: "ID and documents",
          links: [
            { label: "National ID card", href: "/id", icon: "user", description: "Apply or renew" },
            { label: "Passport", href: "/passport", icon: "globe" },
          ],
        },
        { title: "Housing", links: [{ label: "Hulhumalé flats", href: "/flats" }] },
      ],
      featured: <Card size="sm" title="eFaas" description="One login for every service." href="/efaas" />,
    },
    { label: "News", href: "/news" },
  ]}
/>
```

## Props

| Prop         | Type                                      | Default | Description                    |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------ |
| `items`      | `MegaMenuItem[]`                          |         | Top-level items                |
| `logo`       | `ReactNode`                               |         | Top of the phone drawer        |
| `mobileSide` | `'start' \| 'end'`                        | `'end'` | Side the drawer slides in from |
| `navLabel`   | `string`                                  | "Main"  | Accessible name                |
| `classNames` | `{ trigger, panel, column, link, sheet }` |         | Classes for each part          |

`MegaMenuItem`: `{ label, href?, columns?: { title?, links: { label, href, description?, icon?, external? }[] }[], featured? }`. Up to four columns sit side by side from `md`; the featured area shows from `lg`.

## Accessibility

| Key                                 | Action                              |
| ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | Open a panel                        |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>                      | Move through the links in a panel   |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd>                   | Close the panel or the phone drawer |

The phone drawer traps focus and returns it to the menu button when closed.

## RTL

Panels open from the inline start and columns mirror; the drawer opens from the inline end.

---

<!-- docs/layout-and-navigation/app-sidebar.md -->

# AppSidebar

The app's main sidebar with a simple `items` / `groups` API: icons, badges, nested items and the active state from the current URL. It renders shadcn's `Sidebar`, so every shadcn sidebar feature still works: collapse to icons (`collapsible="icon"`, the default), off-canvas, the rail, the <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>⌘</kbd>+<kbd>B</kbd> shortcut, the cookie-persisted state and the phone drawer.

```tsx
import { AppSidebar, Logo, UserProfile } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<AppSidebar
  currentHref={url}
  header={<Logo src="/logo.svg" alt="Onu" text="Onu" />}
  footer={<UserProfile name="Aishath Shifa" subtitle="Admin" onSignOut={signOut} side="top" />}
  groups={[
    {
      label: "Main",
      items: [
        { label: "Dashboard", href: "/", icon: "home" },
        { label: "Applications", href: "/applications", icon: "file-text", badge: 12 },
        {
          label: "Users",
          href: "/users",
          icon: "users",
          items: [
            { label: "All users", href: "/users/all" },
            { label: "Invitations", href: "/users/invitations", badge: 3 },
          ],
        },
      ],
    },
  ]}
/>
```

Use it inside [`AppLayout`](./app-layout.md) or your own `SidebarProvider`.

## Proton shell (the default)

Inside a panel `AppLayout` (the default) the sidebar uses `surface="shell"`: Proton Mail's look on the app shell colour, the same surface as the header and the frame around the content panel.

- **Items** are 36px rows with 8px corners, a grey hover and a grey active state with a semibold label and a brand icon (no edge line, no brand tint).
- **`action`**: the main call to action under the header, as a full-width 44px button (Proton's "New message"). Collapsed to icons, only its icon shows; the label stays its accessible name.
- **Count pills**: numeric badges are brand-coloured pills for unread-like counts, read as "12 new" by screen readers. Set `badgeTone: "neutral"` on an item for a plain muted total, read as the number alone.
- **Folders and labels**: give an item a `color`. With a semantic icon (`icon: "folder"`) the icon is tinted; with no icon it shows a coloured dot. The colour is decorative; the label carries the meaning.
- **Header and footer**: put a `Logo` and an [`AppSwitcher`](./app-switcher.md) in `header`, and a [`UsageMeter`](./usage-meter.md) (or a `UserProfile`) in `footer`.

```tsx
<AppSidebar
  currentHref={url}
  header={
    <div className="flex items-center justify-between gap-2">
      <Logo src="/logo.svg" alt="" text="Atoll Records" />
      <AppSwitcher apps={apps} />
    </div>
  }
  action={
    <LinkButton href="/applications/new" startIcon="add">
      New application
    </LinkButton>
  }
  groups={[
    {
      items: [
        { label: "Inbox", href: "/inbox", icon: "home", badge: 12 },
        { label: "In review", href: "/review", icon: "clock", badge: 34, badgeTone: "neutral" },
      ],
    },
    { label: "Folders", items: [{ label: "Building permits", href: "/f/building", icon: "folder", color: "#8080ff" }] },
    { label: "Labels", items: [{ label: "Malé", href: "/l/male", color: "#1da583" }] },
  ]}
  footer={<UsageMeter label="Storage" value={1284} max={2000} link={{ label: "Get more space", href: "/billing" }} />}
/>
```

`surface="sidebar"` (the default inside a `variant="flat"` layout or a plain `SidebarProvider`) keeps the sidebar colour, its edge line and brand-tinted active items.

## Items

Items use the shared `NavItem` shape: `{ label, href?, icon?, badge?, badgeTone?, color?, isActive?, disabled?, external?, items?, onSelect? }`.

- `icon`: a semantic icon name (`"home"`) or any node.
- `badge`: a number (shown as a count, "99+" above 99, with "3 new" for screen readers) or any node. On an item with nested items the badge sits inside the button, before the chevron or the submenu toggle, so the two never overlap (LTR and RTL).
- `items`: nested items. A parent with an `href` gets a separate expand button; without one, the whole row toggles.
- **Active state**: the item matching `currentHref` gets `aria-current="page"`; its parent starts expanded, and expands when `currentHref` moves into it later. `match="prefix"` (default) keeps `/users` active on `/users/12/edit`; set `isActive` to override. Items whose `href` has a query string (`/users?status=active`) also match on its parameters.
- **Collapsed to icons**: labels become tooltips and nested items open in a flyout menu.
- On phones the drawer takes focus itself when it opens (so a filter or search field at the top doesn't bring up the keyboard; <kbd>Tab</kbd> moves into it) and closes after an item is chosen.

## Props

| Prop          | Type                                                          | Default     | Description                       |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | --------------------------------- |
| `items`       | `NavItem[]`                                                   |             | Flat list (or use `groups`)       |
| `groups`      | `{ label?, items }[]`                                         |             | Labelled groups                   |
| `currentHref` | `string`                                                      |             | Current URL (path and query)  |
| `match`       | `'prefix' \| 'exact'`                                         | `'prefix'`  | How `currentHref` matches         |
| `header`      | `ReactNode`                                                   |             | Top area (logo, app switcher)     |
| `action`      | `ReactNode`                                                   |             | Full-width call to action under the header |
| `surface`     | `'shell' \| 'sidebar'`                                        | `'shell'` in a panel `AppLayout` | Proton shell or sidebar colour |
| `footer`      | `ReactNode`                                                   |             | Bottom area (user profile)        |
| `children`    | `ReactNode`                                                   |             | Extra content after the groups    |
| `rail`        | `boolean`                                                     | `true`      | Show the toggle rail              |
| `onNavigate`  | `(item) => void`                                              |             | Called after an item is activated |
| `navLabel`    | `string`                                                      | "Main"      | Accessible name of the navigation |
| `collapsible` | `'icon' \| 'offcanvas' \| 'none'`                             | `'icon'`    | Desktop collapse mode             |
| `side`        | `'start' \| 'end'`                                            | `'start'`   | Logical side                      |
| `variant`     | `'sidebar' \| 'floating' \| 'inset'`                          | `'sidebar'` | shadcn variant                    |
| `classNames`  | `{ header, action, content, footer, group, groupLabel, item, badge }` |             | Classes for each part             |

On the shell the sidebar reads the shell tokens (`--shell`, `--shell-foreground`, `--shell-hover`, `--shell-active`), falling back to Proton's warm greys (`#f5f4f2` light, `#16141c` dark). With `surface="sidebar"` the theme tokens are `--onu-sidebar`, `--onu-sidebar-foreground`, `--onu-sidebar-primary`, `--onu-sidebar-accent` and `--onu-sidebar-border`.

## Accessibility

| Key                                       | Action                           |
| ----------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>                            | Move between items               |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd>       | Follow a link or expand a group  |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>⌘</kbd>+<kbd>B</kbd> | Toggle the sidebar               |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd>                         | Close the phone drawer or flyout |

## RTL

`side="start"` puts the sidebar on the right in RTL; chevrons mirror and flyouts open towards the content.

---

<!-- docs/layout-and-navigation/app-switcher.md -->

# AppSwitcher

The app switcher next to the logo, like Proton's grid button: a menu of the products in a suite, each on a brand-tinted tile. Put it in the [`AppSidebar`](./app-sidebar.md) header beside the `Logo`.

```tsx
import { AppSidebar, AppSwitcher, Logo } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<AppSidebar
  groups={groups}
  header={
    <div className="flex items-center justify-between gap-2">
      <Logo src="/logo.svg" alt="" text="Atoll Records" href="/" />
      <AppSwitcher
        label="Atoll apps"
        apps={[
          { label: "Records", href: "/records", icon: "file-text", current: true },
          { label: "Payments", href: "/payments", icon: "credit-card" },
          { label: "Help centre", href: "https://help.example.mv", icon: "help", external: true },
        ]}
      />
    </div>
  }
/>
```

The button hides when the sidebar is collapsed to icons.

## Props

| Prop           | Type                                               | Default        | Description                    |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `apps`         | `{ label, href, icon?, current?, external? }[]`    |                | The apps                       |
| `label`        | `ReactNode`                                        | "Apps"         | Heading at the top of the menu |
| `triggerLabel` | `string`                                           | "Switch app"   | Accessible name of the button  |
| `align`        | `'start' \| 'center' \| 'end'`                     | `'start'`      | Menu alignment                 |
| `className`    | `string`                                           |                | Classes for the button         |
| `classNames`   | `{ trigger, content, item, tile }`                 |                | Classes for each part          |

## Accessibility

- A 36px icon button (44px on touch screens) with a translated name, opening a Radix dropdown menu.
- The current app has `aria-current="page"`; tiles are decorative. External apps open in a new tab with a screen-reader note.

| Key                                       | Action                  |
| ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd>       | Open the menu           |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> / <kbd>↓</kbd>                | Move between apps       |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd>                         | Close the menu          |

## RTL

The menu opens towards the content and the labels are right-aligned in RTL.

---

<!-- docs/layout-and-navigation/side-nav.md -->

# SideNav

A vertical navigation list that works on its own (settings pages, documentation, account pages) and inside drawers: groups, icons, badges, descriptions and collapsible nested items. [`TopNav`](./top-nav.md) and [`OverlayMenu`](./overlay-menu.md) use it for their phone/overlay menus.

```tsx
import { SideNav } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<SideNav
  aria-label="Settings"
  currentHref={url}
  groups={[
    {
      label: "Organisation",
      items: [
        { label: "General", href: "/settings", icon: "settings" },
        {
          label: "Members",
          href: "/settings/members",
          icon: "users",
          badge: 24,
          items: [{ label: "Invitations", href: "/settings/members/invitations", badge: 3 }],
        },
      ],
    },
  ]}
/>
```

The current page gets `aria-current="page"` and its parents start expanded. Links render through `OnuProvider linkComponent`.

## Props

| Prop          | Type                                            | Default     | Description                                   |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ----------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `items`       | `NavItem[]`                                     |             | Flat list (or use `groups`)                   |
| `groups`      | `{ label?, items }[]`                           |             | Labelled groups (each list is labelled by it) |
| `currentHref` | `string`                                        |             | Current URL (path and query)              |
| `match`       | `'prefix' \| 'exact'`                           | `'prefix'`  | How `currentHref` matches                     |
| `size`        | `'sm' \| 'default' \| 'lg'`                     | `'default'` | `lg` gives 48px rows for kiosks and overlays  |
| `onNavigate`  | `(item) => void`                                |             | Called after an item is activated             |
| `aria-label`  | `string`                                        | "Main"      | Name of the navigation landmark               |
| `classNames`  | `{ group, groupLabel, list, item, sub, badge }` |             | Classes for each part                         |

`sideNavItemVariants` is exported. Items without `href` render as buttons (use `onSelect`).

## Accessibility

- A `navigation` landmark; each group's list is labelled by the group label.
- Expand buttons expose `aria-expanded` and are named "Show or hide …".
- Rows are at least 44px tall on touch screens.

| Key                                 | Action                  |
| ----------------------------------- | ----------------------- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>                      | Move between items      |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | Follow a link or expand |

## RTL

Nested lists indent from the inline start and the guide line sits on the right in RTL.

---

<!-- docs/layout-and-navigation/bottom-nav.md -->

# BottomNav

Phone bottom navigation: three to five destinations with icons and short labels, badges and the active state. Targets are at least 56px tall, and the bar is padded for the home indicator (`env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`, R3.30). Hidden from 768px by default.

```tsx
import { BottomNav } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<BottomNav
  currentHref={url}
  items={[
    { label: "Home", href: "/", icon: "home" },
    { label: "Applications", href: "/applications", icon: "file-text", badge: 2 },
    { label: "Inbox", href: "/inbox", icon: "mail", badge: 128 },
    { label: "Profile", href: "/profile", icon: "user" },
  ]}
/>
```

Pass it to [`AppLayout`](./app-layout.md)'s `bottomNav` so the content is padded above it.

## Props

| Prop          | Type                                 | Default            | Description                                                   |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `items`       | `NavItem[]`                          |                    | Destinations (`label`, `href` or `onSelect`, `icon`, `badge`) |
| `currentHref` | `string`                             |                    | Current URL (path and query)                              |
| `match`       | `'prefix' \| 'exact'`                | `'prefix'`         | How `currentHref` matches                                     |
| `position`    | `'fixed' \| 'static'`                | `'fixed'`          | Fixed to the viewport bottom, or in place                     |
| `hideFrom`    | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'never'`    | `'md'`             | Breakpoint from which it hides                                |
| `aria-label`  | `string`                             | "Quick navigation" | Landmark name                                                 |
| `classNames`  | `{ list, item, icon, label, badge }` |                    | Classes for each part                                         |

Numeric badges show "99+" above 99 and read as "3 new" to screen readers.

## Accessibility

- A `navigation` landmark; the current item has `aria-current="page"`.
- The accessible name of each item is its label plus the badge text ("Inbox, 3 new").

| Key              | Action             |
| ---------------- | ------------------ |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>   | Move between items |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> | Follow the link    |

## RTL

Items run right to left in RTL; badges sit on the inline end of the icon.

---

<!-- docs/layout-and-navigation/site-footer.md -->

# SiteFooter

The footer for portals and public pages: brand and description, link columns, social links, a copyright line, legal links and a slot for a [`LanguageSwitcher`](./language-switcher.md). Columns reflow by the footer's own width (container queries): two columns on phones, four on wide screens.

```tsx
import { LanguageSwitcher, Logo, SiteFooter } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<SiteFooter
  logo={<Logo src="/logo.svg" alt="Javaabu" text="Javaabu" />}
  description="Software for government and businesses in the Maldives."
  name="Javaabu Pvt Ltd"
  columns={[
    { title: "Services", links: [{ label: "Websites", href: "/websites" }] },
    { title: "Company", links: [{ label: "About", href: "/about" }] },
  ]}
  social={[{ label: "Email", href: "mailto:hello@javaabu.com", icon: "mail" }]}
  legalLinks={[{ label: "Privacy", href: "/privacy" }]}
  languageSwitcher={<LanguageSwitcher size="sm" onChange={setLocale} />}
/>
```

The default copyright line is "© {year} {name}. All rights reserved." in the active language.

## Props

| Prop               | Type                                                            | Default      | Description                               |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| `logo`             | `ReactNode`                                                     |              | Brand                                     |
| `description`      | `ReactNode`                                                     |              | Text under the brand                      |
| `columns`          | `{ title, links: { label, href, external? }[] }[]`              |              | Link columns                              |
| `social`           | `{ label, href, icon }[]`                                       |              | Icon links (label is the accessible name) |
| `name`             | `string`                                                        |              | Organisation name for the copyright line  |
| `copyright`        | `ReactNode`                                                     |              | Replaces the copyright line               |
| `year`             | `number`                                                        | current year | Year in the copyright line                |
| `legalLinks`       | `FooterLink[]`                                                  |              | Bottom-bar links                          |
| `languageSwitcher` | `ReactNode`                                                     |              | Slot in the bottom bar                    |
| `classNames`       | `{ brand, columns, column, columnTitle, link, social, bottom }` |              | Classes for each part                     |

Extra `children` render between the columns and the bottom bar.

## Accessibility

- Rendered as `<footer>` (`contentinfo`). Each column is a `navigation` landmark labelled by its heading.
- Social links are icon buttons with an accessible name; external links open in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.
- Links are 44px tall on touch screens.

| Key            | Action             |
| -------------- | ------------------ |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Move between links |

## RTL

Columns and the bottom bar mirror. Use brand icons from Iconify or FontAwesome brands for social links.

---

<!-- docs/layout-and-navigation/page-title.md -->

# PageTitle

The page header of index, view and edit pages ([§25.6](../requirements.md), [§25.8](../requirements.md)): the title, the main action button, and secondary links where a small dot marks e.g. a non-empty **Trash**. Record pages add breadcrumbs, back links and record actions. Actions move under the title when the header is narrow.

```tsx
import { Breadcrumbs, Button, PageTitle } from "@javaabu/onu"

// Index page
;<PageTitle
  title="Users"
  action={<Button>New user</Button>}
  links={[{ label: "Trash", href: "/users/trash", icon: "trash", dot: trashCount > 0 }]}
/>

// Record page
<PageTitle
  breadcrumbs={<Breadcrumbs items={[{ label: "Users", href: "/users" }, { label: user.name }]} />}
  title={user.name}
  links={[
    { label: "All users", href: "/users", icon: "back" },
    { label: "Trash", href: "/users/trash", dot: true },
  ]}
  actions={<Button variant="outline">Logs</Button>}
  action={<Button variant="destructive">Delete</Button>}
/>
```

## Page header band (Ant PageHeader)

Inside a panel [`AppLayout`](./app-layout.md) (the default), a page's `h1` header is **Ant Design's PageHeader**: a white band across the top of the content panel with a bottom line, holding

- the **breadcrumbs** (by default the `AppLayout`'s `breadcrumbs`, so pages need not repeat them),
- the **title** (20px) with a grey `subtitle` and `tags`, and the actions at the inline end,
- the **description** with key `figures` at the end of its row (a `<dl>`: label above a 20px value, split by lines),
- secondary `links` and extra `content`,
- a `tabs` row (`FilterTabs`, `Tabs` or `NavTabs`) as Ant's line tabs with the brand ink bar on the band's bottom edge.

```tsx
<PageTitle
  title="Applications"
  tags={<Tag size="sm">67 open</Tag>}
  description="Permit and licence applications from every island."
  figures={[
    { label: "In review", value: 34 },
    { label: "Approved", value: 50 },
  ]}
  actions={<LinkButton href="/trash" variant="outline" startIcon="trash">Trash</LinkButton>}
  action={<LinkButton href="/applications/new" startIcon="add">New application</LinkButton>}
  tabs={<FilterTabs tabs={tabs} value={status} onValueChange={setStatus} />}
/>
```

Sub-headings (`headingLevel` 2 or 3) and headers outside a panel layout stay `plain`. Set `variant="band"` or `variant="plain"` to choose.

## Props

| Prop           | Type                                                        | Default | Description                          |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `title`        | `ReactNode`                                                 |         | Page title                           |
| `description`  | `ReactNode`                                                 |         | Text under the title                 |
| `action`       | `ReactNode`                                                 |         | Main action (last at the inline end) |
| `actions`      | `ReactNode`                                                 |         | More actions before the main one     |
| `links`        | `{ label, href, icon?, dot?, count?, external? }[]`         |         | Secondary links under the title      |
| `breadcrumbs`  | `ReactNode \| BreadcrumbsItem[]`                            |         | Above the title (a band defaults to the layout's) |
| `subtitle`     | `ReactNode`                                                 |         | Grey text next to the title          |
| `tags`         | `ReactNode`                                                 |         | Tags after the title                 |
| `figures`      | `{ label, value }[]`                                        |         | Key figures at the end of the description row |
| `content`      | `ReactNode`                                                 |         | More content under the heading       |
| `tabs`         | `ReactNode`                                                 |         | A tab row at the bottom (ink bar)    |
| `variant`      | `'band' \| 'plain'`                                         | `'band'` for an `h1` in a panel `AppLayout`, else `'plain'` | Ant PageHeader band or the plain block |
| `media`        | `ReactNode`                                                 |         | Before the title (avatar, icon)      |
| `headingLevel` | `1 \| 2 \| 3`                                               | `1`     | Heading element                      |
| `classNames`   | `{ breadcrumbs, title, subtitle, description, links, link, actions, figures, content, tabs }` |         | Classes for each part                |

Other `<header>` props (including `ref`) go to the root.

## Behaviour (§25.6)

- The title is the page's `h1`.
- The main action button sits at the end of the header.
- A link with `dot` shows a small primary-coloured dot; screen readers hear "Trash (not empty)". Without `dot`, nothing is shown.

## Accessibility

| Key            | Action                         |
| -------------- | ------------------------------ |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Move through links and actions |

## RTL

Actions sit on the left in RTL; the back icon mirrors.

---

<!-- docs/layout-and-navigation/breadcrumbs.md -->

# Breadcrumbs

A breadcrumb trail built on shadcn's `breadcrumb` ([§25.8](../requirements.md)): every part is a link except the last, which is the current page. On phones the middle parts collapse into a "…" menu, keeping the first and last; `maxItems` collapses on wider screens too. The chevron separators mirror in RTL.

```tsx
import { Breadcrumbs } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<Breadcrumbs
  items={[{ label: "Home", href: "/", icon: "home" }, { label: "Users", href: "/users" }, { label: "Jane Doe" }]}
/>
```

Links render through `OnuProvider linkComponent` (R16.2).

## Props

| Prop               | Type                                          | Default | Description                                  |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `items`            | `{ label, href?, icon? }[]`                   |         | Trail; the last item is the current page     |
| `maxItems`         | `number`                                      |         | Collapse when there are more items than this |
| `collapseOnMobile` | `boolean`                                     | `true`  | Collapse to first › … › last below 768px     |
| `separator`        | `ReactNode`                                   | chevron | Custom separator                             |
| `classNames`       | `{ list, item, link, page, separator, menu }` |         | Classes for each part                        |

Other `<nav>` props are passed through.

## Behaviour (§25.8)

- Every part is a link except the last, which has `aria-current="page"`.
- Hidden parts are links in the "…" menu.
- Separators are directional icons, so they point left in RTL.

## Accessibility

- A `navigation` landmark named "Breadcrumb"; separators are hidden from screen readers.
- The "…" button is named "Show hidden pages"; the menu returns focus to it when closed.

| Key                         | Action             |
| --------------------------- | ------------------ |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>              | Move between links |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd>            | Open the "…" menu  |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> / <kbd>↓</kbd> | Move in the menu   |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd>           | Close the menu     |

---

<!-- docs/layout-and-navigation/section.md -->

# Section

A page section with a heading, description and actions. It is a `<section>` labelled by its heading, so it shows up as a region landmark. Actions sit beside the heading and move underneath it when the section is narrow (container query).

```tsx
import { Button, Section } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<Section
  title="Contact details"
  description="How we reach this member."
  actions={<Button variant="outline">Edit</Button>}
  variant="card"
>
  <DescriptionList items={details} />
</Section>
```

## Props

| Prop           | Type                                               | Default   | Description                                 |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `title`        | `ReactNode`                                        |           | Heading                                     |
| `description`  | `ReactNode`                                        |           | Text under the heading (`aria-describedby`) |
| `actions`      | `ReactNode`                                        |           | Buttons or links at the end of the header   |
| `headingLevel` | `1–6`                                              | `2`       | Heading element                             |
| `variant`      | `'plain' \| 'card' \| 'muted'`                     | `'plain'` | Surface                                     |
| `classNames`   | `{ header, title, description, actions, content }` |           | Classes for each part                       |

`sectionVariants` is exported. Other `<section>` props (including `ref` and `id`) go to the root.

## Accessibility

- With a `title`, the section is a `region` named by its heading. Without one, give it an `aria-label` or it is a plain section.
- Pick `headingLevel` to keep the page outline in order.

## RTL

Actions sit at the inline end, so on the left in RTL.

---

<!-- docs/layout-and-navigation/card.md -->

# Card

shadcn's `Card`, extended. Without the new props it renders exactly like the shadcn card, so `CardHeader`, `CardTitle`, `CardDescription`, `CardAction`, `CardContent` and `CardFooter` still compose as before. The Onu `Card` is the one exported from `@javaabu/onu`; the original stays available from `@javaabu/onu/primitives`.

```tsx
import { Button, Card } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<Card
  title="Payments received"
  description="Last 30 days"
  actions={
    <Button variant="ghost" size="icon-sm" aria-label="More">
      …
    </Button>
  }
  footer={
    <Button variant="outline" size="sm">
      View all
    </Button>
  }
>
  MVR 48,250.00
</Card>
```

## Look

Cards follow Ant Design: 24px padding, an 8px corner (it follows `--radius`), a 1px line in the border colour and no shadow. A card with a `title` has a 56px **header row with its own bottom line**, a 16px semibold title and the `actions` centred at the end. `size="sm"` tightens the spacing.

## Content padding

Content placed straight in a card, without `title`, `description`, `actions` or `footer`, gets the same inline padding as `CardContent`, so a quick card needs no wrapper:

```tsx
<Card>
  <p>Your application was received.</p>
</Card>
```

Each direct child is padded (images stay edge to edge); loose text is wrapped in a `CardContent`. Cards composed from `CardHeader`/`CardContent`/`CardFooter` look exactly as before. Set `padded={false}` for edge-to-edge content such as a table or a map: the card then adds no padding at all (the content brings its own).

## Link cards

With `href`, the title becomes a link stretched over the whole card (the "block link" pattern), so the card is one tab stop and its text stays selectable. Header actions and the footer sit above the link and stay clickable.

```tsx
<Card href="/cities/addu" title="Addu City" description="6 islands" />
```

Put other interactive elements in the content inside a `relative z-10` wrapper.

## asChild

Render the card as another element. Header and footer props still work; the child's own children sit between them.

```tsx
<Card asChild title="News">
  <article>
    <CardContent>…</CardContent>
  </article>
</Card>
```

## Props

| Prop           | Type                                                       | Default     | Description                   |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | ----------------------------- |
| `title`        | `ReactNode`                                                |             | Title (renders the header)    |
| `description`  | `ReactNode`                                                |             | Text under the title          |
| `actions`      | `ReactNode`                                                |             | End of the header             |
| `footer`       | `ReactNode`                                                |             | Footer content                |
| `href`         | `string`                                                   |             | Makes it a link card          |
| `external`     | `boolean`                                                  | `false`     | Open the link in a new tab    |
| `headingLevel` | `2–6`                                                      | `3`         | Heading element for the title |
| `size`         | `'default' \| 'sm'`                                        | `'default'` | Spacing                       |
| `variant`      | `'default' \| 'outline' \| 'muted'`                        | `'default'` | Surface                       |
| `asChild`      | `boolean`                                                  | `false`     | Render as the child element   |
| `padded`       | `boolean`                                                  | `true`      | Pad content placed straight in the card (`false`: no padding) |
| `classNames`   | `{ header, title, description, actions, content, footer }` |             | Classes for each part         |

`cardVariants` is exported. Other `<div>` props (including `ref`) go to the root.

## Accessibility

- The title is a real heading; link cards have one link whose name is the title.
- Link cards show a focus ring on the whole card (`focus-within`).

| Key              | Action              |
| ---------------- | ------------------- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>   | Focus the card link |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> | Follow the link     |

## RTL

Header actions sit at the inline end.

---

<!-- docs/layout-and-navigation/tabs.md -->

# Tabs

shadcn's `Tabs` (Radix, WAI-ARIA tabs), extended with an `items` API, icons, counts and a tab list that scrolls sideways on phones. Without `items` it is the shadcn component, so `TabsList`, `TabsTrigger` and `TabsContent` compose as before. The original stays available from `@javaabu/onu/primitives`.

```tsx
import { Tabs } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<Tabs
  listLabel="Member"
  items={[
    { value: "details", label: "Details", icon: "info", content: <Details /> },
    { value: "documents", label: "Documents", count: 4, content: <Documents /> },
    { value: "history", label: "History", count: 128, content: <History /> },
  ]}
/>
```

Use [`NavTabs`](./nav-tabs.md) when each tab is its own page.

## Props

| Prop            | Type                                                     | Default        | Description                              |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `items`         | `{ value, label, icon?, count?, disabled?, content? }[]` |                | Data-driven tabs                         |
| `value`         | `string`                                                 |                | Controlled value                         |
| `defaultValue`  | `string`                                                 | first enabled  | Initial value                            |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void`                                |                | Called on change                         |
| `variant`       | `'default' \| 'line'`                                    | `'default'`    | Tab list style                           |
| `orientation`   | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'`                             | `'horizontal'` | Layout and arrow keys                    |
| `scrollable`    | `boolean`                                                | `true`         | Let the list scroll when it does not fit |
| `listLabel`     | `string`                                                 |                | Accessible name of the tab list          |
| `classNames`    | `{ list, trigger, content, count }`                      |                | Classes for each part                    |

Counts are formatted with the active locale ("Activity (12)"). Other Radix `Tabs.Root` props are passed through.

## Accessibility

| Key                              | Action                                |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| <kbd>←</kbd> / <kbd>→</kbd>      | Previous / next tab (mirrored in RTL) |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> / <kbd>↓</kbd>      | Previous / next tab (vertical)        |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> / <kbd>End</kbd> | First / last tab                      |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>                   | Into the panel                        |

Screen readers announce the selected tab (§25.10).

## RTL

Direction comes from `OnuProvider`, so in RTL <kbd>←</kbd> moves to the next tab (R11.5).

---

<!-- docs/layout-and-navigation/nav-tabs.md -->

# NavTabs

Link-based tabs for record pages ([§25.8](../requirements.md)): "Profile", "Edit", "Activity (12)". Each tab opens its own page, the current one is highlighted, and the row scrolls sideways on phones (the current tab is scrolled into view). Links render through `OnuProvider linkComponent` (R16.2).

```tsx
import { NavTabs } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<NavTabs
  currentHref={url}
  items={[
    { label: "Profile", href: `/users/${id}` },
    { label: "Edit", href: `/users/${id}/edit` },
    { label: "Activity", href: `/users/${id}/activity`, count: 12 },
  ]}
/>
```

On a **create** page ([§25.9](../requirements.md)) mark the tabs that need a saved record as `disabled`: they are greyed out and not links.

## Props

| Prop          | Type                                                             | Default    | Description                                  |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `items`       | `{ label, href, count?, icon?, badge?, disabled?, isActive? }[]` |            | Tabs                                         |
| `currentHref` | `string`                                                         |            | Current URL (path and query)             |
| `match`       | `'exact' \| 'prefix'`                                            | `'exact'`  | `prefix` keeps a tab active on its sub-pages |
| `variant`     | `'line' \| 'pill'`                                               | `'line'`   | Ant line tabs (brand colour and a 2px ink bar on the current tab, 32px apart) or pills |
| `aria-label`  | `string`                                                         | "Sections" | Landmark name                                |
| `classNames`  | `{ list, item, count }`                                          |            | Classes for each part                        |

`navTabsVariants` is exported.

## Behaviour (§25.8)

- Each tab is a link to its own page.
- The tab matching `currentHref` is highlighted and has `aria-current="page"`.
- Matching uses the path, and the query string when a tab's `href` has one, so tabs that differ only by a parameter (`?tab=documents`, `?tab=history`) highlight one at a time. The tab sharing the most parameters with `currentHref` wins (extra parameters such as `page` are ignored); on a bare URL with none of the tabs' parameters, the first such tab is the default. Hash-router hrefs (`#/records/7?tab=history`) work too.
- Counts show as "Activity (12)", formatted with the active locale.

## Accessibility

NavTabs is a `nav` with links and `aria-current`, not an ARIA `tablist`: each tab navigates to a new page, so the links pattern is the correct one. Tabs are 44px tall on touch screens.

| Key              | Action            |
| ---------------- | ----------------- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>   | Move between tabs |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> | Open the tab      |

## RTL

Tabs run right to left in RTL and the row scrolls in the reading direction.

---

<!-- docs/layout-and-navigation/stacked-tabs.md -->

# StackedTabs

Vertical tabs for settings-style pages: the tab list sits at the inline start with the panel beside it. In narrow containers (below about 42rem, a container query) the list becomes a native **select** (`mobile="select"`, default) or a horizontally scrolling row (`mobile="scroll"`).

```tsx
import { StackedTabs } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<StackedTabs
  items={[
    { value: "general", label: "General", icon: "settings", description: "Name and logo", content: <General /> },
    { value: "members", label: "Members", icon: "users", badge: 3, content: <Members /> },
    { value: "billing", label: "Billing", icon: "credit-card", content: <Billing /> },
  ]}
/>
```

## Props

| Prop            | Type                                                                               | Default            | Description                                |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------ |
| `items`         | `{ value, label, textLabel?, description?, icon?, badge?, disabled?, content? }[]` |                    | Tabs                                       |
| `value`         | `string`                                                                           |                    | Controlled value                           |
| `defaultValue`  | `string`                                                                           | first enabled      | Initial value                              |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void`                                                          |                    | Called on change                           |
| `mobile`        | `'select' \| 'scroll'`                                                             | `'select'`         | What the list becomes in narrow containers |
| `listLabel`     | `string`                                                                           | "Choose a section" | Name of the tab list and the select        |
| `classNames`    | `{ list, trigger, content, select }`                                               |                    | Classes for each part                      |

Use `textLabel` when `label` is not plain text, so the select has an option label.

## Accessibility

- A WAI-ARIA `tablist` with `aria-orientation="vertical"`; the select is labelled for screen readers.
- Triggers and the select are 44px tall on touch screens.

| Key                              | Action              |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------- |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> / <kbd>↓</kbd>      | Previous / next tab |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> / <kbd>End</kbd> | First / last tab    |

In `scroll` mode the row is horizontal but keeps vertical arrow keys.

## RTL

The list sits on the right in RTL.

---

<!-- docs/layout-and-navigation/accordion.md -->

# Accordion

shadcn's `Accordion` (Radix, WAI-ARIA accordion), extended with an `items` API and visual variants. `type` defaults to `"single"`, and a single accordion is collapsible by default. Without `items` it composes like the shadcn component (`AccordionItem`, `AccordionTrigger`, `AccordionContent`). The original stays available from `@javaabu/onu/primitives`.

```tsx
import { Accordion } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<Accordion
  items={[
    { value: "fees", title: "What are the fees?", icon: "credit-card", content: "MVR 50 per application." },
    { value: "time", title: "How long does it take?", content: "Up to 5 working days." },
  ]}
/>

<Accordion type="multiple" variant="bordered" items={items} defaultValue={["fees"]} />
```

## Props

| Prop                                       | Type                                            | Default     | Description                           |
| ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `items`                                    | `{ value, title, content, icon?, disabled? }[]` |             | Data-driven items                     |
| `type`                                     | `'single' \| 'multiple'`                        | `'single'`  | One or several panels open            |
| `collapsible`                              | `boolean`                                       | `true`      | (single) allow closing the open panel |
| `value` / `defaultValue` / `onValueChange` | `string` or `string[]`                          |             | Controlled / uncontrolled state       |
| `variant`                                  | `'default' \| 'bordered' \| 'separated'`        | `'default'` | Visual style                          |
| `classNames`                               | `{ item, trigger, content }`                    |             | Classes for each part                 |

`accordionVariants` is exported.

## Accessibility

| Key                                 | Action                   |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | Toggle the focused panel |
| <kbd>↓</kbd> / <kbd>↑</kbd>         | Next / previous header   |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> / <kbd>End</kbd>    | First / last header      |

Headers expose `aria-expanded` and control their panel.

## RTL

The chevron sits at the inline end.

---

<!-- docs/layout-and-navigation/wizard.md -->

# Wizard

A multi-step flow (application wizards, onboarding): a step list with each step's status, Back / Next buttons with per-step validation, jumping back to completed steps, a compact "Step 2 of 4" header with a progress bar in narrow containers, and step changes announced to screen readers.

```tsx
import { Wizard } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<Wizard
  steps={[
    {
      id: "applicant",
      title: "Applicant",
      content: <ApplicantFields />,
      validate: () => form.trigger(["name", "nid"]),
    },
    { id: "address", title: "Address", content: <AddressFields /> },
    { id: "documents", title: "Documents", optional: true, content: <Uploads /> },
    { id: "review", title: "Review", content: <Review /> },
  ]}
  onComplete={submit}
  finishLabel="Submit"
/>
```

`validate` can be async (e.g. react-hook-form's `trigger`). While it runs, Next shows a spinner and ignores further clicks. If it returns `false`, the step is marked "Has errors" and the wizard stays.

## Navigation

- **Next** validates the current step (`validate`, then `onValidateStep`) and moves on; on the last step it calls `onComplete`.
- **Back** never validates.
- With `linear` (default), users can jump back to completed steps, and forward to the furthest unlocked step. `linear={false}` lets them jump anywhere.
- `errorSteps={["address"]}` marks steps with server-side errors.

## useWizard

Inside the wizard, `useWizard()` returns `{ index, total, step, isFirst, isLast, validating, next, back, goTo, statusOf }` for custom footers (set `hideFooter`).

## Props

| Prop             | Type                                                                        | Default        | Description                               |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `steps`          | `{ id, title, textTitle?, description?, optional?, content?, validate? }[]` |                | Steps                                     |
| `step`           | `number`                                                                    |                | Controlled step index                     |
| `defaultStep`    | `number`                                                                    | `0`            | Initial step                              |
| `onStepChange`   | `(index) => void`                                                           |                | Called when the step changes              |
| `onValidateStep` | `(index, step) => boolean \| Promise<boolean>`                              |                | Validation hook for every step            |
| `onComplete`     | `() => void \| Promise<void>`                                               |                | Called when the last step validates       |
| `linear`         | `boolean`                                                                   | `true`         | Restrict jumping                          |
| `errorSteps`     | `string[]`                                                                  |                | Step ids with errors                      |
| `orientation`    | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'`                                                | `'horizontal'` | Steps on top or at the inline start       |
| `finishLabel`    | `ReactNode`                                                                 | "Finish"       | Label of the last button                  |
| `hideFooter`     | `boolean`                                                                   | `false`        | Hide Back / Next                          |
| `footerExtra`    | `ReactNode`                                                                 |                | Between Back and Next (e.g. "Save draft") |
| `classNames`     | `{ steps, step, marker, panel, title, footer, compact }`                    |                | Classes for each part                     |

## Accessibility

- The step list is a `navigation` named "Steps"; the current step has `aria-current="step"` and every step has a screen-reader status (Completed, Current step, Not started, Has errors). Colour is never the only cue: completed steps show a check, errors an icon.
- After a step change, focus moves to the step heading and a live region announces "Step 2 of 4: Address".

| Key                                 | Action                                  |
| ----------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>                      | Move through fields, Back and Next      |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | Activate Next, Back or a completed step |

## RTL

Steps run right to left; the Back and Next arrows mirror. Step numbers use the locale's digits (Western digits in Dhivehi).

---

<!-- docs/layout-and-navigation/timeline.md -->

# Timeline

A vertical timeline for status trackers and activity histories. Each entry has a status marker (icon and colour), a title, a timestamp formatted for the active locale, a description and optional extra content.

```tsx
import { Timeline } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<Timeline
  items={[
    { title: "Application submitted", time: submittedAt, status: "success" },
    { title: "Documents under review", time: reviewAt, status: "current" },
    { title: "Additional document requested", status: "warning", content: <Button size="sm">Upload</Button> },
    { title: "Final approval", status: "pending" },
  ]}
/>
```

## Statuses

| `status`  | Marker                    | Screen-reader text |
| --------- | ------------------------- | ------------------ |
| `default` | muted dot                 | —                  |
| `success` | check, success colour     | Completed          |
| `error`   | cross, destructive colour | Failed             |
| `warning` | warning, warning colour   | Needs attention    |
| `info`    | info, info colour         | Information        |
| `pending` | clock, dashed outline     | Pending            |
| `current` | dot, primary colour       | In progress        |

## Props

| Prop          | Type                                                         | Default      | Description                            |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------ | -------------------------------------- |
| `items`       | `{ title, description?, time?, status?, icon?, content? }[]` |              | Entries                                |
| `timeFormat`  | `'absolute' \| 'relative'`                                   | `'absolute'` | "Oct 1, 2026, 9:30 AM" or "3 days ago" |
| `datePattern` | `string`                                                     | `'PPp'`      | date-fns pattern for absolute times    |
| `now`         | `Date`                                                       |              | Reference time for relative times      |
| `size`        | `'sm' \| 'default'`                                          | `'default'`  | Marker size                            |
| `aria-label`  | `string`                                                     | "Timeline"   | List name                              |
| `classNames`  | `{ item, marker, title, time, description }`                 |              | Classes for each part                  |

`timelineMarkerVariants` is exported. Times use the locale's date-fns locale, so Dhivehi shows Dhivehi month names.

## Accessibility

- An ordered list; the `current` entry has `aria-current="step"`.
- Status is given as text, not only colour (R14.6). Times are `<time datetime>`.

## RTL

The line and markers sit on the inline start (the right in RTL).

---

<!-- docs/layout-and-navigation/divider.md -->

# Divider

A separator line built on shadcn's `Separator`, optionally with a label in the middle, at the start or at the end.

```tsx
import { Divider } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<Divider />
<Divider label="or" />
<Divider label="Today" align="start" variant="dashed" />
<Divider orientation="vertical" />
```

## Props

| Prop          | Type                             | Default        | Description                                           |
| ------------- | -------------------------------- | -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `label`       | `ReactNode`                      |                | Text on the line                                      |
| `align`       | `'start' \| 'center' \| 'end'`   | `'center'`     | Label position                                        |
| `orientation` | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'`     | `'horizontal'` | Direction                                             |
| `variant`     | `'solid' \| 'dashed'`            | `'solid'`      | Line style                                            |
| `spacing`     | `'none' \| 'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'none'`       | Margin around the line                                |
| `decorative`  | `boolean`                        | `true`         | Without a label, expose a `separator` role when false |
| `classNames`  | `{ line, label }`                |                | Classes for each part                                 |

`dividerVariants` is exported.

## Accessibility

Dividers are decorative by default (hidden from screen readers). Set `decorative={false}` when the line separates content meaningfully. A label is ordinary text and is read.

## RTL

`align="start"` puts the label on the right in RTL.

---

<!-- docs/layout-and-navigation/language-switcher.md -->

# LanguageSwitcher

Switches between languages using their **native names** (English, ދިވެހި). Each option carries its own `lang` and `dir`, so screen readers use the right voice (R14.12). Renders as a native select (default), a segmented toggle, or a globe button with a menu.

```tsx
import { LanguageSwitcher, OnuProvider } from "@javaabu/onu"

function App() {
  const [locale, setLocale] = React.useState<"en" | "dv">("en")
  return (
    <OnuProvider locale={locale}>
      <LanguageSwitcher onChange={(code) => setLocale(code as "en" | "dv")} />
    </OnuProvider>
  )
}
```

With Laravel, call your locale route in `onChange` (e.g. `router.post('/locale', { locale: code })`).

## Props

| Prop        | Type                             | Default            | Description                               |
| ----------- | -------------------------------- | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| `value`     | `string`                         | active locale code | Selected language                         |
| `onChange`  | `(code: string) => void`         |                    | Called with the chosen code               |
| `languages` | `{ code, name, dir? }[]`         | built-in locales   | Languages to offer                        |
| `variant`   | `'select' \| 'toggle' \| 'menu'` | `'select'`         | Presentation                              |
| `size`      | `'sm' \| 'default'`              | `'default'`        | Size                                      |
| `showIcon`  | `boolean`                        | `true`             | Show the languages icon (select and menu) |
| `disabled`  | `boolean`                        | `false`            | Disable                                   |
| `id`        | `string`                         | generated          | Id of the select                          |

## Accessibility

- `select`: a native select with a visually hidden "Language" label; works with every assistive technology and on phones.
- `toggle`: a radio group named "Language".
- `menu`: the button is named "Language: English"; the menu is a radio group and returns focus to the button.

| Key                         | Action                                         |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> / <kbd>↓</kbd> | Change language (select, menu)                 |
| <kbd>←</kbd> / <kbd>→</kbd> | Move between options (toggle; mirrored in RTL) |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd>           | Close the menu                                 |

---

<!-- docs/layout-and-navigation/theme-toggle.md -->

# ThemeToggle

Light / dark / system switch using `useTheme()` from [`ThemeProvider`](../guides.md) (R10.3). The choice is persisted to `localStorage` by the provider and announced to screen readers ("Theme: Dark").

```tsx
import { ThemeProvider, ThemeToggle } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<ThemeProvider>
  <ThemeToggle />
</ThemeProvider>
```

## Variants

- `menu` (default): an icon button (sun or moon, following the resolved theme) with a Light / Dark / System menu.
- `segmented`: three toggle buttons.
- `cycle`: one button that cycles Light → Dark → System.

## Props

| Prop         | Type                               | Default     | Description             |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------- | ----------- | ----------------------- |
| `variant`    | `'menu' \| 'segmented' \| 'cycle'` | `'menu'`    | Presentation            |
| `showSystem` | `boolean`                          | `true`      | Offer the System option |
| `size`       | `'sm' \| 'default'`                | `'default'` | Size                    |
| `className`  | `string`                           |             | Classes for the control |

## Accessibility

- The button is named "Theme: Light" (the current choice); options are radio items / radio buttons.
- A polite live region announces the new theme.
- Buttons are 44px on touch screens.

| Key                                 | Action                |
| ----------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | Open the menu / cycle |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> / <kbd>↓</kbd>         | Move in the menu      |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd>                   | Close the menu        |

---

<!-- docs/layout-and-navigation/notification-center.md -->

# NotificationCenter

A bell button with the unread count that opens the notification list: a popover on desktop and a bottom sheet (vaul drawer) on phones. Items can be marked read one by one or all at once, there is an empty state, and new unread items are announced in a live region.

```tsx
import { NotificationCenter } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<NotificationCenter
  notifications={notifications}
  onMarkRead={(id) => markRead(id)}
  onMarkAllRead={markAllRead}
  viewAllHref="/notifications"
/>
```

Notifications are data you own (from Laravel's database notifications, a websocket, polling …). Update the array and the bell, list and announcement follow.

## Items

`{ id, title, description?, time?, read?, href?, icon?, variant? }`

- `time` (`Date`, ISO string or timestamp) is shown as relative time in the active locale ("about 1 hour ago", Dhivehi in `dv`).
- `href` makes the row a link (through `OnuProvider linkComponent`); following it closes the list.
- `variant`: `default | success | warning | error | info` tints the icon.
- Clicking an unread item calls `onMarkRead` (turn off with `markReadOnClick={false}`).

## Props

| Prop                                    | Type                                      | Default   | Description                                    |
| --------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | --------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `notifications`                         | `NotificationItem[]`                      |           | The list                                       |
| `onMarkRead`                            | `(id) => void`                            |           | Shows per-item "Mark as read" buttons          |
| `onMarkAllRead`                         | `() => void`                              |           | Shows "Mark all as read" when there are unread |
| `onItemClick`                           | `(item) => void`                          |           | Called when an item is clicked                 |
| `viewAllHref`                           | `string`                                  |           | Footer link to the full page                   |
| `open` / `defaultOpen` / `onOpenChange` | `boolean` / callback                      |           | Controlled or uncontrolled                     |
| `empty`                                 | `ReactNode`                               |           | Custom empty state                             |
| `mobile`                                | `'sheet' \| 'popover'`                    | `'sheet'` | Presentation below 768px                       |
| `markReadOnClick`                       | `boolean`                                 | `true`    | Mark read when clicked                         |
| `now`                                   | `Date`                                    |           | Reference time (tests, SSR)                    |
| `classNames`                            | `{ trigger, count, content, list, item }` |           | Classes for each part                          |

## Accessibility

- The bell's name includes the count: "Notifications, 3 unread". The visual badge is hidden from screen readers; counts above 99 show "99+".
- The list is labelled "Notifications"; unread items include an "Unread" note.
- New unread items are announced politely: "2 new notifications".
- Focus returns to the bell when the popover or sheet closes.

| Key                                 | Action                         |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | Open the list                  |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>                      | Move through items and buttons |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd>                   | Close                          |

## RTL

The popover aligns to the inline end; the count badge sits on the inline end of the bell.

---

<!-- docs/layout-and-navigation/user-profile.md -->

# UserProfile

The signed-in user's avatar, name and role (or email), opening a menu with Profile, Settings, your own items and Sign out. Use the full version in a sidebar footer and `compact` (avatar only) in a header.

```tsx
import { UserProfile } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<UserProfile
  name="Aishath Shifa"
  subtitle="Administrator"
  avatarSrc={user.avatar}
  profileHref="/profile"
  settingsHref="/settings"
  items={[{ label: "Billing", icon: "credit-card", href: "/billing" }]}
  onSignOut={() => router.post("/logout")}
/>
```

Initials are derived from the name when there is no image (`getInitials`, works for Thaana names too).

## Props

| Prop           | Type                                             | Default    | Description                          |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ---------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `name`         | `string`                                         |            | Full name                            |
| `subtitle`     | `ReactNode`                                      |            | Role, email, …                       |
| `avatarSrc`    | `string`                                         |            | Avatar image                         |
| `initials`     | `string`                                         | from name  | Fallback initials                    |
| `profileHref`  | `string`                                         |            | Adds a Profile item                  |
| `settingsHref` | `string`                                         |            | Adds a Settings item                 |
| `items`        | `{ label, icon?, href?, onSelect?, variant? }[]` |            | Extra items                          |
| `onSignOut`    | `() => void`                                     |            | Adds a Sign out item                 |
| `compact`      | `boolean`                                        | `false`    | Avatar only                          |
| `side`         | `'top' \| 'bottom'`                              | `'bottom'` | Menu side (`top` in sidebar footers) |
| `align`        | `'start' \| 'end'`                               | `'end'`    | Menu alignment                       |
| `classNames`   | `{ trigger, avatar, name, subtitle, content }`   |            | Classes for each part                |

## Accessibility

- The trigger is named "Account menu for Aishath Shifa"; the avatar image is decorative.
- The menu follows the WAI-ARIA menu pattern and returns focus to the trigger.

| Key                                 | Action             |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------ |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | Open the menu      |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> / <kbd>↓</kbd>         | Move between items |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd>                   | Close              |

## RTL

Text aligns to the start and the menu aligns to the inline end.

---

<!-- docs/layout-and-navigation/logo.md -->

# Logo

The product or organisation logo with separate light and dark images, an optional wordmark, linking home.

```tsx
import { Logo } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<Logo src="/logo.svg" darkSrc="/logo-dark.svg" alt="Javaabu" text="Javaabu" />

// Inline SVG mark, no link
<Logo alt="Onu" href={null}>
  <OnuMark className="size-8" />
</Logo>
```

## Props

| Prop               | Type                    | Default | Description                                    |
| ------------------ | ----------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `alt`              | `string`                |         | Required. Organisation name                    |
| `src`              | `string`                |         | Image (light mode, and dark without `darkSrc`) |
| `darkSrc`          | `string`                |         | Image for dark mode                            |
| `href`             | `string \| null`        | `"/"`   | Link target; `null` for no link                |
| `text`             | `ReactNode`             |         | Wordmark beside the image                      |
