| `children`         | `ReactNode`             |         | Custom mark instead of `src`                   |
| `asChild`          | `boolean`               | `false` | Merge image classes into the custom mark       |
| `width` / `height` | `number`                |         | Image dimensions (avoid layout shift)          |
| `classNames`       | `{ image, text, link }` |         | Classes for each part                          |

## Accessibility

- As a link, its name is "Javaabu, home" (translated); the images inside are decorative.
- Without a link, the image carries `alt` (or the wrapper gets `role="img"` for a custom mark).

## RTL

The wordmark sits after the mark in reading order.

---

<!-- docs/layout-and-navigation/usage-meter.md -->

# UsageMeter

A quota meter for the bottom of the sidebar, like Proton's storage meter: a labelled bar with "used / total", an optional link (e.g. to upgrade) and a small note such as the app version. It is built on [`ProgressBar`](../loading/progress-bar.md), so the value is announced and the bar fills from the inline start.

```tsx
import { AppSidebar, UsageMeter } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<AppSidebar
  groups={groups}
  footer={
    <UsageMeter
      label="Records quota"
      icon="file-archive"
      value={1284}
      max={2000}
      link={{ label: "Get more space", href: "/billing" }}
      meta="v5.0.42"
    />
  }
/>
```

## Behaviour

- The value reads "1,284 / 2,000" in the active locale's digits; pass `formatValue` for other text (e.g. `(v, m) => \`${v} GB of ${m} GB\``).
- The bar is the brand colour, turns `warning` from 80% and `destructive` from 95% so a nearly full quota stands out. Set `color` to fix it.
- A line above separates it from the navigation; the track uses the shell's weak grey so it reads on the sidebar and on cards.

## Props

| Prop          | Type                                                    | Default             | Description                              |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `label`       | `ReactNode`                                             |                     | What is being used                       |
| `icon`        | `string \| ReactNode`                                   |                     | Semantic icon name or node before it     |
| `value`       | `number`                                                |                     | Amount used                              |
| `max`         | `number`                                                |                     | The quota                                |
| `formatValue` | `(value, max) => string`                                | "used / total"      | Value text (also read by screen readers) |
| `color`       | `ProgressBar` colour                                    | by how full it is   | Bar colour                               |
| `link`        | `{ label, href, external? }`                            |                     | A link under the bar                     |
| `meta`        | `ReactNode`                                             |                     | Small text at the end of the bottom row  |
| `classNames`  | `{ bar, label, value, footer, link, meta }`             |                     | Classes for each part                    |

Other `<div>` props go to the root.

## Accessibility

- The bar is a `progressbar` named by the label, with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemax` and the value text.
- The link goes through the configured link component and has a 44px target on touch screens.

## RTL

The bar fills from the right in RTL; the link and note swap sides.

---

<!-- docs/layout-and-navigation/skip-link.md -->

# SkipLink

A "Skip to content" link (R14.4). Render it as the first focusable element on the page: it is visually hidden until it receives keyboard focus, then moves focus to the main content. [`AppLayout`](./app-layout.md) includes one.

```tsx
import { SkipLink } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<>
  <SkipLink />
  <Header />
  <main id="main-content">…</main>
</>
```

## Props

| Prop        | Type        | Default           | Description          |
| ----------- | ----------- | ----------------- | -------------------- |
| `href`      | `string`    | `"#main-content"` | Target element       |
| `children`  | `ReactNode` | "Skip to content" | Link text            |
| `className` | `string`    |                   | Classes for the link |

Other `<a>` props (including `ref`) are passed through.

## Behaviour

On activation the target gets `tabindex="-1"` (if it has none) and receives focus, so the next <kbd>Tab</kbd> continues from the content. This works even where browsers do not move focus on in-page links.

## Accessibility

| Key                    | Action                    |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> (first) | Shows the link            |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd>       | Jumps to the main content |

## RTL

Appears at the top inline start (top right in RTL).

---

<!-- docs/layout-and-navigation/back-to-top.md -->

# BackToTop

A floating "Back to top" button that appears after scrolling. It scrolls smoothly, or jumps instantly when the user prefers reduced motion (R3.6, R14.8). It floats at the bottom inline end, above the home indicator.

```tsx
import { BackToTop } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<BackToTop focusTargetId="main-content" />

// In a scroll container
const ref = React.useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
<div ref={ref} className="h-96 overflow-y-auto">
  …
  <BackToTop scrollContainer={ref} position="static" showLabel />
</div>
```

## Props

| Prop              | Type                     | Default   | Description                                      |
| ----------------- | ------------------------ | --------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `threshold`       | `number`                 | `400`     | Show after scrolling this many pixels            |
| `scrollContainer` | `RefObject<HTMLElement>` |           | Scroll a container instead of the window         |
| `focusTargetId`   | `string`                 |           | Move focus here after scrolling (keyboard users) |
| `showLabel`       | `boolean`                | `false`   | Show "Back to top" next to the icon              |
| `position`        | `'fixed' \| 'static'`    | `'fixed'` | Float or render in place                         |
| `alwaysVisible`   | `boolean`                | `false`   | Ignore the threshold                             |

Other `Button` props are passed through.

## Accessibility

- Icon-only, it is named "Back to top"; 44px on touch screens.
- Use `focusTargetId` so keyboard focus moves with the scroll position.

| Key                                 | Action        |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | Scroll to top |

---

<!-- docs/layout-and-navigation/masonry-grid.md -->

# MasonryGrid

A masonry layout with CSS columns (no JavaScript layout): items of different heights pack into columns. Column counts follow the **container** width (container queries, R3.19), so the grid adapts inside sidebars and narrow columns too.

```tsx
import { Card, MasonryGrid } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<MasonryGrid columns={{ base: 1, sm: 2, lg: 3 }}>
  {posts.map((post) => (
    <Card key={post.id} title={post.title}>
      {post.excerpt}
    </Card>
  ))}
</MasonryGrid>
```

## Props

| Prop            | Type                                   | Default                     | Description                   |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| `columns`       | `1–6 \| { base?, sm?, md?, lg?, xl? }` | `{ base: 1, sm: 2, lg: 3 }` | Column counts                 |
| `gap`           | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'`                 | `'md'`                      | Gap between items             |
| `itemClassName` | `string`                               |                             | Classes for each item wrapper |

Breakpoints are container widths: `sm` ≥ 24rem, `md` ≥ 36rem, `lg` ≥ 56rem, `xl` ≥ 72rem. `masonryGridVariants` and `masonryColumnClasses` are exported. Other `<div>` props go to the inner grid element.

## Accessibility

CSS columns flow top to bottom, then to the next column, so the visual order differs from a row-based grid. The DOM (and tab) order is the source order: make sure it makes sense on its own.

## RTL

Columns fill from the inline start (right to left in RTL).

---

<!-- docs/layout-and-navigation/overlay-menu.md -->

# OverlayMenu

A full-screen overlay menu for portals, learning sites and kiosks. It renders in a portal (Radix Dialog), traps focus, closes with <kbd>Escape</kbd> or the close button and returns focus to the trigger. Items use [`SideNav`](./side-nav.md) at the large size (48px rows), and the content respects safe-area insets.

```tsx
import { Button, LanguageSwitcher, Logo, OverlayMenu } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<OverlayMenu
  currentHref={url}
  logo={<Logo src="/logo.svg" alt="Academy" />}
  items={[
    { label: "Home", href: "/", icon: "home" },
    { label: "Courses", href: "/courses", description: "48 courses" },
    { label: "Programmes", items: [{ label: "Diplomas", href: "/programmes/diplomas" }] },
  ]}
  footer={<LanguageSwitcher variant="toggle" />}
/>
```

## Props

| Prop                                    | Type                                         | Default     | Description                         |
| --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `items` / `groups`                      | `NavItem[]` / `NavGroup[]`                   |             | Navigation                          |
| `currentHref`                           | `string`                                     |             | Current URL path                    |
| `match`                                 | `'prefix' \| 'exact'`                        | `'prefix'`  | How `currentHref` matches           |
| `open` / `defaultOpen` / `onOpenChange` | `boolean` / callback                         |             | Controlled or uncontrolled          |
| `trigger`                               | `ReactNode`                                  | menu button | Custom trigger (rendered `asChild`) |
| `logo`                                  | `ReactNode`                                  |             | Top start of the overlay            |
| `footer`                                | `ReactNode`                                  |             | Under the navigation                |
| `title`                                 | `string`                                     | "Menu"      | Accessible dialog title             |
| `classNames`                            | `{ trigger, overlay, content, nav, footer }` |             | Classes for each part               |

The overlay closes after an item is chosen.

## Accessibility

- A modal dialog named "Menu" with the navigation inside; focus is trapped and restored.
- The close button is named "Close menu" and is 44px.

| Key               | Action                          |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>    | Move between items (wraps)      |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd> | Close and return to the trigger |

Animations are disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## RTL

The close button sits at the inline end; nested items indent from the inline start.

---

<!-- docs/layout-and-navigation/hero.md -->

# Hero

The opening block of a portal or content page (R3.7): a heading, lead text, calls to action, an optional search field, and either media beside the text or a photo behind it. The heading and lead use the [fluid type scale](../guides/design-and-density.md#fluid-type) (`clamp()`, R3.4), and the layout follows the hero's own width (container queries), so it works full width or inside a column.

```tsx
import { Button, Hero, SearchBox } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<Hero
  tone="muted"
  align="center"
  eyebrow="National portal"
  title="Government services, in one place"
  description="Apply for passports, pay taxes and track your requests online."
  search={<SearchBox aria-label="Search services" placeholder="Search services" />}
  actions={
    <>
      <Button>Get started</Button>
      <Button variant="outline">Browse all services</Button>
    </>
  }
/>
```

## Media and background images

- `media` puts an image or illustration beside the text. It sits at the inline end (left in RTL) from a 56rem container width and moves below the text in narrower containers.
- `backgroundImage` puts a photo behind the content, covered by a scrim in the hero's `tone` (a gradient of `--background`, `--muted` or `--primary`), so text keeps its contrast on any photo and follows light/dark mode and the brand colour. The image is decorative (`alt=""`) unless you pass `alt`.

```tsx
<Hero
  tone="primary"
  size="lg"
  backgroundImage={{ src: "/img/addu.jpg", srcSet: "…", sizes: "100vw", position: "center 30%" }}
  title="Welcome to Addu City"
  description="The southernmost city of the Maldives."
  actions={<Button variant="secondary">Plan your trip</Button>}
/>
```

## Props

| Prop              | Type                                                       | Default   | Description                                                       |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `title`           | `ReactNode`                                                | required  | The heading                                                       |
| `eyebrow`         | `ReactNode`                                                |           | Short label above the title                                       |
| `description`     | `ReactNode`                                                |           | Lead text                                                         |
| `actions`         | `ReactNode`                                                |           | Buttons or links                                                  |
| `search`          | `ReactNode`                                                |           | A search field under the lead text                                |
| `media`           | `ReactNode`                                                |           | Image or illustration beside the text                             |
| `backgroundImage` | `string \| { src, alt?, srcSet?, sizes?, position? }`      |           | Photo behind the content, with a token scrim                      |
| `tone`            | `"plain" \| "muted" \| "primary"`                          | `"plain"` | Surface colour, or scrim colour over a background image           |
| `size`            | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"`                                     | `"md"`    | Padding and title size (`text-fluid-3xl` / `4xl` / `5xl`)         |
| `align`           | `"start" \| "center"`                                      | `"start"` | Text alignment (centred only without `media`)                     |
| `headingLevel`    | `1 \| 2 \| 3`                                              | `1`       | Heading element                                                   |
| `maxWidth`        | `"3xl" \| "4xl" \| "5xl" \| "6xl" \| "7xl" \| "none"`      | `"6xl"`   | Width of the centred content container                            |
| `rounded`         | `boolean`                                                  | `false`   | Rounded corners (for a hero inside a page, not edge to edge)      |
| `classNames`      | `{ container, content, eyebrow, title, description, search, actions, media, image, overlay }` | | Classes for each part |

Other `<section>` props go to the root. `heroVariants` is exported.

## Accessibility

- The hero is a `<section>` labelled by its heading, so it is a region landmark. The heading is an `<h1>` by default; use `headingLevel` when the page already has one.
- Background images are decorative by default; give `alt` when the photo carries information.
- Text sizes are mostly `rem`, so they follow browser zoom (WCAG 1.4.4), and long headings wrap with `text-wrap: balance`.

## RTL and Dhivehi

Alignment, padding and the media column use logical properties: the text starts on the right and the media is on the left in RTL. With `lang="dv"` the fluid headings get a taller line height so Thaana fili are not clipped.

---

<!-- docs/layout-and-navigation/feature-grid.md -->

# FeatureGrid

A responsive grid of features or services (R3.7): each item has an icon, a title, a description and an optional link. Columns come from **container** queries (R3.19), so the grid fits a full-width page, a two-column layout or a sidebar.

```tsx
import { FeatureGrid, Section } from "@javaabu/onu"

;<Section title="Popular services">
  <FeatureGrid
    items={[
      { icon: "file-text", title: "Passports", description: "Apply or renew online.", href: "/passports" },
      { icon: "banknote", title: "Pay tax", description: "GST and income tax to MIRA.", href: "https://mira.gov.mv", external: true },
      { icon: "help", title: "Help centre", description: "Answers to common questions." },
    ]}
  />
</Section>
```

## Items

| Field         | Type                     | Description                                                              |
| ------------- | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `title`       | `ReactNode`              | Required. The item heading (and its link text)                           |
| `description` | `ReactNode`              | Supporting text                                                          |
| `icon`        | `string \| ReactNode`    | A semantic icon name (follows the configured icon set) or any node       |
| `href`        | `string`                 | Makes the item a link, rendered with the app's link component            |
| `external`    | `boolean`                | Opens in a new tab, with "(opens in a new tab)" for screen readers       |
| `linkLabel`   | `ReactNode \| false`     | Visible cue on linked items. Default "Learn more" (translated); `false` hides it |
| `id`          | `string`                 | Stable key                                                               |

## Props

| Prop           | Type                                | Default   | Description                                                   |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `items`        | `FeatureItem[]`                     | required  | The features                                                  |
| `columns`      | `2 \| 3 \| 4`                       | `3`       | Most columns: 1 → 2 (≥ 36rem) → 3 (≥ 56rem) → 4 (≥ 72rem)      |
| `variant`      | `"card" \| "plain" \| "muted"`      | `"card"`  | Item surface                                                  |
| `align`        | `"start" \| "center"`               | `"start"` | Item alignment                                                |
| `headingLevel` | `2–6`                               | `3`       | Heading level of each title                                   |
| `classNames`   | `{ root, item, icon, title, description, link }` |  | Classes for each part (`root` is the list)                    |

Other `<ul>` props (e.g. `aria-label`) go to the list. `featureGridItemVariants` is exported.

## Accessibility

- The grid is a list (`<ul>`), and each title is a heading, so screen-reader users can jump between items.
- A linked item is **one** link: its title. The link's hit area is stretched over the whole card, and the focus ring shows on the card. The "Learn more" cue is hidden from screen readers so the link isn't announced twice.
- Icons are decorative.

## RTL

Items fill from the inline start, text aligns to the start and the arrow on the link cue points left in RTL.

---

<!-- docs/display-and-feedback/description-list.md -->

# DescriptionList

Label–value pairs for record views ("Email: jane@example.com"). Missing values show "—" (REQUIREMENTS §25.8). Built in-house on a semantic `<dl>`: shadcn has no description list.

```tsx
import { DescriptionList, DescriptionListItem } from "@javaabu/onu"
;<DescriptionList
  items={[
    { label: "Full name", value: "Aishath Shiuna" },
    { label: "ID card", value: "A123456", copyable: true },
    { label: "Phone", value: null }, // shows "—"
  ]}
/>
```

Compose items yourself when values are rich:

```tsx
<DescriptionList layout="inline" striped>
  <DescriptionListItem label="Status">
    <StatusBadge status="success">Active</StatusBadge>
  </DescriptionListItem>
  <DescriptionListItem label="Account" copyable copyValue="7730000123456">
    7730 0001 23456
  </DescriptionListItem>
  <DescriptionListItem label="Remarks" fullWidth>
    Long text spans both columns.
  </DescriptionListItem>
</DescriptionList>
```

## Layout

- `auto` (default): stacked (label above value) in narrow containers, and side by side once the **container** is at least 28rem wide (container query), so it works in sidebars and cards.
- `inline`: always side by side. `stacked`: always stacked.
- The label column width comes from `--onu-dl-label-width` (default `12rem`).

## Props

### DescriptionList

| Prop        | Type                              | Default  | Description                       |
| ----------- | --------------------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------- |
| `items`     | `DescriptionListItemData[]`       |          | Items to render (or use children) |
| `layout`    | `'auto' \| 'stacked' \| 'inline'` | `'auto'` | Label placement                   |
| `striped`   | `boolean`                         | `false`  | Alternate row backgrounds         |
| `divided`   | `boolean`                         | `true`   | Lines between items               |
| `className` | `string`                          |          | Classes for the `<dl>`            |

`DescriptionListItemData`: `{ id?, label, value?, copyable?, copyValue?, fullWidth? }`.

### DescriptionListItem

| Prop         | Type                     | Description                                                         |
| ------------ | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label`      | `ReactNode`              | The term                                                            |
| `children`   | `ReactNode`              | The value; `null`, `undefined`, `""` or `[]` show "—"               |
| `copyable`   | `boolean`                | Show a copy button (copies `copyValue`, or the value if it is text) |
| `copyValue`  | `string`                 | Text to copy                                                        |
| `fullWidth`  | `boolean`                | Span both columns                                                   |
| `classNames` | `{ label, value, copy }` | Classes for each part                                               |

`isEmptyValue(value)` is exported for your own "—" checks.

## Accessibility

- Uses `<dl>`, `<dt>` and `<dd>`, so screen readers announce term/definition pairs.
- "—" is hidden from screen readers and replaced by "Not set" (translated).
- The copy button is labelled "Copy {label}" and "Copied" is announced in a polite live region.

| Key                                 | Action                |
| ----------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>                      | Move to a copy button |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | Copy the value        |

## RTL and Dhivehi

Labels sit on the right in RTL. Values follow the text direction of their content.

---

<!-- docs/display-and-feedback/status-badge.md -->

# StatusBadge

A status label that always pairs colour with an icon and text, so colour is never the only signal (R14.6). It looks like Ant Design's bordered preset-colour tags: a tinted fill, a matching border, AA text and 4px corners.

```tsx
import { StatusBadge } from "@javaabu/onu"

<StatusBadge status="success" />          // ✓ Success
<StatusBadge status="pending">In review</StatusBadge>
```

## Tones

| Tone      | Icon      | Default label | Colour                      | Typical status        |
| --------- | --------- | ------------- | --------------------------- | --------------------- |
| `success` | `success` | Success       | Green (`--onu-preset-green`) | Approved, active      |
| `warning` | `warning` | Warning       | Gold (`--onu-preset-gold`)   | Suspended, expiring   |
| `danger`  | `error`   | Error         | Red (`--onu-preset-red`)     | Rejected, failed      |
| `info`    | `info`    | Info          | Blue (`--onu-preset-blue`)   | Submitted, new        |
| `neutral` | `dot`     | Neutral       | Grey (default tag)          | Draft, unassigned     |
| `pending` | `clock`   | Pending       | Cyan (`--onu-preset-cyan`)   | In review, processing |

The colours are tokens, so a project can retune them; see [Theming](../guides/theming.md#preset-colours).

## Custom statuses

Map your own status values (e.g. from an API) to a tone, label and icon:

```tsx
const statuses: StatusMap = {
  approved: { tone: "success", label: "Approved" },
  rejected: { tone: "danger", label: "Rejected" },
  paid: { tone: "info", label: "Paid", icon: "credit-card" },
}

<StatusBadge status={application.status} statusMap={statuses} />
```

Unknown statuses fall back to the `neutral` tone with the raw value as the label.

## Props

| Prop        | Type                               | Default | Description                                             |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `status`    | `StatusTone \| string`             |         | A tone or a key of `statusMap`                          |
| `statusMap` | `Record<string, StatusDefinition>` |         | `{ tone, label?, icon? }` per status                    |
| `children`  | `ReactNode`                        |         | Label override                                          |
| `icon`      | `string \| ReactNode \| false`     |         | Icon override; `false` hides it                         |
| `size`      | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'`             | `'md'`  | Size                                                    |
| `asChild`   | `boolean`                          | `false` | Render your element (e.g. a link) with the badge styles |

Variants are exported as `statusBadgeVariants` (`tone`, `size`). The root has `data-slot="status-badge"`, `data-tone` and `data-status`.

## Accessibility

- The text label is always present; the icon is decorative.
- Not interactive unless you render a link or button with `asChild`.

## RTL and Dhivehi

Default labels are translated. The icon sits at the inline start in both directions.

---

<!-- docs/display-and-feedback/tag.md -->

# Tag

A compact label (chip) for categories, keywords and filters. It can be static, clickable, a link, removable, or all of these. It looks like an Ant Design tag: 22px tall, 4px corners, a hairline border and 12px text.

```tsx
import { Tag } from "@javaabu/onu"

<Tag>Malé</Tag>
<Tag icon="map-pin" variant="outline">Addu</Tag>
<Tag onRemove={() => remove("laamu")}>Laamu</Tag>
<Tag onClick={toggle} selected={active}>Fuvahmulah</Tag>
<Tag href="/tags/news">News</Tag>
<Tag color="green">Paid</Tag>
```

## Colours

`variant="default"` is the grey tag, `primary` is tinted with the brand colour (`--primary-1` fill, `--primary-3` border), and `outline` is a plain bordered tag. `color` picks one of Ant Design's preset colours instead: `blue`, `cyan`, `green`, `red` or `gold`. They come from the `--onu-preset-<colour>`, `-border` and `-foreground` tokens (see [Theming](../guides/theming.md#preset-colours)), with AA text in light and dark mode.

## Props

| Prop          | Type                                  | Default     | Description                                       |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `variant`     | `'default' \| 'primary' \| 'outline'` | `'default'` | Look                                              |
| `color`       | `'blue' \| 'cyan' \| 'green' \| 'red' \| 'gold'` |  | Ant preset colour (overrides the variant's colours) |
| `size`        | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'`                | `'md'`      | Size                                              |
| `icon`        | `string \| ReactNode`                 |             | Icon before the label                             |
| `onClick`     | `(e) => void`                         |             | Makes the label a button                          |
| `href`        | `string`                              |             | Makes the label a link                            |
| `selected`    | `boolean`                             |             | Selected state (`aria-pressed` on clickable tags) |
| `onRemove`    | `() => void`                          |             | Shows a × button                                  |
| `removeLabel` | `string`                              |             | Accessible name for × (default "Remove {label}")  |
| `disabled`    | `boolean`                             |             | Disables the tag and its × button                 |
| `classNames`  | `{ label, remove, icon }`             |             | Classes for each part                             |

Variants are exported as `tagVariants` (`variant`, `color`, `size`). Parts have `data-slot="tag"` (with `data-variant` and `data-color`), `tag-label` and `tag-remove`.

## Accessibility

- The remove button has its own accessible name ("Remove Malé").
- On touch screens the label and × get a 44px hit area without changing the layout.

| Key                                      | Action                                   |
| ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd>      | Activate a clickable tag or the × button |
| <kbd>Delete</kbd> / <kbd>Backspace</kbd> | Remove a focused clickable/link tag      |

## RTL and Dhivehi

The × button sits at the inline end, so it moves to the left in RTL. Dhivehi labels use the Thaana font automatically.

---

<!-- docs/display-and-feedback/user-avatar.md -->

# UserAvatar

A person's picture with an initials fallback that handles English **and Dhivehi** names, sizes, shapes and a presence dot. Extends shadcn's `Avatar` (which stays available unchanged as `Avatar`).

```tsx
import { UserAvatar, getInitials } from "@javaabu/onu"

<UserAvatar name="Aishath Shiuna" src={user.photo_url} />
<UserAvatar name="އަޙްމަދު ޢަލީ" status="online" size="lg" />
getInitials("Ahmed Ali") // "AA"
getInitials("އަޙްމަދު ޢަލީ") // "އަޢަ"
```

## Initials

`getInitials(name, max = 2)` takes the first letters of the first and last words. Thaana initials keep the vowel sign (fili) with the consonant, so "އަޙްމަދު" gives "އަ", not a bare "އ". Punctuation such as "(Ali)" or "Mr." is ignored. Thaana initials render with `lang="dv"` and the Thaana font.

## Props

| Prop         | Type                                        | Default    | Description                                                  |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `name`       | `string`                                    |            | Used for initials and the accessible name                    |
| `src`        | `string`                                    |            | Image URL; initials show while loading or if it fails        |
| `alt`        | `string`                                    | `name`     | Image alt text                                               |
| `size`       | `'xs' \| 'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'xl'`      | `'md'`     | 24, 32, 40, 48 or 64px                                       |
| `shape`      | `'circle' \| 'square'`                      | `'circle'` | Shape                                                        |
| `status`     | `'online' \| 'offline' \| 'busy' \| 'away'` |            | Presence dot                                                 |
| `decorative` | `boolean`                                   | `false`    | Hide from screen readers (when the name is shown next to it) |
| `fallback`   | `ReactNode`                                 |            | Replace the initials                                         |
| `classNames` | `{ image, fallback, status }`               |            | Classes for each part                                        |

Variants are exported as `userAvatarVariants`.

## Accessibility

- The avatar is an image named after the person, plus the presence ("Aishath Shiuna, Online"), so the dot's colour is not the only signal.
- Use `decorative` when the name is already visible next to the avatar, so it isn't read twice.

## RTL

The presence dot sits at the bottom inline-end corner, so it moves to the left in RTL.

---

<!-- docs/display-and-feedback/user-avatar-group.md -->

# UserAvatarGroup

Overlapping avatars with a "+N" button that lists everyone else. Named `UserAvatarGroup` so shadcn's `AvatarGroup` primitive stays available.

```tsx
import { UserAvatarGroup } from "@javaabu/onu"
;<UserAvatarGroup
  users={[
    { id: 1, name: "Aishath Shiuna", status: "online" },
    { id: 2, name: "Ahmed Ali" },
    { id: 3, name: "މަރިޔަމް ޒާހިރާ", src: "/m.jpg" },
  ]}
  max={4}
/>
```

When there are more than `max` people, `max - 1` avatars are shown followed by "+N". The button opens a popover with the remaining names (tap or keyboard, nothing depends on hover).

## Props

| Prop             | Type                                   | Default | Description                              |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `users`          | `{ id?, name, src?, status? }[]`       |         | People to show                           |
| `max`            | `number`                               | `4`     | Avatars shown, including the "+N" button |
| `size`           | `'xs' \| 'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'xl'` | `'md'`  | Avatar size                              |
| `shape`          | `'circle' \| 'square'`                 |         | Avatar shape                             |
| `renderOverflow` | `(hidden) => ReactNode`                |         | Custom popover content                   |
| `classNames`     | `{ avatar, count, popover }`           |         | Classes for each part                    |

## Accessibility

- The group is a `role="group"` named "{count} people".
- "+N" is a button named "Show N more people"; focus returns to it when the list closes.

| Key                                 | Action                         |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | Open the list of hidden people |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd>                   | Close the list                 |

## RTL

Avatars overlap toward the inline end, so the stack reads right to left in RTL.

---

<!-- docs/display-and-feedback/keyboard-key.md -->

# KeyboardKey

Shows a key or keyboard shortcut using shadcn's `Kbd`. Combos adapt to the platform: <kbd>⌘</kbd><kbd>K</kbd> on macOS and iOS, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>K</kbd> on Windows and Linux.

```tsx
import { KeyboardKey, formatShortcut } from "@javaabu/onu"

<KeyboardKey>Esc</KeyboardKey>
<KeyboardKey keys="mod+k" />        // ⌘K or Ctrl+K
<KeyboardKey keys="ctrl+shift+p" />
<KeyboardKey keys="g d" />          // sequence: G then D
formatShortcut("mod+s", "other")    // "Ctrl+S"
```

## Key names

`mod` is ⌘ on Apple platforms and Ctrl elsewhere. Also understood: `cmd`/`meta`, `ctrl`, `alt`/`option`, `shift`, `enter`, `esc`, `tab`, `backspace`, `delete`, `space`, `up`, `down`, `left`, `right`. Anything else is shown as typed (single letters upper-cased).

## Props

| Prop         | Type                 | Default  | Description                            |
| ------------ | -------------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `keys`       | `string`             |          | Combination (`+`) and sequence (space) |
| `children`   | `ReactNode`          |          | Custom single key instead of `keys`    |
| `platform`   | `'mac' \| 'other'`   | detected | Force a platform                       |
| `classNames` | `{ key, separator }` |          | Classes for each part                  |

`detectPlatform()` and `formatShortcut(shortcut, platform?)` are exported for menus and tooltips. Detection is SSR-safe (server renders the non-Apple form).

## Accessibility

Screen readers hear the key names ("Command K", "Control Shift P"), not the symbols; the visual keys are hidden from them.

## RTL and Dhivehi

Shortcuts always read left to right, also in RTL pages. Spoken key names are translated.

---

<!-- docs/display-and-feedback/callout.md -->

# Callout (Alert)

An alert box for messages that need attention: info, success, warning or destructive, with a title, description, actions and an optional dismiss button. Extends shadcn's `Alert` (which stays available as `Alert`).

```tsx
import { Callout } from "@javaabu/onu"

<Callout variant="success" title="Application submitted" description="Reference APP-2026-00412." />

<Callout
  variant="warning"
  title="Permit expires in 5 days"
  description="Renew before 30 June to avoid a late fee."
  actions={<Button size="sm">Renew now</Button>}
  dismissible
/>
```

## Props

| Prop           | Type                                                             | Default     | Description                            |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `variant`      | `'default' \| 'info' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'destructive'` | `'default'` | Tone                                   |
| `title`        | `ReactNode`                                                      |             | Title                                  |
| `description`  | `ReactNode`                                                      |             | Body (or `children`)                   |
| `actions`      | `ReactNode`                                                      |             | Buttons or links under the description |
| `icon`         | `string \| ReactNode \| false`                                   | per variant | Icon override; `false` hides it        |
| `dismissible`  | `boolean`                                                        | `false`     | Show a dismiss (×) button              |
| `open`         | `boolean`                                                        |             | Controlled visibility                  |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open) => void`                                                 |             | Called when dismissed                  |
| `onDismiss`    | `() => void`                                                     |             | Called after dismissing                |
| `role`         | `string`                                                         | see below   | ARIA role override                     |
| `classNames`   | `{ icon, title, description, actions, dismiss }`                 |             | Classes for each part                  |

Variants are exported as `calloutVariants`.

## Accessibility

- `warning` and `destructive` use `role="alert"` (announced immediately); the others use `role="status"` (announced politely). Pass `role="note"` for static content that shouldn't be announced.
- Each variant has its own icon, so meaning doesn't rely on colour.
- The dismiss button is labelled "Dismiss" and is 44px on touch screens.

| Key                                 | Action                    |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>                      | Move to actions / dismiss |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | Activate                  |

## RTL

The icon is at the inline start and the dismiss button at the inline end, so they swap sides in RTL.

---

<!-- docs/display-and-feedback/notice.md -->

# Notice

A subtle inline notice: a short line of supporting text with an icon, quieter than a [Callout](./callout.md). Good for hints under a section or next to a form.

```tsx
import { Notice } from "@javaabu/onu"

<Notice>Changes apply from the next billing period.</Notice>
<Notice tone="warning" variant="bordered">Card payments may include a bank fee.</Notice>
<Notice tone="info" variant="subtle" icon="clock">Last synced 5 minutes ago.</Notice>
```

## Props

| Prop      | Type                                                             | Default     | Description                      |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | -------------------------------- |
| `tone`    | `'neutral' \| 'info' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'destructive'` | `'neutral'` | Colour and default icon          |
| `variant` | `'plain' \| 'subtle' \| 'bordered'`                              | `'plain'`   | Background / inline-start border |
| `icon`    | `string \| ReactNode \| false`                                   | per tone    | Icon override; `false` hides it  |

Variants are exported as `noticeVariants`.

## Accessibility

Rendered with `role="note"`, so it is not announced as an alert. Use a `Callout` for messages that must interrupt.

## RTL

The `bordered` variant draws its border on the inline start, so it moves to the right in RTL.

---

<!-- docs/display-and-feedback/announcement-bar.md -->

# AnnouncementBar

A full-width bar at the top of the page for site-wide news. Dismissible, and when you give it an `id` the dismissal is remembered in `localStorage`.

```tsx
import { AnnouncementBar } from "@javaabu/onu"
;<AnnouncementBar id="housing-2026" icon="megaphone" href="/housing" linkText="Apply now">
  Housing scheme applications close on 30 June.
</AnnouncementBar>
```

Change the `id` to show a new announcement to people who dismissed the old one.

## Props

| Prop            | Type                                            | Default               | Description                         |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `id`            | `string`                                        |                       | Persist the dismissal under this id |
| `variant`       | `'primary' \| 'neutral' \| 'info' \| 'warning'` | `'primary'`           | Colours                             |
| `href`          | `string`                                        |                       | Link after the message              |
| `linkText`      | `ReactNode`                                     |                       | Link text                           |
| `icon`          | `string \| ReactNode`                           |                       | Icon before the message             |
| `dismissible`   | `boolean`                                       | `true`                | Show the dismiss button             |
| `onDismiss`     | `() => void`                                    |                       | Called after dismissing             |
| `storagePrefix` | `string`                                        | `'onu-announcement:'` | `localStorage` key prefix           |
| `classNames`    | `{ message, link, dismiss }`                    |                       | Classes for each part               |

The link uses the `linkComponent` from `OnuProvider` (Inertia, Next.js, …). Variants are exported as `announcementBarVariants`.

## Accessibility

- A `role="region"` landmark named "Announcement".
- The dismiss button is labelled "Dismiss" and is 44px on touch screens.

## SSR

The stored dismissal is read on the client, so a dismissed bar may flash during hydration in SSR apps. Render it client-side only if that matters.

## RTL

The dismiss button sits at the inline end, and the link arrow mirrors in RTL.

---

<!-- docs/display-and-feedback/cookie-consent.md -->

# CookieConsent

A cookie banner with a preferences dialog. People can **accept all**, **reject non-essential** cookies, or choose per category. The choice is saved in `localStorage`, and the banner stays away until you change `version`. Built on shadcn's `Dialog`, `Switch` and `Button`.

```tsx
import { CookieConsent, useCookieConsent, openCookiePreferences } from "@javaabu/onu"

// Once, near the root:
<CookieConsent policyHref="/privacy" onChange={(consent) => analytics.configure(consent.categories)} />

// Anywhere:
const consent = useCookieConsent()
if (consent?.categories.analytics) loadAnalytics()

// A "Cookie settings" link in the footer:
<button onClick={openCookiePreferences}>Cookie settings</button>
```

## Categories

The defaults are `necessary` (always on), `preferences`, `analytics` and `marketing`, with translated labels. Pass your own:

```tsx
<CookieConsent
  categories={[
    { id: "necessary", label: "Essential", required: true },
    { id: "analytics", label: "Statistics", description: "Anonymous usage data", defaultEnabled: false },
  ]}
  version={2}
/>
```

## Props

| Prop                      | Type                                    | Default                | Description                                               |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `categories`              | `CookieCategory[]`                      | 4 defaults             | `{ id, label, description?, required?, defaultEnabled? }` |
| `version`                 | `string \| number`                      | `1`                    | Bump to ask everyone again                                |
| `storageKey`              | `string`                                | `'onu-cookie-consent'` | `localStorage` key                                        |
| `onChange`                | `(consent) => void`                     |                        | Called when a choice is saved                             |
| `title` / `description`   | `ReactNode`                             | translated             | Banner text                                               |
| `policyHref`              | `string`                                |                        | Link to the cookie policy                                 |
| `policyLinkText`          | `ReactNode`                             | "Cookie policy"        | Link text                                                 |
| `preferencesOpen`         | `boolean`                               |                        | Controlled dialog                                         |
| `onPreferencesOpenChange` | `(open) => void`                        |                        | Dialog open change                                        |
| `classNames`              | `{ banner, actions, dialog, category }` |                        | Classes for each part                                     |

Stored value (`CookieConsentValue`): `{ categories: Record<string, boolean>, version, updatedAt }`. Helpers: `useCookieConsent(storageKey?)`, `readCookieConsent(storageKey?)`, `openCookiePreferences()`.

## Accessibility

- The banner is a region labelled by its heading; it does not trap focus or block the page.
- The preferences dialog traps focus, closes with <kbd>Escape</kbd>, and returns focus to what opened it.
- Each category is a labelled switch with its description; required categories are disabled and marked "Always on".

| Key               | Action                          |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>    | Move between buttons / switches |
| <kbd>Space</kbd>  | Toggle a category               |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd> | Close the dialog without saving |

## Responsive

The banner is fixed to the bottom (respecting the safe-area inset); buttons stack on narrow screens and line up from 28rem.

---

<!-- docs/display-and-feedback/toast.md -->

# Toast

Short notifications, using [sonner](https://sonner.emilkowal.ski) (shadcn's toast). Onu's `Toaster` adds Onu icons, follows `useTheme()`, uses logical positions that flip in RTL, and the Dhivehi font. It replaces the shadcn `Toaster` export with a compatible API.

```tsx
import { Toaster, toast } from "@javaabu/onu"

// Once, inside OnuProvider (and ThemeProvider):
;<Toaster />

toast("Draft saved")
toast.success("User saved", { description: "Aishath Shiuna" })
toast.error("Payment failed")
toast.warning("Session expires in 2 minutes")
toast.info("3 new applications")
toast.promise(upload(file), { loading: "Uploading…", success: "Uploaded", error: "Upload failed" })
toast("Moved to trash", { action: { label: "Undo", onClick: restore } })
```

## Toaster props

| Prop       | Type                                                                                            | Default        | Description               |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------------- |
| `position` | `'top-start' \| 'top-center' \| 'top-end' \| 'bottom-start' \| 'bottom-center' \| 'bottom-end'` | `'bottom-end'` | `start`/`end` flip in RTL |
| `theme`    | `'light' \| 'dark' \| 'system'`                                                                 | `useTheme()`   | Override the theme        |
| `icons`    | `ToastIcons`                                                                                    | Onu icons      | Override icons            |

All other [sonner `Toaster` props](https://sonner.emilkowal.ski/toaster) are passed through. `resolveToastPosition(position, dir)` is exported.

`toast` is sonner's `toast` function, re-exported so you only import from Onu.

## Accessibility

- Toasts are announced by sonner's live region, labelled "Notifications" (translated).
- The close button is labelled "Close" (translated).
- Don't put the only copy of important information in a toast; it disappears.

| Key                         | Action                    |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>T</kbd> | Focus the toasts (sonner) |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>              | Move to a toast's action  |

## RTL and Dhivehi

`dir` comes from `OnuProvider`, so `bottom-end` is bottom-left in RTL and swipe-to-dismiss follows. With `locale="dv"` toasts use the Thaana font.

---

<!-- docs/display-and-feedback/conditional-link.md -->

# ConditionalLink

Renders a link only when there is somewhere to go **and** the user may go there; otherwise renders the same content as plain text. Handy in tables and detail views.

```tsx
import { ConditionalLink } from "@javaabu/onu"

<ConditionalLink href={user.url} when={can("view", user)}>
  {user.name}
</ConditionalLink>

<ConditionalLink href={null}>No profile</ConditionalLink> // plain <span>
```

The link uses the `linkComponent` from `OnuProvider` (R16.2), so it works with Inertia's or Next.js's `Link`.

## Props

| Prop            | Type             | Default  | Description                         |
| --------------- | ---------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `href`          | `string \| null` |          | Link target; empty means plain text |
| `when`          | `boolean`        | `true`   | Extra condition (e.g. a permission) |
| `fallbackAs`    | `ElementType`    | `'span'` | Element for the plain-text version  |
| `className`     | `string`         |          | Classes for both versions           |
| `linkClassName` | `string`         |          | Classes for the link version only   |

Other anchor props and `ref` go to the link. Both versions have `data-slot="conditional-link"` and `data-linked="true|false"`.

## Accessibility

Plain text is not focusable, so keyboard users only stop on real links.

---

<!-- docs/display-and-feedback/conditional-display.md -->

# ConditionalDisplay

Shows/hides or enables/disables part of a form depending on another field's value. A React port of `conditionalDisplay` from Javaabu's js-utilities. Hidden content is wrapped in a `disabled` fieldset, so its fields are **not submitted**.

```tsx
import { ConditionalDisplay } from "@javaabu/onu"

// react-hook-form: pass control + name and the value is watched for you
<ConditionalDisplay control={control} name="applicant_type" when="company">
  <FormField label="Company name" name="company_name">
    <TextInput {...register("company_name")} />
  </FormField>
</ConditionalDisplay>

// Any value (state, watch(), props)
<ConditionalDisplay value={type} when={["company", "ngo"]}>…</ConditionalDisplay>

// Enable instead of show
<ConditionalDisplay control={control} name="has_vehicle" action="enable">…</ConditionalDisplay>
```

## Matching

- `when` omitted: matches any non-empty value (not `""`, `"0"`, `0`, `false`, `null` or `[]`), e.g. a ticked checkbox.
- `when` a value or a list: compared as strings, so `1` matches `"1"`. Array field values (checkbox groups, multi-selects) match if any item matches.
- `when` a function: `(value) => boolean`.
- `not` inverts the match.

## Actions

| `action`         | Matches           | Doesn't match     |
| ---------------- | ----------------- | ----------------- |
| `show` (default) | visible, enabled  | hidden, disabled  |
| `hide`           | hidden, disabled  | visible, enabled  |
| `enable`         | visible, enabled  | visible, disabled |
| `disable`        | visible, disabled | visible, enabled  |

## Props

| Prop      | Type                                        | Default   | Description                                          |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------- | --------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`   | `unknown`                                   |           | Value to test                                        |
| `control` | `Control`                                   |           | react-hook-form control (with `name`)                |
| `name`    | `FieldPath`                                 |           | Field to watch (needs `control` or a `FormProvider`) |
| `when`    | `value \| value[] \| (value) => boolean`    | non-empty | Condition                                            |
| `not`     | `boolean`                                   | `false`   | Invert                                               |
| `action`  | `'show' \| 'hide' \| 'enable' \| 'disable'` | `'show'`  | What a match does                                    |
| `unmount` | `boolean`                                   | `false`   | Unmount hidden children instead of hiding them       |

The wrapper is a `<fieldset>` with `display: contents`, `data-slot="conditional-display"` and `data-state="enabled|disabled|hidden"`. `matchesCondition()` and `resolveConditional()` are exported.

:::info react-hook-form
A natively disabled fieldset stops the browser from submitting the fields. react-hook-form reads values from its own state, so also skip hidden fields in your schema (e.g. zod `.optional()` with a refinement on the controlling field) or use `shouldUnregister`.
:::

## Accessibility

Hidden content uses the `hidden` attribute, so it is removed from the accessibility tree; disabled content is announced as disabled.

---

<!-- docs/display-and-feedback/publish-box.md -->

# PublishBox

The "Publish" panel of a content editor: status, visibility and publish date, with **Preview**, **Save draft** and **Publish** actions. The primary button reads **Schedule** for a future date and **Update** once published. Fits a sidebar; the buttons stack in narrow containers.

```tsx
import { PublishBox } from "@javaabu/onu"
;<PublishBox
  status={post.status}
  onStatusChange={setStatus}
  visibility={post.visibility}
  onVisibilityChange={setVisibility}
  publishAt={post.published_at}
  onPublishAtChange={setPublishedAt}
  previewHref={`/news/${post.slug}?preview=1`}
  onSaveDraft={() => save({ status: "draft" })}
  onPublish={() => save({ status: "published" })}
/>
```

Returning a promise from `onSaveDraft` / `onPublish` shows a spinner on that button and disables both until it settles.

Without the `on…Change` handlers each row is read-only (a status badge, an icon + label, a formatted date or "Immediately").

## Props

| Prop                 | Type                                                           | Default                   | Description                                     |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `status`             | `'draft' \| 'pending' \| 'scheduled' \| 'published' \| string` |                           | Current status                                  |
| `onStatusChange`     | `(status) => void`                                             |                           | Show a status select                            |
| `statusOptions`      | `{ value, label }[]`                                           | draft, pending, published | Select options                                  |
| `statusMap`          | `StatusMap`                                                    |                           | Badge tones/labels for custom statuses          |
| `visibility`         | `'public' \| 'private' \| string`                              |                           | Shows the visibility row when set               |
| `onVisibilityChange` | `(visibility) => void`                                         |                           | Show a visibility select                        |
| `visibilityOptions`  | `{ value, label }[]`                                           | public, private           | Select options                                  |
| `publishAt`          | `Date \| string \| number \| null`                             |                           | Publish date                                    |
| `onPublishAtChange`  | `(date \| null) => void`                                       |                           | Show a date-time field                          |
| `renderDateInput`    | `({ id, value, onChange }) => ReactNode`                       |                           | Use your own picker (e.g. Onu's DateTimePicker) |
| `previewHref`        | `string`                                                       |                           | Preview link (opens a new tab)                  |
| `onPreview`          | `() => void`                                                   |                           | Preview button                                  |
| `onSaveDraft`        | `() => void \| Promise`                                        |                           | Save draft button (hidden once published)       |
| `onPublish`          | `() => void \| Promise`                                        |                           | Publish / Schedule / Update button              |
| `busy`               | `'draft' \| 'publish' \| null`                                 | automatic                 | Force a busy state                              |
| `disabled`           | `boolean`                                                      | `false`                   | Disable every control                           |
| `title`              | `ReactNode`                                                    | "Publish"                 | Card title                                      |
| `classNames`         | `{ header, content, footer, row }`                             |                           | Classes for each part                           |

## Accessibility

- Every control is labelled; selects follow the shadcn `Select` (listbox) pattern.
- The card has `aria-busy` while an action runs, and the busy button is disabled to prevent double submits.

## RTL and Dhivehi

Labels, statuses and buttons are translated. The date field stays left-to-right.

<!-- docs/display-and-feedback/last-edited-by.md -->

# LastEditedBy

"Last edited by Aishath Shiuna · 5 minutes ago", with a small avatar. The time is a [RelativeDate](./relative-date.md), so the exact date shows on hover, focus, or underneath on touch screens.

```tsx
import { LastEditedBy } from "@javaabu/onu"
;<LastEditedBy
  user={{ name: record.editor.name, avatar: record.editor.photo, href: record.editor.url }}
  at={record.updated_at}
/>
```

## Props

| Prop         | Type                               | Default | Description                                  |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `user`       | `{ name, avatar?, href? } \| null` |         | Who made the change (name links when `href`) |
| `at`         | `Date \| string \| number \| null` |         | When; empty shows "—"                        |
| `hideAvatar` | `boolean`                          | `false` | Hide the avatar                              |
| `dateProps`  | `RelativeDateProps`                |         | Passed to the relative date                  |
| `classNames` | `{ avatar, name, date }`           |         | Classes for each part                        |

## Accessibility

The avatar is decorative (the name is in the text). The sentence is translated as a whole, so word order is right in Dhivehi.

<!-- docs/display-and-feedback/relative-date.md -->

# RelativeDate

A date shown relative to now ("just now", "5 minutes ago", "3 days ago", "in 2 hours"), as specified in REQUIREMENTS §25.5. Uses the active locale's date-fns `formatDistance`, so Dhivehi reads "5 މިނެޓު ކުރިން".

```tsx
import { RelativeDate } from "@javaabu/onu"

<RelativeDate value={comment.created_at} />
<RelativeDate value={null} /> // —
```

## Behaviour (§25.5)

- Shows "just now" (under 45 seconds either way), "5 minutes ago", "3 days ago" or "in 2 hours".
- **Hovering or focusing** it shows the exact date and time in a tooltip.
- On **touch screens** (`(hover: none)`), the exact date and time is shown in smaller text underneath instead.
- With no value (or an invalid one) it shows "—" ("Not set" for screen readers).
- It keeps itself up to date: every 10 s for the first minute, 30 s for the first hour, 5 min for the first day, then hourly.
- Renders `<time dateTime="…ISO…">`.

## Props

| Prop             | Type                               | Default   | Description                                         |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------- | --------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`          | `Date \| string \| number \| null` |           | The date                                            |
| `now`            | `Date \| string \| number`         | live      | Fixed reference time (tests, SSR); disables updates |
| `updateInterval` | `number \| false`                  | automatic | Refresh interval in ms, or never                    |
| `format`         | `string`                           | `'PPPp'`  | date-fns format of the exact date                   |
| `showExact`      | `boolean`                          | `true`    | Tooltip / touch line; `false` uses a `title` only   |
| `tooltipDelay`   | `number`                           | `300`     | Hover delay in ms                                   |
| `classNames`     | `{ exact, tooltip, empty }`        |           | Classes for each part                               |

`formatRelativeDate(date, now, locale, t)` and `autoUpdateInterval(date, now)` are exported.

## Accessibility

- The `<time>` is focusable (when the tooltip is used) so keyboard users can reveal the exact date; the tooltip also opens on focus, and closes with <kbd>Escape</kbd>.
- A dotted underline hints that more detail is available.

| Key               | Action                     |
| ----------------- | -------------------------- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>    | Focus and show the tooltip |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd> | Hide the tooltip           |

## SSR

The first render uses the server's time; pass `now` if you need identical server and client output.

---

<!-- docs/display-and-feedback/countdown.md -->

# Countdown

Counts down to a date in days, hours, minutes and seconds, with tabular numbers (R7.5). The visible clock ticks every second, but screen reader announcements are throttled so they aren't flooded.

```tsx
import { Countdown } from "@javaabu/onu"

<Countdown to="2026-06-30T23:59:59+05:00" onComplete={() => setClosed(true)} />
<Countdown to={deadline} variant="inline" completeText="Registration closed" />
```

## Props

| Prop            | Type                               | Default   | Description                                                           |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------- | --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `to`            | `Date \| string \| number`         |           | Target date and time                                                  |
| `onComplete`    | `() => void`                       |           | Called once at zero (straight away if `to` is already past)           |
| `variant`       | `'boxes' \| 'inline'`              | `'boxes'` | Boxes with labels, or `00:00:00`                                      |
| `size`          | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'`             | `'md'`    | Number size (boxes)                                                   |
| `showDays`      | `boolean \| 'auto'`                | `'auto'`  | `auto` hides days when there are none left (hours then count past 24) |
| `showSeconds`   | `boolean`                          | `true`    | Show seconds                                                          |
| `announceEvery` | `number`                           | `60`      | Seconds between screen reader announcements                           |
| `completeText`  | `ReactNode`                        |           | Shown instead of zeros when finished                                  |
| `classNames`    | `{ unit, value, label, complete }` |           | Classes for each part                                                 |

`getCountdownParts(target, now)` and `describeDuration(seconds, t)` are exported. The root has `data-state="running|complete"`.

## Accessibility

- The clock has `role="timer"` (not announced on every tick).
- A separate polite live region announces "2 days, 3 hours, 5 minutes remaining" once per `announceEvery` seconds, and "Time's up" at the end.

## RTL and Dhivehi

Unit labels are translated. Boxes follow the page direction (days first, at the inline start); the inline `00:00:00` clock always reads left to right.

---

<!-- docs/display-and-feedback/activity-feed.md -->

# ActivityFeed

A log of who did what and when: grouped by day (Today, Yesterday, 3 October 2026), with actor avatars, relative timestamps and a "Load more" button.

```tsx
import { ActivityFeed } from "@javaabu/onu"
;<ActivityFeed
  items={[
    { id: 1, actor: { name: "Aishath Shiuna" }, action: "approved the application", timestamp: "2026-03-12T09:12:00Z" },
    { id: 2, icon: "settings", action: "Status changed to Pending", timestamp: "2026-03-11T14:00:00Z" },
  ]}
  hasMore={page < lastPage}
  onLoadMore={() => fetchNextPage()}
/>
```

## Props

| Prop          | Type                                 | Default    | Description                                         |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------ | ---------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `items`       | `ActivityItem[]`                     |            | `{ id, actor?, action, timestamp, icon?, detail? }` |
| `hasMore`     | `boolean`                            | `false`    | Show "Load more"                                    |
| `onLoadMore`  | `() => void \| Promise`              |            | Load the next page (spinner while the promise runs) |
| `loadingMore` | `boolean`                            | automatic  | Force the loading state                             |
| `groupByDay`  | `boolean`                            | `true`     | Day headings                                        |
| `dayFormat`   | `string`                             | `'PPP'`    | date-fns format for older days                      |
| `title`       | `ReactNode \| null`                  | "Activity" | Heading; `null` hides it                            |
| `emptyText`   | `ReactNode`                          | translated | Shown with no items                                 |
| `now`         | `Date`                               | live       | Reference time (tests, SSR)                         |
| `classNames`  | `{ group, heading, item, loadMore }` |            | Classes for each part                               |

`groupActivityByDay(items)` is exported.

## Accessibility

- A `<section>` labelled by its heading; each day is an ordered list under an `h3`.
- `aria-busy` is set while loading more; the button is disabled to prevent double loads.

| Key                                 | Action    |
| ----------------------------------- | --------- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | Load more |

## RTL

Avatars and the timeline line sit at the inline start, so they move to the right in RTL.
