<!-- docs/display-and-feedback/comment-thread.md -->

# CommentThread

A discussion with nested replies. People can edit and delete their own comments, and the composer can type Thaana (`thaana` prop, R13.3). Mentions are not built in.

```tsx
import { CommentThread } from "@javaabu/onu"
;<CommentThread
  comments={comments}
  currentUserId={user.id}
  thaana
  onAdd={(body, parentId) => api.post("/comments", { body, parent_id: parentId })}
  onEdit={(id, body) => api.patch(`/comments/${id}`, { body })}
  onDelete={(id) => api.delete(`/comments/${id}`)}
/>
```

`CommentData`: `{ id, author: { id, name, avatar? }, body, createdAt, editedAt?, replies? }`. Return a promise from the callbacks to show a spinner; the composer clears after a successful submit.

## Props

| Prop            | Type                                          | Default    | Description                                   |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ---------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `comments`      | `CommentData[]`                               |            | Top-level comments with nested `replies`      |
| `currentUserId` | `string \| number`                            |            | Own comments get Edit and Delete              |
| `onAdd`         | `(body, parentId \| null) => void \| Promise` |            | Enables the composer and Reply                |
| `onEdit`        | `(id, body) => void \| Promise`               |            | Enables Edit (text bodies only)               |
| `onDelete`      | `(id) => void \| Promise`                     |            | Enables Delete (asks for confirmation)        |
| `canEdit`       | `(comment) => boolean`                        | own        | Who may edit                                  |
| `canDelete`     | `(comment) => boolean`                        | own        | Who may delete                                |
| `maxDepth`      | `number`                                      | `3`        | Indented levels; deeper replies line up       |
| `thaana`        | `boolean \| ThaanaOptions`                    |            | Thaana typing in the composer (with a toggle) |
| `title`         | `ReactNode \| null`                           | "Comments" | Heading; `null` hides it                      |
| `now`           | `Date`                                        | live       | Reference time for relative dates             |
| `classNames`    | `{ list, comment, body, composer }`           |            | Classes for each part                         |

## Accessibility

- Each comment is an `<article>` named after its author; replies are nested lists.
- Reply opens a composer and moves focus into it; <kbd>Escape</kbd> or Cancel returns focus to the Reply button. Edit works the same way.
- Delete asks for confirmation in an alert dialog; focus returns to the delete button.

| Key                                           | Action                              |
| --------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>⌘</kbd>+<kbd>Enter</kbd> | Send                                |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd>                             | Cancel a reply or edit              |
| <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>T</kbd>  | Switch Thaana/Latin (with `thaana`) |

## RTL and Thaana

Bodies use `dir="auto"`, so Dhivehi comments align right even on an English page. Reply lines are on the inline start.

---

<!-- docs/display-and-feedback/notes.md -->

# Notes

Internal notes on a record: who wrote what and when, with an add-note box that can type Thaana (`thaana` prop, R13.3) and delete with confirmation.

```tsx
import { Notes } from "@javaabu/onu"
;<Notes
  notes={record.notes}
  currentUserId={user.id}
  thaana
  onAdd={(body) => api.post(`/records/${id}/notes`, { body })}
  onDelete={(noteId) => api.delete(`/notes/${noteId}`)}
/>
```

`NoteData`: `{ id, author: { id?, name, avatar? }, body, createdAt }`.

## Props

| Prop               | Type                        | Default | Description                                                          |
| ------------------ | --------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `notes`            | `NoteData[]`                |         | Notes, newest first                                                  |
| `onAdd`            | `(body) => void \| Promise` |         | Shows the add-note box                                               |
| `onDelete`         | `(id) => void \| Promise`   |         | Delete (after confirmation)                                          |
| `canDelete`        | `(note) => boolean`         |         | Who may delete; default everyone, or the author with `currentUserId` |
| `currentUserId`    | `string \| number`          |         | Restricts delete to the author                                       |
| `thaana`           | `boolean \| ThaanaOptions`  |         | Thaana typing in the note box                                        |
| `composerPosition` | `'top' \| 'bottom'`         | `'top'` | Where the box sits                                                   |
| `title`            | `ReactNode \| null`         | "Notes" | Heading; `null` hides it                                             |
| `now`              | `Date`                      | live    | Reference time                                                       |
| `classNames`       | `{ list, note, composer }`  |         | Classes for each part                                                |

## Accessibility

- A labelled `<section>`; the note box has an accessible name and a hint for <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Enter</kbd>.
- Delete opens an alert dialog; focus returns to the delete button when it closes.

| Key                                           | Action                              |
| --------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>⌘</kbd>+<kbd>Enter</kbd> | Add the note                        |
| <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>T</kbd>  | Switch Thaana/Latin (with `thaana`) |

## RTL and Thaana

Note bodies use `dir="auto"`. With `thaana` the box is RTL with `lang="dv"` and the Thaana font.

---

<!-- docs/display-and-feedback/icon-text.md -->

# IconText

An icon next to a short piece of text, aligned and sized together: meta rows such as location, date or phone number.

```tsx
import { IconText } from "@javaabu/onu"

<IconText icon="map-pin" tone="muted">Malé</IconText>
<IconText icon="external-link" iconPosition="end" iconLabel="opens in a new tab" asChild>
  <a href="https://gazette.gov.mv" target="_blank">Gazette</a>
</IconText>
```

## Props

| Prop           | Type                                                                                     | Default     | Description                              |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `icon`         | `string \| ReactNode`                                                                    |             | Semantic icon name or a node             |
| `iconPosition` | `'start' \| 'end'`                                                                       | `'start'`   | Icon side                                |
| `iconLabel`    | `string`                                                                                 |             | Makes the icon meaningful (`role="img"`) |
| `size`         | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'`                                                                   | `'md'`      | Text and icon size                       |
| `tone`         | `'default' \| 'muted' \| 'primary' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'destructive' \| 'info'` | `'default'` | Colour                                   |
| `asChild`      | `boolean`                                                                                | `false`     | Render your element (e.g. a link)        |
| `classNames`   | `{ icon, text }`                                                                         |             | Classes for each part                    |

Variants are exported as `iconTextVariants`.

## Accessibility

The icon is decorative unless `iconLabel` is set. Give it a label only when it adds meaning the text doesn't.

## RTL

`start`/`end` are logical; directional icons (arrows, external link) mirror in RTL.

---

<!-- docs/display-and-feedback/share-buttons.md -->

# ShareButtons

Share a page. Where the device supports the [Web Share API](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Navigator/share) (most phones), one **Share** button opens the system share sheet. Elsewhere it falls back to **Copy link**, Facebook, X, WhatsApp, Viber, Telegram and email.

```tsx
import { ShareButtons } from "@javaabu/onu"

<ShareButtons url={article.url} title={article.title} />
<ShareButtons native="never" networks={["copy", "whatsapp", "viber", "email"]} iconOnly />
```

## Props

| Prop       | Type                                              | Default      | Description                                                       |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `url`      | `string`                                          | current page | URL to share                                                      |
| `title`    | `string`                                          |              | Title (share sheet, X, Telegram, email subject)                   |
| `text`     | `string`                                          |              | Extra text (share sheet, email body)                              |
| `networks` | `ShareNetwork[]`                                  | all          | `copy`, `facebook`, `x`, `whatsapp`, `viber`, `telegram`, `email` |
| `native`   | `'auto' \| 'always' \| 'never'`                   | `'auto'`     | Share sheet only / plus networks / networks only                  |
| `iconOnly` | `boolean`                                         | `false`      | Icon buttons (labels stay as accessible names)                    |
| `icons`    | `Partial<Record<network \| 'native', ReactNode>>` |              | Replace icons, e.g. with brand logos                              |
| `size`     | `'sm' \| 'default' \| 'lg'`                       | `'default'`  | Button size                                                       |
| `variant`  | `'outline' \| 'ghost' \| 'secondary'`             | `'outline'`  | Button look                                                       |
| `onShare`  | `(network) => void`                               |              | Called after a share action                                       |

`shareUrl(network, url, title?, text?)` builds the share links.

:::info Brand icons
Onu's icon sets (Lucide, FontAwesome Free solid) don't include brand logos, so networks use generic icons with their names as text. Pass `icons` (e.g. from Simple Icons via the Iconify adapter) for logos.
:::

## Accessibility

- A `role="group"` named "Share".
- Network links are named "Share on Facebook", etc., and open in a new tab (email opens the mail app).
- "Link copied" is announced in a polite live region.

## RTL and Dhivehi

Labels are translated; the order follows the page direction.

---

<!-- docs/display-and-feedback/print-back-buttons.md -->

# PrintButton and BackButton

Two small helpers for detail pages, receipts and certificates. Both are shadcn `Button`s, hide themselves when printing (`print:hidden`) and are 44px tall on touch screens.

```tsx
import { BackButton, PrintButton } from "@javaabu/onu"

<BackButton fallbackHref="/applications" />
<BackButton href="/users">All users</BackButton>
<PrintButton onBeforePrint={() => setExpanded(true)} />
<PrintButton iconOnly variant="ghost" />
```

## PrintButton props

| Prop            | Type           | Default     | Description                                  |
| --------------- | -------------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `onBeforePrint` | `() => void`   |             | Runs before `window.print()`                 |
| `iconOnly`      | `boolean`      | `false`     | Icon only; "Print" stays the accessible name |
| `variant`       | Button variant | `'outline'` | Look                                         |
| `children`      | `ReactNode`    | "Print"     | Label                                        |

Calling `event.preventDefault()` in `onClick` cancels printing.

## BackButton props

| Prop           | Type           | Default   | Description                                                      |
| -------------- | -------------- | --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `href`         | `string`       |           | Go here (rendered as a link with the provider's `linkComponent`) |
| `fallbackHref` | `string`       |           | Used when there is no history (page opened directly)             |
| `iconOnly`     | `boolean`      | `false`   | Icon only; "Back" stays the accessible name                      |
| `variant`      | Button variant | `'ghost'` | Look                                                             |
| `children`     | `ReactNode`    | "Back"    | Label                                                            |

Without `href`, it calls `history.back()`.

## Accessibility

Both are real buttons (or a link with `href`) with translated names.

## RTL

The back arrow mirrors in RTL.

---

<!-- docs/display-and-feedback/mini-calendar.md -->

# MiniCalendar

A compact, **read-only** month calendar with event dots, for portal sidebars and dashboards ("Upcoming events"). Built on shadcn's `Calendar` (react-day-picker). It is not a date picker: clicking a day lists that day's events. For the full scheduling calendar use `@javaabu/onu/calendar`.

```tsx
import { MiniCalendar } from "@javaabu/onu"
;<MiniCalendar
  events={[
    { id: 1, date: "2026-03-12T10:00", title: "Council meeting", tone: "primary" },
    { id: 2, date: "2026-03-20", title: "Job fair", tone: "success", href: "/events/job-fair" },
  ]}
  onDayClick={(date, events) => console.log(date, events)}
/>
```

## Props

| Prop            | Type                      | Default       | Description                              |
| --------------- | ------------------------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `events`        | `MiniCalendarEvent[]`     | `[]`          | `{ id?, date, title, tone?, href? }`     |
| `month`         | `Date`                    |               | Controlled month                         |
| `defaultMonth`  | `Date`                    | current month | Initial month                            |
| `onMonthChange` | `(month) => void`         |               | Month navigation                         |
| `onDayClick`    | `(date, events) => void`  |               | Day clicked                              |
| `showEventList` | `boolean`                 | `true`        | List the clicked day's events underneath |
| `maxDots`       | `number`                  | `3`           | Dots per day                             |
| `classNames`    | `{ calendar, list, dot }` |               | Classes for each part                    |

Event `tone`: `primary`, `success`, `warning`, `destructive`, `info` or `muted`.

## Accessibility

- Each day's accessible name includes its event count ("Thursday, March 12th, 2026, 2 events"), so the dots aren't the only signal.
- The event list updates in a polite live region.
- Keyboard navigation is react-day-picker's grid pattern.

| Key                                                 | Action                              |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> <kbd>↑</kbd> <kbd>↓</kbd> | Move between days (mirrored in RTL) |
| <kbd>Page Up</kbd> / <kbd>Page Down</kbd>           | Previous / next month               |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd>                 | List the day's events               |

## RTL and Dhivehi

Month and weekday names, and the first day of the week, come from the active locale. The grid and navigation mirror in RTL.

---

<!-- docs/display-and-feedback/content-card.md -->

# ContentCard

A card for news articles, services and events: image, title, excerpt, date, category, extra meta and a link. Vertical (image on top) or horizontal (image beside the text, stacking when the card is narrow).

```tsx
import { ContentCard } from "@javaabu/onu"
;<ContentCard
  title="New ferry routes connect Hulhumalé and Villimalé"
  excerpt="The new routes run every 30 minutes…"
  image={{ src: "/img/ferry.jpg", alt: "Ferry at the Hulhumalé jetty" }}
  href="/news/ferry-routes"
  date="2026-03-12"
  category="News"
/>
```

## Props

| Prop           | Type                                            | Default      | Description                                        |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ------------ | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `title`        | `ReactNode`                                     |              | Title (the link text)                              |
| `excerpt`      | `ReactNode`                                     |              | Summary, clamped to three lines                    |
| `image`        | `{ src, alt }`                                  |              | `alt` is required; use `""` for decorative images  |
| `href`         | `string`                                        |              | Makes the card clickable                           |
| `date`         | `Date \| string \| number`                      |              | Shown in the locale's format                       |
| `dateFormat`   | `string`                                        | `'PP'`       | date-fns format                                    |
| `category`     | `ReactNode`                                     |              | Category label                                     |
| `meta`         | `ReactNode`                                     |              | Extra meta (venue, read time)                      |
| `footer`       | `ReactNode`                                     |              | Tags, buttons (stay clickable above the card link) |
| `orientation`  | `'vertical' \| 'horizontal'`                    | `'vertical'` | Layout; horizontal stacks under 32rem              |
| `headingLevel` | `2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6`                         | `3`          | Title heading level                                |
| `classNames`   | `{ image, body, title, excerpt, meta, footer }` |              | Classes for each part                              |

## Accessibility

- An `<article>` with a real heading. Only the title is a link, stretched over the card, so screen readers hear a short link name while the whole card stays clickable.
- The focus ring wraps the whole card.

## RTL and Dhivehi

Dates use the active locale (Dhivehi month names). The horizontal image sits at the inline start.

---

<!-- docs/display-and-feedback/error-page.md -->

# Error pages

Full-page error states with a code, title, message, illustration and actions (**Go home**, **Go back**, **Try again**), translated into English and Dhivehi.

```tsx
import { ErrorPage, ForbiddenPage, MaintenancePage, NotFoundPage, ServerErrorPage } from "@javaabu/onu"

<NotFoundPage />                      // 404
<ForbiddenPage homeHref="/dashboard" /> // 403
<ServerErrorPage onRetry={refetch} />   // 500, with Try again
<MaintenancePage homeHref={null} />     // 503
<ErrorPage code={419} title="Session expired" message="Please sign in again." />
```

| Page              | Code | Default icon | Try again |
| ----------------- | ---- | ------------ | --------- |
| `ForbiddenPage`   | 403  | `lock`       | no        |
| `NotFoundPage`    | 404  | `search`     | no        |
| `ServerErrorPage` | 500  | `error`      | yes       |
| `MaintenancePage` | 503  | `wrench`     | yes       |

## Props

| Prop           | Type                                              | Default  | Description                                         |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `code`         | `403 \| 404 \| 500 \| 503 \| number`              |          | Status code (`ErrorPage` only)                      |
| `title`        | `ReactNode`                                       | per code | Heading                                             |
| `message`      | `ReactNode`                                       | per code | Explanation                                         |
| `illustration` | `ReactNode`                                       | icon     | Image or SVG slot                                   |
| `homeHref`     | `string \| null`                                  | `'/'`    | "Go home" link; `null` hides it                     |
| `showBack`     | `boolean`                                         | `true`   | "Go back" (`history.back()`)                        |
| `showRetry`    | `boolean`                                         | 500/503  | "Try again"                                         |
| `onRetry`      | `() => void`                                      | reload   | Retry action                                        |
| `extraActions` | `ReactNode`                                       |          | Added after the default actions                     |
| `actions`      | `ReactNode`                                       |          | Replace all actions                                 |
| `as`           | `'main' \| 'div'`                                 | `'main'` | Use `div` inside a layout that already has `<main>` |
| `classNames`   | `{ illustration, code, title, message, actions }` |          | Classes for each part                               |

## Accessibility

- Rendered as a `<main>` landmark labelled by its `h1`.
- The illustration should be decorative (`alt=""` / `aria-hidden`).
- Buttons stack full-width on phones and are 44px tall on touch screens.

## Framework notes

In Laravel + Inertia, render these from your `Error` page component by status. In Next.js, use them in `not-found.tsx` and `error.tsx` (pass `onRetry={reset}`).
